title: @origingame/engine API v1
description:
The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.
Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

x-og-units.cssPx: CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left
x-og-units.newton: newtons: the force that gives a kilogram one metre per second squared
x-og-units.newtonSecond: newton-seconds: an impulse, the momentum that changes a kilogram's velocity by one metre per second
x-og-units.newtonMetre: newton-metres: a torque, a newton pushing one metre from the axis it turns about
x-og-units.perSecond: a rate per second: the fraction of a value that decays in one second
x-og-units.kgPerM3: kilograms per cubic metre (per square metre in the 2D profile)
x-og-units.pascal: pascals: newtons per square metre, a stress
x-og-units.newtonSecondPerM2: newton-seconds per square metre: an impulse spread over an area
x-og-units.evPerSecond: exposure stops (EV) per second of simulation time

x-og-modules.doc: Plain math values in the three.js vocabulary. They are data: the engine owns the operations, so results are identical on every host.

interfaces.name: Vector3Math
interfaces.doc:
Pure functions over Vector3, as three.js Vector3's methods of the same names: each returns a new value and changes none of its arguments. The value `vec3`: `vec3.add(a, b)`.
No member reads Math.sin, Math.pow or the clock: results are the same bits on every host, so a system may store them in world state.

interfaces.name: Matrix4Math
interfaces.doc: Pure functions over Matrix4 (column-major elements, as three.js), each returning a new value. The value `mat4`: `mat4.multiply(a, b)`.

members.doc: The inverse, as three.js Matrix4.invert; a singular matrix inverts to all zeros, as three.js.

members.name: compose

members.name: empty

members.name: fromPoints

members.name: containsPoint

members.name: containsBox

members.name: intersectsSphere

members.name: union

members.name: getCenter
members.doc: The centre, as three.js Box3.getCenter; the empty box's is the origin.

members.name: getSize
members.doc: The size along each axis, as three.js Box3.getSize; the empty box's is zero.

members.name: applyMatrix4

interfaces.name: PlaneMath
interfaces.doc: Pure functions over Plane, as three.js Plane's methods, each returning a new value. The value `plane`.

members.name: fromNormalAndCoplanarPoint

members.name: fromCoplanarPoints

interfaces.name: FrustumMath
interfaces.doc: Pure functions over Frustum, as three.js Frustum's methods. The value `frustum`: `frustum.intersectsBox(frustum.fromCamera(camera, 16 / 9), box)` culls as the renderer would.

members.name: fromProjectionMatrix

members.name: containsPoint
members.doc: Whether p is inside the frustum, as three.js Frustum.containsPoint.

members.name: intersectsBox

members.name: intersectsSphere
members.doc: Whether the sphere is at least partly inside, as three.js Frustum.intersectsSphere.

members.name: toHex

members.name: lerp

interfaces.name: ScalarMath
interfaces.doc:
JavaScript's Math functions whose results differ between JavaScript engines (Math.sin, Math.pow and the rest are only approximations, and V8, JavaScriptCore and SpiderMonkey round them differently), written with + - * / and sqrt only: the same bits on every host and every browser. The value `math`: `math.sin(a)`. A system whose result reaches the world (lockstep, replays, saves) uses these; `og check` names each Math call that should be one in a game with og.Lockstep.
Math.sqrt, Math.abs, Math.floor, Math.round, Math.min and Math.max are exact everywhere and stay as they are.

members.name: sin
members.doc: The sine of x radians, as Math.sin.

members.name: cos
members.doc: The cosine of x radians, as Math.cos.

members.name: tan
members.doc: The tangent of x radians, as Math.tan.

members.name: asin
members.doc: The arcsine, as Math.asin: -pi/2 to pi/2, NaN outside -1 to 1.

members.name: acos
members.doc: The arccosine, as Math.acos: 0 to pi, NaN outside -1 to 1.

members.name: atan
members.doc: The arctangent, as Math.atan: -pi/2 to pi/2.

members.name: atan2
members.doc: The angle of the point (x, y) from +x, as Math.atan2: -pi to pi, 0 at the origin.

members.name: exp
members.doc: e to the x, as Math.exp.

members.name: log
members.doc: The natural logarithm, as Math.log: -Infinity at 0, NaN below.

members.name: pow
members.doc: x to the y, as Math.pow and `**`: an integer y is multiplication by squaring (x * x for 2), any other y exp(y log x), NaN for a negative x.

x-og-modules.name: reflect
x-og-modules.doc:
Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name.
The inspector, Tune, the probe, scene text and the wiki read this one schema. Each column factory below makes one field.
A field holds one value, or a list of at most a fixed number of one number type or handle: `list(u32(), 8)`, `list(Asset(), 4)` (the list factory below). A list is read as a frozen copy (`push` throws) and written whole (`chain.passes = [...chain.passes, h]`); one over its capacity is refused, never truncated. A few vectors are numbered fields (`p0` to `p7`, as og.CameraRail does); a list of things with fields of their own is an entity each, with its own component, looped over by a query (a ring of skid marks, the laps of a race); a long record (a lap's taped inputs) is text in `str` fields of at most 4,096 bytes each, chunked over entities. Keep none of it in module variables: they are not world state, so a snapshot, a replay and a hot reload lose them.
A handle (an og.load answer, a texture, a sound, a geometry, a material, an entity) is a 64-bit number: keep it in a field of its own kind (`Asset()`, `Texture()`, `Sound()`, `Font()`, `Style()`, `Geometry()`, `Material()`, `Entity()`: every handle type of the API has its factory, named as the type), never cast to another kind, in a component or a resource. A `u32` field refuses one (handles pass 2^32: `4294967298 is not a u32`); an `f64` holds the number but loses its type.

functions.name: defineComponent
functions.doc:
Declare a component: plain data stored per entity in engine memory, one column per field.
Registration is by name, so a hot reload re-registers the same component and migrates its fields by name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The component's unique name, PascalCase, as it appears in scenes and dumps.

params.name: fields
params.doc: The layout: field names to column factories, as `{ hp: f32(100) }`.

functions.returnsDoc: The token systems, queries and the world take.

functions.name: defineResource
functions.doc: Declare a resource: a reflected singleton, such as a tuning table. Its fields start at their defaults.
functions.returnsDoc: The token `world.resource` and system declarations take.

x-og-modules.name: world
x-og-modules.doc:
The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory.
Structural changes (spawn, despawn, insert, remove) invalidate typed views; the API refuses a stale view.

interfaces.name: SaveEdit
interfaces.doc: A save opened for editing (world.openSave), as a migration sees it: the engine's own migrations already applied, every type with its saved fields. Each edit changes the save, not the world; world.restore takes the result. An edit refused changes nothing. Entity ids are the saved world's.

members.name: version
members.doc: The game's save version the save was written at (1 for a save of a game that never declared one).

members.name: types
members.doc: The types the save holds, in its table's order.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the save holds a type.

members.name: records
members.doc: A type's saved values: its components by entity in storage order, then its resource.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a type the save does not hold.

members.name: setRecords
members.doc: Replace a type's values (its components, its resource) with records written as this build's type `into`: the old type's values and queued events go, an entity keeps its other components and its place. A type the save does not hold is added (a component a new version gives saved entities).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The type to write and the records.

members.returnsDoc: Refused, with nothing changed, for a type this build does not declare, a record that does not fit it, or an entity the save does not hold.

members.name: transform
members.doc: Rewrite every value of a type through `map`, which sees the old record: records(name), then setRecords with what map returned. With `into`, the type becomes that one (a rename that reshapes).

params.name: map
params.doc: The old record to the new one.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The type the results are written as.

members.returnsDoc: Refused as setRecords is, or when map throws.

members.name: split
members.doc: Split a type into several: each saved value is handed to `map`, whose answer names the new types' records; the old type goes. The migrated world holds the records a world built at the new version holds, and every peer and every restore of the same save migrates to the same world and hash; its hash differs from a built one's only by the archetypes the built one passed through (inserting the new types one at a time leaves an empty archetype of the first alone, which the split never makes), so compare a split's result record by record, not by hash. renameField, renameType, transform, dropType and spawn keep which types sit together: those migrate to a built world's hash exactly.

params.name: map
params.doc: The old record to the new types' records.

members.returnsDoc: Refused as setRecords is, or when map throws.

members.name: renameType
members.doc: Give a saved type another name, its fields and values as they are (a later restore maps them field by field against the type of the new name).
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a name the save lacks, or one it already has.

members.name: renameField
members.doc: Give a saved type's field another name, its values as they are: `gold` saved, `coins` declared now, and every balance arrives.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a type or field the save lacks, or a name the type already has.

members.name: dropType
members.doc: Remove a type from the save: its components, resource and queued events.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a type the save does not hold.

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Add an entity to the save, with components of this build's types: a whole save gives it the id the next spawn would take, a selection the next free one.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a taken name, a type this build does not declare or a value that does not fit it.

members.name: text
members.doc: The save as text, at GameDesc.saveVersion: what world.restore takes.

members.name: close
members.doc: Let go of the open save. world.restore closes the ones it opens.

interfaces.name: SpatialIndex
interfaces.doc: A spatial hash of entities' positions as they were when world.spatial built it: it does not follow later moves (build it again after they move). Answers are ordered by distance, then by entity, so equal distances come out alike on every run and host. Valid for the system call or the call outside systems it was built in.

members.name: count
members.doc: The entities it holds.

members.name: within
members.doc: Every entity at most `radius` from `center`, nearest first.

params.name: radius
params.doc: The radius in metres; a negative one finds nothing.

members.name: nearest
members.doc: The `count` entities nearest `center`, nearest first; fewer when it holds fewer.

interfaces.name: World
interfaces.doc: The world a system, a command or a game callback is handed. Game code never holds a world beyond the call it was passed to.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps taken since the world was created.

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Spawn an entity.
members.returnsDoc: The new entity, or why it was refused (a duplicate name, a dead parent).

members.name: despawn
members.doc: Despawn an entity and its descendants.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity.

members.name: alive
members.doc: Whether an entity handle is live.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether an entity has a component.

members.name: insert
members.doc: Add a component to an entity, or overwrite it when present. A structural change. Every field is checked against its reflected min/max before the component is changed; an out-of-range value returns an error, never a clamped value.

params.name: value
params.doc: Field values; omitted fields take their defaults.

members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity, an unregistered component or a field outside its reflected range.

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove a component from an entity. A structural change.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: get
members.doc: Copy one entity's component value. For bulk work use a system's typed views.

members.name: set
members.doc: Write some fields of one entity's component.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: resource
members.doc: A resource's live value: the same handle in a world every time, its fields typed reads and writes of the resource's packed record (no JSON, whatever its size). The record is fetched again only by the first read after another engine call or a system boundary, and writes reach the engine in one call before the next engine call and when the system or command returns, so two handles agree and a read after an engine call sees the engine's value (og-core §4). Inside a system, the resource must be among the system's reads or writes (writes to set a field): an undeclared one throws in a dev or release build, naming the system and the resource, and fails the tick; a publish build refuses it and logs it once per system in the engine log.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered resource (or, in a publish build, one the running system did not declare).

members.name: children
members.doc: The entities whose og.Parent is `entity`, in entity order (index, then generation). Any system may ask: it reads only the hierarchy.
members.returnsDoc: Empty for a dead entity or one without children.

members.name: removed
members.doc: Entities that lost a component: removed from them, or despawned with it. Inside a system, since the system last ran (the component among its reads or writes); between ticks, since the last tick began. The world keeps a tick's removals through the next tick. The component must be tracked (a system filters on it: SystemDesc.changed, added or removed).
members.returnsDoc: In entity order; refused for a component no system tracks.

members.name: spatial
members.doc: A spatial hash of the entities SpatialDesc selects, for radius and k-nearest queries on entities without colliders (og.physics answers those with). Inside a system, og.Transform must be among its reads or writes; the index holds the positions as the system sees them when it is built.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Which entities, and the cell size.

members.name: state
members.doc: A state machine's current value (GameDesc.states).
members.returnsDoc: Null for a name GameDesc.states does not declare.

members.name: setState
members.doc: Ask a state machine to move to a value as the next tick begins: that tick runs the systems leaving the old value (SystemDesc.when exit), then those entering the new one (enter), then its systems, those bound to a value (during) only while the machine holds it. The last ask before the tick wins; asking for the value it holds cancels one asked for. Any system may ask.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown state machine or value.

members.name: find
members.doc: The entity with a name.
members.returnsDoc: Null when no live entity has the name.

members.name: prefabOf
members.doc: Where an entity came from when it was placed from a prefab: its og.PrefabLink (the prefab, its node, the instance's root).
members.returnsDoc: Null for an entity not placed from a prefab, or a dead one.

members.name: nameOf
members.doc: An entity's name.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unnamed or dead entity.

members.name: query
members.doc: A query over the current archetypes, for commands and callbacks (GameDesc.start, a command, a UI callback). Inside a system it is refused, by design: a system receives its one query (every component of its reads and writes) as its first argument; loop over another archetype in a system of its own.

members.name: events
members.doc: The events of one type emitted during the previous tick and this one, oldest first. Inside a system the event must be among its reads or writes (undeclared: thrown, or in a publish build refused and logged once).

members.name: emit
members.doc: Emit an event; readers see it this tick and the next. Inside a system the event must be among its writes (undeclared: thrown, or in a publish build refused and logged once).

members.name: instantiate
members.doc:
Spawn a loaded scene, prefab or glTF asset into the world: a root entity from the desc, then (for a scene or prefab) every entity under it with its components (a scene's with their names, a prefab's unnamed, each with an og.PrefabLink to it), or (for a glTF) a Model on the root.
Scene entity names must be free: a name already in use refuses the whole instantiation before anything spawns.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, parent and transform of the root entity.

members.returnsDoc: The root entity, or why it was refused (an asset still loading, a failed asset).

members.name: snapshot
members.doc: The whole world as text, to save a game's progress in the platform store: every entity with its components and names, every resource (og.Time's clock and the og.Rng streams too), the pending events and the modules' state (physics, animation, flipbooks, tweens, tilemap and terrain edits), each type with its schema hash, and the game's save version (GameDesc.saveVersion), deflated and base64-encoded after `og-save:2:`. Every build has it, publish included, and the same world saves to the same text on both hosts. Save it with og.platform.saveSlot (`{ slot: "slot1", text, meta: { name, chimes } }`), which spreads it over as many store keys as it needs (a key holds 64 KiB) and writes the slot's manifest last, then og.platform.loadSlot and world.restore of the answer's `text` (examples/hollowbell, a 2D platformer of 189 entities on a 96 x 48 tile map, saves to about 25 KiB; examples/kestrel-stair, a 3D world of 93 entities with skinned characters, cloths and minds, to about 78 KB; a world of a few entities to about 11 KiB, most of it the table of every registered type; 5,000 entities, half of them physics bodies, to about 436 KiB, written in about 95 ms and restored in about 60 ms natively). With SnapshotDesc's `with` or `resources`, only the tagged entities and the chosen resources (a selection). Inside a system it is the world in the middle of that tick, as that system sees it: what earlier systems wrote this tick is in it, a structural change the system queued (applied when it returns) is not, and it names the system, so a world restored from it completes that tick: its next step runs the systems after this one and the engine's (physics included) with the tick's own events, then ends the tick, and the world goes on tick for tick as the one that saved did (a replay from it matches; make the snapshot the system's last write of the tick, since what it does after the call is not in the save). Between ticks (GameDesc.start, a command, a UI callback) it is the world between two ticks. Physics carries its mesh, convex-hull and height-field colliders by their geometry's handle and scale, not their triangles (og.physics.setMesh). Asset and material handles in components are saved as their numbers: load what a saved entity uses in the same order on every launch (in GameDesc.start) before restoring.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The whole world, or a selection: tagged entities and chosen resources.

members.returnsDoc: The save, or why not (the world could not be read, or SnapshotDesc names a type this world does not register).

members.name: openSave
members.doc: Open a save for editing, as a migration does (SaveEdit): the engine's own migrations applied (an engine upgrade's changes to its components and its modules' state, such as og.ui's state of engine 0.7.7), the game's not yet. world.restore opens and migrates by itself; use this to read a save without restoring it, or to migrate one by hand.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for text world.snapshot did not write, or a save of a newer GameDesc.saveVersion.

members.name: restore
members.doc: Replace the world with a save that world.snapshot wrote (a selection replaces only its tagged entities and its resources: SnapshotDesc). First the engine's own migrations upgrade what an older engine wrote of the engine's state, then GameDesc.migrations run from the save's version to GameDesc.saveVersion, in order, on the save (SaveEdit); a refused or throwing step refuses the restore with its reason and the world is left as it was. A save of a newer saveVersion is refused. Then: entities, components, names, resources, events and the modules' state, so the restored world hashes as the saved one did, on either host. The session stays: input (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.PointerLock), the player's bus volumes (og.Audio), the player's action bindings and dead zones (og.input), the UI's focus and hover, and what lives outside the world (the platform's calls and clock, the language, the loaded assets, the command channel's scheduled steps, which keep their remaining delays though og.Time takes the saved tick, so an `og run --commands` script goes on to its last step or `quit` whether the save is of a later tick or an earlier one). Called in a system or a command it applies when the tick ends, after the last system; elsewhere (GameDesc.start, between ticks) at once. Either way the tick after it delivers og.WorldRestored, for the systems that reset what lives in the session. A save a system took mid-tick restores to that moment of its tick (og.Time reads its tick): the next step completes it (the systems after the saver, then the engine's), so the ticks after it are the saved run's. The meshes and height fields its colliders name must be loaded or registered first (a save naming one that is not is refused). A save holds only the world: progress kept in module variables is not in it, so keep it in components and resources.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Whether a type whose layout changed since the save is mapped field by field.

members.returnsDoc: Refused, with nothing changed, for text world.snapshot did not write, a save from a newer engine or of a newer GameDesc.saveVersion, a migration that refused, or a type whose layout changed since the save (a field added, removed or retyped, an enum's variants) and that the save holds data of (a type it holds none of, no component, resource value or event, takes this build's layout; an engine og.* type that only gained fields takes their declared defaults): the reason names the type and the fields, and the fix (`{ migrate: true }`, a migration in GameDesc.migrations, or keeping a saved type's fields stable between releases).

interfaces.name: Query
interfaces.doc: A set of matched archetypes. Iterate archetypes, never entities one by one.

members.name: archetypes
members.doc: The matched archetypes this tick.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of matched entities.

interfaces.name: ArchetypeView
interfaces.doc: One archetype's columns for this tick. Views are invalidated by structural changes; using a stale view throws with the tick and the system it belonged to.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of entities in the archetype.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The tick this view belongs to.

members.name: entities
members.doc: The entities as (index, generation) pairs: entity i is at 2i and 2i + 1. These are not handles: for a handle use entity(i) (world.despawn, get, set, insert and remove refuse a bare index, naming the call).

members.name: rows
members.doc: The rows the query's change filters pass (SystemDesc.changed, added, removed; QueryDesc's), in row order; every row, 0 to count - 1, for a query without them. Columns still hold every row: loop over rows and index the columns with them.

members.name: entity
members.doc: The handle of entity i.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the archetype carries a component.

members.name: column
members.doc:
The typed views of a component's fields: one typed array per field, `count * stride` long.
Writing requires the component among the system's writes; reading among its reads or writes.

callbacks.name: RecordFn
callbacks.doc: A value's new form: called once per saved value of the type, in storage order.

params.name: value
params.doc: The old record: its fields by name, as saved.

params.name: entity
params.doc: Its entity, or null for the type's resource.

callbacks.name: SplitFn
callbacks.doc: Where one saved value goes when its type splits.

params.name: entity
params.doc: Its entity, or null for the resource.

callbacks.name: MigrateFn
callbacks.doc: One step of a game's save migration: changes the save from SaveMigration.from to the next version.

x-og-modules.name: system
x-og-modules.doc:
Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes.
A system declares what it reads and writes; a write to an undeclared component is refused at registration with the field name.
Its query is every component of its reads and writes together: an entity matches only when it has all of them (and none of `without`). A component declared to read one entity with world.get (the player's car) therefore narrows the loop to entities that have it too, often to none, silently. world.query is refused inside a system, by design (a system reaches only what it declared, so its access is known before it runs): loop over each archetype in a system of its own, declaring only that archetype's components, and carry what crosses between systems in a resource.
Resources and events it reaches through the world must be declared too: in a dev or release build (og run, og test) an undeclared read or write throws with the system's name and the record and fails the tick; a publish build refuses it and logs it once per system in the engine log, and the game keeps running. og.Rng among the reads may fork (a fork reads the seed only and leaves the stream as it is); a draw moves the stream, so it needs og.Rng among the writes.

functions.name: defineHook
functions.doc: Declare a hook on a component; list it in GameDesc.hooks.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Add or remove, and its access.

functions.name: defineSystem
functions.doc: Declare a system.

interfaces.name: Hook
interfaces.doc: A declared hook.

members.name: name
members.doc: The hook's unique name.

interfaces.name: System
interfaces.doc: A registered system.

members.name: name
members.doc: The system's unique name.

members.name: reads
members.doc: What it reads.

members.name: writes
members.doc: What it writes.

callbacks.name: RunCondition
callbacks.doc: Whether a system runs this tick: called before its run, after the systems before it, with the system's reads and writes as read-only access. It may not change the world.

callbacks.name: HookRun
callbacks.doc: A hook's body: called once per entity the component is added to or removed from, wherever the change came from (a system's structural changes as they apply when it returns, or a call between ticks), in the order hooks are listed in GameDesc.hooks. Its own structural changes apply when it returns and may run hooks in turn (16 deep at most). A restore runs none.

callbacks.name: SystemRun
callbacks.doc: A system's body. It is called once per tick; loop over `q.archetypes()`, then over rows.

params.name: q
params.doc: The archetypes matching the declared components.

params.name: time
params.doc: The Time resource for this tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world, for resources, events and structural changes.

x-og-modules.name: game
x-og-modules.doc: The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares.

functions.name: game
functions.doc: Declare the game. The bundle's default export is its result.

interfaces.name: Game
interfaces.doc: A declared game, the bundle's default export.

members.name: tick
members.doc: GameDesc.tick, or 60 when it is unset (the engine then runs at project.ogt's `tick` when the host passes the project, as og run and og build do).

members.name: systems
members.doc: The systems in declaration order.

callbacks.name: FactsFn
callbacks.doc: The game's own facts for the probe's state(): a small JSON object, computed from the world without changing it.

callbacks.name: StartFn
callbacks.doc: The game's setup: called once before the first tick, after GameDesc.scene has spawned. Spawn, insert, load and set resources here; systems then only read and write their views.

x-og-modules.name: transform
x-og-modules.doc: Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain.

functions.name: compose
functions.doc: A matrix from position, rotation and scale, as three.js Matrix4.compose.

functions.name: decompose
functions.doc: Position, rotation and scale from a matrix, as three.js Matrix4.decompose.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.doc: The rotation that points -Z from an eye towards a target, as three.js Object3D.lookAt for cameras.

params.name: up
params.doc: The up direction; the zero vector means +Y.

functions.name: fromAxisAngle
functions.doc: A rotation about an axis, as three.js Quaternion.setFromAxisAngle.

x-og-modules.name: time
x-og-modules.doc:
Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time.
Time groups slow or freeze some entities and not others (a bullet-time enemy beside a player at full speed, a frozen boss, a paused UI diorama): put an entity in a group with og.TimeGroup and set the group's scale with og.time.setGroupScale. og.anim, flipbooks, 2D skeletons, the entity's scaled tweens and its og.nav agent then advance by scaledDt times its group's scale, and its og.ParticleSystem's particles spawn, age and move at the group's scale (the renderer's particles do not follow the global scale or hit stop, so only the group's applies). Physics stays on the global scale (one solver steps every body together; slow a body's motion with its velocity, or move it kinematically), and timelines and the UI keep their own pace. A world that never names og.TimeGroup or og.TimeGroups keeps its saves and hash.

functions.name: setScale
functions.doc: Set the global time scale (slow motion): physics, og.anim, flipbooks and tweens advance by dt * scale from the system after the call; systems may call it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused outside 0..10.

functions.name: hitStop
functions.doc: Freeze scaled time for `ticks` ticks from now (this tick included): physics, og.anim, flipbooks and scaled tweens hold while input, the UI, unscaled tweens and camera shake keep moving. A longer hit stop in progress is never shortened. Typical values at 60 Hz: 2-3 ticks for a light hit, 4-6 medium, 8-12 heavy, 12-20 a finishing blow (paired with slow motion).

functions.name: setGroupScale
functions.doc: Set one time group's scale on top of the global one: 0.25 a quarter speed, 0 frozen, 1 the global pace. Entities with og.TimeGroup in it animate, tween and walk at the new pace from the system after the call; physics stays on the global scale. Outside a system the first call registers og.TimeGroups; inside one it must be registered already (name og.TimeGroup or og.TimeGroups in a system's reads or writes, or call it once in setup).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group past 15, a scale outside 0..10, or inside a system before og.TimeGroups is registered.

functions.name: groupDt
functions.doc: This tick's scaled length for an entity: scaledDt times its time group's scale (scaledDt for an entity in no group). Move an entity's own gameplay by it so a slowed group slows everything it does.

x-og-modules.name: rng
x-og-modules.doc:
Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts.
Inside a system: forking needs og.Rng among the reads (a fork is derived from the seed and the label, and leaves the main stream where it is); drawing from og.Rng itself (next, range, integer, chance, weighted, permutation) moves its state, so it needs og.Rng among the writes. A stream a fork returned is the system's own to draw from.

interfaces.name: RngStream
interfaces.doc: One generator stream, forked from the Rng resource for a subsystem that must not perturb the main sequence.

members.name: seed
members.doc: The stream's derived seed.

members.name: next
members.doc: Uniform in [0, 1).

members.name: range
members.doc: Uniform in [low, high).

members.name: integer
members.doc: A uniform integer in [low, high].

members.name: chance
members.doc: True with probability p.

members.name: weighted
members.doc: An index drawn in proportion to its weight (one draw): `weighted([1, 3])` is 1 three times in four. Zero, negative and non-finite weights are never drawn; -1 when none is positive.

members.name: permutation
members.doc: 0 to n - 1 in a drawn order (Fisher-Yates, n - 1 draws). A shuffled copy of an array is `rng.permutation(a.length).map((i) => a[i])`.

members.name: fork
members.doc: A fresh stream on a seed derived from this stream's seed and a label.

params.name: label
params.doc: The subsystem's name; the same label always gives the same stream.

x-og-modules.name: procgen
x-og-modules.doc:
Procedural generation: gradient noise (Perlin, simplex, FBM), Poisson-disk points, BSP dungeons and wave function collapse, all deterministic. Each generator takes a `seed`; give it the seed of a fork of og.Rng, `world.resource(og.Rng)`'s value `.fork("dungeon").seed` (a fork needs og.Rng among a system's reads only), so the same world and label give the same output and the main stream does not move. A generator draws only from a stream on that seed, in a fixed order, with arithmetic that is bit-identical on every host: the same seed gives the same map natively and on the web, in a replay and after a restore.
Weighted picks and shuffles are og.Rng's and RngStream's own (`weighted`, `permutation`; a shuffle is a permutation applied to an array). og.tilemap.fill writes a generated grid into a tilemap layer.

functions.name: noise
functions.doc: Noise at one point, about -1 to 1: a pure function of the desc and the point.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The seed, kind and fractal settings.

functions.name: noiseGrid
functions.doc: Noise over a grid in one call, row-major: `values[j * width + i]` is the sample at (x + i * step, y + j * step).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for more than 16,777,216 samples.

functions.name: poissonDisk
functions.doc: Poisson-disk points in [0, width) × [0, height), in the order they were placed.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The area, the radius and the seed.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a size or radius that is not finite and above 0, or a radius so small the area needs more than 16,777,216 grid cells.

functions.name: bsp
functions.doc: A BSP dungeon: rooms that never overlap, every floor cell reachable from every other.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The area, the room sizes and the seed.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an area that cannot hold one room of minRoom with its padding.

functions.name: wfc
functions.doc: A grid of tiles whose edges all fit, by wave function collapse.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The grid, the tiles and the seed.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty tile list, a fixed cell outside the grid or naming no tile, or no tiling in `attempts` tries (naming the cell the last try ran out at).

x-og-modules.name: input
x-og-modules.doc:
Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges.
The shell collects pointer, keyboard and wheel input on the main thread; the probe and the command channel inject through the same path.
Several pointers at once (multi-touch) are og.Pointers; up to eight gamepads, mapped to the W3C standard layout, are og.Gamepad. Both are world state, as og.Input is, so they replay.
Gameplay actions (og.input.defineAction) name what the player does instead of the keys that do it: buttons and one- or two-axis values bound to keys, the mouse, pad buttons, sticks, triggers and touch, in contexts, with dead zones and sensitivity. The player rebinds them (og.input.rebind, og.input.startCapture for a controls screen, conflicts reported), the bindings are kept as text (og.input.saveBindings), and prompts read each action's glyph on the device used last (og.input.glyph). Actions are read once per tick from og.Input, og.Pointers and og.Gamepad, so they replay; in lockstep they are this peer's own, handed on with og.net.submit as og.Input is.
Mouse-look (pointer lock, mouse delta, relative mouse movement): set og.PointerLock.wanted and turn the camera by og.Pointers.movement each tick.

consts.name: MAX_POINTERS
consts.doc: The most pointers og.Pointers tracks at once: ids 0 (the primary pointer) to 4.

consts.name: MAX_GAMEPADS
consts.doc: The most gamepads og.Gamepad reads: pads 0 to 7.

functions.name: defineAction
functions.doc: Define (or redefine) a gameplay action. A redefinition keeps the player's bindings while they fit it, and its state while its kind stays. Callable anywhere (GameDesc.start, a system); the map is world state, so snapshots carry it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused, naming the fix, for a binding whose control names none or that does not fit the kind (a stick on a button, a key alone on a two-axis action).

functions.name: actions
functions.doc: Every action, in definition order, with its bindings now and its defaults: what a controls screen lists.

functions.name: action
functions.doc: An action this tick: down, the edges, held, its value and vector, and the device that drove it. Null for an unknown action.

functions.name: actionDown
functions.doc: Whether an action is down this tick (false for an unknown one).

functions.name: actionPressed
functions.doc: Whether an action went down this tick.

functions.name: actionReleased
functions.doc: Whether an action went up this tick.

functions.name: actionHeld
functions.doc: Whether an action has been down for its holdMs.

functions.name: actionValue
functions.doc: An action's value: a button's strength (0 to 1), an axis's value, a two-axis value's length. 0 for an unknown action.

functions.name: actionVector
functions.doc: A two-axis action's value (x right, y up; each -1 to 1 but the mouse's movement); (value, 0) for the others.

functions.name: setContexts
functions.doc: The contexts whose actions are live, first the one whose bindings win a control another context also binds (`["vehicle", "gameplay"]`: E exits the car, not interacts). Empty (the default) is every context, none winning. Takes effect from the next tick's actions.

functions.name: contexts
functions.doc: The live contexts as og.input.setContexts set them (empty: every context).

functions.name: rebind
functions.doc: Rebind one slot of an action (or one part of a composite) for the player. With policy refuse (the default) a binding that shares a control with another action of its context changes nothing and answers the conflicts; swap, replace and allow resolve them. The player's bindings stay until reset and are what og.input.saveBindings writes.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The action, slot, part, binding and policy.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown or locked action, a slot past one after the last, a part the kind has not, or a binding that does not fit.

functions.name: conflicts
functions.doc: What a rebinding would share a control with, changing nothing.

functions.name: resetBindings
functions.doc: Back to the defaults: one action's bindings and toggle, or (no action) every action's, and the pads' dead zones.

params.name: action
params.doc: The action; omitted is every action.

functions.name: setToggle
functions.doc: The player's choice for a button action: a press turns it on and the next off (true), or it is down while held (false).

functions.name: saveBindings
functions.doc: The player's settings as text to keep (og.platform.saveSettings, a save): every rebound action's bindings, the toggles and the dead zones that differ from the defaults.

functions.name: loadBindings
functions.doc: Take what og.input.saveBindings wrote, in place of the player's settings now. Bindings for an action not defined yet are kept until it is (load at start, before or after defining).
functions.returnsDoc: A warning for each entry it could not take (that action keeps its defaults); refused for text that is not saved bindings.

functions.name: startCapture
functions.doc: Start capturing the player's next input for a slot of an action (a controls screen's "press a key"): read og.input.capture each tick until it is done or cancelled, then og.input.applyCapture.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The action, slot, part and the devices it takes.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown or locked action, a slot or part a rebinding would refuse, or a cancel control that names none.

functions.name: capture
functions.doc: Where the capture is: active while it waits, done with the control it took, its binding and the conflicts applying it would meet, or cancelled.

functions.name: cancelCapture
functions.doc: Stop a capture without taking anything.

functions.name: applyCapture
functions.doc: Apply what the capture took: og.input.rebind with its slot and binding.

params.name: policy
params.doc: What to do with a conflict; omitted is refuse.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when no capture is done.

functions.name: glyph
functions.doc: An action's prompt glyph: its first binding on the device (the device used last when omitted); a composite's in one (`W A S D`, `key.wasd`). Null for an unknown action or one with no binding on that device.

params.name: device
params.doc: The device; omitted is the one used last.

functions.name: glyphs
functions.doc: An action's first binding on the device, one glyph per control (a composite's parts in prompt order: up, left, down, right; negative, positive). Empty for an unknown action or one with no binding there.

params.name: device
params.doc: The device; omitted is the one used last.

functions.name: controlGlyph
functions.doc: A control's glyph (what a capture took, before it is applied). Null for a name that names no control.

params.name: device
params.doc: The device it is drawn for (a pad's family); omitted is xbox for a pad control.

functions.name: device
functions.doc: The device the player used last: a key or the mouse, a pad (its family as the host told it, else xbox), or a touch. Prompts follow it live.

functions.name: padDevice
functions.doc: A pad's family as the host told it from the pad's id (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch or a generic pad). Null for a pad that is not connected or that the host did not name.

functions.name: setDeadzones
functions.doc: A pad's dead zones (or every pad's): the player's setting, kept by og.input.saveBindings.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The pad and its dead zones.

functions.name: setSensitivity
functions.doc: Set the player's sensitivity and inversion of an axis action on a device class (SensitivityDesc): applied from the next tick's actions, kept by og.input.saveBindings.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The action, the device class, the scale and the inversions.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown action, a button action, or a scale that is not above 0.

functions.name: sensitivity
functions.doc: An action's sensitivity on a device class (the device used last when omitted): the player's, else scale 1 and nothing inverted.

params.name: device
params.doc: The device class; omitted is the one used last.

functions.name: setKeyboardLayout
functions.doc: The keys the player's keyboard layout prints, for glyphs: the web shell sets it from navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap() (Chrome, Edge), and where the browser has none from the characters the player's unmodified keys type as they are pressed (Firefox, Safari: a key reads as on a US layout until it is pressed once). Bindings still name physical keys (KeyboardEvent.code), so WASD is the same four keys on every layout; only their glyphs change (Z Q S D on AZERTY). Empty is the US layout (native runs). The host's, one for the page: no world state.

params.name: labels
params.doc: Each key's printed label, in place of the last list.

functions.name: keyboardLayout
functions.doc: The keys the layout prints as og.input.setKeyboardLayout last set them, sorted by code (empty: the US layout).

functions.name: setMouse
functions.doc: Set how the host reads the mouse (MouseDesc: raw input). Host only, never world state; fields left out keep their values.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world that is not alive.

functions.name: mouse
functions.doc: How the host reads the mouse: raw input asked for, granted or refused by the browser.

functions.name: rumble
functions.doc: Rumble a pad (or every connected pad): the web shell plays it on the pad's vibration actuator. Output only: it never feeds back into the simulation, and a native run records it in the frame answer's `rumble`.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The pad, the motors and how long.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pad outside -1 to 7 or a value that is not finite.

x-og-modules.name: camera
x-og-modules.doc:
The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names.
Camera controllers are components (OrbitCamera, FollowCamera, Follow2D) on the entity the camera orbits or follows; the systems that drive them ship in TypeScript as og.systems.cameras.

functions.name: shake
functions.doc: Add screen shake: trauma, clamped to 1, which og.Camera decays by traumaDecay. The shake grows with trauma squared, so 0.1-0.2 is a light hit, 0.25-0.4 a medium one, 0.5-0.8 an explosion or a boss slam; 1 is almost never right (nauseating). Visual only. Systems may call it; it takes effect at the engine's og.camera system this tick.

functions.name: punch
functions.doc: A zoom punch: the view narrows by `amount` (0.05 is a tap, 0.15 a slam) and springs back by Camera.punchDecay. Visual only.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The fraction to zoom in (negative zooms out), -0.9 to 4.

functions.name: kick
functions.doc: A directional nudge of the view (recoil, an impact from one side): offset by `distance` along `direction`, returning by Camera.kickDecay. Visual only.

params.name: direction
params.doc: The direction to push the view (normalised here; zero does nothing).

x-og-modules.name: render
x-og-modules.doc: What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call.

consts.name: PARTICLES_ARMED
consts.doc: ParticleSystem.startTick's default: never written. A looping emitter emits as if started at tick 0; a one-shot (`looping false`) emits nothing until its startTick is written, so a burst spawned in `start` waits for its first use. Write it back to re-arm a one-shot without firing it.

consts.name: MAX_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights one frame draws, among those in view; past it the ones brightest at the camera are kept.

consts.name: MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights that shade one screen cluster (a 1/16 by 1/9 tile of the view and one of 24 depth slices); past it the ones brightest at the camera are kept there.

consts.name: UI_LAYER
consts.doc: The UI's layer among screen sprites and screen text (SpriteDesc and TextDesc with screen): those at or below it draw under every og.ui element, those above it over every one, modals, toasts and the screen transition included (a HUD element made of sprites sitting on a UI panel: draw it only while its screen shows), in their layers' order either way.

consts.name: MAX_REFLECTION_PROBES
consts.doc: The most og.ReflectionProbe components one frame samples, nearest the camera first; the rest are skipped.

functions.name: snap
functions.doc: Draw entity, and everything under it through og.Parent, at its tick transform on the frames until the next tick instead of blending from where it was (RenderSettings.interpolate): call it on the tick a game teleports, respawns or resets an entity, so it does not glide across the screen. A move past RenderSettings.snapDistance snaps without it. Systems and commands may call it; it is presentation only and never reaches the world, world_hash or a snapshot.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity.

functions.name: snapCamera
functions.doc: Draw og.Camera at its tick pose on the frames until the next tick instead of blending from where it was: a cut. A camera move past RenderSettings.snapDistance snaps without it. Presentation only, as og.render.snap.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

functions.name: ribbon
functions.doc: Draw a ribbon this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead texture or fewer than two points.

functions.name: sprite
functions.doc: Draw a sprite this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit it every tick the sprite should show.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The texture, placement, region and colour.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead texture.

functions.name: floatingText
functions.doc: Spawn a floating text (damage numbers, +coins, `blocked`). It lives `lifetime` seconds of scaled time on its own; systems and commands may call it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The text, the point and the style.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font, or no font when the UI has none.

functions.name: measureText
functions.doc: The size text takes when og.render.text draws it, for centring, wrapping and layout.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: boxGeometry
functions.doc: Make a box geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a convex or triangle-mesh Collider.mesh too.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: planeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a plane geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh too.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: sphereGeometry
functions.doc: Make a sphere geometry for og.Mesh (give its body a sphere Collider, not this mesh).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its radius, tessellation and texture repeat.

functions.name: standardMaterial
functions.doc: Create a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters; omitted ones take three.js defaults.

functions.name: updateMaterial
functions.doc: Change some parameters of a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters to change; omitted ones keep their values.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead material.

functions.name: shaderMaterial
functions.doc: Create a standard material that draws with a material shader's hooks (vertex_offset, surface_color, surface_normal, surface_emissive; og-render §9 has their WGSL contract), its parameters at their defaults. The hooks apply to skinned meshes too, and shadows and the depth prepass (ambient occlusion, outlines, depth of field) see the mesh where vertex_offset moved it and cut where surface_color's alpha falls below alphaTest.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The base material; omitted parameters take three.js defaults. A dissolve sets alphaTest so that alpha below it is cut.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a shader not loaded in this world.

functions.name: setMaterialShader
functions.doc: Give an existing material a material shader, or take it away with null: a loaded model's material (GltfInfo.materials) draws its skinned or static meshes through the hooks, with the shader's parameters at their defaults. Every mesh drawn with that material changes.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: material
params.doc: The material, from og.render.standardMaterial, og.render.shaderMaterial or a loaded glTF.

params.name: shader
params.doc: The shader, or null to draw the material plain again.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead material or a shader not loaded in this world.

functions.name: setShaderParam
functions.doc: Set a parameter of a shader material, by the name its shader declares: a number for float, two to four for vec2, vec3, vec4 and color.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: material
params.doc: A material made by og.render.shaderMaterial or given a shader by og.render.setMaterialShader.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a material without a shader or a parameter its shader does not declare.

functions.name: applyLook
functions.doc: Apply a look, in GameDesc.start (or name it in GameDesc.look) or at any tick for a level's mood, a flashback or a photo mode: every resource the look names is replaced whole (the fields it sets take its values, the rest their defaults; PostEffects.flash and PostEffects.shakeTrauma, which game code animates, keep theirs), and the UI is configured with its style, keeping the rest of the last UiDesc. Resources it does not name are left as they are. Inside a system, the system must declare those resources among its writes, except the art contract's (ArtPalette, ArtPixels, ArtTexels, ArtShape, ArtLine, ArtMotion, ArtCamera): one the system does not declare is left as it is, so a system that declares the frame's resources applies looks that carry a contract. A look that switches the stylisation (a Stylise pass on or off, the pixel grid, retro 3D, the material style) starts TAA's history over, as a camera cut does, so its first frame holds no ghost of the old look.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a look not loaded in this world, one in a streaming group that is not resident (the reason names it), or a resource the system did not declare.

functions.name: applyQuality
functions.doc:
Apply a graphics preset: write its row of RenderSettings' quality fields (the rest of RenderSettings keeps its values) and record it in RenderSettings.quality. The renderer reads those fields and nothing else, so what the probe and dump_world show of RenderSettings is what the next frame draws. A game calls it when the player picks a preset on its settings page (og.ui.settingsTree), and applies a saved preset itself at start. Inside a system, the system must declare RenderSettings among its writes. The rows:
| Field | low | medium | high |
|---|---|---|---|
| rectShadows | false | true | true |
| shadowedLights | 2 | 8 | 16 |
| shadowCascades | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| shadowMapScale | 0.5 | 1 | 2 |
| volumetricFog | false | true | true |
| softParticles | false | true | true |
| screenSpaceReflections | false | true | true |
| ambientOcclusion | false | true | true |
| aoResolution | half | postEffects | full |
| ssrStepScale | 0.5 | 1 | 2 |
| volumetricStepScale | 0.5 | 1 | 2 |
| msaaSamples | 1 | 4 | 4 |
| upscaler | taau | taau | fsr3 |
Medium is every field's default, the frame drawn before any preset. The device caps two of the rows, as RenderCapabilities says: shadowedLights by maxShadowedLights and msaaSamples by maxMsaaSamples; the fields keep the row's value.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world that is not alive, or inside a system that did not declare RenderSettings among its writes.

functions.name: setDisplay
functions.doc: Set the player's graphics settings (DisplaySettings: preset, frame cap, battery saver, render scale, automatic quality, fullscreen, power preference). A call merges over the current settings: only the fields it names change, so a settings screen sets the one the player moved without restating the rest (og.render.resetDisplay goes back to the defaults). Applied from the next frame (the power preference at the next load); presentation only, so it is allowed inside any system and never changes the simulation.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose display it is.

params.name: settings
params.doc: The settings to change: fields left out keep their values (the defaults before any call), so a game that sets its frame cap keeps the player's render scale; quality null is the game's own.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world that is not alive.

functions.name: resetDisplay
functions.doc: Put every graphics setting back to its default (DisplaySettings' zero value: the game's own quality, frame cap auto, render scale 1, automatic quality on, no battery saver, windowed, high performance): a settings page's Reset to defaults. Applied from the next frame like og.render.setDisplay; a power preference that changes back applies at the next load.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose display it is.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world that is not alive.

functions.name: display
functions.doc: What the display draws now: the settings, the frame cap resolved, the render scale automatic quality chose, the scene's size, the device losses survived, the GPU memory, and what the browser decides (vsync, fullscreen now, the adapter's power preference and whether a restart is needed).

functions.name: look
functions.doc: The look last applied (by og.render.applyLook or GameDesc.look), as og.load.lookInfo describes it; null before any.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: The renderer's tier and limits on this device.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer is asked.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: Draw text this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit it every tick the text should show. Multi-page fonts are drawn page by page with one layout.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The font, text, placement and colour.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: bufferGeometry
functions.doc: Make a geometry from attribute arrays (three.js BufferGeometry): procedural levels, 2D polygons, meshes a tool made. It draws as any geometry (og.Mesh), its BVH is built for og.render.raycast, and (desc.physics) it is a Collider.mesh at once.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an attribute whose length does not fit the vertex count, an index past the vertices, or a number that is not finite (the reason names the attribute).

functions.name: updateGeometry
functions.doc: Rewrite a dynamic geometry's attributes in place (desc as og.render.bufferGeometry's, every attribute given again; `dynamic` and `physics` keep their values from when it was made). The same vertex and index counts rewrite its GPU buffers in place; other counts reallocate them, which costs more and is fine now and then. Its BVH is rebuilt, and its physics mesh re-registered (colliders made from it are rebuilt at the next step). Every og.Mesh, og.Lines and og.Points showing it changes.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: geometry
params.doc: A geometry og.render.bufferGeometry made with dynamic true.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead or static geometry, or attributes og.render.bufferGeometry refuses.

functions.name: geometryInfo
functions.doc: A geometry's counts and bounds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: geometry
params.doc: Any geometry: made, a primitive or a loaded glTF's.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead geometry.

functions.name: cylinderGeometry
functions.doc: Make a cylinder geometry for og.Mesh (give its body a cylinder-like Collider: a capsule, a convex Collider.mesh of it, or the geometry itself).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: coneGeometry
functions.doc: Make a cone geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a convex Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: capsuleGeometry
functions.doc: Make a capsule geometry for og.Mesh (its body's Collider is a capsule of the same radius and half the height).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: torusGeometry
functions.doc: Make a torus geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: ringGeometry
functions.doc: Make a ring geometry for og.Mesh (one-sided: give it a double-sided material to see it from behind).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: circleGeometry
functions.doc: Make a circle geometry for og.Mesh (one-sided, as ringGeometry).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: tubeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a tube along a curve through points for og.Mesh: pipes, cables, rails, a path shown as a ribbon of geometry. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for fewer than two points or a point that is not finite (without a path), or a path that is not alive.

functions.name: shapeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a flat shape for og.Mesh (one-sided, as circleGeometry): an og.Shape with holes, or a points array. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a shape whose points are not finite or that triangulates to nothing.

functions.name: extrudeGeometry
functions.doc: Make an extruded solid for og.Mesh: a three.js extrusion is a paste (`og.render.extrudeGeometry(world, { shapes: shape, depth: 0.2, bevelEnabled: true })`). Gears, signs, keys, logos, cookie cutters; along a path, a rail or a moulding.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shapes, depth, bevel and path.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a shape whose points are not finite or that triangulates to nothing, or an extrudePath that is not alive.

functions.name: latheGeometry
functions.doc: Make a solid of revolution for og.Mesh: a profile turned round +Y.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for fewer than two points or one that is not finite.

functions.name: polyhedronGeometry
functions.doc: Make a polyhedron from vertices and faces for og.Mesh, subdivided onto a sphere.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The vertices, faces, radius and detail.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for no faces, an index past the vertices, or a count that is not a multiple of three.

functions.name: icosahedronGeometry
functions.doc: Make an icosahedron (twenty faces) for og.Mesh; with detail, a geodesic sphere.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: dodecahedronGeometry
functions.doc: Make a dodecahedron (twelve pentagons, thirty-six triangles) for og.Mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: octahedronGeometry
functions.doc: Make an octahedron (eight faces) for og.Mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: tetrahedronGeometry
functions.doc: Make a tetrahedron (four faces) for og.Mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: sweepGeometry
functions.doc: Make a section swept along a path for og.Mesh, tapered and twisted by keys.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The section, path, keys and caps.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not alive, a section of fewer than three points or of no area, or a value that is not finite.

functions.name: csgGeometry
functions.doc: Make the union, difference or intersection of two placed geometries for og.Mesh. Chain calls for more operands (a cube minus six spheres is six calls); each result is a geometry like any other.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead geometry, a placement with a zero scale, or a position that is not finite.

functions.name: mergeGeometries
functions.doc: Make one geometry of several placed ones for og.Mesh: one draw instead of many, mirrored halves, arrays.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for no parts, a dead geometry, or a placement with a zero scale.

functions.name: lines
functions.doc: Draw lines this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit them every tick they should show (og.Lines keeps a static set).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws them.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for fewer than two points or a colours list whose length is not the points'.

functions.name: points
functions.doc: Draw a point cloud this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a colours list whose length is not the points'.

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: Every drawn triangle a ray crosses, nearest first, as three.js Raycaster.intersectObjects: what is drawn, not the colliders (og.physics.raycast answers those). It tests og.Mesh and og.Model entities at their world transforms through a BVH per geometry (built when the geometry is made, loaded or updated), both faces of each triangle, skinned models in their bind pose. Read the world as of the call; inside a system, its transforms as earlier systems left them.

params.name: ray
params.doc: The ray; its direction need not be normalised and must not be zero.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a zero or non-finite direction.

functions.name: light2dAt
functions.doc:
The 2D light reaching a point, for game rules (a stealth game's "is the player lit"): the sum of every og.Light2D whose layers share a bit with `layers`, each its color times intensity times its falloff (and a spot's cone), point and spot lights blocked when castShadows and an og.Occluder2D on their layers stands between them and the point (hard shadows through the same rectangles and polygons the light map draws; an occluder holding the point or the light blocks nothing). Ambient light is not included. Lights and occluders are read at their world transforms as of the call.
The result is the same bits on every host (og-core's deterministic math, never the GPU), so a system may store it in the world. Inside a system, declare reads of og.Light2D, og.Occluder2D, og.Transform and og.Parent.

params.name: point
params.doc: The point in the 2D plane, in world units.

params.name: layers
params.doc: The light layers the point is on, a bit per layer as og.LightMask2D.layers.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a non-finite point, or inside a system that did not declare the reads.

functions.name: renderTarget
functions.doc: Make a render target: a texture an og.CameraView or og.Mirror draws into, its colour (RenderTargetInfo.texture) usable by any map, sprite or UI image, as three.js WebGLRenderTarget and its texture. Targets are drawn before the frame, so a material shows this frame's image; one a camera draws while it sees itself (a monitor in the room it films) shows the frame before.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a side past RenderCapabilities.maxRenderTargetSize.

functions.name: setPostParam
functions.doc: Set a parameter of a custom post pass, by the name its asset declares: a number for float, two to four for vec2, vec3, vec4 and color. Every frame it runs in reads it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the pass.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pass not loaded in this world or a parameter it does not declare.

functions.name: postErrors
functions.doc: The custom post passes PostEffects.custom names that failed to compile on this device, each skipped (the frame draws as without it). The cook validates every pass for each back end, so this is a device's own refusal.

functions.name: bakedLighting
functions.doc: The baked lighting of every scene instantiated in the world, in instantiation order: whether it is drawn, and why not. A scene with no static model and no LightVolume is not listed.

x-og-modules.name: shapes
x-og-modules.doc:
Two-dimensional outlines in three.js's words: og.Shape and og.Path2 are three.js's Shape and Path, built by the same calls (moveTo, lineTo, quadraticCurveTo, bezierCurveTo, splineThru, arc, absarc, ellipse, absellipse, closePath) and flattened to points by getPoints, so a three.js outline is a paste. og.render.shapeGeometry, extrudeGeometry and sweepGeometry take them; only their points cross to the engine.
They are TypeScript values, not world state: make them in start or a command and let the geometry made from them be what the world keeps. Points come from basic arithmetic (no Math.sin), so they are the same on every host.
A prop of these parts belongs in an asset: an `.ogt` of `type model` names each part's geometry by its og.render call (`extrudeGeometry { shape { absarc 0 0 1 0 6.283185307179586 false } depth 0.2 }`), its shapes as og.Shape's calls one a line with `hole { }` blocks, places parts as mergeGeometries does (`position`, `quaternion`, `scale`, `mirror`, or several `at { }` blocks: one mesh drawn instanced), gives each a `material` and hangs it from a named `pivot` (a node). og cook builds it into the model blob a glTF cooks to (levels of detail, raycast BVH, nodes), refuses it past project.ogt's triangle and vertex budgets, and og dev re-cooks it on an edit; og.load.gltf and a scene's `model` line take it as any model. og-model §9 has a whole example.

values.name: Path2
values.doc: three.js's Path (named Path2 beside og.path's 3D paths): `new og.Path2().moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(1, 0)`.

values.name: Shape
values.doc: three.js's Shape: `const s = new og.Shape(); s.moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(1, 0).lineTo(0, 1); s.holes.push(hole)`.

interfaces.name: PathList
interfaces.doc: A shape's holes, as three.js Shape.holes: an array; push a path to add a hole.

members.name: length
members.doc: How many holes.

members.name: push
members.doc: Add a hole (Array.push).

interfaces.name: Path2
interfaces.doc: An outline of curves, as three.js Path: each call adds a curve from the current point (moveTo only moves it). Every method but getPoints returns the path, so calls chain.

members.name: moveTo
members.doc: Move the current point without drawing, as three.js Path.moveTo.

members.name: lineTo
members.doc: A straight line to (x, y), as three.js Path.lineTo.

members.name: quadraticCurveTo
members.doc: A quadratic Bézier curve through one control point to (x, y), as three.js Path.quadraticCurveTo.

members.name: bezierCurveTo
members.doc: A cubic Bézier curve through two control points to (x, y), as three.js Path.bezierCurveTo.

members.name: splineThru
members.doc: A Catmull-Rom spline from the current point through the points, as three.js Path.splineThru (a SplineCurve).

params.name: points
params.doc: The points it passes through, in order.

members.name: arc
members.doc: A circular arc centred at (x, y) from the current point, as three.js Path.arc.

params.name: x
params.doc: The centre's x, from the current point.

params.name: y
params.doc: The centre's y, from the current point.

members.name: absarc
members.doc: A circular arc centred at (x, y), as three.js Path.absarc: a line joins it to the current point when they differ.

members.name: ellipse
members.doc: An elliptic arc centred at (x, y) from the current point, as three.js Path.ellipse.

params.name: x
params.doc: The centre's x, from the current point.

params.name: y
params.doc: The centre's y, from the current point.

params.name: rotation
params.doc: The ellipse's turn round its centre.

members.name: absellipse
members.doc: An elliptic arc centred at (x, y), as three.js Path.absellipse.

params.name: rotation
params.doc: The ellipse's turn round its centre.

members.name: setFromPoints
members.doc: Start at the first point and draw lines through the rest, as three.js Path.setFromPoints.

members.name: closePath
members.doc: A line back to the first point when the outline does not end there, as three.js CurvePath.closePath.

members.name: getPoints
members.doc: The outline as points, as three.js CurvePath.getPoints: each curve divided into `divisions` (an ellipse twice as many, a spline as many per point, a line one), repeated points dropped.

interfaces.name: Shape
interfaces.doc: An outline with holes, as three.js Shape.

members.name: holes
members.doc: The holes: `shape.holes.push(hole)`.

members.name: extractPoints
members.doc: The outline's and the holes' points, as three.js Shape.extractPoints.

interfaces.name: Path2Class
interfaces.doc: og.Path2: `new og.Path2(points?)`.

members.name: new
members.doc: A path, through the points when given (setFromPoints).

interfaces.name: ShapeClass
interfaces.doc: og.Shape: `new og.Shape(points?)`.

members.name: new
members.doc: A shape, through the points when given (setFromPoints).

x-og-modules.name: load
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/.
Paths are asset ids: the path under assets/ (`models/ship.glb`, `scenes/main.ogt`); an `assets/` prefix is accepted. Every blob is checked against the manifest's type, schema version and cook stamp.
The game's bundle (`cooked`) is opened before the first tick and GameDesc.scene is spawned then. Loads from an open bundle complete at once on both hosts (the web host fetches the bundle's files before the engine starts); only og.load.bundle of another bundle can be pending, and it completes at a tick boundary.

functions.name: bundle
functions.doc: Open another cooked bundle (the game's own `cooked` is open before the first tick). Its loads read through it once it is ready.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The cooked directory, relative to the project (or the page), such as `dlc/cooked`.

functions.returnsDoc: The bundle's handle: pending until its manifest is read, then ready or failed.

functions.name: bundleInfo
functions.doc: What an open bundle holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: asset
params.doc: A bundle handle; the game's own bundle is og.load.bundle's first answer, also given by `defaultBundle`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-bundle asset.

functions.name: defaultBundle
functions.doc: The game's own bundle, opened before the first tick from `cooked/`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when cooked/ was missing or unreadable (run og cook); the reason names the path.

functions.name: gltf
functions.doc:
Load a cooked glTF (.gltf or .glb), as three.js GLTFLoader.load: its meshes, materials and textures join the renderer once.
A MagicaVoxel `.vox` cooks to a glTF and loads here too: greedy-meshed, flat-shaded, its palette as vertex colours, z-up turned y-up, each model about its centre (MagicaVoxel's pivot, with a scene graph or without). Its import settings (`models/hut.vox.ogt`, `type import`) size and place it: `model { voxScale 0.1 voxOrigin bottom }` is 0.1 m a voxel (default 1) and the lowest voxel on y = 0 (default `center`, the editor's origin). A `.vox` with frames (MagicaVoxel's animation) cooks to clips that swap the frames' models, played by og.AnimationPlayer as any skinned clip: `voxFps 8` (default 10) and `voxClip walk 0 3` (frames 0 to 3; default one clip `frames` of the file's playback range, else of every frame); a node's `_loop` repeats its keys as the editor plays them.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle, or why it was refused (an uncooked path, a cook stamp mismatch, no open bundle).

functions.name: scene
functions.doc: Load a cooked scene (.ogt). world.instantiate spawns its entities: depth first, parents before children, each component table matched to a registered component by its reflected name (`Transform` is og.Transform) and migrated field by field; a field the scene lacks keeps its default, one the component lacks is dropped with a warning.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The scene's asset id, such as `scenes/main.ogt`.

functions.name: prefab
functions.doc: Load a cooked prefab (an .ogt of `type prefab`: one entity tree authored once and placed many times, docs/design.md §2.5). world.instantiate spawns it as it spawns a scene, its root under the desc's root entity, each entity unnamed (place a prefab many times without name clashes) and carrying an og.PrefabLink. A scene places one with a `prefab` line in an entity, and the cook flattens it there.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The prefab's asset id, such as `prefabs/crate.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: The prefab, or why not (not cooked, or not a prefab).

functions.name: font
functions.doc: Load a cooked MSDF font for og.render.text, or an icon set (an `.ogt` of `type icons`: SVG icons cooked into a distance-field atlas like a font) for UiDesc.icons.font.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

params.name: path
params.doc: The font's asset id, such as `fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular-subset.ttf`.

functions.name: fontInfo
functions.doc: A loaded font's metrics.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: sound
functions.doc:
Load a cooked sound for the audio module. Sounds are `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.ogg` (Vorbis) and `.flac` files under assets/ (and procedural `.ogt` presets): og cook decodes each to 16-bit PCM and encodes it to QOA, so every format plays, streams and loops the same. The asset id keeps the source's extension (`audio/theme.mp3`).
