functions.doc: Fail an active quest now: its undone objectives are marked failed.
functions.returnsDoc: False when it is not active. Refused for a quest not loaded.

functions.name: quest
functions.doc: A started quest as the log shows it.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a quest not started.

functions.name: quests
functions.doc: Every started quest, in the order they started (a quest log).

functions.name: track
functions.doc: Show a quest in the HUD tracker, or stop showing it.
functions.returnsDoc: False for a quest not started.

functions.name: markSeen
functions.doc: The player looked at a quest: clear QuestView.isNew and updated.
functions.returnsDoc: False for a quest not started.

functions.name: mark
functions.doc: Point a quest at an entity or a point (the map, compass and tracker read QuestView.marker), over its objectives' own markers.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The entity or point; both zero clears it.

functions.returnsDoc: False for a quest not started.

x-og-modules.name: platform
x-og-modules.doc:
Platform services as host capabilities (docs/design.md §2.8): cloud store, leaderboards, telemetry, Origin Point and AI marks. Game code names a method and its arguments, never a credential, a URL or a cookie: the host owns them. On the web the shell forwards each call to the Player through origin-checked postMessage (Player protocol 2, docs/web-export.md); natively the host answers from a local JSON store (`og run --platform-store`, default `<project>/.og/platform.json`).
Calls are asynchronous: each returns a request number at once, and the answer arrives at the start of a later tick, when og.platform sends PlatformAnswered; read it with og.platform.result. Answers are host input, like key presses: the probe's `dump_platform` lists every call, its arguments, its answer and the ticks.
Errors carry the Player's stable codes: offline, timeout, invalid, unauthorized, not_found, conflict, too_large, rate_limited, unavailable, failed, cancelled (the player backed out of a purchase, an ad or a share sheet) and no_fill (no ad to show now); retryable is true for offline, timeout, unavailable, rate_limited and no_fill.
Purchases, ads, achievements, the player, friends, invites and share (products, purchase, showAd, achievementUnlock, player, friends, inviteSend, share, ...) are the platform's: accounts and money never enter the engine. Each call is a method name and its arguments, the host attaches the player's game-scoped credential, and every id it hands back (the player, a friend, a purchase, an invite) is opaque and scoped to this game. A host that lacks one answers it `unavailable`: ask og.platform.supports first. Natively and in playtests a deterministic fake answers them (`og run --platform-fake`, PlaytestDesc.platform); a published page never fakes them. Entitlements are always the host's answer, never the engine's log or a save: ask og.platform.entitlements when the game starts, and grant a consumable once per purchase with og.platform.grant.
Unasked host input (a pending purchase settled, a refund, an entitlement changed on another device, an invite arrived) is a notice: og.PlatformNotice at the start of a tick, read with og.platform.notice, logged with the answers. In a running lockstep or rollback session (og.Lockstep) a platform answer or notice is this peer's alone: a system that reads og.PlatformAnswered or og.PlatformNotice, or calls og.platform.result or og.platform.notice, while it writes shared state (anything but the session's own records: input, audio, camera, og.Lockstep) hears nothing and reads null, and the engine logs it once; carry what every peer must see in og.PlayerInput (og.net.submit).
Rooms (roomCreate, roomJoin, roomSend, ...) put this engine with other players' engines: the host carries them (natively `og relay` with `og run --room`, on the web the platform's rooms through the shell, docs/platform-asks.md) and its answers and the other peers' messages arrive as events at the start of a tick (og.RoomJoined, og.RoomPeerJoined, og.RoomPeerLeft, og.RoomMessage), host input like key presses. Deterministic play over a room is og.net's lockstep.

functions.name: storeGet
functions.doc: Read one key of the player's store for this game.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed key. The answer's data is `{ key, value, revision }` (value null and revision 0 for a key never written).

functions.name: storeSet
functions.doc: Write one key of the player's store for this game; with a revision, only if nobody wrote it since (another device, another tab).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The key, the value and the revision it must be at.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed key or a value over 64 KiB. The answer's data is `{ key, revision }` (the new revision); `conflict` when the key moved past desc.revision.

functions.name: storeList
functions.doc: The keys of the player's store and their revisions.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ keys: [{ key, revision }] }`.

functions.name: leaderboardSubmit
functions.doc: Submit a score; the board keeps the player's best.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The board, the score and its order.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a score that is not finite. The answer's data is `{ board, rank, best }`, or `{ board, rank: null, queued: true }` while offline.

functions.name: leaderboardTop
functions.doc: The best entries of a board, and the player's own.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ board, order, entries: [{ rank, name, score, me }], me }`.

functions.name: leaderboardAround
functions.doc: The entries around the player's rank.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The board and how many around the player.

functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is the leaderboardTop shape with the entries around the player's rank.

functions.name: telemetry
functions.doc: Record a game event for the game's analytics.

params.name: name
params.doc: The event: `level.started`, `level.completed`, `boss.defeated` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`; the Player files it as `game.custom.<name>`).

params.name: attrs
params.doc: Its attributes: an object of at most 16 strings (up to 512 characters), numbers, booleans or null, keys a lowercase letter then letters, digits and `_`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed name or attributes. Fire and forget: nothing answers.

functions.name: point
functions.doc: Ask for Origin Point for something the player did.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a reason outside 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. The answer's data is `{ granted, balance }`; under a Player today always `{ granted: 0, balance: null }` (the platform grants nothing until a release carries an approved point policy), locally the amount asked.

functions.name: aiMark
functions.doc: Disclose AI-generated content the game shows.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty kind or label. The answer's data is `{ marked: true }`.

functions.name: loadSettings
functions.doc: Ask for the game's saved settings (volume, controls, language): store.get of the key `og.settings`. Where the Player has no store, or is offline, the shell answers from the browser's own storage; natively, from the local store.
functions.returnsDoc: The request; its answer's data is `{ key, value, revision }` (value null before the first save).

functions.name: saveSettings
functions.doc: Save the game's settings under `og.settings` (the last save wins), with the same local fallback as loadSettings.

params.name: value
params.doc: The settings: an object, at most 64 KiB encoded.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a value that is not an object or is too large.

functions.name: saveSlot
functions.doc: Save a long text under a slot, in as many store keys as it needs: a mid-size 3D world's snapshot is over a key's 64 KiB (examples/kestrel-stair's 93 entities: about 78 KB). The parts go in the bank of keys the slot's last save did not use (`<slot>.a*` or `<slot>.b*`), then the manifest (`<slot>`: the bank, the part count, the length, a checksum and `meta`) is written last, at the revision read before: so a save cut short leaves the last one whole, and another device's save landing meanwhile is a conflict, never a mix. One request for all of it; a slot takes at most 17 of the player's 64 keys for this game (its two banks and the manifest: 1 MiB, the platform's budget for a player and game), and a world that would take more saves a selection of what it keeps (world.snapshot's SnapshotDesc). og-game §8.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The slot, the text and what a title shows of it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed slot name, a text over 512 KiB or a meta over 4 KiB. The answer arrives when the manifest is written: data `{ slot, parts, bytes, revision }`; an error is the first refused part's, or the manifest's (`conflict`: another save of the slot landed meanwhile; the slot holds that one).

functions.name: loadSlot
functions.doc: Read a slot saveSlot wrote: its manifest, then its parts, joined and checked against the manifest's length and checksum. One request for all of it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The slot, and whether to read its meta alone.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed slot name. The answer's data is `{ slot, text, meta, parts, bytes, revision }`: text and meta null for a slot never saved, text null with metaOnly; `invalid` for a key that holds no slot manifest or parts that do not match it.

functions.name: products
functions.doc: Describe the products the game sells: titles and prices as the player's store shows them. The catalogue and the prices are the platform's.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id or more than 100. The answer's data is `{ products: [{ id, kind, title, description, price: { amount, currency, display } }] }`: kind `consumable`, `durable` or `subscription`, amount in the currency's units, display as the player's store writes it.

functions.name: purchase
functions.doc: Ask the player to buy a product: the host shows its own purchase sheet and takes the money. The answer is the host's word on it; deliver a consumable with og.platform.grant and then og.platform.consume.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed product id. The answer's data is `{ purchase, product, quantity, state }`: state `completed`, or `pending` (waiting for a parent's approval or a payment; a `purchase` notice settles it). Errors: `cancelled` (the player backed out), `not_found` (no such product), `conflict` (a durable already owned), `unavailable`.

functions.name: entitlements
functions.doc: What the player owns in this game, as the host knows it: durables, active subscriptions and consumables not yet consumed. Ask when the game starts and after a restore, never trust a save for it.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ entitlements: [{ purchase, product, kind, quantity, expires }] }`, expires UTC milliseconds for a subscription, null otherwise.

functions.name: consume
functions.doc: Tell the host a consumable purchase was delivered: it leaves the entitlements. Grant it first (og.platform.grant).

params.name: purchase
params.doc: The purchase id an answer, an entitlement or a notice carried.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id (1 to 128 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and `:`). The answer's data is `{ purchase, product, consumed: true }`; `not_found` for a purchase not owned or already consumed.

functions.name: grant
functions.doc: Record that this world granted purchase `purchase` (in og.PlatformGrants): true the first time, false for one already granted, so a purchase's answer, notice or entitlement seen again (a replay, a relaunch, a save restored from before og.platform.consume) grants once. It records; it is not proof of payment (the host's answer is). Inside a system, declare og.PlatformGrants among its writes.
functions.returnsDoc: Whether it was new. Refused for a malformed id, or inside a system that did not declare og.PlatformGrants.

functions.name: granted
functions.doc: Whether this world granted purchase `purchase` (og.platform.grant). Inside a system, declare og.PlatformGrants among its reads.

functions.name: adReady
functions.doc: Ask whether an ad can be shown now, to offer a rewarded one only when there is one.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed placement. The answer's data is `{ kind, placement, ready }`.

functions.name: showAd
functions.doc: Show an ad. While it shows, the host pauses the game through its lifecycle (no ticks, no audio: on the web the Player's pause and resume) and the answer arrives after it resumed, at a tick's start. Grant a reward only on `completed`.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed placement. The answer's data is `{ kind, placement, outcome }`: outcome `completed` or `skipped` for a rewarded ad, `shown` for an interstitial. Errors: `no_fill` (no ad now; retryable), `rate_limited` (the platform's frequency cap), `unavailable`.

functions.name: achievementUnlock
functions.doc: Unlock an achievement. The achievements and their titles are the platform's, by id.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id. The answer's data is `{ id, percent: 100, unlocked: true, new }`, new false when it was unlocked before.

functions.name: achievementProgress
functions.doc: Report progress towards an achievement; 100 unlocks it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id or a percent outside 0 to 100. The answer's data is `{ id, percent, unlocked, new }`.

functions.name: achievements
functions.doc: The player's achievements in this game.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ achievements: [{ id, percent, unlocked, time }] }`, time the unlock's UTC milliseconds or null.

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Who is playing: an id scoped to this game (the same player has another id in another game) and the name to show.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ player, name, guest }`, guest true for a player without an account.

functions.name: friends
functions.doc: The player's friends, those playing this game first.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ friends: [{ player, name, online, playing }] }`, ids scoped to this game; `unauthorized` for a guest.

functions.name: inviteSend
functions.doc: Invite a friend to this game, or offer an invite link through the share sheet. The invited player opens the game with the invite in og.platform.invites.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Whom, the words and what the game hands them.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed friend id, a message over 120 characters or a payload over 1 KiB. The answer's data is `{ invite, to }` (to null for a link); `cancelled` when the player closed the share sheet.

functions.name: invites
functions.doc: The invites to this game the player has not acted on, the one the game was opened with marked `opened`.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ invites: [{ invite, from: { player, name }, payload, time, opened }] }`.

functions.name: share
functions.doc: Share through the device's share sheet: the text, the game's own Play link and, with image, the frame drawn last.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty text, one over 280 characters, a title over 80 or a malformed path. The answer's data is `{ shared: true, target }` (target the app the player picked, when the host knows it, else null); `cancelled` when the player closed the sheet.

functions.name: supports
functions.doc: Whether the host answers platform method `method` (`purchase.buy`, `ad.show`, `share`: og.platform.info's capabilities): what to offer the player before asking. A method it lacks is answered `unavailable`.

functions.name: notice
functions.doc: A notice og.PlatformNotice announced. The engine keeps the last 256.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a number never given, one older than the last 256, or inside a system that writes shared state in a running lockstep session.

functions.name: result
functions.doc: The answer to a call, once it arrived.
functions.returnsDoc: Null while it is in flight, for an unknown request, or inside a system that writes shared state in a running lockstep session.

functions.name: info
functions.doc: What answers platform calls here, and what it answers.

functions.name: now
functions.doc: The host's wall-clock time, UTC milliseconds since 1970, as of this tick: what the host last told the engine (when it attached, and with every answer, applied at a tick's start like the answers) moved on by the ticks since. The one wall-clock read game code may make: it is host input, so a replay with the same answers gives the same values. Use it to know how long the game was closed (a save's time against a launch's), never to time play (that is og.Time).
functions.returnsDoc: UTC milliseconds; 0 until a host has told the time (`none`).

functions.name: roomCreate
functions.doc: Create a room and join it. The answer is og.RoomJoined, with the room's id to share (natively the relay names it `room-N`; on the web the platform does).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no room host (og.platform.roomInfo's host `none`), while in or joining a room (roomLeave first), or for a malformed name.

functions.name: roomJoin
functions.doc: Join a room by its id. The answer is og.RoomJoined (with ok false and `not_found` or `full` when it cannot); then og.RoomPeerJoined and og.RoomPeerLeft as others come and go.

params.name: room
params.doc: The room's id: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no room host, while in or joining a room, or for a malformed id.

functions.name: quickPlay
functions.doc: Quick play: wait to be matched with other players asking for the same mode and number of players, then play in a room of their own. The answer is og.RoomJoined once the room has filled (every matched peer hears it at once, numbered in the order they asked), or ok false with `timeout` after timeoutMs. roomLeave stops waiting (og.RoomJoined with `cancelled`). Natively `og relay` matches the engines connected to it (`og run --room ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/`); on the web the platform's matchmaking does (platform ask 21: until then the Player answers `unavailable`).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The mode, the players, how long to wait and this player's name.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no room host, while in or joining a room, or for a malformed mode or name.

functions.name: roomLeave
functions.doc: Leave the room: og.RoomPeerLeft with this engine's own peer number answers, and the other peers hear it leave after its last message. While joining (quick play waiting for its match) it stops waiting: og.RoomJoined answers with ok false and `cancelled`.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused when in no room and not joining one.

functions.name: roomSend
functions.doc: Send a message to every other peer in the room, or to one: a JSON value, or bytes (a Uint8Array). It arrives as og.RoomMessage, after every earlier message of this peer.

params.name: data
params.doc: What to send: a Uint8Array, or any JSON value; at most 64 KiB encoded.

params.name: to
params.doc: The one peer to send it to; omitted is every other peer.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when in no room, for a message over 64 KiB, or a peer not in the room.

functions.name: roomPeers
functions.doc: The peers in this engine's room, this one included, by number; empty in none.

functions.name: roomInfo
functions.doc: The room this engine is in, and what carries rooms here.

functions.name: roomMessage
functions.doc: A message og.RoomMessage announced: who sent it and what it carries. The engine keeps the last 256.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a number never given, or a message older than the last 256.

x-og-modules.name: i18n
x-og-modules.doc:
Localization: one string table per locale (`.ogt` of `type strings`: `locale "ja"`, its font chain `fonts "..."`, `string "key" "message"`), messages in a subset of ICU MessageFormat (`{name}`, `{n, number}`, `{n, plural, =0 {..} one {..} other {..}}` with `#`, `{g, select, a {..} other {..}}`), CLDR plural rules, and the locale the host asks for (the browser's `navigator.language` on the web, `og run --locale` natively).
The active locale is the best loaded table for the request (ja-JP takes ja; zh-TW takes zh-Hant or zh-TW), else the base table (`base true`, else en, else the first). A key it lacks is read from its `fallback` table, then the base. It also sets the UI's font chain (its fonts first, then the other tables') and direction: a right-to-left locale (ar, he, fa, ur) mirrors og.ui's layout, and og-ui shapes Arabic words with the font's own tables (a font cooked with the `arabic` charset carries them). `og cook` warns about every key a locale lacks, or takes other arguments for, than the base.
Formatting (formatCompact, formatCurrency, formatDate, formatTime, formatDuration, and the message styles `{n, number, compact}`, `{p, number, currency/EUR}`, `{d, date, short}`, `{d, time}`) writes from a CLDR subset built into the engine, for the languages the plural rules cover and zh-Hant; another language is written as en. It follows the active locale (else the requested one, else en). A date or time is seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC that the game passes in (a save's timestamp, a server's event time): nothing reads a clock, so the same value gives the same text on every host and in a replay. A message's dates are UTC; formatDate and formatTime take an offset.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: Load a cooked string table; the active locale is negotiated again.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked string table, or a font of its chain that is not cooked.

functions.name: setLocale
functions.doc: Ask for a locale (a player's choice in settings); the active one is the best table for it.

functions.name: locale
functions.doc: The requested and active locales, the direction and the font chain.

functions.name: t
functions.doc: A key's message in the active locale, formatted with its arguments; a key no table has answers the key itself and logs one warning.

params.name: args
params.doc: The arguments: an object of strings and numbers, `{ count: 3, name: "Kai" }`.

functions.name: has
functions.doc: Whether the active locale's own table has the key (not a fallback).

functions.name: formatCompact
functions.doc: A number written short in the active locale: `1.2K`, `12K`, `1.2M` (en), `1,2 Mio.` (de), `1.2万` (ja). Below the locale's first compact size (de compacts no thousands) the whole number, grouped.

functions.name: formatCurrency
functions.doc: An amount of money in the active locale: `$1,234.50` (en), `1.234,50 €` (de), `￥1,235` (ja), with the currency's own fraction digits (none for JPY and KRW). A code the subset lacks is written as itself.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The amount, in the currency's whole units (dollars, not cents).

functions.name: formatDate
functions.doc: A date in the active locale, in the style asked for: `Nov 2, 2026` (en), `02.11.2026` (de).

params.name: seconds
params.doc: Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; fractions are dropped.

functions.name: formatTime
functions.doc: A time of day in the active locale: `3:05 PM` (en), `15:05` (de).

params.name: seconds
params.doc: Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; fractions are dropped.

functions.name: formatDuration
functions.doc: A length of time as a clock face, `1:02:03` from an hour and `2:05` below, in the locale's digits; whole seconds, rounded down. og.ui's `duration` and `clock` formats are the in-document equivalents.

params.name: seconds
params.doc: The length in seconds; negative is written with a minus.

x-og-modules.name: ui
x-og-modules.doc:
The engine's UI: an immediate-mode toolkit. Systems describe the tree every tick with these calls; the engine lays it out Clay-style, styles it with the game's UI style (the engine's default style, for prototypes only, until the game picks one), draws it over the frame and answers the probe (dump_ui, touch_move_to, move_to_text) from it.
The engine opens the frame before the game's systems (from og.Input and the play surface) and closes it after them, so calls belong inside systems; outside one they do nothing and log a warning. Interaction is decided against the previous tick's rectangles, which are also what the probe resolves, so a scripted touch_move_to and a click agree; response edges (clicked, changed, submitted) last one tick.
Lengths are CSS pixels of the play surface (origin top left, y down), the unit of og.Input and the probe. Ids: an element's id is unique among its siblings (`idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`); a path `Inventory/Slot#3` names it after its nearest ancestors. The UI state (hover, press, focus, caret, scroll) is world state: snapshots and the world hash carry it.

functions.name: configure
functions.doc: Set how the UI looks (the scheme, density, fonts, style, sounds, motion…), typically in GameDesc.start; it takes effect from the next tick. The desc is a partial: a field left out keeps the last UiDesc's value, the one an earlier call or a look's style (og.render.applyLook) gave it, so a settings screen that configures sounds or reducedMotion keeps the style and the fonts; null clears a field to its default (`style: null` goes back to the default style). A UI left with no font at all (no font, no style with fonts, no fallback or locale font) warns: it would draw no text.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI is configured.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The fields to change; the others keep their values.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font or style, or a desc that is not an object.

functions.name: viewport
functions.doc: This tick's play surface as the UI lays out on it: the render target's size, safe area and covered region in og-ui units (CSS pixels over UiTheme.unit, docs/ui.md §15.2: 1 on touch and up to 720p, so CSS pixels there) and device pixels per unit, from what the host reports.

functions.name: theme
functions.doc: The style values the UI draws with.

functions.name: open
functions.doc: Open a container; the calls until its close() build its children.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id, unique among its siblings.

functions.name: openPanel
functions.doc: Open a card, closed by close(): og.ui.panel without the callback.

functions.name: openScroll
functions.doc: Open a vertical scroll container, closed by close(): og.ui.scroll without the callback.

functions.name: close
functions.doc: Close the open container.
functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive container; the zero response otherwise.

functions.name: row
functions.doc: A row built by `build`: open(id, {...desc, direction: row}), build(), close().

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its layout and look; direction is row.

functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive row.

functions.name: column
functions.doc: A column built by `build`: open(id, {...desc, direction: column}), build(), close().

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its layout and look; direction is column.

functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive column.

functions.name: panel
functions.doc: A card built by `build`: openPanel(id, desc), build(), close().

functions.name: scroll
functions.doc: A vertical scroll container built by `build`: openScroll(id, desc), build(), close().

functions.name: richText
functions.doc: A paragraph of inline spans from markup, for a string-table message (og.i18n.t) so a translation carries its own emphasis: `[b]bold[/b]` (thickened in the distance field as far as it reaches, plus a second copy one device pixel right), `[color=danger]` or `[color=#ff8800]` (a ThemeColor follows the style), `[size=xl]` (a TypeStepName), `[font=mono]`, `[icon=coin]` (a cell of the icon atlas, one em), `[link=shop]Open the shop[/link]` (accent ink, underlined, focusable by keys and pads; a child element `<id>/shop` of kind link for the probe) and per-glyph motion `[wave]`, `[shake]`, `[pulse]` (by the tick; still under reduced motion). `[[` is a literal bracket. Lines break between the spans' words (a word restyled mid-way stays whole), each as tall as its tallest span on one baseline. Markup it cannot read shows as text and logs a warning.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Defaults for its spans: type step, ink, alignment, wrapping, width and font.

functions.name: label
functions.doc: MSDF text that wraps at its width (word breaks; between CJK characters under kinsoku, katakana words kept whole; long words between characters) unless nowrap. The probe reads its text.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Type step, ink, alignment, wrapping, width and font.

functions.name: button
functions.doc: A button with a label; `clicked` is a press and a release inside it. The probe reads its label.

functions.name: image
functions.doc: A texture region, or a solid rectangle; with ImageDesc.aspect, a fitting side follows the other.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Texture, region, tint, size and aspect ratio.

functions.name: zoomView
functions.doc: A zoomable picture (a map, an artwork): two fingers pinch it to zoom about their centre and pan it as they move (og.Pointers), the wheel zooms about the pointer, a drag pans; Tab or a pad focuses it, and then + (= and the keypad's) and - zoom it about its centre, 0 fits it again and the arrows pan it a tenth of its size. It stays on its picture and within its zoom limits; its zoom and centre are UI state (snapshots carry them). Two fingers over a scroll container scroll it the same way, and fling it as they lift. The probe reads its zoom as its value.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The picture, its size and zoom limits.

functions.name: progress
functions.doc: A track filled to a fraction.

params.name: value
params.doc: How full it is, from 0 to 1.

functions.name: slider
functions.doc: A track with a fill and a thumb: a press anywhere on it sets the value and dragging follows. Pass back the value it answers next tick.

functions.name: toggle
functions.doc: A switch with a label; a click flips it. Pass back the state it answers next tick. The probe reads its label.

functions.name: textField
functions.doc: One line of text: a press focuses it with the caret at the press, a drag selects (and scrolls the text past the field's ends), a double click selects a word and a triple click everything; typed text (og.input's TextInput events: the page's typing, the probe's type: and commit:; until a world has had one, a printable key pressed types its US-layout character, and after it keys only edit) replaces the selection at the caret; Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home and End edit, Shift with them selects, Alt or Ctrl with them moves or deletes by words (Ctrl with Home and End: the text's ends); Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all, with C copies and with X cuts (the page's clipboard, through the shell), with Z undoes and with Shift+Z or Y redoes (a history of 100 steps per field, typing undone a word at a time; a text the game sets starts it again); an input method's composition shows underlined at the caret until it commits; Enter submits and leaves, Escape leaves. The text scrolls to keep the caret in view and the caret blinks by the tick (steady under reduced motion). Pass back the text it answers next tick. The probe reads its text, or the placeholder while empty.

functions.name: textArea
functions.doc: Several lines of text: textField's editing, with Enter starting a new line, Up and Down moving between lines and Home and End to a line's ends, a triple click selecting the line between its breaks, the text wrapped between words at the area's width and scrolled to keep the caret's line in view (a drag above or below the area scrolls it, faster the further out). Pass back the text it answers next tick. The probe reads its text, or the placeholder while empty.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Placeholder, width, rows and length limit.

functions.name: tooltip
functions.doc: A tooltip for the element just built: shown below it (above without room) once the pointer has rested on it for the slow motion duration, drawn over everything. The probe reads its text.

functions.name: idi
functions.doc: The id of the index-th of several siblings of one name: `idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`.

functions.name: breakpoint
functions.doc: The size class of the play surface of the frame being built (desktop outside a frame).

functions.name: framePointer
functions.doc: The primary pointer of the frame being built, without the world: for a component that hit-tests a shape it draws itself (a pie's wedges, a wheel's slices) by angle and radius rather than by rectangles. Keys and pads reach the same choices through focusable parts.

functions.name: frameCursor
functions.doc: The pointer's shape the last frame resolved (never auto): the cursor set on what the press holds or the pointer is over, or around it, else its kind's. The web shell sets the canvas's CSS cursor from each frame's answer (`cursor`); a native host that draws its own window (og dev, Origin Desktop's shared frames) reads the same answer.

functions.name: frameViewport
functions.doc: The play surface of the frame being built: og.ui.viewport without the world, for code that only builds UI.

functions.name: hasIcon
functions.doc: Whether the icon atlas has an icon of this name (components draw a fallback otherwise).

functions.name: seconds
functions.doc: The UI's clock in seconds: frames built over the tick rate (simulation time, never the wall clock).

functions.name: lastPath
functions.doc: The full path of the element built just before (a container just closed, or a widget), as og.ui.bounds, og.ui.gesture, og.ui.forceState and the probe name it: a component reads its own parts' rectangles and gestures by it. Empty when nothing was built before it.

functions.name: setFocus
functions.doc: Move the focus (the pointer's, the keys' and pad 0's) to the element at a full path when this frame ends, if a focusable control is there then: a component moving the focus with its choice (a radio group's arrow keys, a list opening at its chosen option, a keyboard's first key). The ring shows as navigation's does. The last call in a frame wins; a path with no focusable control leaves the focus where it is.

functions.name: scrollIntoView
functions.doc: Scroll the scroll container around a control (an interactive or focusable element, by its full path) so the control is in its view, by where both were in the last frame: by the least that shows it whole, or centred in the view (a saga map opening on the current level, a list on its chosen row). The offset stays in the container's range and stops a fling. Nothing for a path the last frame had no control at or that is in no scroll container.

params.name: center
params.doc: Centre it in the view, as far as the range allows; false scrolls by the least that shows it.

functions.name: frameDirection
functions.doc: The writing direction of the frame being built, `ltr` or `rtl` (og.i18n's locale sets it): code that draws its own arrows, chevrons or progress along a line mirrors them by it; layout mirrors rows and insets itself.

functions.name: frameTheme
functions.doc: The style values of the frame being built: og.ui.theme without the world, for code that only builds UI (the components and patterns).

functions.name: openAnchor
functions.doc: Open an anchored group, closed by close(): og.ui.anchor without the callback.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id; the probe path is the id alone.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where it sits and how it lays out.

functions.name: anchor
functions.doc: An anchored group built by `build`: a layer at a point of the safe area, over the tree, for HUD corners and touch controls.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where it sits and how it lays out.

functions.name: openTransition
functions.doc: Open a transition container (a column), closed by close(); build its children only while the answer is visible: it stays visible while it leaves. Its content takes no input while it moves.

functions.name: transition
functions.doc: Content that enters and leaves: fade, slide or scale by the tick from the style's motion. `build` runs while it is visible.

functions.name: openModal
functions.doc: Open a dialog, closed by closeModal(); build its content only while the answer is visible. The probe sees the backdrop as `<id>` and the panel as `<id>/Panel`.

functions.name: closeModal
functions.doc: Close a dialog opened with openModal (its panel and backdrop).

functions.name: modal
functions.doc: A dialog built by `build` while visible: scrim, centred panel, focus kept inside, Back and the backdrop dismiss it unless locked. Set your open flag false on `dismissed`.

functions.name: spotlight
functions.doc: A spotlight over everything (a tutorial step): the scrim on four sides of the hole, a primary edge around it. Presses on the dimmed parts stop there (clicked); presses in the hole reach what is under it. Shades are `<id>/Top`, `Left`, `Right`, `Bottom`; the hole is `<id>/Hole`.

params.name: hole
params.doc: The rectangle to leave lit, as og.ui.bounds answers; null dims everything.

functions.name: bounds
functions.doc: Where an element was in the last frame, by id or `Parent/Child` path (topmost first), as touch_move_to resolves it.

functions.name: scrollState
functions.doc: A scroll container's offset, view and whole content, by its full path (og.ui.lastPath after closing it): what a component virtualises its rows by, since og.ui.bounds is cut to the view and a row scrolled away has none. The offset is this tick's; the sizes are the last frame's. Null for a path that was no scroll container.

functions.name: openList
functions.doc: Open a virtualised list (a scroll column) and learn which rows to build: listItem(i) and close() for each, then closeList().

functions.name: openGrid
functions.doc: Open a virtualised grid and learn which cells to build: gridItem(i) and close() for each, then closeList().

functions.name: listItem
functions.doc: Open row `index` of the open list (`Row#index`): selectable and focusable; its content follows until close(). A press that started on one row and is released on this one answers `dropped`.

functions.name: gridItem
functions.doc: Open cell `index` of the open grid (`Cell#index`): a slot on control, focusable; its content follows until close(). Drops answer `dropped` as listItem's.

params.name: selected
params.doc: Drawn selected (controlStrong with a primary bar).

functions.name: closeList
functions.doc: Close a list or grid opened with openList or openGrid.

functions.name: dragging
functions.doc: The row or cell a held press started on in the list or grid of this id (built under the same parent): a drag in progress, to draw what is dragged under the pointer.

functions.name: list
functions.doc: A virtualised list built by `build(index)` for the rows in view.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Row count, size and the selected row.

functions.name: grid
functions.doc: A virtualised grid built by `build(index)` for the cells in view.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Cell count, size, columns and the selected cell.

functions.name: tabs
functions.doc: A segmented control: a neutral track, the chosen tab on the thumb. Tabs are `Tab#i` and the probe reads their labels.

params.name: selected
params.doc: The chosen index from game state.

functions.name: select
functions.doc: A select: a field-like trigger with the chosen label and a chevron; a press or Activate opens its menu `<id>.menu` (options `Option#i`) under it, a focus scope; choosing closes it with changed. Back or a press outside closes it.

params.name: selected
params.doc: The chosen index from game state.

functions.name: stepper
functions.doc: A number stepper: `Dec`, `Value`, `Inc`. The buttons step within the range; Left and Right step it while a button is focused; a screen reader's increment and decrement on the stepper itself (its spinbutton, which the web shell mirrors as an adjustable range) step it too.

functions.name: radio
functions.doc: A radio group of `Option#i` rows: a ring, filled primary when chosen, and a label.

params.name: selected
params.doc: The chosen index from game state.

functions.name: checkbox
functions.doc: A checkbox with a label; a press flips it.

functions.name: checkboxList
functions.doc: Checkboxes in a column (`Option#i`).

functions.name: chip
functions.doc: A chip: a control-filled tag; selected inverts to ink. For filters and tags.

functions.name: badge
functions.doc: A badge: a small status tag in its tone.

functions.name: divider
functions.doc: A hairline in the border colour across its parent.

functions.name: spacer
functions.doc: Empty space.

params.name: size
params.doc: Its size along both axes; null grows into the free space.

functions.name: keyValue
functions.doc: A key (inkMuted) and its value (ink, at the end) on one row: stats, settings summaries, receipts.

params.name: mono
params.doc: The value in the monospaced font (prices, ids).

functions.name: skeleton
functions.doc: A skeleton: the neutral fill standing in for content that is loading, with a sheen that passes every 1.6 s (still under reduced motion).

functions.name: spinner
functions.doc: A loading spinner: eight dots around a circle, the bright one turning by the tick.

params.name: size
params.doc: Its diameter in CSS px; 0 is the small control height.

functions.name: icon
functions.doc: An icon of the atlas (UiDesc.icons) by name: a texture cell, or an icon set's distance-field glyph fitted to its square; an unknown name draws an empty slot and warns. Rich text takes the same icons inline with `[icon=name]`. The probe reads the name.

functions.name: meter
functions.doc: A health, mana or xp bar. A drop shows at once and leaves a pale trail that follows after a beat; a rise grows into place with a ghost of the target; both by the tick.

functions.name: cooldown
functions.doc: A cooldown: a disc whose primary ring fills clockwise from the top as it runs out, bright and full when ready, a label or icon in the middle. A press reports clicked (ready or not).

params.name: remaining
params.doc: How much of the cooldown is left, 0 to 1: 1 just used, 0 ready.

functions.name: minimap
functions.doc: A mini-map frame: the map in a lineStrong frame, markers as dots (the player primary and ringed), an N mark and a zone label.

functions.name: dialogue
functions.doc: A dialogue box: a portrait slot, the speaker in primary ink and the line typed out by the tick. A press or Activate while typing shows the whole line; once shown it answers advanced. The line is `<id>/Body/Line` and the probe reads what is shown.

functions.name: joystick
functions.doc: A virtual joystick: a base and a knob that follows a press that started on it. It keeps the finger that grabbed it (any of og.Pointers), so another finger can hold an action button at the same time.

functions.name: dpad
functions.doc: A d-pad of four arms (`Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`), each at least 44 CSS px.

functions.name: actionButton
functions.doc: A square touch action button, cornered by the style's control radius: pressed while held (jump, fire), clicked on a tap; at least 44 CSS px.

params.name: text
params.doc: Its label (and what the probe reads).

functions.name: toast
functions.doc: Queue a toast: it stacks at UiDesc.toastAnchor, enters, stays its time and leaves; at most three are up (older ones leave first); a press dismisses it. Callable anywhere (systems, commands, start); it is world state, so snapshots carry it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI shows it.

functions.returnsDoc: Its id, for dismissToast.

functions.name: dismissToast
functions.doc: Start a toast's exit.

functions.name: navigate
functions.doc: Queue a navigation intent for the next tick: a gamepad og.Input does not read yet, a custom binding, a command. A move queued while the focus is on nothing puts the focus on the first control, whatever its direction, and no further: moves asked again before the focus lands (each tick until og.ui.focus answers a path) land on that same first control.

functions.name: back
functions.doc: Escape or gamepad B this tick, not taken by a dialog or menu: true once, then taken. A pause screen closes on it. While a dialog or menu that Back closes is open (the topmost of the last frame) it answers false and leaves Back to it, even when asked before the dialog is built this tick: a HUD drawn under pause never takes the Back that closes pause. A locked dialog lets Back through.

functions.name: setPlayers
functions.doc: Local multiplayer: how many players this screen takes (1 to 4; 1 by default). Pads 1 to count - 1 each move a focus of their own among the same controls, shown as a ring in the player's colour (info, success, warn), and their A presses the control under it (Response.pad says which pad); pad 0 shares the one focus with the keyboard and the pointer, and Back and adjusting a slider stay pad 0's. Declare it every tick the screen shows; it takes effect from the next tick, and a dialog's focus scope holds every pad's focus inside it.

functions.name: setVirtualCursor
functions.doc: A pad's virtual cursor, for a screen built for the pointer (a map, a shop grid, a strategy HUD) played on a pad: pad 0's left stick moves it instead of the focus, slowing and sticking over controls; its A presses where it points as the mouse's button does (drags, sliders and long presses work); its right stick scrolls under it. The style draws it and the system cursor hides (og.ui.frameCursor answers none). The real pointer moving hides it and the stick shows it again. Declare it every tick the screen shows; it takes effect from the next tick. Null turns it off.

params.name: desc
params.doc: How it moves; null is none.

functions.name: virtualCursor
functions.doc: The virtual cursor as the last frame left it; null when none is declared.

functions.name: setHudEdit
functions.doc: Turns the HUD edit mode on or off (docs/ui.md §8.4; kept until changed). While it is on, elements with ElementProps.customize stop answering their own presses and show their outlines: a press selects one and a drag moves it, two touches or the wheel scale it, and with no virtual cursor pad 0's left stick moves the selected one. Build og.ui.hudLayoutEditor for steps, Next, Reset and Done.

functions.name: setHudPlayer
functions.doc: Whose layout this screen shows and edits, 0 to 3 (0 by default; kept until changed): each player of a shared screen keeps a layout of their own.

functions.name: hudEdit
functions.doc: The HUD edit mode as the last frame left it.

functions.name: hudLayout
functions.doc: A player's HUD layout as JSON, for the game's settings: each moved, scaled or faded element's key with its x, y, scale and opacity. Save it when HudEdit.changed says so; give it back with og.ui.setHudLayout on the next run.

functions.name: setHudLayout
functions.doc: Gives a player's HUD layout back (og.ui.hudLayout's JSON; `{}` resets it). Answers false and leaves the layout as it was when it does not read (the reason is in the frame's warnings).

functions.name: hudSelect
functions.doc: Selects an element to edit by its key (empty: none).

functions.name: hudStep
functions.doc: Steps the selected element's size and opacity: each -1, 0 or +1 step (a tenth larger or smaller, a tenth more or less opaque), within its limits.

functions.name: hudReset
functions.doc: Puts an element back where it was laid out: its key, empty for the selected one, `*` for every one.

functions.name: hudLayoutEditor
functions.doc: The HUD edit mode's panel (docs/ui.md §8.4): the selected element's key, size and opacity steps, Next (the next element: how keys and pads choose one), Reset (the selected one, or all with none selected) and Done, which turns the edit mode off. Build it where it fits, while og.ui.hudEdit().on; presses on it edit nothing behind it. Its children are `Title`, `Selected`, `Size/Less`, `Size/More`, `Opacity/Less`, `Opacity/More`, `Actions/Next`, `Actions/Reset`, `Actions/Done`.

functions.name: focus
functions.doc: The path of the control pad pad's focus is on in the last frame (pad 0: the shared focus of the pointer, keyboard and pad 0), as touch_move_to resolves it; empty when it is on none.

params.name: pad
params.doc: The pad, 0 to 3; past 3 answers empty.

functions.name: a11y
functions.doc: The accessibility tree of the last frame: every element with a role, its name, value, states and bounds, and the focus order Tab walks. A shell mirrors it into the page for screen readers; a playtest reads the same fields on dump_ui's elements.

functions.name: feedback
functions.doc: Play a UI event's feedback from the style (docs/ui.md §7.8): one sound of its set, at random and never the one it played last, at a volume and pitch from the set's ranges, and its haptic pattern at the player's strength (setHaptics). Widgets play their own events (press, focus, select, confirm, back, open, close, tab, toggleOn, toggleOff, sliderTick); game code plays the rest: scrollTick, typewriter, counterTick, notification, warning, error, success, reward and the reveals revealCommon to revealMythic. The choices come from the UI state, so a replay plays the same. An unknown event or one the style leaves silent plays nothing.

params.name: rise
params.doc: A rising cascade's step, 0 to 1, walking the set's pitch range up (a counter's ticks); below 0 picks the pitch at random.

functions.name: setHaptics
functions.doc: The player's haptic strength (a settings screen's vibration slider or switch): 0 turns the UI's haptics off, 1 (the default) plays the style's patterns as set; between scales them. The web shell rumbles the gamepad and vibrates a phone; the native host rumbles its pad.

functions.name: setNavigation
functions.doc: Whether keyboard and gamepad navigation moves focus on this screen (on by default). A gameplay HUD whose keys move the player turns it off; an open dialog or menu turns it back on while it is open. Takes effect from the next tick.

functions.name: memory
functions.doc: A number the UI keeps for an id under the open element (a component's tab, a count-up's start tick), in snapshots like the rest of the UI state. Read it every tick it is used: an unused memory is dropped.

params.name: id
params.doc: The id, unique among its siblings' memories.

functions.name: remember
functions.doc: Set a number memory (see memory).

functions.name: tick
functions.doc: Frames the UI has built: its clock, for animations by the tick.

functions.name: counter
functions.doc: A number label that counts (ease-out cubic, by the tick) from where it was to the value each time the value changes, grouped with commas; a style with motion.pop bumps it when it lands. Scores, currency, rewards.
functions.returnsDoc: The number shown this tick.

functions.name: burst
functions.doc: Throw rays and sparks from the element built just before (a star landing, a reward), once, from when it first appears. Off under reduced motion.

functions.name: shake
functions.doc: Shake the element built just before, from this tick (a wrong answer, a locked door, a refused purchase): call it once, on the tick it happens; the element swings and comes to rest by itself, and snapshots carry it. Still under reduced motion. A refused press on a disabled button already shakes when the style's motion.shake is set.

functions.name: screenTransition
functions.doc: A transition between game screens drawn over the whole frame (through the overlay, over every other UI layer). Pass the screen the game wants every tick and build the one it answers: when the wanted screen changes the cover closes over the old screen for half the duration, the answer switches, and the cover opens on the new one. Deterministic by the tick; snapshots carry it; under reduced motion every kind is a fade.

params.name: screen
params.doc: The screen the game wants now.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Kind, duration, colour or texture, side.

functions.name: previewViewport
functions.doc: Lay the UI out for another play surface (a phone in portrait at 3x, a notch) until cleared with null: for headless previews and playtests of responsive layouts. Render at width x dpr by height x dpr (`og run --size`).

params.name: viewport
params.doc: The surface to lay out for; null returns to the host's.

functions.name: card
functions.doc:
A card over a body the game builds. Answers its response (clicked when interactive).
Its corners: a badge at the top end, a number plate at the top start, a cost disc at the bottom end; each mirrors right to left.
Parts: Card.frame[selected][<variant>], Card.media[placeholder], Card.number, Card.cost. Accessibility: a button (interactive) or group named by its eyebrow, title and subtitle, else its text; the number and the cost are read as text. Probe ids: <id>/Media, <id>/Body (with a cost and media, the disc at <id>/Media/Cost/Text; with a cost and no media, the game's body in <id>/Body/Content and the disc at <id>/Body/Cost/Text), <id>/Number/Text, <id>/Badge, <id>/Selected.

functions.name: scrollArea
functions.doc: A scroll container whose content fades out at an edge where more lies beyond.

functions.name: accordion
functions.doc: Sections whose headers open and close their bodies; the sections under one move on the panel spring.

params.name: build
params.doc: Builds an open section's body by its index.

functions.name: splitView
functions.doc: Two panes with a divider a drag moves and a press of the focused divider steps.

functions.name: dialog
functions.doc: A dialog on the modal layer: tone mark, message, body and actions.

params.name: build
params.doc: Builds its body under the message.

functions.name: confirm
functions.doc: A confirmation dialog: the message, Cancel and the action (danger when it cannot be undone).

functions.name: popover
functions.doc: A popover beside an element with an arrow at it; Back or a press outside dismisses it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The element, the side and the size.

functions.name: menu
functions.doc: A menu of commands, checks, radios, separators, headers and submenus, hanging from an element or at a point. A submenu opens beside its row; where none fits beside the menu (a phone) it drills in, its rows replacing the menu's under a back row, and Back goes up a level.

functions.name: contextMenu
functions.doc: A menu at a point: where a right press or a long press happened.

functions.name: sheet
functions.doc: A sheet sliding in from the bottom (resting at detents, dragged) or a side.

functions.name: tabBar
functions.doc: Tabs with a sliding indicator and bumpers over the panel of the selected one.

params.name: build
params.doc: Builds the selected tab's panel by its index.

functions.name: carousel
functions.doc: Pages a drag or a flick moves, snapping to a page, with arrows and dots.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Count, the current page and options.

params.name: build
params.doc: Builds a page by its index (the current one and two each side).

functions.name: breadcrumbs
functions.doc: The path to where the player is, collapsing its middle into a menu when long.

functions.name: pagination
functions.doc: Previous, next and the pages around the current one.

functions.name: actionHints
functions.doc: The action bar: each action the top layer accepts as its glyph and hint; on touch, buttons.

functions.name: radialMenu
functions.doc: A radial wheel chosen by where the pointer or a stick points. A slice's cost sits under its label, in the danger hue while it cannot be paid; with the labels hidden (a small wheel, a large text size), the centre shows the aimed slice's cost under its name.

functions.name: dataList
functions.doc: A virtualised list with its empty, loading and error states.

params.name: build
params.doc: Builds a row's content by its index.

functions.name: dataGrid
functions.doc: A virtualised grid of cells with its empty, loading and error states.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Count, cell size, selection and state.

params.name: build
params.doc: Builds a cell's content by its index.

functions.name: table
functions.doc: A sortable, filterable table; only the rows in view are built, so 10,000 rows and more stay within budget.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Rows, columns, the sort and the filter.

functions.name: tree
functions.doc: A tree of expandable items, virtualised.

functions.name: nodeGraph
functions.doc:
A pan-and-zoom graph of nodes and links: skill trees, run maps, flowcharts.
Each node is a circle, rounded square, hexagon, diamond or triangle; a node with a team (a sector map's allied and hostile systems) is filled in its side's colour, a sided node with no icon showing no letters (its shape and colour mark it). Its state shows by its ring and a mark.
Parts: Graph.frame (its ground's texture on <id>/Window/View/Canvas), Graph.node[<state>][<kind>][<shape>][team=<n>][selected], Graph.zoom, Graph.zoomButton. Accessibility: group named label, value the zoom; each node a button named by its label, value its state, selected when selected. Probe ids: <id>/Window/View/Canvas/Node#i, <id>/Window/View/Canvas/Caption#i, <id>/Bar/Zoom/In, <id>/Bar/Zoom/Out.

functions.name: chart
functions.doc: A line, area, bar, radar, pie or donut chart.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The kind, the series and the categories.

functions.name: keyValueRows
functions.doc: Key-value rows: labels at the start, values at the end.

functions.name: statCompare
functions.doc: Stat-compare rows: current, new and the signed change with its mark.

functions.name: calendar
functions.doc: A month grid of days.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The month, today, the selection and marks.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: Text in a role (docs/ui.md §11, Foundations): the style's type step, font and weight for display, title, heading, body, label, caption or numeric (monospaced figures), in a tone, cut after maxLines with an ellipsis (the probe and a screen reader still read it whole). Display, title and heading are headings to a screen reader (a style's flourish frames them). It grows with the player's text size and wraps between CJK characters by kinsoku. Probe: the element `<id>`, kind label, its whole text.

functions.name: prose
functions.doc: A passage of rich text (og.ui.richText's markup: `[b]`, `[color=…]`, `[icon=…]`, `[link=…]`, `[wave]`…), split into paragraphs at blank lines, at a readable measure, each a text element `<id>/P#i` whose links are focusable children (`<id>/P#i/<link>`). Answers the link clicked this tick (keys and pads press links too). Its region reads as one group to a screen reader.

params.name: markup
params.doc: The markup; a blank line starts a paragraph.

functions.name: iconMark
functions.doc: An icon of the style's set (og.ui.icon) in a tone, on a plate, with a badge or a dot: the foundation every icon in a control is. An icon the set lacks is drawn as a mark of the same name where the controls know one (tick, cross, plus, minus, search, chevrons, lock, star, warning, info, eye, reset, globe), else a dot: never a missing glyph. Parts: `Icon.plate[circle]`, `Icon.badge`, `Icon.dot`. Probe: `<id>/Glyph`, `<id>/Badge` (its text).

params.name: name
params.doc: The icon's name in the style's set.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its size, tone, plate, badge and name.

functions.name: artSlot
functions.doc: An image or art slot: the texture fitted and cut as its desc says, fading in when it arrives (the style's enter motion; at once under reduced motion); until then a placeholder drawn from the style (a gradient of its soft fills and the kind's silhouette, a passing sheen while loading), never a grey box. Parts: `Art.frame[placeholder][loading]` (a style dresses the frame by state), `Art.placeholder` (the kind's silhouette and sheen), `Art.image`. Role image when labelled. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Image` once loaded, `<id>/Placeholder` before.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The art, its slot and its placeholder.

functions.name: shapeBox
functions.doc: A decorative shape drawn by the UI pass (docs/ui.md §5.1) in the style's colours: a pip, a gem, a star, a ring, a backdrop blob. It takes no input and is decoration to a screen reader. Part: `Shape.<kind>` (a style dresses `Shape.star` with art). Probe: `<id>`.

functions.name: separator
functions.doc: A separator between groups: the style's line (its divider ornament where the style has one and no label is given), across or upright, with a label in its middle between two lines. Role separator. Parts: `Separator.line[strong]`. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Label`.

functions.name: space
functions.doc: Empty space of a step of the style's spacing scale (so a style's density moves every gap at once), or all the room left. Probe: `<id>`, kind spacer.

functions.name: viewFrame
functions.doc: A viewport in a frame (docs/ui.md §5.5, Foundations): og.ui.sceneViewport in a style-dressed slot that turns with a drag (keeping the fling's speed for a moment), tilts within its limits, zooms with the wheel or a pinch, and turns by 15° per Left or Right while it has the focus (Tab, a pad). Until the target has a texture it shows a placeholder with a spinner. Draw the scene into a target of view.pixelWidth × view.pixelHeight with the yaw, pitch and zoom it answers; a target of another shape covers the frame, cropped, never squashed. Parts: `ViewFrame.frame[focused]`, `ViewFrame.hint`. Role image (its label), its turn as its value. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Box/Picture/View`, `<id>/Box/HintRow/Hint`.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The target, its camera and its turn.

functions.name: emitter
functions.doc: An ambient particle emitter (docs/ui.md §5.5) laid over its parent's area: sparkles on a rare card, embers on a forge, snow over a winter menu, confetti on a win. It takes no input, is decoration to a screen reader, and stops under reduced motion. Built on og.ui.particles; every particle is the engine's, seeded and in the snapshot. Probe: `<id>`.

functions.name: effectLayer
functions.doc: A layer (docs/ui.md §5.4): its subtree, built by `build`, drawn offscreen and composited through a material (a card dissolving as it is spent, a shine passing over a rare item, a hologram panel, a hit's glitch, a locked tile in grey), the material's parameters set from one amount. Its children keep their input and accessibility. Part: `Layer.frame`. Probe: `<id>` and its children.

functions.name: pushButton
functions.doc: A button (docs/ui.md §11, Controls): primary, secondary, ghost (outlined), quiet (text) or danger, small, medium or large, with icons, a badge, a loading spinner and a disabled reason. It lifts under the pointer and the focus and sinks as it is pressed (its interaction group, on the style's motion), and the style dresses it as `Button.base[<variant>][hover|pressed|focused|disabled][selected]` (a version 1 style's button art included), its label in the ink that reads on its fill. A click is a press and a release inside it, Enter, Space or the pad's A while it has the focus. Role button (pressed while selected, busy while loading). Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Label`, `<id>/Icon`, `<id>/Badge`.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its role, size, icons and states.

functions.name: iconButton
functions.doc: An icon button: a square (or round) button of the control height around one icon, named by its label (its tooltip, and what a screen reader says), with a badge or a dot. It moves and is dressed as pushButton, `Button.base[icon]`. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Icon`, `<id>/Badge`.

params.name: icon
params.doc: The icon's name (the style's set; a drawn mark where it has none).

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its name, role, size and badge.

functions.name: holdButton
functions.doc: A hold-to-confirm button: held (a press on it, a touch), it fills from its start edge over holdMs, ticking up in pitch, and confirms with the style's confirm sound and a pop; let go early, it drains back. Keys and pads take its toggle alternative (XAG 107: activate starts it, it runs by itself, activate again or moving the focus stops it), as the pointer does with toggle. Its progress is UI state (in snapshots). Parts: `HoldButton.base[<variant>][holding][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `HoldButton.fill`. Role button, its fill as its value (percent). Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Button`, `<id>/Button/Label`, `<id>/Button/Fill`.

functions.name: toggleSwitch
functions.doc: A switch: a track and a knob that slides from its start to its end as it turns on (its selection group, on the style's motion), the track filling with primary, with a label and a description; the whole row takes a press, Enter, Space or A. Plays toggleOn and toggleOff. Parts: `Toggle.track[on|off][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `Toggle.knob[on]`, `Toggle.row[hover|pressed|focused|disabled]` (the whole row, which takes the press). Role switch, checked when on. Probe: `<id>` (its label as name), `<id>/Track`, `<id>/Track/Knob`.

functions.name: checkField
functions.doc: A checkbox: a box that fills with primary and draws its tick (a dash when mixed) with a pop as it turns on (its selection group), with a label and a description; the whole row takes a press, Enter, Space or A. Plays toggleOn and toggleOff. Parts: `Checkbox.box[checked|mixed][invalid][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `Checkbox.mark`, `Checkbox.row[hover|pressed|focused|disabled]` (the whole row). Role checkbox, checked when on (and its value `mixed`). Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Box`, `<id>/Box/Mark`.

functions.name: radioGroup
functions.doc: A radio group: one of several choices, as rings with labels or as cards. A press, Enter, Space or A chooses; Left and Right (and a pad's) step the choice while one has the focus, skipping disabled ones, as a native radio group does. The ring's dot grows in with a pop (selection group). Plays select. Parts: `Radio.option[selected][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `Radio.ring[selected]`, `Radio.dot`, `Radio.card[selected]`. Role radiogroup with radio children, checked on the chosen. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Options/Option#i`.

functions.name: valueSlider
functions.doc: A slider: a track, a fill from min (or from an origin, both ways) and a knob. A press anywhere on the track jumps the knob there and a drag follows (a touch too; the knob grows under a finger), Left and Right step it while it has the focus (a held key or d-pad repeats), with ticks at its steps, labelled marks, a readout and a bubble over the knob while it moves. Plays sliderTick at each step passed (rising in pitch with the value). Parts: `Slider.track[hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `Slider.rail`, `Slider.fill`, `Slider.knob[pressed|focused]`, `Slider.core` (the knob's dot while held or focused), `Slider.tick[passed]`, `Slider.bubble`. Role slider with its range. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Track`, `<id>/Track/Knob`, `<id>/Head/Value`.

functions.name: rangeSlider
functions.doc: A range slider: two knobs on one track and the fill between them. A press on the track takes the nearer knob there and a drag moves it (never past the other, kept minGap apart); each knob is its own focus stop, Left and Right step it. Parts: `RangeSlider.track`, `RangeSlider.rail`, `RangeSlider.fill`, `RangeSlider.knob[low|high][pressed|focused]` (under a finger drawn inside `RangeSlider.reach`, its 44 px target). Two sliders to a screen reader (lowLabel, highLabel). Probe: `<id>/Track/Low`, `<id>/Track/High`.

params.name: low
params.doc: The low end from game state.

params.name: high
params.doc: The high end from game state.

functions.name: numberStepper
functions.doc: A number stepper: minus, the value and plus. A press steps once, a held press repeats after 400 ms and speeds up (large steps after a second); Left and Right step it while the value has the focus. A bound's button goes disabled at the bound. Plays sliderTick per step. Parts: `Stepper.frame[focused|disabled]`, `Stepper.button[dec|inc][hover|pressed|disabled]`, `Stepper.value`. Its label and the buttons share a line while they fit, the buttons go under the label when they do not (larger text, a narrow column). Role spinbutton with its range; its − and + are buttons under a finger (stops keys and pads reach too) and named images on a fine pointer (Left and Right on the focused stepper are theirs). Probe: `<id>/Frame/Dec`, `<id>/Frame/Value`, `<id>/Frame/Inc`.

functions.name: cycler
functions.doc: An option cycler, the console settings row: `‹ High ›` with pips. Left and Right (a pad's d-pad or stick) change it while it has the focus, the arrows take a press, and a press on the value steps forward; the value slides in from the side it came (selection on the style's motion). Arrows follow the writing direction. Plays select. Parts: `Cycler.frame[hover|focused|disabled]`, `Cycler.arrow[prev|next][disabled]`, `Cycler.pip[current]`. Role spinbutton reading the option; its arrows are buttons under a finger and named images on a fine pointer (Left and Right on the focused cycler are theirs). Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Prev`, `<id>/Middle/Clip/Value#i` (the option shown), `<id>/Next`, `<id>/Middle/Pips/Pip#i`.

params.name: index
params.doc: The current one from game state.

functions.name: segmented
functions.doc: A segmented control (segmented tabs): a track whose raised thumb slides to the chosen segment and takes its width on the style's spring (layout animation; it jumps under reduced motion). A press chooses; Left and Right step the choice while it has the focus, skipping disabled segments, mirrored right to left. The segments share the width they are given, never narrower than their labels: when they do not fit, the track scrolls sideways under a fade at the cut edge. Under a finger each segment is at least 44 px tall. Plays tab. Parts: `Segmented.track[focused|disabled]`, `Segmented.thumb`, `Segmented.item[selected][hover|pressed|disabled]`. Role radiogroup of radios. Probe: `<id>`, `<id>/Strip/Track/Item#i`, `<id>/Strip/Track/Thumb`.

functions.name: dropdown
functions.doc: A dropdown (a select): a field-like trigger with the chosen option and a chevron that turns as it opens; its list opens below it (above without room, kept on screen) as a floating layer that takes the focus at the chosen option, with groups, icons, descriptions, a tick on the chosen and a filter past 10 options. A press, Enter, Space or A opens it and chooses; Back, Escape or a press outside closes it and the focus returns to the trigger. Plays open, select and close. Parts: `Dropdown.trigger[open][invalid][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `Dropdown.list`, `Dropdown.option[selected][hover|focused|disabled]`, `Dropdown.group`. Role combobox (expanded while open) and a listbox of options. Probe: `<id>/Trigger`, `<id>.list/Panel/Content/Option#i`.

functions.name: inputField
functions.doc: A text field (og.ui.textField's editing: IME, selection, clipboard, undo) in a framed row with a label above, an icon, a suffix, a clear button and a helper, error or counter line below. Its frame takes the focus ring as it is edited, turns danger and shakes once when an error appears (validity group). On a coarse pointer its row is 44 CSS px at least. Parts: `Input.frame[focused][invalid][disabled][hover]`, `Input.clear`. Role textbox named by its label; the error is an alert; the clear button is a button under a finger (a stop keys and pads reach too) and a named image on a fine pointer. Disabled, its text is drawn in muted ink on a fainter frame, out of the focus order, a textbox the tree calls disabled. Probe: `<id>/Frame/Field` (its text), `<id>/Frame/Clear`, `<id>/Foot/Error`.

functions.name: inputArea
functions.doc: A text area (og.ui.textArea's editing) framed as inputField is, with its label, helper, error and counter. Parts: `Input.frame[area][focused][invalid]` and the field's. Probe: `<id>/Frame/Area`, `<id>/Foot/Counter`.

functions.name: searchBox
functions.doc: A search box with suggestions: a field with a lens, a clear button and, while it has the focus and something matches, a list of suggestions under it (recent searches while it is empty) whose matching part is bold, laid over what follows the field (it never pushes it down), or over what comes before it when below it would run past the screen's bottom. Down (or a pad's down) moves into the list, Enter or a press chooses; Escape (Back) closes the list and leaves the field focused, and typing or a press on the field opens it again. Typing stays in the field (the list takes no focus scope). Parts: `Search.frame[focused]`, `Search.list`, `Search.option[hover|focused]` (the query's match in bold). Role textbox with a listbox of options. Probe: `<id>/Frame/Field`, `<id>/List/Option#i`.

functions.name: colorPicker
functions.doc: A colour picker: a saturation and brightness square with a ring at the colour, a hue strip, an opacity strip, swatches and a hex field, with the colour before and after. A press or a drag on the square or a strip sets it (a touch too); Left and Right step the hue strip, the opacity strip and the square's saturation while they have the focus; swatches are buttons; a hex field takes `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` and `#rrggbbaa`. The hue is kept while the colour is grey (UI state). Parts: `ColorPicker.square[focused]`, `ColorPicker.hue` and `ColorPicker.alpha` (the strips' reach, 44 px tall under a finger) with `ColorPicker.hueBar` and `ColorPicker.alphaBar` (the strips drawn in them), `ColorPicker.thumb[focused]`, `ColorPicker.swatch[selected][hover|focused]`, `ColorPicker.preview`. Roles: two sliders and a slider-like square (its hex as its value), swatches as radios. Probe: `<id>/Square`, `<id>/Hue`, `<id>/Alpha`, `<id>/Swatches/Swatch#i`, `<id>/Bottom/Hex/Input/Frame/Field`.

functions.name: keyBindingRow
functions.doc: A key-binding row (the settings tree's controls page, docs/ui.md §11): the action's name and a slot per binding on a device (keyboard and mouse, or a pad, the device used last by default) showing its glyphs from og.input (keys as caps, pad buttons as their family's discs, composites as their parts). A press on a slot (Enter, A) starts og.input.startCapture for it: the slot pulses `Press a key…` with the cancel hint until the player presses something (Escape, the pad's back or the timeout cancels). A capture with no conflict is applied at once; one that shares a control asks inline (`W is used by Move forward`: Swap, Replace, Cancel) with og.input's conflict report. A locked action shows a lock and takes no press; a rebound one shows a reset. Plays select, confirm, cancel and error. Parts: `Rebind.row[capturing][conflict][locked]`, `Rebind.slot[empty][capturing][conflict][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]`, `Rebind.conflict`; the caps are the action bar's `ActionBar.glyph[key|face|shoulder]`, the reset an icon button (`Button.base[quiet][icon]`). A group named by the action, slots as buttons named `<action>, <slot>: <binding>`. Probe: `<id>/Main/Bound/Slots/Slot#i`, `<id>/Conflict/Swap`, `<id>/Conflict/Replace`, `<id>/Conflict/Cancel`, `<id>/Main/Bound/Reset` (once rebound). Where its slots and Reset do not fit beside each other at their least width (200 % text, a narrow column), the row stacks them, the first slot over the second, so every row of a list stacks alike; a key cluster (W A S D) keeps its order right to left.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world (the action map is world state).

functions.name: onScreenKeyboard
functions.doc: An on-screen keyboard for pads and touch (docs/ui.md §11, Appendix D: search and names with a pad): a panel at the screen's bottom with the text being typed and its caret, a candidate bar while composing, and keys a pad walks with focus wrapping by rows (Y erases, LB and RB move the caret, Back closes) and a finger presses (a key pops its letter above the finger on a press). Letters (shift for one, double tap for caps), symbols, a number pad and the Japanese kana table, with composition for an IME: typed kana (or letters with compose) stay underlined in KeyboardResult.composition until a candidate (the game's, plus the katakana) or Enter commits them. Plays press, select and back sounds. Parts: `Keyboard.panel`, `Keyboard.key[wide][action][active][primary][hover|pressed|focused|disabled]` (primary: the enter key; disabled: a gap in the kana table), `Keyboard.preview`, `Keyboard.candidates`, `Keyboard.candidate[hover|pressed|focused]`, `Keyboard.popup`. A dialog named by its title; keys are buttons named by what they type. Probe: `<id>/Panel/Content/Keys/Row#r/Key#k`, `<id>/Panel/Content/Preview`, `<id>/Panel/Content/Candidates/Candidate#i`.

params.name: desc
params.doc: What it edits and how it types.

functions.name: cardHand
functions.doc:
A hand of cards (Slay the Spire, Hearthstone, Marvel Snap, Balatro): fanned along an arc at the bottom of the play area, each card a frame in its tier's colour with its cost gem, art, name banner, type line and rich-text rules. The card under the pointer or the focus lifts clear of the fan, straightens and grows so it reads whole, and its neighbours part. Dragged above the play line a card plays on release; a card that needs a target stays over the hand while an arc follows the pointer, snapping to the target under it (success ink on a valid one, danger on an invalid one), and plays on release there. Keys and pads walk the hand with Left and Right, confirm plays or starts aiming (Left and Right then step through the valid targets, confirm plays, Back cancels), the details action shows a card large. An unplayable card is dimmed with its cost in danger ink, and trying it shakes it.
Parts: CardHand.fan, Card.frame[rarity=<tier>][lifted][dragging][aiming][unplayable][glow], Card.cost[up|down|unaffordable], Card.art, Card.name, Card.type, Card.text, CardHand.arc[valid|invalid|none], CardHand.reticle, CardHand.playLine, CardHand.inspect. Slots: each card's art (art kind card, 5:4). States: on each card, group lift (rest, lifted, held, aiming) and play (playable, unplayable); on the arc, group verdict (none, valid, invalid). Motion: cards move to their fan places on the ui spring (layout motion), a lifted card rises and grows, a fresh card flies in from the start edge, a played one leaves upward, a refusal shakes. Sounds: hover as a card lifts, select as a drag or aim starts, confirm on a play, error on a refusal, cancel when aiming stops. Accessibility: a listbox named by label; each card an option named by its name, cost and type, its rules as its description, unplayable said as disabled; aiming says the target. Probe ids: <id>/Fan/<key>, <id>/Arc, <id>/Reticle, <id>/Inspect.

functions.name: heroButton
functions.doc:
The one action a genre screen leads with (End turn, Summon, Play, Ready): a raised face lit from the top over a ledge of its own dark and a soft shadow on the scene, so it reads as a thing to press over any backdrop, beside the flat controls of og.ui.button. It lifts under the pointer and the focus and sinks when pressed; disabled it lies flat. A keycap after the label shows the action's binding on a desktop.
Parts: Pattern.button[primary|premium|secondary|danger][sm|md|lg], Pattern.buttonFace, Pattern.keycap. States: group interaction (normal, hover, pressed, focused, disabled). Motion: the ui token's lift and press. Sounds: the style's press. Accessibility: a button named by its label (and key). Probe id: <id>.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Tone, size, keycap, disabled and width.

functions.name: rewardChoice
functions.doc:
A choice of N rewards (Slay the Spire's card reward, Hades' boons, Vampire Survivors' level-up, Balatro's shop packs): each reward a card in its tier's colour with its art, kind, title, tag and rich-text effect, dealt in one after another and flipped face up.
