The card under the pointer or the focus lifts and its edge brightens; a press takes it (or selects it, with confirm or several picks, its ring and a tick in the focus ink), the taken one rises and grows while the others fall away. Reroll, Banish (armed, every card shows a cross until one is pressed) and Skip sit under the cards. Keys and pads move along the cards, confirm takes or selects, Back disarms banishing. Side by side on a desktop and a phone on its side; one above another, compact, on a phone in portrait.
Parts: Reward.frame, Reward.card[rarity=<tier>][selected][banishing][locked], Reward.art, Reward.kind, Reward.title, Reward.text, Reward.tag, Reward.check, Reward.banishMark, Reward.actions, Reward.reroll, Reward.banish[armed], Reward.skip, Reward.confirm. Slots: each reward's art (art kind item or card). States: on each card, group selection (off, on) and fate (offered, banishing, locked). Motion: cards deal in with a stagger and turn face up on the emphasis spring; hover lifts on the ui spring; a taken card rises and the others fall and fade. Sounds: open as they deal, hover, select, confirm on a take, error on a locked one, toggle for banishing. Accessibility: a radiogroup (one pick) or group named by title; each reward a radio or checkbox named by its title, kind and tier, its effect as its description; locked said disabled with its hint. Probe ids: <id>/Options/<key>, <id>/Actions/Reroll, <id>/Actions/Banish, <id>/Actions/Skip, <id>/Actions/Confirm.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The rewards and what the choice allows.

functions.name: starBar
functions.doc:
A level's score toward its stars (Candy Crush, Homescapes, Angry Birds): the score in the display face over a bar that fills in a warm gold, a star standing on the bar at each threshold, lit as the score passes it with a pop and the success sound, an outline until then. The bar runs start to end, mirrored right to left.
Parts: StarBar.frame[compact], StarBar.label, StarBar.value, StarBar.track, StarBar.fill, StarBar.star[lit]. States: on each star, group lit (off, on). Motion: the fill eases to the score on the ui spring; a star crossed pops on the emphasis spring (still under reduced motion). Sounds: success on each star crossed. Accessibility: a meter named by label with the score as its value and its stars as its description. Probe ids: <id>/Bar/Track, <id>/Bar/Stars/Star#i, <id>/Value.

functions.name: idleGenerator
functions.doc:
One generator of an idle game (AdVenture Capitalist, Cookie Clicker, Idle Miner): its art, name, level, owned count, the cycle's bar filling toward its next payout, what it makes, and a buy button with its cost, lit when the purse pays and glass when it does not. Held, Buy repeats (after a beat, every few ticks) as long as the purse pays. A locked generator lies dim with what unlocks it. One row; a game stacks them in a scrolling list with the buy amount chosen above (og.ui.segmented).
Parts: Idle.generator[locked][affordable], Idle.art, Idle.name, Idle.level, Idle.owned, Idle.cycle[fast], Idle.cycleFill, Idle.rate, Idle.buy[affordable|short], Idle.cost, Idle.lock. Slots: its art (art kind item), the currency's icon. States: group purse (afford, short) on the buy button; group cycle (slow, fast) on the bar. Motion: a fast cycle's shimmer and a purchase's pop (still under reduced motion); the buy button lifts and sinks as a raised button. Sounds: the style's press on a purchase, error when short. Accessibility: a group named by name; the bar a meter; Buy a button named by its label, cost and short when the purse cannot pay. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Info/Name, <id>/Info/Cycle, <id>/Buy.

functions.name: prestigePanel
functions.doc:
An idle game's prestige (AdVenture Capitalist's angels, Cookie Clicker's ascension): its emblem, the line over what a reset gives in the display face, what a reset does with a tick each, and a premium hold-to-confirm button (og.ui.holdButton), so a run is never reset by a slip. Until a reset gives something, the button lies flat with why.
Parts: Prestige.frame[available], Prestige.emblem, Prestige.title, Prestige.lead, Prestige.reward, Prestige.point, Prestige.action, Prestige.hint. Slots: the emblem (art kind emblem). States: group availability (ready, waiting) on the frame. Motion: the hold fills the button from its start edge; the emblem glows while ready (still under reduced motion). Sounds: the hold button's rising ticks and confirm. Accessibility: a region named by title; the reward and points as text; the button a button whose value is the hold's progress. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Body/Reward, <id>/Action (og.ui.holdButton's, its own /Button within).

functions.name: storeFront
functions.doc:
A store (Fortnite's item shop, Genshin's, Clash Royale's): the purse at its head with a plus to top up, then each section under its heading with its refresh timer, its offers as tiles of art in their tier's rim. A tile's name sits on its art over a shade, its price at its foot (a struck original and a saving ribbon when discounted, the danger ink when short); a featured tile is twice as wide and lists its bundle; an owned one shows a tick, a sold-out one is dimmed. Pressing one that can be bought answers chosen; one that cannot shakes and says why.
Parts: Store.frame, Store.wallet, Store.currency, Store.topUp, Store.section, Store.heading, Store.refresh, Store.offer[rarity=<tier>][featured][owned][soldOut][short][selected], Store.art, Store.name, Store.kind, Store.contents, Store.price, Store.ribbon, Store.tag, Store.left, Store.timer. Slots: each offer's art (art kind item, or splash when featured), each currency's (art kind currency). States: on each offer, group availability (available, short, owned, soldOut) and group selection (off, on). Motion: a hovered tile lifts on the ui spring and its art eases in; a refused press shakes it. Sounds: hover, select on chosen, error on refused. Accessibility: a region named label; each section a list named by its title; each offer a button named by its name, kind, tier and price or state, its contents as its description. Probe ids: <id>/Wallet/<key>, <id>/Wallet/<key>/TopUp, <id>/Sections/<section>/Offers/<key>.

functions.name: battlePass
functions.doc:
A battle pass (Fortnite, Apex Legends, Brawl Stars): a header over the season's art with its name, the time left, the level in a badge and the XP bar, then the track: the tiers side by side in a scrolling row on a desktop (the free track under the level line, the premium one over it) and stacked in portrait. Tiers reached are lit up to the player's level; a reward ready to claim glows and pulses with Claim, a claimed one shows a tick and dims, a premium one without the track wears a lock. The track opens on the player's level; Claim all and Unlock Premium stand at its head.
Parts: Pass.frame, Pass.header, Pass.title, Pass.level, Pass.xpTrack, Pass.xpFill, Pass.timer, Pass.track, Pass.tier[reached][current][milestone], Pass.levelBadge, Pass.line[lit], Pass.reward[premium][ready][claimed][locked][rarity=<tier>], Pass.art, Pass.amount, Pass.lock, Pass.check, Pass.claimAll, Pass.unlock. Slots: the season's art (art kind banner); each reward's (art kind item). States: on each reward, group claim (ahead, ready, claimed, locked); on each tier, group progress (ahead, reached, current). Motion: a ready reward breathes (still under reduced motion); a claim pops it on the emphasis spring; the XP bar eases on the ui spring; the track scrolls to the player's level when it opens. Sounds: select on a claim, success on Claim all, error on a refusal. Accessibility: a region named label; the XP bar a meter; the track a list of tiers named by level, each reward a button named by its name, track and claim state. Probe ids: <id>/Header/Level, <id>/Header/Xp, <id>/Actions/ClaimAll, <id>/Actions/Unlock, <id>/Track/Tiers/L<level>/Free, <id>/Track/Tiers/L<level>/Premium.

functions.name: backlog
functions.doc:
A visual novel's backlog (Ren'Py, Persona, Ace Attorney): a panel over the dimmed scene that opens on the newest line and scrolls back, each line under its speaker's name, the narrator's in muted italics, the choice the player made on a line under it as their reply, a voiced line with a button that plays it again; Close (and back) hides it.
Parts: Backlog.frame, Backlog.title, Backlog.list, Backlog.entry[narrator][seen], Backlog.name, Backlog.text, Backlog.reply, Backlog.replay, Backlog.close. States: on each entry, group voice (silent, voiced). Motion: it rises in on the panel spring; the list opens at its foot. Sounds: open, back on close, select on a replay. Accessibility: a dialog named by title; the list a log of its lines, each named speaker: text; each replay a button. Probe ids: <id>/List/L<seq>, <id>/List/L<seq>/Replay, <id>/Close.

functions.name: barks
functions.doc:
Barks over their speakers (The Last of Us, Hitman, Sea of Thieves): one og.ui.speechBubble for each bark og.story is saying, typed out from the tick it began and leaving as og.story's time for it (BarkView.ticksLeft) runs out; a new line on the same entity replaces the old at once; a shout from shoutPriority up.
Parts: those of og.ui.speechBubble. Accessibility: each bubble text named its speaker. Probe ids: <id>/E<entity> (the speech bubble's own ids under it).

functions.name: lobby
functions.doc:
A party lobby (Valorant, Fortnite, Rocket League, Overwatch): the party stands as a lineup of tall cards, each the player's character art with a scrim at its foot carrying the name in the display face, the level and a title, and a ready foot lit in success with a tick (not ready muted; a status line in its place); the local player's card first and larger, the leader's crown at its corner, each empty seat an Invite. At the foot, the mode card (its art, name and detail) at the start and one primary action at the end: Ready up and Ready for a member, Find match for the leader, Cancel while searching with a chip counting the time in queue and the estimate. A ready check rises over everything on a scrim: Match found in the display face, a ring that runs out with the seconds left, a pip per player lit as each accepts (danger for a decline), and Accept large in the accent beside Decline. On a phone in portrait the lineup is two columns of shorter cards and the foot docks at the thumb.
Parts: Lobby.frame, Lobby.lineup, Lobby.member[you][leader][ready], Lobby.art, Lobby.plate, Lobby.foot[ready], Lobby.crown, Lobby.seat, Lobby.bar, Lobby.mode, Lobby.action, Lobby.search, Lobby.check, Lobby.pip[accepted|declined], Lobby.accept, Lobby.decline. Slots: each member's portrait (art kind character), the mode's image (art kind thumbnail). States: on each member, group ready (waiting, ready); on the check's pips, group answer (pending, accepted, declined). Motion: the cards rise in one after another on the panel spring; a card turning ready pops its foot; the search chip's dot breathes; the check scales in on the emphasis spring and its ring runs down (still under reduced motion). Sounds: select on a card or seat, confirm on ready, start and accept, back on cancel and decline, open when the check rises, success when every player has accepted. Accessibility: the lineup a list; each card a button named its name, level, title, leader and ready word; each seat a button named the invite word; the check a dialog named the found word with the time left as a timer. Probe ids: <id>/Lineup/<key>, <id>/Lineup/Seat#<i>, <id>/Bar/Mode, <id>/Bar/Action, <id>/Bar/Search, <id>/Check/Accept, <id>/Check/Decline.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The party, the mode, matchmaking and the ready check.

functions.name: characterSelect
functions.doc:
A character select (Street Fighter 6, Valorant, Overwatch, Smash): the local player's character standing large on the start side, its splash art filling that half over a scrim with its role in the eyebrow, its name in the display face and a line of description; with two players the other's on the end side, mirrored, each tagged in its team's colour; the roster under or beside them as a grid of portrait tiles in whole rows, each cursor a rim in its player's team colour with the player's tag at the tile's corner (two on one tile split the corner), a confirmed pick a tick, a locked tile dark behind a lock, a taken one dimmed. Lock in in the accent at the foot (Locked in, quiet, once confirmed); a timer when the game gives one. Keys and pads walk the tiles (the focus is the local cursor), confirm locks in, Back unlocks. On a phone in portrait the splash takes the top and the grid scrolls under it.
Parts: Select.frame, Select.stage, Select.splash[you|rival][confirmed], Select.name, Select.roster, Select.tile[cursor][confirmed][locked][taken], Select.tag, Select.lock, Select.confirm[on], Select.timer. Slots: each entry's portrait (art kind portrait) and splash (art kind splash). States: on each tile, group pick (open, cursor, confirmed, locked, taken). Motion: a new character's splash slides in from its side on the panel spring; a confirmed pick flashes its tile and its splash's name pops on the emphasis spring (still under reduced motion); a refused tile shakes. Sounds: hover as the cursor moves, confirm on a pick, error on a refused one, back on Back. Accessibility: the roster a grid of buttons named name, role, locked or taken and whose cursor is on it; each splash a region named the player and the character. Probe ids: <id>/Stage/Roster/Row#<r>/<key>, <id>/Stage/Roster/Row#<r>/Random, <id>/Stage/Start, <id>/Stage/End, <id>/Foot/Lock.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The roster, the cursors and the words.

functions.name: versus
functions.doc:
A versus screen (Street Fighter, Tekken, Mortal Kombat, a MOBA's loading screen): the screen split on a slant into two sides, each a character's splash filling its half in the tint of its team, the character's name huge in the display face and the player's name and detail under it at the foot; the mark between them on the slant, the stage under it, and loading progress along the foot when the game gives it. The sides slam in from their edges, the mark pops in after them and both splashes drift slowly (still under reduced motion).
Parts: Versus.frame, Versus.side[left|right], Versus.splash, Versus.name, Versus.player, Versus.mark, Versus.stage, Versus.progress, Versus.skip. Slots: each side's splash (art kind splash). Motion: the sides slide in from their edges on the panel spring, the mark scales in on the emphasis spring 200 ms later, the splashes drift by a few pixels over the screen's life. Sounds: open as it shows, confirm on a skip. Accessibility: a region named both sides and the mark (Aria versus Kael). Probe ids: <id>/Left, <id>/Right, <id>/Mark, <id>/Progress.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The sides, the stage and the words.

functions.name: draft
functions.doc:
A draft with bans (League of Legends, Dota 2, Marvel Snap's draft mode, a sports draft): the two teams in columns at the sides, each pick a wide slot with the character's art across it (dimmed while only hovered), the player's name and the character's, the slot that picks now lit in its team's colour with a light running along it; each team's bans a row of small tiles under its picks, struck through in danger, the bans to come empty. In the middle the phase banner (ban in danger, pick in the accent) with a bar that runs down with the turn's time and the seconds, the roster as a grid of portrait tiles in whole rows (banned ones struck and dark, picked ones dimmed, the hovered one rimmed in the local team's colour), and under it one action: Ban in danger or Lock in in the accent in the local player's turn, Waiting otherwise. On a phone in portrait the teams stand as two rows of portraits above the roster.
Parts: Draft.frame, Draft.team[start|end], Draft.slot[active][locked][you], Draft.slotArt, Draft.bans, Draft.ban[empty], Draft.banner[ban|pick], Draft.timer, Draft.roster, Draft.tile[cursor][banned][taken], Draft.action[ban|pick|waiting]. Slots: each slot's and tile's art (the entry's splash or portrait, art kind portrait). States: on each tile, group pick (open, cursor, taken, banned); on each slot, group slot (empty, hovered, locked). Motion: a pick locking in flashes its slot and slides its art in on the panel spring; the active slot's light sweeps along it; a ban's slash draws across (still under reduced motion); a refused tile shakes. Sounds: hover as the hover moves, confirm on a pick, error on a refused tile, alert in the last five seconds of the local player's turn. Accessibility: each team a list named its name of slots named player, character and state; the roster a grid of buttons named name and banned or picked; the timer a timer. Probe ids: <id>/Start/Picks/Slot#<i>, <id>/End/Picks/Slot#<i>, <id>/Start/Bans/Ban#<i>, <id>/Middle/Room/Roster/Row#<r>/<key>, <id>/Middle/Banner, <id>/Middle/Foot/Action (on a phone in portrait the teams are under <id>/Teams/Wrap).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The teams, the roster, the phase and the words.

functions.name: worldMap
functions.doc:
A world map (The Witcher 3, Breath of the Wild, Genshin Impact, Elden Ring): the painted map filling the screen, pinched, wheeled and dragged to zoom and pan (og.ui.zoomView); the regions' names set across it in the display face's caps while zoomed out, each undiscovered region under a cloud of fog with its name ???; the places as pins in their kind's mark, the tracked one ringed and pulsing, undiscovered ones faint under the fog, their names beside them once zoomed in; the player's arrow by its heading. A legend on the end side lists each kind with its count and turns it off and on; a pressed pin opens its detail as a card beside the legend: the place's picture, name and line, and Fast travel in the accent on a discovered fast-travel point, else Set or Remove waypoint. On a phone the legend is a row of chips at the top and the detail a card docked at the foot; where covering the screen would cut much of the map (a phone in portrait), the map sits whole across its width.
Parts: WorldMap.frame, WorldMap.map, WorldMap.fog, WorldMap.region[discovered], WorldMap.pin[<kind>][tracked][undiscovered][selected], WorldMap.player, WorldMap.legend, WorldMap.entry[off], WorldMap.detail, WorldMap.action. Slots: the map (art kind map), each place's image (art kind thumbnail). States: on each pin, group find (discovered, undiscovered); on each legend entry, group shown (on, off). Motion: a tracked pin's ring pulses; the detail slides in on the panel spring; region names fade as the map zooms in and pin labels fade in (still under reduced motion). Sounds: select on a pin and a legend entry, confirm on travel and waypoint, back on closing the detail. Accessibility: the map an image named its title with its zoom as its value; each pin a button named its name (or ???) and kind, tracked; the legend a list of switches; the detail a region named the place. Probe ids: <id>/Map/Pins/<key>, <id>/Map/Pins/Player, <id>/Side/Legend/<kind>, <id>/Side/Detail, <id>/Side/Detail/Action.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The map, its regions and places, the player and the words.

functions.name: songSelect
functions.doc:
A song select (Project Sekai, osu!, Beat Saber, Taiko): the songs on an angled wheel at the end side, each row its jacket, title and artist with its tempo, the selected row larger and lit, the rows above and below it leaning away and fading, gliding as the selection moves; beside it the selected song large: its jacket filling a square, the title in the display face, the artist, the tempo and length in tabular numerals, the charts as chips with their levels (the selected one lit, a locked one dimmed with a lock), the best score with its grade and a full combo badge; at the foot the preview's bar, its waveform lit up to where the preview is, with its play toggle and time, the accuracy as a ring beside it, and Play in the accent. Up and down (keys, a pad, the wheel's rows under the focus) move the selection, the tab actions (Q and E, the bumpers) step the chart over locked ones, confirm plays. On a phone in portrait the jacket and the detail stand at the top, the wheel scrolls under them and Play docks at the thumb.
Parts: Songs.frame, Songs.wheel, Songs.row[selected][locked][new], Songs.jacket, Songs.detail, Songs.title, Songs.stats, Songs.chip[selected][locked], Songs.score, Songs.grade, Songs.combo, Songs.accuracy, Songs.preview[playing], Songs.wave, Songs.play. Slots: each song's jacket (art kind jacket). States: on each row, group pick (open, selected, locked); on each chip, group chart (open, selected, locked). Motion: the wheel's rows glide to their places on the ui spring as the selection moves; the detail's jacket and title cross-fade on a change of song; the played part of the waveform grows with the preview (still under reduced motion). Sounds: hover as the selection moves, tab on a chart step, confirm on Play, error on a refused one. Accessibility: the wheel a listbox of options named title, artist and tempo; the charts a radio group named name and level; the preview a button named the preview word with its time; the score and grade a status. Probe ids: <id>/Wheel/<key>, <id>/Main/Top/Detail/Charts/<key>, <id>/Main/Top/Detail/Head/Title, <id>/Main/Foot/Preview/Toggle, <id>/Main/Foot/Play (on a phone in portrait <id>/Detail/Charts/<key>, <id>/Preview/Toggle, <id>/Play).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The songs, the selection, the preview and the words.

functions.name: ledger
functions.doc:
A management ledger (Cities: Skylines' budget, Crusader Kings' and Stellaris' ledgers, Football Manager's finances): the headline figures as tiles across the top, each its art, its caption, its value large in the numeric face and its change since the last period signed with an arrow, in success or danger by whether the change is good; under them the ledger, a column header whose name, amount and change headings sort the lines (the sorted one marked with its direction), then each section's heading with its total, then its lines, each a row of its art, its name (a warning mark and its words when it has a problem), its amount, its change in percent and, for a budgeted line, its funding slider with its percent; the net at the foot in success or danger. Beside the ledger the history graph (og.ui.chart over the periods) and, when `breakdown` names a section, a donut of its lines' shares. Tabs at the head switch the period. On a phone in portrait the figures are a two-column grid, the ledger follows them with each line's slider in its own row under its name, and the graphs close the page; the page scrolls and the net stays docked at the foot. A desktop short of room for its text (200 % on a laptop) stacks the same way with its sliders inline.
Parts: Ledger.frame, Ledger.figure, Ledger.delta[up|down|good|bad], Ledger.header, Ledger.section, Ledger.line[selected|warning], Ledger.net[good|bad], Ledger.graph. Slots: each figure's and line's art (itemIcon). Sounds: select on a line or a heading, tab on a tab; the slider's own. Accessibility: each figure a status named with its value and change; the ledger a table, each heading a column header with its sort, each line a row named with its amount, change and budget; the slider a slider. Probe ids: <id>/Head/Tabs/<tab>, <id>/Figures/<key>, <id>/Body/Ledger/Header/<name|amount|change>, <id>/Body/Ledger/List/<section>, <id>/Body/Ledger/List/<key>, <id>/Body/Ledger/List/<key>/Main/Budget/Funding (<key>/Budget/Funding when stacked), <id>/Body/Ledger/Net (<id>/Net when stacked), <id>/Body/Side/Graphs/History (<id>/Body/Graphs/History when stacked).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The figures, sections, lines, history and words.

functions.name: overlayBar
functions.doc:
A map's overlay picker (Cities: Skylines' info views, Civilization's lenses): a row of round buttons, each its overlay's art, the shown one lit with its name, and over the bar the shown overlay's legend, its name, its ramp of colours from low to high with the two words at its ends. A press shows an overlay, a second press on the shown one turns it off; a finger, keys and a pad reach each button. The game draws the overlay on its map; the bar draws the picker and the legend only. On a phone the bar scrolls sideways and keeps its buttons whole touch targets.
Parts: Overlay.bar, Overlay.button[selected], Overlay.legend, Overlay.ramp. Slots: each overlay's art (itemIcon). Sounds: toggle on a press. Accessibility: the bar a toolbar, each button a toggle button with its pressed state; the legend a status named with the overlay and its ends. Probe ids: <id>/Bar/<key>, <id>/Legend.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The overlays and the shown one.

functions.name: chat
functions.doc:
A chat window (World of Warcraft, Final Fantasy XIV, Discord in a game): the channel tabs, each its name and its unread count (in the highlight when a message there names the player); the log, each message one wrapping line of its time, its channel's tag in the channel's ink where the tab shows every channel, the author's name in that ink (a press answers them), and the words as typed, with each link a bracketed press in its tier's ink and each @mention in the highlight; a message naming the player is lit along its edge, a system line is muted. The log stays on the newest message while the player is at its foot; scrolled up, new messages gather in a pill (3 new) that brings the view down. Under it the input: the channel chip in its ink (a press steps to the next channel that can be sent to), the field and Send (a round button with its arrow where the window is narrow for its text, the chip's name then cut short); Enter sends, and while an @word is typed the matching members are offered over the input, a press writing the name. The HUD form draws no panel, only the newest lines over the game, which fade once idle, and shows the tabs and the input while the player types. On a phone the window takes its room and Send is a whole touch target.
Parts: Chat.frame, Chat.tab[selected|mention], Chat.log, Chat.line[mention|own|system], Chat.avatar, Chat.new, Chat.input, Chat.channel, Chat.suggestion. Slots: avatars (portrait). Sounds: tab on a tab, select on a link or a name, confirm on a send. Accessibility: the tabs a tablist, the log a log and one focus group whose lines keys and a pad walk (reading back scrolls it), each line a listitem named author: words; links are links. Probe ids: <id>/Tabs/Row/<channel>, <id>/Log/<key>, <id>/Log/<key>/Text/<link> (a link: L<key>; a name: U<authorKey>), <id>/New, <id>/Input/Channel, <id>/Input/Field, <id>/Input/Send, <id>/Suggest/<member>.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The channels, messages, draft and words.

functions.name: photoMode
functions.doc:
Photo mode's controls (Horizon Forbidden West, Ghost of Tsushima, Forza Horizon) over the game's own paused view, which this never draws: on a desktop a glass panel at the end side with the title, the tabs (a lit underline on the one shown; the tab actions step them), the tab's sliders (og.ui.valueSlider), each its name, its reading and a track filling from its origin, or for `filters` and `frames` a grid of tiles showing the shot through each, the chosen one rimmed and ticked, with the filter's strength under them; at the foot the shutter, a large round button, between Grid, Hide UI, Reset and Exit as round icon buttons with their names. The rule of thirds and the chosen frame's art lie over the whole picture. Hidden, only a quiet hint stays at the foot; any press, Back, or the hide action brings the controls back, and confirm takes the shot. The shutter's flash (a white wash fading over flashMs, still under reduced motion) follows a capture. On a phone in portrait the panel is a sheet at the foot over the lower third, its tabs a row of chips, and the shutter row under it.
Parts: Photo.panel, Photo.tab[selected], Photo.tile[selected], Photo.shutter, Photo.tool[on], Photo.grid, Photo.frame, Photo.flash, Photo.hint. Slots: each look's thumbnail (thumbnail), the frame (overlay). Sounds: tab on a tab, select on a tile, confirm on the shutter, toggle on Grid and Hide. Accessibility: the panel a region named by its title, the tabs a tablist, each slider a slider, each tile a radio, the shutter a button. Probe ids: <id>/Panel/Tabs/<tab>, <id>/Panel/Rows/<control>, <id>/Panel/Rows/Line#<row>/<look>, <id>/Panel/Rows/Strength, <id>/Bar/Shutter, <id>/Bar/Grid, <id>/Bar/Hide, <id>/Bar/Reset, <id>/Bar/Exit, <id>/Hint.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The tabs, sliders, looks and the state.

functions.name: deckBuilder
functions.doc:
A deck builder (Hearthstone, Marvel Snap, Legends of Runeterra): at the top the filters, chips of cost (0 to 7 and up), of tier and of kind, each with All, the search and the sort; under them the collection's grid, each card the face og.ui.cardHand draws (its gem, its art, its name banner), a card not owned dimmed (×0), a card whose copies are all in the deck quieter; the card hovered or focused stands large over the grid with its rules. At the end, the whole height beside the filters and the grid, the deck: its name over its art, its count (30/30, in danger past the whole), then a row per card in it by cost, its cost gem, its tier's mark, its name over a strip of its art fading in, and its copies; the mana curve, a bar per cost with its count over it; the kinds' counts; Done. Under each card stands its own row, the copies owned (×2), and a mark of the copies in the deck rides its top end corner. A press on a collection card adds a copy, a press on a deck row takes one out; a card the deck cannot take shakes and the reason shows under the count. Whole rows of the grid scroll. On a phone in portrait the two halves are tabs, Cards and the deck (with its count), and the curve, counts and Done stand under the deck's list.
Parts: DeckBuilder.chip[selected], DeckBuilder.card[unowned][full], DeckBuilder.count, DeckBuilder.preview, DeckBuilder.deck, DeckBuilder.row, DeckBuilder.curve, DeckBuilder.bar, DeckBuilder.kinds, DeckBuilder.refusal. Slots: each card's art (cardArt), each row's strip (cardArt), the deck's art (cardArt), each kind's mark (icon). Sounds: select on a chip, confirm on an add or a removal, error on a refusal, confirm on Done. Accessibility: the filters radio groups, the grid a grid of buttons named by the card, its cost and copies, the deck a list of buttons, the curve an image named by its counts, the refusal a status. Probe ids: <id>/Body/Cards/Filters/Costs/<n> (all is -1; on a phone <id>/Filters/Chips/Row/Costs/<n>), …/Filters/Rarities/<rarity>, …/Filters/Kinds/<kind>, …/Filters/Search, …/Collection/Grid/Line#<n>/<key>, <id>/Body/Deck/List/<key>, <id>/Body/Deck/Done; on a phone <id>/Views/cards and <id>/Views/deck.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The collection, the deck's counts and the filters' state.

functions.name: cgGallery
functions.doc:
A visual novel's CG gallery (Steins;Gate, Clannad, Doki Doki Literature Club): a head with the title, the count of pictures seen ({n} / {total}) and the chapters as tabs (the tab actions step them); a grid of tiles at 16:9 in whole rows that scroll, each its picture with its title in its own row under it, a fresh one with a New mark, a locked one veiled dark with a lock and its hint in place of the picture and lockedLabel for its title, refused with a shake when pressed. The viewer is the picture over the whole surface (contain, on black), a bar at the foot fading in with its title, the version's pips (its variants), previous and next round buttons and Close; Left and Right step the pictures skipping the locked, Up and Down the versions, Back closes. On a phone in portrait the grid has two columns and the tabs are chips; the viewer keeps the picture at its width, its bar under it.
Parts: CgGallery.tab[selected], CgGallery.tile[locked][fresh], CgGallery.veil, CgGallery.viewer, CgGallery.bar, CgGallery.pip[selected]. Slots: each tile's picture (cg), the viewer's (cg). Sounds: tab on a tab, select on a tile, error on a refusal, back on close. Accessibility: the tabs a tablist, the grid a grid of buttons named by the title (or the locked word and the hint), the viewer a dialog named by the title, the pips a radio group. Probe ids: <id>/Head/Tabs/Row/<chapter>, <id>/Grid/Line#<n>/<key>, <id>/Viewer, <id>/Viewer/Bar/Prev, <id>/Viewer/Bar/Next, <id>/Viewer/Bar/Close, <id>/Viewer/Bar/Pips/<n>.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The chapters, the pictures and the viewer's state.

functions.name: routeChart
functions.doc:
A visual novel's route flowchart (Zero Escape, 428: Shibuya Scramble, Detroit: Become Human): the chapters' headings over their columns, each scene a card on its column and lane (its thumbnail, its title in its own row under it), seen cards lit, unseen ones quiet, locked ones veiled with a lock and lockedLabel, the current one ringed in the focus colour with its mark, an ending with its band; the branches as elbow lines between the cards, taken ones lit and the rest thin and dim, a choice's words on its line at the fork. The chart scrolls both ways, opening on the current scene. At the end the selected scene's detail: its thumbnail large, its title, its ending, and Jump here for a seen scene. A press on a locked card is refused with a shake. On a phone in portrait the detail stands under the chart.
Parts: RouteChart.heading, RouteChart.scene[seen][locked][current][ending], RouteChart.link[taken], RouteChart.choice, RouteChart.detail. Slots: each scene's thumbnail (cg), the detail's (cg). Sounds: select on a scene, error on a refusal, confirm on the jump. Accessibility: the chart a group of buttons named by the title (or the locked word), seen, current and the ending; the detail a region. Probe ids: <id>/Chart/Map/<scene>, <id>/Detail/Jump.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The scenes, the branches and the selection.

functions.name: settingsTree
functions.doc:
A game's settings as data (docs/ui.md Appendix B row 2, roadmap G1-7): the title, the pages as tabs (the tab actions step them), the shown page's entries as rows, each its name (a changed one marked) and its control at the end (a switch, a slider with its reading, a segmented control or a dropdown, og.ui.keyBindingRow for a binding by physical key code shown by the layout's label, a button, or the game's own control in a custom row), a heading where its section changes; whole rows scroll. At the end a detail panel with the hovered or focused entry's name and description. At the foot Defaults, Revert and Apply (Apply the primary, both quiet with nothing pending). After applying a display change the confirm dialog asks to keep it, its seconds counting down on a ring, Keep and Revert; at 0 it reverts. The HUD page mounts og.ui.hudLayoutEditor (the component, not a copy) while og.ui.hudEdit() is on, and Edit HUD to turn it on. On a phone in portrait the tabs are chips that scroll, the detail is the row's description under its name, and the foot's buttons span the width.
Parts: Settings.tab[selected], Settings.section, Settings.row[changed][disabled], Settings.detail, Settings.foot, Settings.confirm, Settings.ring. Sounds: tab on a tab, toggle on a switch, confirm on Apply and Keep, back on Revert. Accessibility: the tabs a tablist, each row a group named by its entry (and changed), the confirm an alertdialog whose countdown is a timer. Probe ids: <id>/Tabs/Row/<page>, <id>/Body/Page/Rows/<entry> (its control <entry>/Control), <id>/Foot/Apply, <id>/Foot/Revert, <id>/Foot/Defaults, <id>/Scrim/Confirm/Buttons/Keep, <id>/Scrim/Confirm/Buttons/Revert, <id>/Body/Page/Hud/Edit, <id>/Body/Page/Hud/Editor.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world (the bindings' action map and capture are world state).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The pages and entries, the pending state, the countdown.

params.name: custom
params.doc: Builds a custom entry's control by its key, inside its row; the game's own widgets, their results its own (a game with no custom entry passes a function that does nothing).

functions.name: props
functions.doc: Give the element built just before (any widget, or a container just closed) the element model's props: transform, opacity, z, placement, grid, variants, overlaps, motion, states, presence, gestures (docs/ui.md §6, §7). Call it right after the element.
functions.returnsDoc: False when no element was built before it.

functions.name: defineTimeline
functions.doc: Define a timeline by name: configuration, like the theme, defined once at start. Plays and state groups name it.

functions.name: play
functions.doc: Play a choreography on an element from the end of this tick: its timelines' keys drive the elements' props and its events fire as it passes them (og.ui.motionEvents). Returns the play's id (0: no element, or a choreo of no known kind).

params.name: path
params.doc: The element's full path; empty is the element built just before.

functions.name: playTimeline
functions.doc: Play one timeline (by name) on an element: og.ui.play with a single step.

params.name: path
params.doc: The element's full path; empty is the element built just before.

functions.name: seek
functions.doc: Move a play to a time; it fires no events on the way. Returns false for an unknown play.

functions.name: pause
functions.doc: Hold a play where it is.

functions.name: resume
functions.doc: Let a held play go on.

functions.name: reverse
functions.doc: Turn a play round where it is: an interrupted opening closes from where it got to.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Stop a play: its elements go back to their own values (on their motion, if they have one).

functions.name: playInfo
functions.doc: Where a play is; null once it is gone.

functions.name: forceState
functions.doc: Force a state group of an element (the probe and agents render and check each state this way); null lets it go.

functions.name: openPath
functions.doc: The full path of the innermost open container (an open row, panel, anchor or world anchor), as bounds, visualState, forceState, playTimeline and the probe name it; empty at the top level. A component reads its root's path right after opening it, to name its parts in those calls.

functions.name: visualState
functions.doc: The state a group of an element is in (last tick); empty for none.

functions.name: animate
functions.doc: Any number on a spring or an ease (docs/ui.md §7.1: every value is animatable): call it every tick with the target and it answers this tick's value. A retarget keeps its value and velocity; under reduced motion it jumps.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id under the open element.

functions.name: gesture
functions.doc: What the drag or pinch on an element is doing.

functions.name: motionEvents
functions.doc: The UI's motion events of the last frame: sounds, haptics, bursts, state changes, callbacks, ends, dismissals, drops and snaps.

functions.name: overlaps
functions.doc: The last frame's undeclared overlaps between elements (docs/ui.md §6.2), with both paths.

functions.name: layoutStats
functions.doc: What the last frame built, rebuilt, laid out and kept.

functions.name: notifications
functions.doc:
A notification stack (toasts, achievements, rewards, invites): cards anchored in the safe area, newest nearest the anchor's edge, that enter on the style's enter spring from that edge, reflow on its panel spring as others leave (layout animation), and leave sliding out. A card's lifetime drains along its bottom edge; the pointer resting on it holds the time; a press dismisses it, and a swipe toward the edge throws it off. More than max wait in a queue whose time does not run.
Parts: Notification.card[<variant>][<tone>] (the card, partClass hud), Notification.accent (the start edge in the tone), Notification.well[rarity=<tier>] (the icon or art slot), Notification.title, Notification.body, Notification.count (the ×3 chip), Notification.progress and Notification.progressFill, Notification.life (the draining time line), Notification.action. Slots: each item's image (art kind item, achievement or avatar, 1:1).
States: on each card, group life (entering, shown, leaving) and group tone (the item's tone). Motion: enter and exit springs, layout motion for the reflow, an achievement's well pops (emphasis spring). Sounds: notification, reward (achievement, reward) or warning (alert) when a card first shows. Accessibility: each card is a status (an alert: an alert) named by its eyebrow, title and body; its action a button. Probe ids: <id>/<key>, its Title, Body, Count, Action, Life.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The items and where they stack.

functions.name: countBadge
functions.doc:
A count badge: a small pill on a corner of the open container, outset by half its height so it straddles the edge, with a ring in the ground colour that cuts it from what it sits on. A count over max reads max+; a rise pops it (emphasis spring) and plays notification once. Hidden at 0.
Parts: CountBadge.base[<kind>][<tone>], CountBadge.text. States: group count (none, some, overflow). Accessibility: status named by name or the count. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Text. Call it inside the container it decorates, after its content; the container should not clip.

functions.name: tooltipCard
functions.doc:
A rich tooltip: a card in the tooltip layer beside its trigger, flipped and clamped inside the safe area, with a title in its rarity's colour and pips, an art slot, rich-text body whose keyword links open nested cards (to any depth, each pinnable, as in Crusader Kings III and Baldur's Gate 3), stat rows, a comparison card of what is equipped with up and down deltas (Diablo IV), a footer and action hints. It fades and rises in on the style's enter spring after delayMs; a pinnable card fills a ring at its corner and locks; a locked card stays while the pointer is on it or on a card it opened.
Parts: TooltipCard.card[<rarity>][pinned], TooltipCard.header, TooltipCard.title, TooltipCard.subtitle, TooltipCard.well, TooltipCard.body, TooltipCard.stat, TooltipCard.delta[up|down], TooltipCard.compare (the second card), TooltipCard.footer, TooltipCard.hint, TooltipCard.pin (the ring). Slots: image (art kind item or ability, 1:1). States: group pin (resting, pinning, pinned); group cover (clear, hidden: a banner or level-up is announcing, and the card fades fully out and takes no input until it has gone). Sounds: open when it pins. Accessibility: tooltip named by the title, described by the body; its links are links. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Title, <id>/Body (its links <id>/Body/<key>), <id>/Stat#i, <id>/Compare, <id>/Pin, a nested card <id>/<key>.

params.name: desc
params.doc: When it shows, what it says and where.

functions.name: progressBar
functions.doc:
A progress bar: a rounded track, a fill that moves to its value on the style's ui spring (never jumping back on a retarget), a buffer ahead of it, a sweeping sheen while it works, segments for steps, a sweeping band when indeterminate, and a caption and value over it. Reaching 1 flashes the fill once and plays success.
Parts: ProgressBar.track[<style>], ProgressBar.buffer, ProgressBar.fill[<tone>][done], ProgressBar.step[filled], ProgressBar.label, ProgressBar.value. States: group progress (working, done) and group mode (determinate, indeterminate). Accessibility: progressbar named by the label, 0 to 100 (busy when indeterminate). Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Track, <id>/Fill, <id>/Label, <id>/Value.

functions.name: progressRing
functions.doc:
A progress ring: an arc filled clockwise from the top on the style's ui spring, or a spinning arc that grows and shrinks as it turns (Material's indeterminate ring, which reads as working at any size); a label in the middle. Under reduced motion the spinner pulses its opacity instead of turning.
Parts: ProgressRing.track, ProgressRing.fill[<tone>][spinning], ProgressRing.label. States: group mode (determinate, indeterminate). Accessibility: progressbar (busy when spinning). Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Fill, <id>/Label.

functions.name: skeletonGroup
functions.doc:
A skeleton: shapes of the neutral fill where content will arrive, swept by one sheen across the whole group (not each piece on its own clock), cornered as the parts they stand for. The sheen stops under reduced motion and the shapes breathe their opacity instead.
Parts: Skeleton.piece[<shape>], Skeleton.sheen. Accessibility: one progressbar, busy, named by name. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Piece#i.

functions.name: formatNumber
functions.doc: A number written in a notation: grouped, compact, idle letters, scientific or engineering, with a sign, prefix and suffix and the locale's separators, and past 1e308 through its exponent. Deterministic: the same text on every host.

functions.name: numberCounter
functions.doc:
A number display for scores, currency and resources: written in its notation (idle letters past trillions, numbers past 1e308), counting to a new value on an ease-out, its digits rolling like an odometer, a +n delta flying off on a rise, a pop when it lands (emphasis spring) and a flash of danger on a fall; on the HUD chip with its outline when anchored. Returns the number shown this tick.
Parts: NumberCounter.frame[hud], NumberCounter.value, NumberCounter.digit, NumberCounter.icon, NumberCounter.label, NumberCounter.delta[up|down]. States: group change (still, rising, falling). Sounds: counterTick while counting, if ticks. Accessibility: text named by the label, value the final number written out (not each frame of the count). Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Value (its text is the whole number shown), <id>/Label, <id>/Delta.

functions.name: banner
functions.doc:
A full-width announcement: a wave or round band that slams in with a squash and a shake, a title card that fades up over a rule that draws out from its centre, a victory band with a burst and confetti, a defeat band, a warning with sweeping danger stripes. Its letters track in as it enters; it holds, then leaves on the style's exit ease. The tick-driven timing makes it the same in a replay.
Parts: Banner.band[<kind>], Banner.rule, Banner.eyebrow, Banner.title, Banner.subtitle, Banner.stripes, Banner.art. Slots: image (art kind banner). States: group phase (entering, holding, leaving, gone). Sounds: by kind on entering. Accessibility: alert (warning, defeat) or status, named by eyebrow, title and subtitle. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Title, <id>/Eyebrow, <id>/Subtitle.

functions.name: ribbon
functions.doc:
A ribbon: a diagonal band wrapping a corner of the open container with its folded tail, a notched banner across its top or bottom, or a stamp slapped across its middle (a New best!: it lands from large and turned, squashes, settles and puffs dust, emphasis spring). The open container should clip its corners for a corner ribbon.
Parts: Ribbon.band[<corner>][<tone>], Ribbon.fold, Ribbon.text. States: group slap (waiting, landing, settled). Sounds: confirm when it lands. Accessibility: status named by the text. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Text.

functions.name: celebration
functions.doc:
A celebration: confetti over the whole screen, a burst from the container it is built in, a level-up flourish centred on the screen, or fireworks. Particles are the UI's own (seeded, so a replay throws the same), drawn over the HUD and under dialogs; under reduced motion only the level-up's text and a soft glow show. Plays reward (levelUp, fireworks) or success (confetti, burst) when it fires.
Parts: Celebration.ring, Celebration.rays, Celebration.title, Celebration.value (level up). States: group play (idle, playing). Accessibility: a level up is a status named by its title and value. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Title, <id>/Value.

functions.name: starRating
functions.doc:
Stars earned: empty sockets, each earned star landing in turn from large with a turn and an overshoot (emphasis spring), a burst of sparks as it lands and a pitch rising star by star; the middle star of three sits higher and larger. Under reduced motion they fade in.
Parts: StarRating.socket, StarRating.star[earned]. States: on each star, group star (empty, landing, earned). Sounds: reward, pitched up a step per star. Accessibility: image named by name. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Star#i.

functions.name: subtitles
functions.doc:
Subtitles and captions to the Xbox Accessibility Guidelines' 104: centred at the bottom of the safe area, at most two lines of at most about 42 characters each across 70 % of the width (the box wraps by words, never by letters), in the player's size (never under 18 px at 1080p), on a box of the player's opacity (an outline when it is clear), with the speaker's name in their colour, sound captions in brackets above speech, an arrow toward a speaker off screen, new lines fading in quickly (never sliding: text that moves is harder to read).
Parts: Subtitles.box, Subtitles.line, Subtitles.speaker, Subtitles.text, Subtitles.caption, Subtitles.arrow. Accessibility: a log whose new lines are read, each line text named speaker: text. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/<key>, its Speaker, Text, Arrow.

functions.name: statBar
functions.doc:
A health or resource bar to the bar of action games: blocks (segment), a ghost chunk that holds after a hit and then drains (Dark Souls, fighting games), a heal preview, an absorb overlay (World of Warcraft's white-blue), grey recoverable damage, the value inside its end or after it, a row of shield cells in their tier's colour over it (Apex Legends), low and critical states (warn, then danger pulsing), a mirrored fill for the right player, flat, slanted or pill ends, or discrete pips with a gap (style pips: n of max lit, the value after them). A drop is instant, a rise moves on the ui spring.
Parts: StatBar.frame[<style>][<level>], StatBar.track, StatBar.fill[<kind>][<level>], StatBar.ghost, StatBar.heal, StatBar.absorb[over], StatBar.recoverable, StatBar.block[filled], StatBar.cell[filled][<tier>], StatBar.track[pips], StatBar.pip[filled], StatBar.label, StatBar.value, StatBar.icon. States: group level (normal, low, critical, empty). Sounds: warning on crossing into critical. Accessibility: meter named by name, valueNow the value, valueMax max. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Track, <id>/Track/Fill, <id>/Track/Ghost, <id>/Track/Block#i, <id>/Shield/Cell#i, <id>/Main/Pips/Pip#i (style pips), <id>/Main/Icon, <id>/Value (inside: <id>/Main/Track/Value/Text, outlined over a soft dark band that fades at both ends, with no absorb seam under it).

functions.name: orbMeter
functions.doc:
An orb (Diablo's health and mana globes): a glass sphere filled from the bottom with a liquid whose surface sways, a highlight on the glass, a frame ring, the value in the middle; the level moves on the ui spring and a drop flashes it. Critical (under 15 %) pulses.
Parts: OrbMeter.frame, OrbMeter.glass, OrbMeter.liquid[<kind>], OrbMeter.surface, OrbMeter.value, OrbMeter.label. States: group level (normal, low, critical). Accessibility: meter. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Orb/Liquid, <id>/Value.

functions.name: radialMeter
functions.doc:
A radial stamina wheel (Breath of the Wild, Elden Ring's spirit gauge): a ring that drains clockwise, outer rings for extra wheels, warn under a third, red and pulsing when exhausted until it refills, fading out once full.
Parts: RadialMeter.track, RadialMeter.fill[normal|low|exhausted], RadialMeter.wheel#i. States: group level (full, normal, low, exhausted). Accessibility: meter. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Wheel#i.

functions.name: abilitySlot
functions.doc:
An ability slot as shipped action bars draw it (Diablo IV, League, Destiny 2, Genshin): the art fills the frame edge to edge and stays the dominant element in every state; one centred numeral per state, the cooldown's seconds (tenths under ten, outlined) over a clockwise darkening of about 60 % (as seen) on the part to come, the part done clean, with a bright leading edge; a flash and a pop the tick it comes ready; charges in a small corner badge (none when the seconds show) with the next one's recharge along the bottom; the cost a small figure on a dark pill while ready; unaffordable, out-of-range, disabled (a red slash) and locked (a lock over dark art) treatments of the art; a soft glow and thin accent edge while active; an ultimate 1.15 times the others with a gold ring filling clockwise and a small percent; a frame of the style's corner with a top-lit rim, an inner shadow and a float shadow; rank pips right under it and the hotkey a quiet label in one neutral ink just below. A press answers on touch and with the pointer.
Parts: AbilitySlot.frame[ready|cooling|disabled|locked|active], AbilitySlot.icon, AbilitySlot.tint[locked|disabled|unaffordable|outOfRange], AbilitySlot.ultimate, AbilitySlot.sweep, AbilitySlot.flash, AbilitySlot.lock, AbilitySlot.slash, AbilitySlot.cost[unaffordable], AbilitySlot.recharge, AbilitySlot.charges, AbilitySlot.edge[active|ultimate], AbilitySlot.pip[filled], AbilitySlot.hotkey. Slots: image (art kind ability). States: group ready (ready, cooling, disabled, locked), group use (idle, active, unaffordable). Sounds: focus (the style's ready chime) the tick it comes ready. Accessibility: button named by name, value its seconds left, Unavailable, Locked or Ready. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Slot/Time, <id>/Slot/Ultimate/Value, <id>/Slot/Cost/Value, <id>/Slot/ChargeBadge/Charges, <id>/Hotkey.

functions.name: abilityBar
functions.doc:
An ability bar: abilitySlot for each slot, in a row (or a column) straight on the scene (a style may dress AbilityBar.frame as a slim bar), evenly spaced; a row with more slots than the HUD band holds wraps into even rows whose columns line up (eight slots on a phone are two rows of four).
Parts: AbilityBar.frame and each slot's. Accessibility: a group named by its slots. Probe ids: <id>/<key>.

functions.name: statusGrid
functions.doc:
Buffs and debuffs to the bar of MMOs: icons in rows, a sweep darkening each as it runs out, the time left under it (12m, 45, 4.2), blinking in its last five seconds, stacks at its corner, debuffs in their own row bordered by their type's colour and notched so their kind is not told by colour alone, more than max folding into a +n tile; the columns as wide as the row's widest timer, so the tiles stay evenly spaced and each time overhangs its tile centred (WoW's auras).
Parts: StatusGrid.tile[buff|debuff][type=<type>][expiring], StatusGrid.icon, StatusGrid.sweep, StatusGrid.time, StatusGrid.stacks, StatusGrid.more. States: on each tile, group time (lasting, running, expiring). Accessibility: list named Buffs and Debuffs; each tile an image named name, stacks and seconds. Probe ids: <id>/Buffs/<key>, <id>/Debuffs/<key>, their Time and Stacks, <id>/Buffs/More/Tile/Count.

functions.name: minimapView
functions.doc:
A minimap to the bar of MOBAs, shooters and open worlds: the map in a round or square frame, centred on the player and zoomed, fixed with north up and the player's arrow turning or turning with the player; markers for allies (their arrows), enemies, loot by rarity, points of interest, objectives and pings, which stay on the frame's edge pointing out when out of range; pings pulse; a north mark on the rim, the zone under it; a press answers clicked (click to move reads the press's position against the map's bounds).
Parts: Minimap.bezel (a dark rounded bezel with a soft drop), Minimap.frame[<shape>] (the map's glass inside it), Minimap.map, Minimap.pitch, Minimap.track, Minimap.start, Minimap.sector, Minimap.marker[<kind>][clamped], Minimap.ring, Minimap.north (straddling the bezel's top edge, over nothing on the map), Minimap.plate (a square map's caption plate at the bezel's foot; a round map's caption is the same plate as a pill centred under the ring), Minimap.ping. Slots: texture (art kind map). Accessibility: image named by the zone; markers images named by their labels. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Bezel/Map/<key>, <id>/Bezel/Plate/Zone (square) or <id>/ZonePlate/Zone (round).

functions.name: compass
functions.doc:
A compass strip to the bar of Skyrim and Apex: degree ticks every 15° and the bearing under a centre notch, the cardinal and intercardinal letters, points of interest at their bearings with their distance under them, objectives (a diamond, a waypoint's mark) and pings held at the strip's ends pointing round when behind; the ends fade.
Parts: Compass.strip, Compass.tick[major], Compass.point[cardinal], Compass.notch, Compass.bearing, Compass.poi[<kind>][clamped], Compass.distance. Accessibility: status named the heading in degrees and its point. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Bearing, <id>/Strip/<key>.

functions.name: objectiveTracker
functions.doc:
An objective tracker to the bar of open worlds and MMOs: each objective's title by its icon with its distance and a countdown, its steps as boxes that tick with a pop when done (dimmed after), counts that pop as they rise, progress bars, optional steps muted, failed steps crossed in danger, the focused one marked, a completed one flashing Complete and leaving; over a soft scrim so it reads over any scene.
Parts: ObjectiveTracker.quest[focused][complete], ObjectiveTracker.title, ObjectiveTracker.step[done|failed|optional], ObjectiveTracker.check[done], ObjectiveTracker.count, ObjectiveTracker.progress, ObjectiveTracker.timer, ObjectiveTracker.distance. States: on each step, group step (open, done, failed). Sounds: success when a step is done, reward when a quest completes. Accessibility: list named Objectives; each quest a group named its title; each step a list item, its value done or failed and its count (the tracker takes no taps). Probe ids: <id>/<key>, <id>/<key>/<step>.

functions.name: hudTimer
functions.doc:
A timer to the bar of fighting and battle royale HUDs: the time in tabular digits on the HUD chip, a ring for a countdown's share left, warn and then danger with a pulse and a tick sound each second of the last ones, tenths in the last ten seconds, dimmed and blinking while paused.
Parts: HudTimer.frame[normal|warn|critical|paused], HudTimer.ring, HudTimer.time, HudTimer.label. States: group time (normal, warn, critical, paused, done). Sounds: counterTick each of the last seconds, pitched up. Accessibility: timer named label, value the time. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Time, <id>/Label.

functions.name: comboCounter
functions.doc:
A combo counter to the bar of character action and rhythm games (Devil May Cry, Hi-Fi Rush, osu!): the count in a big display face that pops with each hit, scaling a little as it climbs, a multiplier chip, a decay bar draining to the next hit, a burst and a bigger pop at milestones, and a shake and fall when it breaks.
Parts: Combo.count, Combo.label, Combo.multiplier, Combo.decay, Combo.burst. States: group combo (idle, live, milestone, broken). Sounds: reward at a milestone. Accessibility: status named the count and label. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Count, <id>/Multiplier, <id>/Decay.

functions.name: judgement
functions.doc:
Judgement pops to the bar of rhythm games (Project Sekai, osu!, Beat Saber): the word pops from large on its tier's colour (gold with a gradient for the best), with Early or Late and the milliseconds under it, rises a little and fades; a miss drops and greys.
Parts: Judgement.word[tier=<n>], Judgement.timing[early|late]. States: group judge (none, best, good, miss). Accessibility: status named the word. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Word, <id>/Timing.

functions.name: scorebug
functions.doc:
A broadcast scorebug to the bar of sports games (EA FC, NBA 2K, Rocket League): each side's colour block with its crest and short name, the scores in tabular digits that flip and flash when they change, possession and time-out pips, the clock and period, a shot clock, added time beside the clock, a final chip (FT) in its place once the match is over, a situation line sliding out under it.
Parts: Scorebug.frame, Scorebug.team[home|away], Scorebug.score, Scorebug.clock, Scorebug.period, Scorebug.shot, Scorebug.added, Scorebug.final, Scorebug.situation, Scorebug.timeout[used], Scorebug.possession. Sounds: success when a score changes. Accessibility: status named home score, away score, clock and period. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Home/Score, <id>/Away/Score, <id>/Clock.

functions.name: matchStats
functions.doc:
Two sides' stats face to face, to the bar of EA FC's and NBA 2K's match facts: each row's values at the two ends in tabular figures, its name centred over one two-colour bar (EA FC's split): the home side's team colour from the start to its share and the away side's from the end, a 2 px gap where they meet, on every row whichever side leads; a tick at its middle marking even; the leading side's numeral in its colour, lightened (a stat where more is worse tints neither). Anchored, it is the HUD's possession plate: the crests at the ends of its one row on the HUD chip.
Parts: MatchStats.frame, MatchStats.header, MatchStats.row[worse], MatchStats.bar, MatchStats.fill[home|away], MatchStats.centre. Accessibility: table named title; each row text named its label with both values. Probe ids: <id>/<key>, its Home and Away; <id>/<key>/Mid/Label; <id>/<key>/Mid/Bar/Home and Mid/Bar/Away (their widths are the shares).

functions.name: goalTimeline
functions.doc:
The scorers of a match by side, as a full-time board lists them: the home side's names, minutes and marks set against a centre rule, the away side's mirrored after it, each side in match order, the minutes in tabular figures beside their marks so the two columns meet at the rule.
Parts: GoalTimeline.frame, GoalTimeline.side[home|away], GoalTimeline.event, GoalTimeline.mark, GoalTimeline.rule. Accessibility: list named Scorers; each event text named its name, minute and side. Probe ids: <id>/Home/<key> and <id>/Away/<key>, their Name and Minute.

functions.name: playerPlate
functions.doc:
The controlled player's plate to the bar of EA FC: the side's crest, the shirt number in a box, the name, and a segmented stamina bar under it in the side's colour that turns to the warning hue when low.
Parts: PlayerPlate.frame, PlayerPlate.crest, PlayerPlate.number, PlayerPlate.stamina[low], PlayerPlate.segment[spent]. States: group stamina (fresh, low). Accessibility: status named the number and name with the stamina's percent. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Body/Number/Text, <id>/Body/Info/Name, <id>/Body/Info/Stamina.

functions.name: substitution
functions.doc:
A substitution's lower third, as a broadcast shows it: a caption tab over one plate, the player going off at the start (portrait, a down mark in the danger hue, number and name, Out) and the one coming on at the end (an up mark in the success hue, In), a hairline between; it rises in when it appears.
Parts: Substitution.frame, Substitution.caption, Substitution.player[off|on], Substitution.portrait, Substitution.mark[off|on], Substitution.rule. Accessibility: status named the caption, off and on. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Plate/Off/Who/Line/Name, <id>/Plate/On/Who/Line/Name.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Who goes off and who comes on.

functions.name: laneKeys
functions.doc:
A rhythm game's lane keys under its hit line, to the bar of osu!mania and DJMAX: a keycap per lane at the lane's x with its letter or the action's glyph on the device used last, the lane's colour on its edge, pressed down and lit while held, flashing on a hit.
Parts: LaneKeys.cap[pressed][hit], LaneKeys.glyph. Accessibility: group named Lanes; each cap text named its letter, pressed when held. Probe ids: <id>/<key>, its Glyph.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The lanes and what is held.

functions.name: flightHud
functions.doc:
A flight HUD to the bar of Ace Combat and DCS: a pitch ladder of few rungs (every 10°, broken below the horizon, numbered in a face that reads at a glance) turning with roll about the boresight in a central window, the horizon line, the waterline and the flight path marker heaviest as the focal pair, a heading tape across the top (numbers every 30°, the cardinals by letter) fading at its ends, quiet speed and altitude tapes with large boxed readouts on either side and the climb rate, all in one ink from the style (its primary, lifted) with a dark outline. A narrow screen drops the ladder's left numbers.
Parts: FlightHud.ladder, FlightHud.rung[up|down|horizon], FlightHud.waterline, FlightHud.path, FlightHud.heading, FlightHud.speed, FlightHud.altitude, FlightHud.box. Accessibility: group named Flight, its value the pitch, heading, speed and altitude; the speed, altitude and heading boxes text. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/SpeedBox, <id>/AltitudeBox, <id>/HeadingBox (each a text whose value is the reading).

functions.name: nameplate
functions.doc:
A nameplate to the bar of World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV: the name in its reaction's colour with a level badge and an icon, a title under it, a slim health bar with its absorb and a cast bar under that, an elite or boss frame, the target larger and outlined and kept on top; crowds stack instead of overlapping, it fades behind walls and sheds detail with distance (title, then name).
Parts: Nameplate.frame[<reaction>][targeted][<class>], Nameplate.name, Nameplate.title, Nameplate.level, Nameplate.bar, Nameplate.fill[<reaction>], Nameplate.shield, Nameplate.cast. States: group lod (full, compact, bar), group selection (none, targeted). Accessibility: text named name, value level and health. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Name, <id>/Bar/Fill, <id>/Cast.

functions.name: overheadBars
functions.doc:
Overhead bars to the bar of RTS and MOBA crowds (StarCraft II, League of Legends): one mass element per unit, thousands a frame, each a dark track with its fill in its reaction's colour and a pale ghost that holds after a hit then drains, scaled by distance and faded behind the scene.
Parts: none per bar (mass elements); the template is named <id>. Accessibility: none (the units' frames carry it). Probe: og.ui.massCount.

functions.name: damageNumbers
functions.doc:
Damage numbers to the bar of Diablo IV, Genshin Impact and World of Warcraft: each hit thrown from where it landed, rising and drifting to its side as it fades, outlined so it reads on any scene; a critical larger in gold, popping past its size and settling; heals in green with a +; damage over time smaller; misses as their word in grey; the player's own damage in danger; numbers compact past ten thousand. Mass elements: thousands at once, in the snapshot.
Parts: none per number (mass elements); the templates are named <id>.number and <id>.word. Accessibility: none (combat text is decoration; the game announces what matters). Probe: og.ui.massCount.

functions.name: interactionPrompt
functions.doc:
An interaction prompt to the bar of The Last of Us, Elden Ring and Genshin Impact: the action's glyph for the device used last (a key cap, a pad's face button) and the verb, the thing's name over it, a ring filling round the glyph for a hold and a pop when it completes, dimmed with its reason when it cannot be used; it springs in when it appears and stays upright and readable at any distance it shows.
Parts: InteractionPrompt.frame[disabled], InteractionPrompt.glyph, InteractionPrompt.hold, InteractionPrompt.verb, InteractionPrompt.name, InteractionPrompt.reason. States: group use (ready, holding, disabled). Accessibility: button named the verb and name, value the glyph's text. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Glyph, <id>/Verb.

functions.name: waypoint
functions.doc:
A waypoint or ping to the bar of Apex Legends and Destiny: a diamond with its kind's icon in its colour, the distance under it, a label and who pinged it; off screen or behind it stays on the safe area's edge with an arrow toward its point; a ping drops in with rings rippling from it and leaves after its time; it shrinks a little far away and dims when the crosshair is not near.
Parts: Waypoint.marker[<kind>][clamped], Waypoint.icon, Waypoint.distance, Waypoint.label, Waypoint.ripple. States: group place (onScreen, clamped). Sounds: notify when a ping lands. Accessibility: image named the label, value the distance. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Marker, <id>/Distance, <id>/Label.

functions.name: selectionRing
functions.doc:
A selection ring to the bar of StarCraft II and Baldur's Gate 3: an ellipse on the ground under the unit (the ground circle projected, lying on the terrain or colliders under it with desc.ground), a bright edge and a soft inner glow in its reaction's colour, springing in from larger when selected, thin and dim on hover, or broken into arcs turning slowly.
Parts: SelectionRing.ring[<reaction>][hover], SelectionRing.glow. Accessibility: none (the unit's frame is selected). Probe ids: <id>, its shapes <id>/Box/Ring (or Arc#i) and Glow, each bounded by its points.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world: its og.Camera projects the ground, so the calling system declares og.Camera among its reads.

functions.name: telegraph
functions.doc:
An attack telegraph to the bar of Final Fantasy XIV and WildStar: the area on the ground (disc, ring, cone or line; with desc.ground over slopes and hills, every vertex on the surface) tinted in danger with a bright edge, a fill growing from its origin to the edge as the wind-up runs so the moment of impact reads without a number, and a flash as it lands.
Parts: Telegraph.area[<shape>][hostile|friendly], Telegraph.edge, Telegraph.fill, Telegraph.flash. States: group windup (charging, impact). Accessibility: none (the game announces what is dangerous). Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Box/Area, Fill, Edge#i.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world: its og.Camera projects the ground, so the calling system declares og.Camera among its reads.

functions.name: pathLine
functions.doc:
A path line to the bar of Baldur's Gate 3, XCOM 2 and RTS move orders: the route on the ground (draped on the surface with desc.ground) as a line with chevrons marching toward its end, the part past this turn's reach in danger, an arrow head or a destination ring at its end with a label (the distance, the cost), a cross when it cannot be taken.
Parts: PathLine.line[reach|beyond][invalid], PathLine.chevron, PathLine.end, PathLine.label. Accessibility: text named the label. Probe ids: <id>, <id>Label (the label, a tag of its own: it declutters with the other tags and stays in the safe area).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world: its og.Camera projects the ground, so the calling system declares og.Camera among its reads.

functions.name: placementGhost
functions.doc:
A placement ghost to the bar of Age of Empires IV, Anno and Cities: Skylines: the footprint on the ground (draped on the surface with desc.ground) in success or danger (hatched when invalid, so it is not told by colour alone), its grid cells, a range ring for a tower's reach, and its cost or the reason it cannot go there; it breathes while held.
Parts: PlacementGhost.footprint[valid|invalid], PlacementGhost.cells, PlacementGhost.range, PlacementGhost.label. States: group place (valid, invalid). Accessibility: status named the label. Probe ids: <id>, <id>Label (the label, a tag of its own: it declutters with the other tags and stays in the safe area).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world: its og.Camera projects the ground, so the calling system declares og.Camera among its reads.

functions.name: lootLabel
functions.doc:
A loot label to the bar of Diablo IV, Path of Exile and Borderlands: the name on a dark chip edged in its rarity's colour with pips so tiers do not rest on colour alone, the stack's count, a beam of light rising over rare and better items, labels stacking instead of overlapping (higher rarity on top), pressable to pick up.
Parts: LootLabel.chip[rarity=<r>], LootLabel.name, LootLabel.pip, LootLabel.count, LootLabel.beam. Accessibility: button named the name, value its rarity. Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Chip/Name.

functions.name: speechBubble
functions.doc:
A speech bubble to the bar of Animal Crossing, Sea of Thieves and The Sims: a rounded bubble over the speaker with a tail pointing down to them, the speaker's name, the text typing out with a soft tick of sound, popping in and fading out after a time that grows with its length; a shout jagged and bold, a thought round with its tail as bubbles; it can hold on the edge when the speaker is off screen.
Parts: SpeechBubble.bubble[shout|thought], SpeechBubble.tail, SpeechBubble.speaker, SpeechBubble.text. States: group speech (typing, shown, leaving). Sounds: counterTick as it types. Accessibility: text named the speaker, value the whole text (a screen reader hears it at once). Probe ids: <id>, <id>/Bubble/Text, <id>/Bubble/Speaker.

functions.name: semantics
functions.doc: Give the element built just before (a container just closed, or a widget) a role, a name, a value and states for the accessibility tree and the probe's dump (dump_ui's role, name, value, states). Components built from containers call it so a screen reader meets a menu, a tree or a table, not rows of buttons. Answers false, with a frame warning, when no element was built before it or the role is unknown.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its role, name, value and states.

functions.name: partAttr
functions.doc: Gives the element open now (a grid's cell, a panel, a card) a selector attribute its style dresses by: partAttr("rarity", "epic") in a bag's cell makes it `Slot.frame[rarity=epic]`, so a style that dresses the tier recolours the cell's own frame (one stroke, never a second). Call it right after the element opens, inside it.
functions.returnsDoc: Whether the style dresses this part by the attribute (for any of its values, `Slot.frame[rarity=rare]` answers for every tier): false, its values draw alike, and a caller that wants a mark draws its own.

functions.name: setDraw
functions.doc: Draws the element added last (a container just opened, or the last control) with desc: shapes beyond rectangles, layered gradient, image and vector fills, strokes with their own paints, shadows, glows, glass, clipping to its shape, masks, blend modes and materials (docs/ui.md §5). Call it right after the element's open or control; immediate mode, so every tick it is drawn.

functions.name: openWorldAnchor
functions.doc: Open an element anchored in the world, closed by close(): its children are an ordinary subtree (labels, bars, icons, buttons) laid out at its own size, then projected, scaled, depth tested, decluttered and clamped as desc says. Drawn under the screen's own elements. og.ui.setDraw after it draws its box. For thousands of tags of one kind (overhead bars on an army) use mass elements instead.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id; the probe path is the id alone.

params.name: desc
params.doc: What it sits on and how it follows the camera.

functions.name: openWorldPanel
functions.doc: Open a world panel, closed by close(): its children are an ordinary UI (buttons, lists, fields) laid out at width by height and drawn into desc.target; a press on its quad reaches its controls. One render target per panel.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id; the probe path is the id alone.

functions.name: defineMass
functions.doc: Declare a mass element template by name and answer its handle; declaring the name again replaces it and keeps the handle.

params.name: desc
params.doc: What it draws and how it moves.

functions.name: spawnMass
functions.doc: Start instances of a template on this tick: each plays its template's timeline over its lifetime and leaves after it (damage numbers, pickups). They live in the UI's state, so a snapshot or a replay carries them.

functions.name: pushMass
functions.doc: Show instances of a template for this tick only (overhead bars, nameplates, status icons rebuilt every tick with their values).

functions.name: massCount
functions.doc: The live spawned instances of a template.

functions.name: particles
functions.doc: Emit particles from the element built just before (a control, or a container just opened). Call every tick it emits; a burst throws on the ticks desc.fire is set. og.ui.burst is a preset of it.

functions.name: meta
functions.doc: A meta layer this tick: a damage vignette, a low-health pulse, a material over the whole frame.

functions.name: sceneViewport
functions.doc: A viewport: a camera's render target shown in the layout, its drag, wheel and pointer ray handed back so a menu can orbit, pick and rotate.

params.name: desc
params.doc: What it shows and its camera.

functions.name: screen
functions.doc: Mount a screen document (`type screen`, loaded with og.load.document) as a layer of the stack, pushed when it is not on it, with its viewmodel for this tick, and build it here: code fills its slots after this call (og.ui.openSlot). Its bindings read the viewmodel every tick, a Capitalised root (`Wallet.gold`) the resource as of the last tick; two-way controls write into it (each write is a `set` event). Layers code does not mount are built at the frame's end with the viewmodel they have.

params.name: vm
params.doc: Its viewmodel: an object (null keeps the one it has).

functions.name: component
functions.doc: Mount a component document (`type component`) here, inside whatever is open: its props are its viewmodel, its two-way writes come back in the answer's props.

functions.name: openSlot
functions.doc: Open a document's slot (a `slot` element built this tick) so code fills it; its children follow until og.ui.close. False when no such slot was built this tick.

functions.name: push
functions.doc: Push a screen onto the layer stack (docs/ui.md §8.1); the layer under it remembers its focus. Callable anywhere (systems, commands, start); the stack is world state, so snapshots carry it.

params.name: vm
params.doc: Its viewmodel (null: its document's first fixture, else an empty object).

functions.returnsDoc: The layer's serial. Refused for a name no screen document has.

functions.name: pop
functions.doc: Pop the top layer; the one under it takes its remembered focus. Answers the popped screen's name (empty: the stack was empty).

functions.name: replace
functions.doc: Replace the top layer with a screen.
functions.returnsDoc: The new layer's serial.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Empty the layer stack.

functions.name: layers
functions.doc: The layer stack, bottom first.

functions.name: screenVm
functions.doc: A layer's viewmodel as its two-way bindings left it (the top layer of that screen); null when it is not on the stack.

functions.name: docEvents
functions.doc: Take the events of documents built where code did not see them (layers built at the frame's end); og.ui.screen answers its own.

functions.name: gameInput
functions.doc: Gameplay takes input this tick: no layer whose input is `menu` is on the stack. Input goes to the top layer that takes it, once per tick.

functions.name: paused
functions.doc: A layer that pauses the game (`pause`) is on the stack: the engine holds the time scale at 0 while one is, and gives back the one it had.

functions.name: defineAction
functions.doc: Define (or redefine) a UI action. confirm (Enter, Space, A), back (Escape, B), tabNext (E, ], RB), tabPrev (Q, [, LB), details (X, Y) and rotate (R, X) are defined by default.

functions.name: action
functions.doc: The action fired this tick (a document's `on action` fires on the top layer that takes input).

functions.name: actionHeld
functions.doc: A hold action is held past its hold, or its toggle is on.

functions.name: glyph
functions.doc: An action's glyph on the device used last: its first binding there. Null for an unknown action or one with no binding on that device.

functions.name: frameGlyph
functions.doc: An action's glyph on the device used last, as og.ui.glyph answers it, without the world: for a component that shows a prompt (a tab row's bumpers, the action bar) and only builds UI. It follows the device live (keyboard, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, a generic pad, touch) and the player's rebinding. A name that is no UI action answers as og.input.glyph does for the world whose frame is being built (a gameplay action an ability slot names).
