move.description: The wanted velocity across the ground (m/s, world space; y is ignored unless gravityScale is 0). Set it every tick.

jump.description: Held to jump: a jump starts on the tick it becomes true while grounded (or in coyote time).

jumpSpeed.description: The upward speed of a jump.

gravityScale.description: Multiplies og.Physics.gravity; 0 for top-down movement in any direction.

maxSlope.description: The steepest slope it walks up.

stepHeight.description: The highest step it climbs without jumping (0: none).

snapDistance.description: How far below it the ground still holds it (stairs down, slopes): 0 lets it leave every edge.

skin.description: The gap kept between it and every surface.

coyoteTime.description: After leaving an edge, a jump still starts within this time.

pushBodies.description: Push dynamic bodies it walks into, with at most `pushStrength`.

pushStrength.description: The most force it pushes with: each tick the bodies it walks into share an impulse of at most this times the tick's length (mass times the speed it asks of them, capped), so a body of a few kilograms is shoved at its speed while one whose friction holds more (a tonne on the ground) does not move. 0 leaves every body where it is, as `pushBodies` false does.

grounded.description: Written: standing on walkable ground after the step.

sliding.description: Written: sliding down a slope steeper than maxSlope.

velocity.description: Written: the velocity it moved at this tick (the platform's carry included).

groundNormal.description: Written: the ground's normal (zero in the air).

coyote.description: Written: seconds left in which a jump may still start (coyote time).

jumpWasHeld.description: Written: `jump` as the last step saw it (a jump starts on its rising edge).

ground.description: Written: the entity it stands on (0 in the air); a moving one carries it.

PlatformerController.description: A 2D platformer character (the 2D profile): run, jump and fall with designer units (jump height and time to apex, not gravity), coyote time, jump buffering, variable jump height (releasing jump while rising cuts the jump), apex hang, air jumps, wall slide and wall jump, one-way platforms (colliders on `oneWayLayers` are solid from above only; hold `down` to drop through), moving platforms (it rides what it stands on) and corner correction (a jump that clips a ceiling corner by less than `cornerCorrection` slides past it). It keeps `skin` off every surface; what blocks it is every solid collider its og.Collider's `layers` and `mask` interact with (each one's layers meeting the other's mask), as for bodies. The entity needs an og.Transform and an og.Collider (a box or capsule); it becomes a kinematic body and pushes the dynamic bodies it runs into (`pushBodies`) with at most `pushStrength`, so a crate's mass tells: a light one is shoved at the run speed, a heavy one holds (set its og.RigidBody `mass`).

moveX.description: The run input, -1 (left) to 1 (right). Set it every tick.

jump.description: Held to jump: a press is buffered for jumpBuffer; releasing while rising cuts the jump.

down.description: Held to drop through a one-way platform.

impulse.description: A velocity change to take on the next step (a knock-back, a spring, a recoil): added to `velocity`, then set back to zero. One with an upward y leaves the ground; the run's acceleration and gravity act on the result from then on, so a knock-back is `{ x: away * 6, y: 7 }` with `moveX` 0 for its few ticks.

acceleration.description: How fast it reaches maxSpeed on the ground.

deceleration.description: How fast it stops on the ground without input.

airDeceleration.description: Deceleration in the air without input.

jumpHeight.description: How high a full jump goes.

timeToApex.description: How long a full jump takes to reach its height (sets gravity and the jump speed).

fallGravity.description: Gravity multiplier while falling (snappier landings above 1).

jumpCut.description: Gravity multiplier while rising with jump released (variable jump height; 1 disables it).

apexGravity.description: Gravity multiplier near the apex while jump is held (hang time; 1 disables it).

apexThreshold.description: The vertical speed below which the apex multiplier applies.

coyoteTime.description: After running off an edge, a jump still starts within this time.

jumpBuffer.description: A jump pressed this long before landing starts on landing.

airJumps.description: Extra jumps in the air (1: a double jump).

wallJumps.description: Slide down walls it pushes against (and jump off them).

wallSlideSpeed.description: The fastest slide down a wall.

wallJump.description: A wall jump's velocity: x away from the wall, y up.

wallJumpLock.description: After a wall jump, the run input is ignored for this long (so it leaves the wall).

oneWayLayers.description: The collision layers that are one-way platforms (solid from above), as bits.

cornerCorrection.description: How far a rising jump is nudged sideways past a ceiling corner (0: never).

maxSlope.description: The steepest slope it runs up.

snapDistance.description: How far below it the ground still holds it (slopes, small drops).

skin.description: The gap kept between it and every surface.

pushBodies.description: Push dynamic bodies it runs into, with at most `pushStrength`.

pushStrength.description: The most force it pushes with: each tick the bodies it runs into share an impulse of at most this times the tick's length (mass times the speed it asks of them, capped), so a body of a few kilograms is shoved at its speed while one whose friction holds more (a tonne on the ground) does not move. 0 leaves every body where it is, as `pushBodies` false does.

grounded.description: Written: standing on ground after the step.

onWall.description: Written: -1 sliding on a wall to its left, 1 to its right, 0 none.

facing.description: Written: -1 facing left, 1 right (the last run direction).

velocity.description: Written: the velocity after the step (the platform's carry excluded).

jumping.description: Written: rising from a jump (until the apex or a release cut).

airJumpsLeft.description: Written: air jumps left before landing.

coyote.description: Written: seconds of coyote time left.

buffer.description: Written: seconds a buffered jump press stays valid.

wallLock.description: Written: seconds the run input stays locked after a wall jump.

dropTime.description: Written: seconds one-way platforms stay passable after dropping through.

jumpWasHeld.description: Written: `jump` as the last step saw it.

ground.description: Written: the entity it stands on (0 in the air); a moving one carries it.

CharacterEvent.description: Something a CharacterController or PlatformerController did this step: the hooks for dust, squash, sounds and camera kicks. Read the next tick: the controllers move in the physics step, after the game's systems, so a jump pressed in tick T moves the character in T and its CHARACTER_JUMPED is read in T + 1 (og-feel §12 has the same-tick alternative).

kind.description: CHARACTER_JUMPED 1, LANDED 2, WALL_JUMPED 3, AIR_JUMPED 4, LEFT_GROUND 5, BUMPED 6.

speed.description: The vertical speed at the moment (a landing's impact speed is negative).

Vehicle.description:
A car on a dynamic chassis (the entity's og.RigidBody and og.Collider). 3D: a raycast car with four wheels (suspension, grip, steering on the front axle), or with the og.VehicleWheel children it has; its forward is the chassis's local +z (three.js Object3D.lookAt aims +z). 2D: two wheel bodies on sprung wheel joints (front at +x), driven by a motor. The implicit wheels are not entities: og.physics.vehicleWheels gives their poses (and each tyre's slip) for drawing, smoke and skid marks.
The defaults drive a road car of about 1,000 kg: give the chassis that mass (og.RigidBody.mass 1000), since a car-sized box at the collider's density 1 weighs a few kilograms and the engine's and brakes' newtons would throw it. The suspension and the grip scale with the chassis's mass (Bullet's units), the engine and the brakes do not: a heavier car wants proportionally more engineForce and brakeForce. og-feel §12 has the numbers a game starts from.
The wheel rays meet what the chassis's collider would (its og.Collider layers against the other's mask, and the other's layers against its mask), so two cars on layers that do not meet (a ghost beside the player) pass through each other.

throttle.description: The accelerator, -1 (reverse) to 1. Set it every tick.

wheelBase.description: The distance between the front and rear axles.

track.description: The distance between the left and right wheels (3D).

mountHeight.description: The height of the wheel mounts below the chassis centre.

suspensionTravel.description: How far the suspension compresses or extends from rest.

grip.description: The tyres' grip (3D: the friction slip, how much of its load a tyre holds before it slides: 2 grips a road car through a bend, below 1 it slides like a drift car; 2D: the wheels' friction).

engineForce.description: The engine's force at full throttle (3D: per driven wheel, in newtons: 2,500 on the two rear wheels push 1,000 kg at 5 m/s²; 2D: the motor's torque, N·m).

maxSpeed.description: The top speed: the engine's force fades out towards it (throttle against the motion brakes first).

brakeForce.description: The brakes' force at full brake (3D: per wheel, in newtons, every wheel braking: 2,000 stop 1,000 kg at 8 m/s²; 2D: the wheels' braking torque).

maxSteer.description: The front wheels' largest steering angle (3D).

wheelMass.description: The wheels' mass (2D: the wheel bodies; 3D ignores it).

rollInfluence.description: How much the tyres' sideways grip rolls the chassis in a bend (3D): 0 pushes at the centre of mass's height, so the car corners flat and never tips over from steering (an arcade car); towards 1 at the road, the roll that tips a tall car over (rapier's own car uses 0.1, which rolls a 1,000 kg car at full lock above about 20 m/s). Raise it a little for body roll, with og.RigidBody.centerOfMass lowered to keep the car on its wheels.

speed.description: Written: the forward speed (m/s; negative reversing).

contacts.description: Written: how many wheels touch the ground.

slip.description: Written: the largest slip of its wheels (og.physics.vehicleWheels' `slip`): 0 every tyre grips, towards 1 one slides; for a squeal's volume or smoke without reading the wheels (3D; 0 in 2D).

model.description: VEHICLE_ARCADE 0 (engineForce, faded out towards maxSpeed) or VEHICLE_DRIVETRAIN 1 (an engine with a torque curve driving through a gearbox: gears, finalDrive, torqueCurve, the rpm fields; engineForce and maxSpeed are then unused). The drivetrain's torque at the driven wheels is the curve's at the engine's speed times throttle, the gear's ratio and finalDrive; the engine's speed follows the wheels while a gear is in.

handbrake.description: The handbrake, 0 to 1: it brakes the handbrake wheels (3D: the rear pair, or the og.VehicleWheel children flagged `handbrake`; 2D: the rear wheel) with that share of brakeForce, takes their drive and loosens their grip, sideways and in all, towards handbrakeGrip: in a bend at speed the tail steps out, and driftGrip keeps it loose while it slides. A handbrake turn is a pull and a release: held, the car slows and the slide dies with its speed.

handbrakeGrip.description: The handbrake wheels' grip at full handbrake, sideways and in all, as a share of their own (3D): 0.2 lets the tail step out in a bend at speed; 1 holds the line.

driftGrip.description: Drift tuning: the handbrake wheels' sideways grip while the car drifts (the handbrake is on, or one of them slid last step), as a share of their own (3D). 1 is off; around 0.6 holds a slide that the throttle and steering balance.

gears.description: Drivetrain: the forward gears' ratios, first gear first; empty uses 3.4, 2.2, 1.6, 1.25, 1.0, 0.82.

finalDrive.description: Drivetrain: the final drive's ratio, after every gear.

idleRpm.description: Drivetrain: the engine's speed at rest.

maxRpm.description: Drivetrain: the rev limit: the engine gives no torque at or above it.

torqueCurve.description: Drivetrain: the engine's torque (N·m) at full throttle, at evenly spaced speeds from 0 to maxRpm, interpolated between them; empty uses 140, 170, 195, 210, 215, 205, 185, 150 (a 1,000 kg road car's).

automatic.description: Drivetrain: the gearbox shifts by itself, up at shiftUpRpm and down at shiftDownRpm, into reverse when throttle is negative at a standstill and back into first when it is positive. False leaves `gear` to the game (a manual gearbox).

shiftUpRpm.description: Drivetrain, automatic: the engine speed it shifts up at.

shiftDownRpm.description: Drivetrain, automatic: the engine speed it shifts down at.

clutchTime.description: Drivetrain: how long a gear change takes; the engine drives nothing meanwhile.

gear.description: Drivetrain: the gear, -1 reverse, 0 neutral, 1 and up forward. An automatic gearbox writes it; for a manual one the game sets it, and each change takes clutchTime.

rpm.description: Written, drivetrain: the engine's speed, for the engine's sound and the tachometer.

VehicleWheel.description: A wheel of the og.Vehicle it is a child of (down its og.Parent chain), at its og.Transform relative to the chassis: the hard point its suspension hangs from. A vehicle with og.VehicleWheel children (up to 16, in entity order) has those wheels in place of its four implicit ones, and og.physics.vehicleWheels lists them in that order: six-wheeled trucks, trikes, rear-wheel steering. 3D only; the 2D vehicle keeps its two wheels.

radius.description: The wheel's radius.

suspensionRest.description: The suspension's length at rest, down from the wheel's position.

suspensionTravel.description: How far the suspension compresses or extends from rest.

steer.description: How much of the vehicle's steering it takes: 1 a front wheel, 0 none, negative steers the other way (rear-wheel steering).

drive.description: Whether the engine drives it (og.Vehicle.drive is then unused).

handbrake.description: Whether the handbrake brakes it, and driftGrip applies to it.

Rope.description: A Verlet rope: `segments` links from the entity's world position (its og.Transform after its parents'; plus `offset`) to `end` (an entity, plus `endOffset`) or hanging free, swung by gravity and wind, colliding with every solid collider at `radius`. It moves nothing (one-way: a rope joint ties bodies together, og.Joint JOINT_ROPE). Its points are world state (the og.physics state block); og.physics.ropePoints reads them and the renderer draws the rope as a strip of `width` and `color`.

segments.description: The number of links (points minus one).

offset.description: The start's offset from the entity's position (world axes).

end.description: The entity the far end is tied to; 0 leaves it free.

endOffset.description: The far end's offset from `end`'s position.

iterations.description: Constraint passes per step: more is stiffer, at more cost.

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick (1: none lost).

radius.description: The thickness it collides at (0: no collision).

color.description: The drawn linear colour.

Cloth.description: A Verlet cloth: a `columns` × `rows` grid of points, `spacing` apart, hanging from the entity's world position (its og.Transform after its parents': its top-left corner, the grid laid out along the entity's local x and down -y), pinned by `pins` (pinned points follow the entity), with stretch and shear constraints, gravity, wind, collision against every solid collider and, with `thickness`, against itself. One-way like og.Rope; its points are world state. Drawn as a double-sided mesh with `material` (og.render.standardMaterial; 0: a plain cloth colour).

spacing.description: The rest distance between neighbouring points.

pins.description: Which points are pinned, a sum of PIN_* bits (1 top row, 2 top corners, 4 left column, 8 top rings).

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick.

wind.description: A steady acceleration (wind); the cloth flutters with it.

gust.description: How much the wind varies over the cloth and the tick (0: steady).

radius.description: The thickness it collides at (0: no collision).

thickness.description: Self-collision: how far apart its points keep from the points of the cloth that are not their near neighbours (0: none). About `spacing` keeps a cloth that folds or piles up from passing through itself.

substeps.description: Simulation steps per tick, each integrating and then solving `iterations` passes; with self-collision enough that a point moves less than `thickness` per step (a point moves at most half the thickness a step).

friction.description: How much of its sliding a point touching a solid loses each step (0: it slides freely; near 1 it sticks where it lands, so a cloth lowered onto the floor folds instead of spreading).

material.description: The material it is drawn with (og.render.standardMaterial); 0 is a plain cloth.

Garment.description: Cloth on a skinned character: glTF mesh `mesh` of the entity's og.Model (a skirt, a cape, a coat's tails), posed by the entity's og.Skeleton and simulated from there. Each tick the animation poses the mesh; then every point of it swings under gravity and wind and drags behind the motion, but stays within `maxDistance` of where the skinned pose puts it, never goes further than `backstop` behind it into the body, and keeps its edges' lengths. Points within `pinTop` of the garment's top, and points whose vertex colour's red or alpha is 0, stay on the skinned pose; red times alpha between 0 and 1 scales `maxDistance` (paint it in the modelling tool: white everywhere frees the whole garment; paint the alpha over a white colour to keep a textured garment's colours, which the red would tint, since an opaque material does not show the alpha). With `radius` it collides with every solid collider too. One-way like og.Cloth (it moves nothing), simulated in the physics step with the rest of the world, so it replays and snapshots carry it. The model draws the garment where the simulation leaves it, with motion vectors for TAA. 3D only. Its blendshapes are not applied.

mesh.description: The glTF mesh of the entity's model that is the garment (its primitives together), as og.Blendshapes.mesh.

maxDistance.description: How far a point may stray from where the skinned pose puts it.

pinTop.description: Points within this height of the garment's top at rest (the bind pose, the model's +y) stay on the skinned pose: a skirt's waistband, a cape's collar.

backstop.description: How far a point may go behind where the skinned pose puts it, against the skinned normal (0: never behind it, so it cannot sink into the body).

stiffness.description: How stiff its edges are, 0 to 1 a pass: 1 holds their length, lower stretches.

bending.description: How much it resists folding, 0 to 1 a pass (across each pair of triangles that share an edge): 0 drapes like silk, near 1 like leather.

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick.

wind.description: A steady acceleration (wind); the garment flutters with it.

gust.description: How much the wind varies over the garment and the tick (0: steady).

radius.description: The thickness it collides with solid colliders at (0: no collision; the skinned pose, through `maxDistance` and `backstop`, holds it on the body). A character's own collider counts: keep it inside the body, or leave this 0.

friction.description: How much of its sliding a point touching a solid loses each step.

SoftBody.description: A PBD soft volume: a closed surface of points (2D: a ring in the xy plane) held by distance constraints along its edges and by one constraint on the volume it encloses (2D: its area), dropped under gravity and pushed out of every solid collider, so it lands, squashes and springs back: jelly, a water balloon, a slime. Built at the entity's world pose (its og.Transform after its parents') when it appears or its shape changes. It moves nothing (one-way like og.Cloth). Its points are world state (the og.physics state block); og.physics.softBodyPoints reads them and the renderer draws its surface with `material`.

radius.description: A sphere's radius.

size.description: A box's full extents.

detail.description: How finely its surface is divided: a sphere 0 to 3 (12, 42, 162 or 642 points; 2D 12 to 96), a box 0 to 7 (cells along a face's edge, minus one). A finer surface needs more iterations to hold its shape: at 642 points and stiffness below 1 the default 8 lets it spread.

mesh.description: SOFT_MESH's geometry: a loaded glTF's (registered automatically) or one given to og.physics.setMesh; closed, its vertices welded where they meet.

stiffness.description: How stiff its edges are, 0 to 1 a pass: 1 holds their length, lower lets the surface stretch and wobble.

pressure.description: The volume it keeps, as a share of its rest volume: 1 holds it, above inflates it, 0 holds none (it slumps like cloth).

volumeStiffness.description: How much of its volume a pass restores, 0 to 1.

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick.

thickness.description: The distance its points keep from solids (0: no collision).

friction.description: How much of its sliding a point touching a solid loses each step.

pinTop.description: Points within this height of its top at rest are pinned to the entity and follow it (0: none): a water balloon on a string.

material.description: The material it is drawn with (og.render.standardMaterial); 0 is a plain one.

volume.description: Written: its volume (2D: area) now over its rest volume; below 1 squashed, above inflated.

center.description: Written: the mean of its points, in world space.

Fluid2D.description: A 2D particle fluid (any profile, in the xy plane): `count` particles spawned in a `size` box centred on the entity, simulated with double density relaxation (Clavet et al. 2005: pressure, near pressure, viscosity) on a fixed grid in a fixed order, so it is deterministic and part of the og.physics state block. Particles collide with every solid collider (pushed out of bodies; they push nothing back) and stay inside `bounds` around the entity when it is set. Fluids of one `group` interact: by `density` they layer, by `mixing` they blend. Drawn as metaballs: the particles blurred into a field the renderer thresholds into one surface of `color`, on sprite layer `layer`.

count.description: How many particles (spawned when the component appears or count changes).

size.description: The spawn box, centred on the entity.

bounds.description: The container around the entity (0 0: none; colliders still hold it).

radius.description: The interaction radius: particles closer than this push and drag each other.

restDensity.description: The density it settles at (neighbours within radius, weighted).

stiffness.description: The pressure's strength (above about 0.15 it gets springy, then unstable).

nearStiffness.description: The near pressure's strength (keeps particles apart, gives surface tension).

group.description: Fluids sharing a group above 0 push, drag and (by `mixing`) mix with each other as one fluid, at most four to a group (in entity order; a fifth is simulated alone), and are drawn as one surface whose colour follows the mix; 0 keeps the fluid to itself.

density.description: How heavy its particles are against the group's other fluids: a heavier fluid sinks under a lighter one.

mixing.description: How readily it mixes with the group's other fluids: 0 keeps them apart in layers (the boundary held), 1 blends them where they touch (their mix, colour and weight even out).

seed.description: The seed of the spawn jitter.

color.description: The surface's linear colour.

blobScale.description: The drawn size of each particle's blob (times radius).

threshold.description: The field value where the surface starts (higher: thinner, separate drops).

layer.description: The sprite layer it is drawn on.

Fluid3D.description: A 3D particle fluid (the 3D profile): `count` particles spawned in a `size` box centred on the entity, simulated with double density relaxation (Clavet et al. 2005: pressure, near pressure that gives surface tension, viscosity) over a spatial hash in a fixed order, so it is deterministic and part of the og.physics state block. Particles collide with every solid collider, the terrain's height field included (pushed out; they push nothing back), and stay inside `bounds` around the entity when it is set. An emitter adds particles at `emitRate` up to `maxCount`; a sink box removes those that enter it. Fluids of one `group` interact: by `density` they layer, by `mixing` they blend. Drawn as a screen-space surface: the particles' depth smoothed into one surface, refracting what is behind by its thickness and reflecting the sky, lit by the scene's lights. Cost: about 0.9 ms of CPU a tick for 2000 particles at 1 substep, 1.8 ms at 2 (native and wasm alike), growing with the particles; keep a scene's fluids to a few thousand particles. The surface costs about 1.1 ms of GPU (an Apple M4 Pro, the fluid covering a third of a 1280×720 frame) whatever the particle count, growing with the pixels it covers.

count.description: How many particles to spawn in the box (when the component appears or count or seed changes; 0: none, the emitter fills it).

size.description: The spawn box, centred on the entity.

bounds.description: The container around the entity (0 on an axis: open on that axis; colliders and the terrain still hold it).

radius.description: The interaction radius: particles closer than this push and drag each other. Cost grows with the particles, not the radius.

restDensity.description: The density it settles at (neighbours within radius, weighted).

stiffness.description: The pressure's strength (above about 0.05 it jitters, then springs apart).

nearStiffness.description: The near pressure's strength (keeps particles apart, gives surface tension).

viscosity.description: Linear viscosity (it also calms the surface; honey above 1).

group.description: Fluids sharing a group above 0 push, drag and (by `mixing`) mix with each other as one fluid, at most four to a group (in entity order; a fifth is simulated alone); 0 keeps the fluid to itself.

density.description: How heavy its particles are against the group's other fluids: a heavier fluid sinks under a lighter one.

mixing.description: How readily it mixes with the group's other fluids: 0 keeps them apart in layers (the boundary held), 1 blends them where they touch (their mix, colour and weight even out).

substeps.description: Simulation steps per tick (each costs a full pass over the particles).

seed.description: The seed of the spawn and emitter jitter.

maxCount.description: The most particles alive at once (the emitter stops there).

emitRate.description: Particles the emitter adds per second (0: no emitter).

emitOffset.description: Where the emitter is, from the entity (world axes).

emitVelocity.description: The velocity emitted particles start with.

emitRadius.description: The half-size of the cube new particles appear in around the emitter.

sinkOffset.description: The sink's centre, from the entity (world axes).

sinkSize.description: The sink box: particles that enter it are removed (0 0 0: no sink).

color.description: The fluid's linear colour (what light passing through it keeps).

opacity.description: How opaque a metre of it is (0: clear as glass, 1: opaque).

reflectivity.description: How much it reflects (scales the Fresnel term).

refraction.description: How far refraction bends what is seen through it.

drawScale.description: The drawn size of each particle (times radius).

smoothing.description: How much the surface is smoothed (0: beads, 1: one surface).

WaterSurface.description: Height-field water (3D): a `resolution` × `resolution` grid of heights over a `size` square centred on the entity (its y is the rest level), waves travelling at `waveSpeed` and fading by `damping`. Dynamic bodies crossing it push waves (splashes; og.Splash events) and float by `buoyancy`. The heights are world state; an og.Water on the same entity draws them.

size.description: The side of the square of water.

damping.description: How much of a wave survives a second (1: no loss).

buoyancy.description: The upward force on a submerged body per cubic metre of its box under water (0: bodies sink).

drag.description: How much a submerged body's velocity is slowed.

WaterLine.description: 2D water for side-scrollers: a `width` × `depth` pool whose top edge (at the entity's y, centred on its x) is `columns` springs, each pulled to its rest height by `tension`, damped by `damping` and passing waves to its neighbours by `spread`. Bodies (and characters) crossing the surface splash it (og.Splash events) and float by `buoyancy`. The springs are world state; an og.Water2D on the same entity draws it.

depth.description: The pool's depth below the surface.

tension.description: How hard each spring pulls back to rest.

damping.description: How fast a spring's motion dies.

spread.description: How much of a spring's height its neighbours feel each pass (waves travel).

buoyancy.description: The upward force on a submerged body per square metre of its box under water (0: bodies sink).

drag.description: How much a submerged body's velocity is slowed.

Buoyancy.description: Floats a dynamic rigid body (3D profile) on the water under it: an og.WaterSurface (at its rest level), an og.Water (a flat lake, or a sea with a wind: its waves as drawn, og.physics.waterHeight's) or both on one entity. Its hull is its colliders' box cut into `samples` cells a side, kept where a cell's centre lies in a solid collider; each cell under the surface pushes up by the water it displaces (Archimedes: `waterDensity` × its share of the colliders' volume × gravity plus the water's own acceleration, so it sinks with a crest that falls away rather than being flung clear) at that cell, so a hull rights itself, pitches and rolls with the waves, and is slowed by `drag` and `angularDrag` against the moving water as far as it is under. Computed in the tick, the same on every run and after a restore; the sea's waves are the absolute world's, so a body moved by og.WorldOrigin rides the same water. A body with it takes no og.WaterSurface `buoyancy` (only its splash). Insert it beside og.RigidBody and og.Collider: `{}` floats a body of the default density half under.

waterDensity.description: The water's density, in og.Collider.density's units: the default 2 floats a body of the colliders' default density 1 half under, as wood floats; at 1 the same body hangs just under the surface, under it sinks.

samples.description: Cells along each side of its colliders' box (1: one point at its centre; up to 12³ points): more follow its shape and the waves more closely, at more cost.

drag.description: How much of its speed through the water it loses each second when fully under (in part when in part); off-centre cells slow its turning too, so it settles instead of bobbing.

angularDrag.description: How much of its spin it loses each second when fully under (in part when in part).

submerged.description: Written: the fraction of its hull under water after the last step (0 above it or out of water, 1 sunk): for wakes, splashes and a sinking ship.

Splash.description: Something crossed a water surface (og.WaterSurface or og.WaterLine): for splash particles and sounds. Read the next tick.

Ragdoll.description: A ragdoll over an og.Skeleton: a capsule body per bone with a parent, joints with limits between them (ball joints with cone limits in 3D; in 2D hinges about z, the bones rapier2d bodies in the xy plane at their animated z, for a skeleton laid out in that plane), built from the skeleton's rest pose. `weight` is where the pose comes from: 0 the animation (the bodies follow it kinematically), 1 the physics (the bodies are dynamic, starting with the animation's velocity); the pose drawn blends between them over `blendTime`, both ways. The bodies are world state (the og.physics state block), not entities.

weight.description: 0 animated, 1 ragdoll. Set it to 1 on a hit; back to 0 to recover.

blendTime.description: How long the blend between animation and physics takes, both ways.

mass.description: The whole body's mass, shared by the bones by length.

thickness.description: A bone capsule's radius as a fraction of its length.

jointLimit.description: How far each joint bends from the rest pose.

damping.description: How much of their motion the bones lose per second.

impulse.description: An impulse given to every bone when weight first goes up (a hit).

blend.description: Written: the blend in use (0 animation .. 1 physics).

QueryFilter.description: Which colliders a scene query considers. The zero value considers every solid collider on every layer.

mask.description: Layers to consider: a collider counts when its layers meet this; 0 means every layer.

exclude.description: An entity to ignore, such as the caster itself.

direction.description: Where it points; it need not be normalised and must not be zero (in 2D, not zero in xy).

maxDistance.description: How far it reaches; 0 is unbounded.

RaycastHit.description: The nearest collider a ray meets.

body.description: The body the collider belongs to: its own entity, or for a compound child collider (an og.Collider on a child of an og.RigidBody) the ancestor body it is part of.

distance.description: From the origin along the normalised direction.

point.description: Where the ray meets the collider.

normal.description: The surface normal there (z is 0 in 2D).

RaycastAllDesc.description: A ray for og.physics.raycastAll: og.physics.raycast's fields and a cap on the hits.

direction.description: Where it points; it need not be normalised and must not be zero (in 2D, not zero in xy).

maxDistance.description: How far it reaches; 0 is unbounded.

maxHits.description: The most hits returned, nearest first; 0 is MAX_RAYCAST_HITS (256), and more is held to it.

point.description: The point to project (its z is ignored in 2D).

maxDistance.description: How far a collider may be; 0 is unbounded.

solid.description: A point inside a collider is its own projection (distance 0); false projects it onto the collider's surface.

PointProjection.description: Where a point projects onto the nearest collider.

point.description: The nearest point on the collider, in world space.

normal.description: Unit direction out of the collider at the point, towards a point outside it (from a point inside, still outward); zero when the distance is 0.

distance.description: From the queried point to `point`.

inside.description: Whether the queried point is inside the collider.

ShapeDesc.description: The shape of a shape cast or an overlap test: the shape fields of a Collider. The zero value is a 1 m box.

size.description: Full extents of a box.

radius.description: Radius of a sphere, circle, capsule or cylinder.

mesh.description: The geometry of a convex or triangle-mesh shape.

ShapeCastDesc.description: A shape swept along a direction for og.physics.shapeCast.

rotation.description: The shape's rotation; a zero quaternion is no rotation.

direction.description: Where it sweeps; it need not be normalised and must not be zero.

maxDistance.description: How far it sweeps; 0 is unbounded.

ShapeCastHit.description: The first collider a swept shape meets.

distance.description: How far the shape travelled before touching.

point.description: The contact point on the hit collider, in world space.

normal.description: The hit collider's surface normal there, in world space.

OverlapDesc.description: A shape placed in the world for og.physics.overlap.

rotation.description: Its rotation; a zero quaternion is no rotation.

MeshDesc.description: Geometry for convex and triangle-mesh colliders, in the mesh's own space.

positions.description: Vertex positions (2D polygons use x and y).

indices.description: Triangles as triples of indices into positions; a convex hull ignores them.

WheelPose.description: A wheel of an og.Vehicle as the last step left it, for drawing.

position.description: The wheel's centre in world space.

rotation.description: Its rotation (steering and spin) in world space.

slip.description: How much the tyre slides (rapier's skid info turned round): 0 it grips, towards 1 it asks for more than its grip holds (0.5 is twice as much); 0 in the air and in 2D. Start smoke and skid marks above about 0.2, and fade a squeal in with it.

sideSpeed.description: How fast the tyre's contact moves sideways over the ground (along its axle; 0 in the air and in 2D): a slide's speed, for the squeal's pitch or a skid mark's darkness.

entity.description: The wheel's og.VehicleWheel entity; 0 for a vehicle's implicit wheels.

RagdollBoneDesc.description: One bone of a ragdoll rig: a capsule from the bone's position along `axis` for `length`.

parent.description: The parent bone's index (it must come earlier); -1 for the root.

position.description: The bone's rest position relative to the entity.

rotation.description: The bone's rest rotation relative to the entity; a zero quaternion is no rotation.

length.description: How long the bone is (to its child).

axis.description: The direction the bone points in its own frame (towards its child).

joint.description: The skeleton joint (its index in the skin) the bone stands for, so the model is drawn with it; -1 for none.

RagdollRigDesc.description: The bones of a ragdoll, parents first, for og.physics.setRagdollRig; og.physics.ragdollRigFromSkeleton makes one from a model's skeleton.

skeleton.description: The skeleton the bones' joints belong to (0: none): the entity's posed model is drawn blended towards the bones by og.Ragdoll.blend.

BonePose.description: A ragdoll bone's pose as the last step left it (blended with the animation by og.Ragdoll.weight).

position.description: The bone's position in world space.

SoftBodyPoints.description: An og.SoftBody's surface after the last step.

indices.description: Its triangles, three indices into `points` each, wound outwards (2D: a fan over the ring).

PhysicsPhase.description: One phase of the last physics step, for og.physics.stats.

name.description: gather (reading the components), sync (bodies and static colliders into rapier), joints (joints and vehicles), ragdolls, water (buoyancy before the step), rapier (rapier's step, every substep), readout (touching pairs and bodies read back, the rest rule), controllers (characters and platformers), soft (ropes and cloths), fluids (2D), fluids3d or writeBack (components and events written back).

ms.description: Wall-clock time it took (0 where the host has no clock); never world state.

split.description: Whether any of its work ran on the lanes pool: rapier's stages when the step went to the pool, the other phases when they split by bodies, contact pairs, ragdolls, soft bodies or particles.

PhysicsStats.description: What the last physics step cost, phase by phase, and where it ran: for finding where physics time goes. Timings are wall clock and vary run to run; the simulation never reads them.

tick.description: The tick the step ran (0 before the first).

bodies.description: The rapier bodies it stepped (with ragdoll bones and vehicle wheels).

threads.description: The lanes pool's threads at the time (1: lanes off or single-threaded).

pool.description: Whether the whole step ran on the lanes pool (from a number of bodies per thread count), where rapier splits its broad phase, narrow phase and solver.

ms.description: Wall-clock time of the whole og.physics system, gather to write-back.

phases.description: Every phase, in the order they run.

Fog.description: Distance and height fog over the 3D scene and world sprites: distance fog, measured from the camera, thickens exponentially by density per metre past start and, when end > start, also by a linear ramp from start to full fog at end; the two apply together, and density defaults to 0.02, so setting only end still adds exponential fog (set density 0 for the ramp alone). Height fog is densest below height and thins by falloff per metre above it; looking into the sun it turns towards sunColor. The overlay is never fogged.

color.description: The colour the fog tends to (linear, before exposure).

density.description: Exponential distance fog per metre past start, with or without end's ramp (0: none).

start.description: The distance from the camera where distance fog starts.

end.description: The distance from the camera where fog is full: with end > start, a linear ramp from start to end applied together with density's exponential fog (0: no ramp).

heightDensity.description: Height fog at and below height (0: none).

height.description: The world height below which height fog is densest.

falloff.description: How fast height fog thins above height, per metre.

sunColor.description: The fog's colour looking into the sun (forward scattering).

sunPower.description: How tight the sun's glow in the fog is (higher: smaller).

sky.description: How much of the fog covers the sky (0: the sky stays clear).

volumetric.description: Light the fog as a participating medium: within volumetricDistance of the camera the fog (density per metre, thickened below height by heightDensity and falloff, as above) scatters the sun through its shadow cascades, so light shafts fall through windows and between trees and move with the sun, and every point, spot and rect light it is lit by (up to RenderCapabilities.volumetricLights at each sample); it dims what lies behind it by the same amounts. RenderCapabilities.volumetricFog names the method (a froxel grid). Opaque surfaces and the sky are seen through the volume; blended surfaces, particles and sprites take the plain distance and height fog of the same medium. Past volumetricDistance nothing more is added.

scattering.description: How much of the light the fog takes from a ray it scatters (its albedo, tinted by color): 0 dims without glowing, 1 sends all of it on, above 1 brightens the shafts for effect.

anisotropy.description: Which way the fog scatters (Henyey–Greenstein g): 0 evenly, towards 1 forward (bright looking into the light: shafts against the sun), below 0 back towards the light.

volumetricDistance.description: How far from the camera the volume reaches.

Sky.description: A procedural sky of chosen colours, drawn behind the scene per pixel and lighting it: the image-based light and the reflections' sky (where a surface reflects no probe and SSR misses) follow it as it is drawn, clouds and all, captured from the camera a slice a frame, eight frames to a whole capture, so a drifting cloud, a lightning flash or a fast day moves in the reflections and the ambient light within sixteen frames (about a quarter of a second at 60 fps). Without it, RenderSettings.sky draws the built-in sky. A DayNight that is enabled sets the sky itself.

enabled.description: Draw and light by this sky.

sunSize.description: The sun disc's angular radius (0: no disc).

stars.description: Stars where the sky is dark: 0 none, 1 a full night sky.

brightness.description: A multiplier on the whole sky.

moonSize.description: The moon disc's angular radius (0: no moon). It sets below the horizon and hides the stars behind it.

moonPhase.description: How much of the moon is lit: 0 new, 0.25 the first quarter (its right half), 0.5 full, 0.75 the last quarter (its left half).

moonDirection.description: Towards the moon; zero puts it opposite sunDirection.

DayNight.description: A day-night cycle: the time of day drives the sun's direction, the sky's colours, stars and the moon disc, the first DirectionalLight (the sun by day, a dim moon opposite it by night), the ambient light and the fog's colour. The clock is start plus the simulated seconds times speed, wrapped to 24 hours; the sky's colours step every `step` minutes of game time while its sun moves smoothly, and the image-based light and the reflections' sky follow the sky as it is drawn (clouds, lightning and all), captured a slice a frame. The drive happens as the frame is drawn and never writes the world: the DirectionalLight keeps the colour, intensity and transform it was given. The probe's `get` answers what is drawn, a pure function of the tick: `get:og.DayNight` adds `hours`, `toSun`, `toLight` (towards the sun by day, the moon by night), `lightColor` and `lightIntensity`, and `get:<sun>.og.DirectionalLight` on the driven light answers the drawn `color` and `intensity` with `toLight` and `drivenBy`.

start.description: The time of day at tick 0, in hours (6 sunrise, 12 noon, 18 sunset).

speed.description: Game hours per simulated second (0.05: a day in 8 minutes; 0 holds the time).

tilt.description: How far the sun's path leans from overhead.

azimuth.description: Where the sun rises, turned about +y from +x.

lightIntensity.description: A multiplier on the sun and moon light.

tintFog.description: Turn the og.Fog colour towards the horizon's.

step.description: Game minutes between steps of the sky's colours (the image-based light follows the sky as drawn).

moonSize.description: The moon disc's angular radius, opposite the sun so it rises as the sun sets (0: no moon).

moonPhase.description: How much of the moon is lit: 0 new, 0.25 the first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 the last quarter.

PhysicalSky.description: A physical sky: sunlight scattered by the air (Rayleigh: the blue overhead, the red sunsets) and by haze (Mie: the white glow around the sun), with ozone keeping the twilight zenith blue, in a spherical atmosphere of Earth's proportions with multiple scattering (Hillaire 2020). It replaces the gradient of og.Sky and og.DayNight, and the image-based light follows it. With og.DayNight enabled the cycle also takes its light from it: the sun's colour is the light that crosses the air (white at noon, orange then red as it sets, gone below the horizon), the ambient light the scattered sky, and the fog's colour the sky's horizon; `get:og.DayNight` answers those. With og.Sky enabled, og.Sky's sun direction, disc, stars, moon and brightness are drawn through the air. Alone it draws the sky towards the first DirectionalLight. Visual only: drawn from the tick, never written to the world.

haze.description: How much haze the air holds, a multiplier on Earth's aerosols (1: a clear day; 0: pure air; 5 to 10: a hazy or smoggy day, a whiter sky and a wider glow round the sun).

airDensity.description: A multiplier on the air's scattering (1: Earth; above 1 a deeper blue and redder sunsets, below 1 a thinner, darker sky).

ozone.description: A multiplier on ozone's absorption, which keeps the sky blue overhead at twilight (0: none, the twilight sky turns grey and yellow).

groundAlbedo.description: The ground's colour as the air sees it from below: it lights the haze and the sky below the horizon.

altitude.description: The height above sea level of the world's y 0 (the camera's height is added): from high up the sky darkens overhead and the sun stays up longer.

night.description: The sky's light with the sun far below the horizon (airglow and starlight), so a night is dark blue rather than black and the land under it keeps a deep blue-grey ambient.

Clouds.description: Clouds in the procedural sky: a volumetric layer of cumulus raymarched through a curved shell over the planet, lit by the first DirectionalLight (shadowed within themselves, with multiple scattering: bright tops, dark bases, silver edges against the sun) and the sky's light, faded into the sky with distance; and a thin, streaked high layer (cirrus) above. The wind carries them with the tick's clock, so they look the same on every run and after a restore. They are drawn over the procedural sky (og.Sky, og.DayNight or og.PhysicalSky; alone they bring the built-in procedural sky with them) and dim the sun and the sky's light by their cover (a broken sky hides the sun a share of the time; an overcast deck hides it from every surface, leaving the deck's flat grey light). Visual only: nothing in the simulation reads them.

coverage.description: How much of the sky the cumulus covers: 0 none, 0.3 fair weather, 0.6 broken, 1 overcast.

density.description: How thick they are per metre (0.04: cumulus; 0.01: thin and translucent; 0.08: dense storm cloud).

base.description: The height of the cloud base above the world's y 0.

thickness.description: How tall the layer is (0: no cumulus, only the high layer).

scale.description: The size of the largest cloud shapes.

wind.description: How fast the wind carries them (x and z; y slowly turns their shapes over).

color.description: Their albedo: white for fair-weather clouds, a grey for rain clouds.

detail.description: How much fine noise erodes their edges (0: smooth blobs, 1: wispy).

layer.description: The high thin layer's cover (0: none).

layerAltitude.description: The high layer's height (kept above the cumulus).

steps.description: Samples along each view ray through the cumulus: more is smoother and costs more.

Aurora.description: The aurora: curtains of light in the upper atmosphere, raymarched in the procedural sky (after Lawlor and Genetti, Interactive Volume Rendering Aurora on the GPU, 2011). Each curtain is a sheet of falling electrons along the auroral oval, folded by slow travelling waves and curled by a Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, extruded upward by how the electrons deposit their energy in the air: green oxygen light peaking near 114 km, a pink-violet nitrogen border below it where the electrons are hard, red oxygen light above 200 km where they are soft (the heights observed by Whiter et al., 2023). Emission only, under the clouds and dimmed by the air near the horizon; invisible against a daylight sky. The display follows the tick's clock, so it looks the same on every run and after a restore. Drawn over the procedural sky (og.Sky, og.DayNight or og.PhysicalSky). Visual only: nothing in the simulation reads it.

intensity.description: How bright the display is: 1 a bright display against a night sky, 0.3 a faint one.

activity.description: 0 quiet, smooth arcs; 0.5 folding, rayed curtains; 1 a substorm's breakup, curled and fragmented, moving fast.

curtains.description: How many arcs, one behind another.

direction.description: Where the arcs lie, turned about +y from +x (the convention of og.DayNight's azimuth).

distance.description: How far the first arc is from the world's origin over the ground (0: overhead).

energy.description: The falling electrons' characteristic energy in keV: about 2 for a typical display; under 1 a high, red-topped aurora; over 5 a low one with a pink-violet lower border.

speed.description: How fast the folds travel and the rays drift (1: as observed).

seed.description: The display's seed: its curtains' shapes and their curls.

greenColor.description: The oxygen green line's colour (557.7 nm): by default its spectral colour, a yellow-green; a camera's photograph renders it bluer (0.1 1 0.55).

redColor.description: The oxygen red line's colour (630.0 nm), of the high tops.

nitrogenColor.description: The nitrogen bands' colour (427.8 nm and the red first positive band), of the lower border: violet to pink.

WeatherState.description: The weather's effect on the world, simulated in the tick from og.Weather (its kind and intensity) so gameplay can read it: how wet the ground is, how much standing water and snow lie on it, and the lightning strikes, drawn from a random stream the engine forks from og.Rng (`fork("og.weather")`) and keeps here, so a replay, a restore and every host strike at the same ticks in the same places. Registered the first time a game names it: a world that never does keeps its type table and hash. The renderer draws the same values on every lit surface (meshes, terrain and grass; StandardMaterialDesc.weathering opts a material out): porous surfaces darken when wet and seal-smooth ones gloss, drying in patches from the high spots once the rain stops; rain runs down walls in streaks; puddles fill the hollows of level ground (a terrain's layer heights first) and ripple and splash in the rain; snow settles on what faces up (deeper snow reaching steeper faces), lifts a terrain's surface by its depth and melts away; dust and sand settle on what faces up and in the low parts; and a strike flashes the scene with a bolt at strikePosition. Roofs, canopies and overhangs keep what is under them dry and free of snow (shelterSize). Rendering never writes it.

soakTime.description: Seconds of rain at intensity 1 to soak dry ground (wetness 0 to 1).

dryTime.description: Seconds for soaked ground to dry once the rain stops.

puddleTime.description: Seconds of rain at intensity 1 on soaked ground to fill the puddles (puddles 0 to 1).

drainTime.description: Seconds for full puddles to drain once the rain stops.

snowfall.description: How much snow settles per minute of snowfall at intensity 1.

melt.description: How much snow melts per minute when none falls (three times as fast in rain).

snowCover.description: The snow depth at which it covers everything that can hold it (the renderer's full cover).

dustTime.description: Seconds of a dust storm at intensity 1 to cover what faces up with dust and sand (dust 0 to 1). It stays when the storm ends; rain washes it off.

washTime.description: Seconds of rain at intensity 1 to wash full dust off.

dustColor.description: The colour of the settled dust and sand (linear): pale ochre by default; a red desert's or a grey quarry's.

lightning.description: Lightning strikes per minute on average, at random ticks (0: none), whatever the kind of weather.

lightningCenter.description: The centre of the area strikes land in (its y is the ground's height there).

lightningRadius.description: The radius of that area: strikes land evenly over the disc.

shelterSize.description: The side of the square around the camera in which roofs, overhangs and canopies keep what is under them dry and free of snow, with a soft edge at the drip line (the renderer's weather occlusion map, looking along the rain or snow as og.Weather's wind slants it); past it every surface is open to the sky. 0: nothing shelters. Drawn only: the tick's wetness, puddles and snowDepth are the open ground's, so a game that needs to know whether a place is sheltered casts a ray up against the colliders (og.physics).

wetness.description: How wet the ground is, 0 dry to 1 soaked (written by og.weather).

puddles.description: How far standing water has spread, 0 none to 1 (written by og.weather).

dust.description: How much dust and sand has settled, 0 none to 1 covering what faces up (written by og.weather).

snowDepth.description: The depth of lying snow (written by og.weather). The drawn terrain rises by it on level ground, up to 10 cm, once the cover has built up; only drawn: collision, og.terrain.sample, picking and what stands on the ground keep the terrain's own height.

strikes.description: Lightning strikes so far (written by og.weather).

lastStrike.description: The tick of the latest strike (0 before the first; written by og.weather).

strikePosition.description: Where the latest strike landed (written by og.weather).

stream.description: The lightning's random state, forked from og.Rng the first tick (written by og.weather).

LightningStrike.description: Lightning struck, in the tick og.weather drew it (og.WeatherState.lightning): read in the systems after og.weather that tick, or the next tick's first.

position.description: Where it landed: in the disc of og.WeatherState.lightningRadius around lightningCenter, at its height.

strike.description: Which strike it is, counting from 1 (og.WeatherState.strikes after it).

Weather.description: A weather preset around the camera: particles (rain, snow, dust), its fog (unless og.Fog is enabled, which takes precedence) and dimmed sunlight. Particles are simulated by the renderer from the tick, so they look the same on every run; they never touch the simulation.

intensity.description: How heavy: scales the particle rate, the fog and the dimming.

wind.description: Where the wind blows the particles.

radius.description: The size of the region around the camera the particles fill.

dim.description: How much of the preset's dimming of the sunlight applies.

layer.description: With an orthographic camera (2D), the sprite layer the particles draw in.

Wind.description: The wind the renderer sways vegetation with: og.TerrainScatter copies and their impostor cards, og.Grass blades, swaying trees, and og.Model instances with a sway, lean downwind and sway in gusts that sweep across the field, each vertex moved by its height (the root stays put, the tip moves furthest). Where the renderer can (RenderCapabilities.compute) it simulates the wind as one field around the camera that every one of them reads, so a gust front crosses grass, copies and trees together, eddies (`turbulence`), carries og.WindMotor pushes, and vegetation springs into a gust and settles after it; og.Model sway keeps the wind's own gusts. Off at strength 0. Visual only: drawn from the tick, so it sways the same on every run and after a restore, and nothing in the simulation reads it (og.Rope, og.Cloth and og.Weather keep their own wind).

strength.description: The mean lean: how far a copy's tip moves downwind per metre of its height (0.2: a 1 m stem's tip leans 20 cm); 0 is still.

direction.description: Where the wind blows: its horizontal part, normalised.

speed.description: How fast the gusts travel downwind, over a 10 m wave.

gust.description: How much the lean varies in the gusts: 0 a steady lean, 1 from upright to twice the mean.

turbulence.description: How much the wind swirls on its own between the gusts, where the renderer simulates it (RenderCapabilities.compute): 0 the gusts alone, 1 eddies as strong as the wind.

gustSize.description: How large the gust patches are.

WindMotorKind.description: How an og.WindMotor pushes the wind.

x-og-variants.omni: Outward from its centre: a blast, a landing, a horse's hooves.
x-og-variants.directional: Along the entity's forward (its -z, horizontal part): a fan, a rotor's downwash leaning the grass one way.
x-og-variants.vortex: Around its centre, counter-clockwise seen from above: a whirlwind, a spell.

WindMotor.description: A local push on the wind the renderer sways vegetation with, at the entity's position: grass blades, og.TerrainScatter copies and their impostor cards, and swaying trees within `radius` lean away from it (omni), along it (directional) or around it (vortex), the push fading to nothing at its edge; the field carries and swirls the push, so it ripples out and settles after the motor stops. Needs no og.Wind (a motor in still air moves only what it reaches). Visual only, where the renderer simulates the wind (RenderCapabilities.compute; elsewhere it does nothing): nothing in the simulation reads it, and the same ticks draw the same push on every run. The 16 nearest the camera act.

radius.description: How far it reaches.

strength.description: Its push at its centre, as a wind speed; vegetation leans by about 0.05 per m/s of it in still air, by og.Wind's lean per m/s of its speed in a wind.

Water.description: A planar water surface on the entity's xz plane (centred on it, turned with it): colour by the water's depth over what is below, foam where it meets geometry, animated waves, refraction and reflections (screen-space, the sky's cubemap where that misses, or a planar reflection), the sun's shadows, caustics below it and an underwater view. With an og.WaterSurface on the same entity its wave heights displace the surface (centred on the entity, unrotated).

size.description: The extent along the entity's x and z.

geometry.description: Draw the water over this mesh (its vertices in the entity's frame) instead of the size × size grid: a stream, channel or pool of any outline, with the same colour by depth, refraction, foam and reflections. 0: the grid. A mesh surface has no wave heights.

river.description: A river along this path (og.path.create or og.path.find; its points where the water runs, their height the water's level): the water is a ribbon riverWidth across down the course, drawn in place of the size grid, its current riverSpeed mid-stream along the path, turning with it and slowing to nothing at the banks; an og.Buoyancy body in it drifts with that current and floats at its level (computed in the tick, the same on every run). Where the course drops steeper than 45 degrees the water falls, a sheet streaked white, and the pool below it churns white for some three widths. 0: none.

riverSpeed.description: The river's current mid-stream; it slows to nothing at the banks.

segments.description: Grid cells per side (the height field's detail).

shallow.description: Shallow water's colour (tints what is seen through it).

depthFade.description: The depth over which water turns from shallow to deep.

absorption.description: How much of each colour the water absorbs per metre of light's path through it (1/m; pure sea water about 0.45 0.07 0.03, the red gone in a few metres). With absorption or scattering set, the water's body is physical: what lies below is dimmed by the path the light takes down to it and back up to the eye, and the water scatters the sun and sky it lets in back out, so shallows over sand turn turquoise and deep water dark blue-green by themselves; shallow, deep, depthFade and opacity are then unused. 0 0 0 with scattering 0 0 0: shallow and deep.

scattering.description: How much of each colour the water scatters per metre (1/m; clear ocean about 0.002 0.004 0.008, a silty coast ten times that). See absorption.

foamWidth.description: The water depth over which foam rings geometry (0: none).

waveSpeed.description: How fast the detail waves travel.

waveStrength.description: How strongly they bend the surface (0: a mirror).

refraction.description: How far refraction shifts what is seen through the water.

planarReflection.description: Reflect the scene by drawing it again from the camera mirrored in the surface, at this fraction of the screen's resolution (0: off, the screen-space and sky reflections). One surface a frame, the first that asks (a grid surface before one over a mesh), or two with RenderOptions.planarReflections 2 (the second while it is in view); each costs about a second scene pass at that resolution.

shadows.description: How much the sun's shadows darken the surface: its highlight, foam and colour (0: none).

f0.description: The reflectance looking straight down (Schlick's F0): 0.02 for clean water; three.js Water.js reflects at least 0.3.

reflectionBias.description: A floor under the reflected colour: bias + (1 - bias) times the reflection (three.js Water.js: 0.1).

underwaterColor.description: With the camera below the surface: the water's fog colour.

underwaterDensity.description: Its fog per metre (0: no underwater view). Below the surface the frame's fog becomes the water's, and the surface seen from below shows the sky inside Snell's window.

caustics.description: Caustics of the sunlight on everything below the surface (0: none). One surface a frame, the first that has them.

normalMap.description: Ripples from a tangent-space normal map (linear; red along +x, green along +z, blue up, as three.js' water normals) instead of the travelling waves: with flow 0, four layers drifting at three.js Water's rates over the world's xz times normalScale (its getNoise); with a flow, two layers sliding along it over the mesh's uv (or the grid's metres), cross-faded each 0.15 of a cycle (three.js Water2: then refraction 1 shifts the scene behind by N.xz · 0.05 of the screen, the reflection is tinted by shallow too, and there is no sun highlight). waveStrength scales the slopes (1: as the map), waveSpeed the lake's clock. 0: the travelling waves.

normalScale.description: The normal map's repeats per metre (the lake) or per uv unit (a flow).

glint.description: three.js Water's sun glint: pow(eye . reflect(-sun, normal), 100) times the sun's light times this, on the reflected image, through the Fresnel term (three.js: spec × sunColor over the light's intensity). With glint the surface is three.js Water.js throughout: deep is its waterColor, the body (sunColor · max(L·N, 0) · sunColor · 0.15 + waterColor · max(N·V, 0)) shaded by the ripples and the shadows, sunColor = the light × glint / 2. 0: the default half-vector highlight and depth colour.

flow.description: Water2's flow: its direction in the mesh's uv (or the grid's x, z) and, as its length, the uv it slides per second. 0 0: the lake's four drifting layers. Without a normalMap a flow carries the travelling waves, in metres a second: a river.

flowMap.description: three.js Water2's flowMap: the flow's direction per point as rg * 2 - 1 (linear; the image's top at v 1), over the mesh's uv or the grid from its -x -z corner (u along x, v along z). With it flow's length is the speed (three.js' flowSpeed; 0 0: its 0.03) and the map the direction, for the normal map's two layers or, without one, the travelling waves: a stream that bends round rocks. 0: the flow alone.

wind.description: The wind over an open sea, its direction in the world's xz and its speed in m/s as its length: the grid rises in a sum of Gerstner waves of a fully developed sea for that wind (Pierson–Moskowitz; at 10 m/s waves about 80 m long and a significant height of 2.1 m), over the world's xz (a level surface), with og.physics.waterHeight reading the tick's waves in the tick. A mesh surface has none. The sea is drawn as a clipmap about the camera, finest under it, from a seeded JONSWAP spectrum transformed on the GPU each frame at the tick's time (up to three tiles of 256² by the graphics quality) over the tick's longest waves, which it draws as they are: the waves a floating body rides are the ones drawn, the shorter ones the GPU's alone (rendering only; never read back). Within size (centred on the entity) unless endless. The detail waves (waveStrength) fade where a pixel cannot hold them. Whitecaps foam where the crests fold. 0 0: no sea.

swell.description: The sea's height, as a fraction of a fully developed sea's for the wind.

choppiness.description: How far the sea's crests lean and sharpen (Gerstner steepness): 0 round swell, 1 the most that never folds over. Whitecaps foam where the crests bunch, by as much.

endless.description: A sea (wind) to the horizon all round the camera, wherever it goes, not only within size: its waves stay where they are in the world. false: the sea ends at the size rectangle (a bay, a lake in a gale).

seabed.description: The og.Terrain entity whose heights are the sea's floor (0: none, the open sea everywhere): the sea feels the depth over it, each wave fading where the water is shallower than half its length and the whole held under its breaking height (a significant height of 0.78 times the depth), so it never runs through a beach; trains of waves roll in parallel to the shore and break into surf (shore, shoreFoam). og.physics.waterHeight and og.Buoyancy read the same shoaled sea: a boat in the shallows rides what is drawn there. Read when the water, the terrain's placement or its edits change.

shore.description: How high the trains rolling in on the seabed's shores are, times a quarter of the sea's significant height (0: none; the waves still shoal).

shoreWaveLength.description: The trains' length from crest to crest (0: 40 m).

shoreFoam.description: How much surf foams where the trains break and the water runs shallow over the seabed (0: none).

foamStreaks.description: How strongly a sea's ageing foam is drawn into streaks along the wind (0: none): a whitecap's dense foam bursts within seconds and leaves a thin lace that lasts some ten seconds, which the surface's convergence along the wind (Langmuir circulation, about 1 % of the wind's speed) gathers into windrows. Rendering only.

meniscus.description: Where the camera's near plane crosses the surface (a camera bobbing at the waterline), the width in pixels of the meniscus drawn along the line between the air above and the water's fog below it, each pixel under the surface or not as the waves are there (as og.physics.waterHeight puts them); 0: the line with no meniscus; below 0: no waterline, the whole frame above or under the water as the eye is. Needs underwaterDensity.

dynamicWaves.description: How high the waves an og.Buoyancy hull raises on a sea are drawn (0: none): a hull presses the water down by its draft, and as it moves it throws a bow wave and leaves a Kelvin wake (the 19.5 degree wedge of transverse and diverging waves deep water makes behind any moving body), with foam where those crests break and along its sides, all running at deep water's own speeds within some 64 m of the camera. Rendering only: the tick floats every hull on the sea's own waves and never sees these.

spray.description: How much spray a sea's breaking crests throw (0: none): droplets torn off where the foam is freshest and the crests steepest, carried by the wind and falling back, more of them as the wind rises past a moderate breeze. Rendering only; the tick never sees them.

Water2D.description: Draws the og.WaterLine on the same entity in the sprite order: the body from its surface down, a gradient from the top colour to the bottom one, and a bright lip along the surface.

top.description: The body's colour at the surface.

lipWidth.description: How thick the lip is (0: none).

layer.description: The sprite layer it is drawn in.

SkeletonAsset.description: A rig: a glTF's nodes in topological order with their rest transforms, and its skins (joints and inverse bind matrices).

ClipAsset.description: An animation clip, resampled at the cook's rate, with its markers.

GraphAsset.description: A blend-tree graph (`type animgraph`) whose clip references were resolved to clip handles.

RootMotion.description: What the root joint's motion does to the entity.

x-og-variants.off: The root animates in place; the entity does not move.
x-og-variants.planar: The root's horizontal (xz) travel and yaw move og.Transform.
x-og-variants.full: The root's whole translation and rotation move og.Transform.

x-og-variants.clips: The playing clips' weight channels write them.

IkSolver.description: How an IK chain is solved.

x-og-variants.twoBone: Analytic two-bone (thigh, shin, foot), bending towards the pole.

IkSpace.description: What an IK chain's target and pole are relative to.

x-og-variants.world: Positions in the frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is written in (its position, rotation and scale are undone): true world for a skeleton entity without a parent, its parent's frame for a child (a body under a character capsule takes targets relative to the capsule; transform world points by the parent's inverse yourself).

Skeleton.description: A posed skeleton: the entity is drawn skinned by the joint palette og.anim writes each tick. The pose itself (every node's local transform) is world state kept by the `og.anim` state block.

skin.description: Which of the asset's skins the joint palette is for (glTF skin index).

rootMotion.description: Root motion extraction: off (animate in place), planar (xz travel and yaw move og.Transform) or full.

rootJoint.description: The joint whose motion is extracted (an index into the skin's joints; 0 is its first joint, usually the hips).

jointCount.description: Written: the number of joints in the palette (0 until the first tick).

CrowdAnimation.description:
Plays a clip on a model on the GPU, for crowds: put it on an entity with og.Model (and no og.Skeleton, which og.anim would pose on the CPU instead) and the model is drawn skinned by `clip` baked into joint palettes, shared by every entity playing the same clip on the same skeleton. Each entity costs no animation work on the CPU, so thousands can walk at once; the price is that nothing reads the pose (no markers, root motion, IK, blendshapes or attachments to joints) and a change of `clip` cuts without a fade.
The clip's time is `offset` plus `speed` times the world's time, so give each member of a crowd its own `offset` to keep them out of step. It is drawn only: it never feeds back into the simulation, and TAA gets its motion vectors from the frame before. The camera culls each entity by its bounds on the CPU, as a model posed by og.anim; crowds do not go through GPU culling or the meshlet path yet.

skeleton.description: The skeleton asset of the model (og.load.animation's `skeleton`); 0 draws nothing posed.

skin.description: Which of the skeleton's skins poses the model (glTF skin index).

clip.description: The clip played (og.load.animation's `clips`); 0 holds the rest pose.

offset.description: Seconds into the clip at the world's time 0.

speed.description: Playback rate (1 = as authored, negative plays backwards).

loop.description: Wrap at the end of the clip; otherwise hold its last frame.

rate.description: Frames per second the clip is baked at (the GPU blends between them): more is smoother and costs more memory, `rate` × the clip's seconds × its joints × 64 bytes, once per clip.

AnimationPlayer.description: Plays one clip on a skeleton. Alone it poses the skeleton from its rest pose; with an og.AnimationGraph it plays over the graph's result with `weight`. Changing `clip` cross-fades from the previous one over `fade`; a clip change starts the new clip at 0 (or at `time` if the game wrote it in the same tick).

time.description: The playback position; written every tick, set it to seek (no markers fire across a seek).

speed.description: Playback rate (1 = as authored, negative plays backwards).

loop.description: Wrap at the end of the clip; otherwise hold the last frame and set `finished`.

weight.description: How much of the pose this player decides (0 = none, 1 = all).

stepFps.description: Stepped playback: each pose is held for 1/stepFps seconds, the clip sampled at its time floored to that step (12 is stop motion "on twos", 8 on threes), the same on every tick rate; 0 samples every tick. `time`, markers and root motion stay continuous; a one-shot still ends on its last frame.

finished.description: Written: a non-looping clip reached its end.

AnimationGraph.description: Runs a blend-tree graph (og.anim.graph) on a skeleton: its layers' state machines pick motions by the parameters p0...p7, which the graph names in `param` order (`param speed` is p0, the next `param` is p1, ...).

weight.description: How much of the pose the graph decides over the rest pose.

speed.description: A playback-rate multiplier for every layer.

state.description: Written: the base layer's current state (its index in the graph file).

stateTime.description: Written: seconds since the base layer entered `state`.

Blendshapes.description: Morph-target weights of the skeleton entity's mesh, in the order of the glTF mesh's targets, up to 64 targets (w0...w7, then `influences`). With `source` clips the playing clips' weight channels write them; with `component` game code does. Under TAA a morphing mesh has motion vectors from its previous weights, so a talking face does not ghost.

source.description: Who decides the weights: component (game code writes w0...w7) or clips (the animation writes them).

mesh.description: The glTF mesh index whose targets the weights drive (0 is the first mesh).

influences.description: Weights of targets 8 to 63, as three.js morphTargetInfluences past the first eight (w0...w7): influences[k] drives target 8 + k; past the list's length 0. A face rig's 52 ARKit shapes fit. Clips write it with `source` clips, as they write w0...w7.

IkChain.description: An inverse-kinematics constraint on a skeleton, applied after its clips and graph: the chain of `bones` bones ending at joint `tip` turns so the tip reaches `target`. Put it on its own entity (a skeleton can have many chains); chains apply in query order.

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton this chain bends.

tip.description: The end joint (an index into the skin's joints): the foot or the hand.

bones.description: How many bones above the tip turn (two-bone always uses 2).

solver.description: twoBone (analytic, with a pole) or fabrik (iterative, any length).

target.description: Where the tip should be, in `space`: for `world`, the frame of the skeleton entity's og.Transform (its parent's frame when it has a parent, not true world).

pole.description: A point the middle joint bends towards (two-bone); the zero vector keeps the animated bend.

space.description: What `target` and `pole` are relative to: world (the frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is in, so its parent's frame for a child entity, not true world) or model.

weight.description: How much of the solved rotation is applied (0 = the animated pose, 1 = fully solved).

tolerance.description: The tip distance (model units) at which the target counts as reached.

reached.description: Written: the tip is within `tolerance` of the target after solving.

error.description: Written: the tip's distance from the target after solving, in model units.

LookAt.description: An aim constraint on a skeleton, applied after its clips, graph and IK chains: `joint` turns so its `axis` points at `target` and its `upAxis` leans towards `up` (three.js Object3D.lookAt: +Z at the target, +Y up). The direction is held within maxYaw and maxPitch of the animated forward; with `bones` above 1 the joint's parents share the turn. Put it on its own entity (a head, the eyes, a turret's barrel); constraints apply in query order, and og.JointLimit clamps the joints it turns.

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton this constraint turns.

joint.description: The joint that aims (an index into the skin's joints): the head, an eye.

bones.description: How many joints share the turn: `joint` and its parents (3 spreads a look over neck, chest and spine), each parent taking an even share and `joint` the rest.

target.description: The point to look at, in `space`.

space.description: What `target` and `up` are relative to: world (the frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is in) or model.

axis.description: The joint's forward, in its own frame: the axis turned onto the target.

upAxis.description: The joint's up, in its own frame: yaw turns about it, pitch towards it, and it rolls towards `up`.

up.description: The up hint, a direction in `space` the joint's `upAxis` leans to (three.js Object3D.up); the zero vector keeps the animated roll.

maxYaw.description: The largest turn about `upAxis`, left or right of the animated forward.

maxPitch.description: The largest turn towards or away from `upAxis`, from the animated forward.

weight.description: How much of the turn is applied (0 = the animated pose, 1 = aimed).

clamped.description: Written: the target lay outside maxYaw or maxPitch, so the joint aims at the nearest direction inside them.

JointLimit.description: How far a joint may turn from its rest rotation when og.anim's solvers (og.IkChain, og.LookAt, og.FootLock) turn it: a swing of `axis` within a cone and a twist about it within a range. A hinge (a knee, an elbow) is `axis` along the hinge, `swing` 0 (or a little play) and the bend range as twistMin...twistMax. Put it on its own entity, one per joint; the animated pose itself is never clamped.

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton whose joint this limits.

joint.description: The limited joint (an index into the skin's joints).
