axis.description: The twist axis in the joint's rest frame: along the bone for a ball joint, along the hinge for a hinge.

swing.description: The cone half-angle the axis may swing away from its rest direction (0 locks it: a hinge; pi is free).

twistMin.description: The least twist about `axis` from rest (a hinge's bend one way).

twistMax.description: The most twist about `axis` from rest (a hinge's bend the other way).

FootLock.description: Foot locking: while the playing clips plant `foot` (within 5 mm of its lowest in each clip, the notion retargeting uses, weighed across blends and cross-fades: planted when the planting clips hold at least half the pose), the foot stays where it touched the ground, through clip blends and root motion, its leg bent by two-bone IK and the foot keeping its animated orientation; when the clips lift it, the foot rejoins its animation over `release`. Put it on its own entity, one per foot; locks apply after root motion and before og.IkChain, in query order, and og.JointLimit clamps the leg. The lock is world state (the `og.anim` state block).

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton whose foot this holds.

foot.description: The foot joint (an index into the skin's joints); the two bones above it are the leg that bends.

weight.description: How much of the lock is applied (0 = the animated foot, 1 = held).

release.description: Seconds the foot takes to rejoin its animation once lifted (0: at once).

maxDistance.description: Farther than this from where the animation puts the foot, the lock lets go (a leg cannot stretch).

planted.description: Written: the playing clips plant the foot this tick.

locked.description: Written: the foot is held at its lock this tick.

SpringSpace.description: Where a spring bone's tails move.

x-og-variants.world: The frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is written in: the chain lags behind the entity's motion (walking, root motion, a jump).
x-og-variants.model: The skeleton's model space: only the animation moves the chain (a teleport or a vehicle carrying the entity does not).

SpringBone.description: A spring (jiggle) bone chain, three-vrm's VRMSpringBone: `joint` and its `bones` - 1 parents swing after their parents' motion. Each joint's tail (the next joint of the chain; for the last joint its first child, or its parent bone continued at the same length) is a point pulled towards where the animated pose puts it by a damped spring (`frequency`, `damping`), under `gravity`, held at the bone's length, and the joint turns to point at it. Applied after og.IkChain and og.LookAt, top joint first; put it on its own entity (a tail, an ear, a strand of hair, a single jiggling node), one per chain. Deterministic under the fixed tick; the tails' positions and velocities are world state (the `og.anim` state block), so a restore continues a swing exactly. A changed chain (another skeleton, length or space) restarts at the animated pose.

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton whose joints this swings.

joint.description: The chain's last joint (an index into the skin's joints): the tip of a tail, an ear.

bones.description: How many joints swing: `joint` and its parents (1 is the joint alone).

frequency.description: How fast a tail springs back to its animated place: the spring's natural frequency (0: no spring, it only hangs and swings).

damping.description: The damping ratio: 0 swings on, 1 settles without overshooting (critical damping).

tipFrequency.description: The last joint's frequency as a multiple of `frequency`, the joints between in proportion along the chain (1: every joint alike; 0.25: the tip springs back four times slower than the top, a soft strand on a stiff root).

tipDamping.description: The last joint's damping ratio as a multiple of `damping`, the joints between in proportion along the chain (1: every joint alike).

gravity.description: An acceleration on every tail, in `space` (three-vrm's gravityDir times gravityPower): (0, -9.8, 0) makes a chain droop.

space.description: Where the tails move: world (the frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is in, so the chain lags behind the entity's motion) or model (only the animation moves it).

weight.description: How much of the swing is applied (0 = the animated pose, 1 = the spring's).

radius.description: The tails' radius against og.SpringCollider (three-vrm's hitRadius): a tail stays this far outside every collider it meets (0: a point).

colliders.description: The og.SpringCollider layers the tails are pushed out of, as bits: a collider on the same skeleton counts when its `layers` meet these.

lag.description: Written: the farthest a tail is from its animated place this tick.

SpringColliderShape.description: The shape of a spring collider.

x-og-variants.capsule: A capsule of `radius` about the segment from `offset` to `tail`.

SpringCollider.description: A collider spring bones are kept out of, three-vrm's VRMSpringBoneCollider: a sphere or a capsule riding on a joint of a skeleton (a head, a chest, an upper arm), so hair, ears and tails do not swing through the body. Each tick, after a tail of an og.SpringBone of the same skeleton has stepped and before its joint turns, the tail is pushed out of every collider whose `layers` meet the spring's `colliders` (in query order) to `radius` plus the spring's `radius`, keeping its bone's length. Put it on its own entity, one per shape; colliders follow the pose as it is when a chain is swung, so one on a joint an earlier chain swung follows that swing.

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton whose spring bones this keeps out.

joint.description: The joint the collider rides on (an index into the skin's joints).

shape.description: A sphere about `offset`, or a capsule from `offset` to `tail`.

offset.description: The sphere's centre, or the capsule's first end, in the joint's frame.

tail.description: The capsule's other end, in the joint's frame (a sphere ignores it).

radius.description: The radius, in metres of the skeleton's model space (the joint's own scale does not apply).

layers.description: The layers this collider is on, as bits (a spring bone's `colliders` picks them).

AnimationEvent.description: A named marker of a clip that playback passed in the last tick (read in the tick after it fired, like every event). Cross-fades and blends fire every contributing clip's markers.

clip.description: The clip asset the marker belongs to.

name.description: The marker's name (at most 63 bytes).

time.description: The marker's time in the clip.

weight.description: The clip's blend weight when it fired.

ClipInfo.description: One clip of a loaded animation.

name.description: The glTF animation's name.

markers.description: Its markers' names, in time order.

Animation.description: What og.load.animation registered from a model's `#anim` blob.

nodes.description: The rig's node names, in topological order.

skins.description: Each skin's joint count, in glTF order.

morphTargets.description: Morph targets across the model's meshes.

text.description: The graph's `.ogt` text (`type animgraph`, `version 1`; og-anim §5 has every line).

clips.description: The clips a `clip <motion> "<name>"` line may name, by ClipInfo.name: usually og.load.animation's `clips`.

Rig.description: A humanoid map from og.load.rig (a cooked `.ogt` of `type rig`): the naming scheme a skeleton's node names follow, the standard bones it names outright and, with `footHeight`, how high its ankles stand above the ground.

HumanBone.description: One standard humanoid bone of a skeleton.

bone.description: The standard bone: hips, spine, chest, upperChest, neck, head, then leftShoulder, leftUpperArm, leftLowerArm, leftHand, the right arm, leftUpperLeg, leftLowerLeg, leftFoot, leftToes and the right leg, then each hand's fingers (VRM 1.0 names): leftThumbMetacarpal, leftThumbProximal, leftThumbDistal, leftIndexProximal, leftIndexIntermediate, leftIndexDistal, the same for Middle, Ring and Little, and the right hand's.

node.description: The skeleton node that is that bone.

Humanoid.description: Which node of a skeleton is each standard humanoid bone (what retargeting maps).

scheme.description: The naming scheme the bones were read in: mixamo, vrm, unity, rigify, ue, blender or soma; custom when a rig named them, none when nothing matched.

bones.description: The bones found, in the standard order (hips first).

HumanoidDesc.description: A skeleton and, optionally, the rig that says how its bones are named.

rig.description: A humanoid map from og.load.rig; 0 detects the bones from the node names (Mixamo, VRM, Unity, Rigify, Unreal, Blender or SOMA names).

RetargetDesc.description: A clip made for one skeleton, to play on another (other proportions, rest pose or bone names).

source.description: The skeleton the clip was made for (og.load.animation's `skeleton`: a character's, or an animation library's).

target.description: The skeleton that will play it.

sourceRig.description: How the source's bones are named (og.load.rig); 0 detects them.

targetRig.description: How the target's bones are named; 0 detects them.

footIk.description: Solve the legs so a planted foot stays planted on the target's ground (and the hips lower when a leg cannot reach).

MirrorDesc.description: A clip to play on the other side of the skeleton it was made for.

skeleton.description: The skeleton the clip was made for (og.load.animation's `skeleton`); its left and right nodes are paired by name, the side tokens every rig naming scheme writes swapped (LeftArm and RightArm, thigh.L and thigh.R, J_Bip_L_ and J_Bip_R_, calf_l and calf_r).

FlipbookSheet.description: A sprite sheet's frames and clips (a cooked `.ogt` of `type flipbook`), from og.load.flipbook.

FlipMode.description: How a flipbook clip runs past its last frame.

x-og-variants.pingPong: Back and forth, without repeating the end frames.
x-og-variants.once: Hold the last frame and set Flipbook.finished.

Flipbook.description:
Plays a clip of a flipbook sheet on the entity's og.Sprite: extraction draws the sprite with the sheet's texture and the current frame's region and pivot, or, for an `array true` sheet, the frame's layer of its texture array whole (the sprite keeps its size, colour, flips and layer). Played by the engine's og.flipbook system by scaled time (Time.scaledDt: slow motion, hit stop), after the game's systems.
Changing clip restarts at the clip's first frame (or at `time`, written in the same tick); writing a different time is a seek. Frame events are og.FlipbookEvent. The playback position is world state (the og.flipbook state block).

clip.description: The clip: an index into FlipbookInfo.clips (og.anim.clip finds one by name).

speed.description: The playback rate: 1 as authored, 2 twice as fast, 0 holds the frame.

frame.description: Written: the clip frame shown (an index into the clip's frames).

time.description: Seconds into the current cycle; written every tick, set it to seek (no events fire across a seek).

finished.description: Written: a `once` clip reached and holds its last frame.

loops.description: Written: cycles completed by a looping or ping-pong clip.

FlipbookEvent.description: A flipbook entered a frame its clip names in an `event` line (`event 2 "step"`): footsteps, the frame a hit lands, a pickup's sparkle. Read in the tick after, like every event; a clip started at 0 fires its first frame's events.

name.description: The event's name (at most 63 bytes).

FlipbookClipInfo.description: One clip of a loaded flipbook sheet.

name.description: Its name in the sheet.

duration.description: Seconds of one cycle (a ping-pong cycle goes there and back).

mode.description: How it runs past its end.

events.description: Its events' names, in frame order.

texture.description: The sheet's texture (loaded with it; sampled nearest unless the sheet says `filter linear`); 0 for an `array true` sheet.

array.description: An `array true` sheet's texture array (its frames as layers, loaded with it); 0 otherwise.

frameWidth.description: The first frame's width in pixels.

frameHeight.description: The first frame's height in pixels.

Rig2D.description: A 2D rig (a cooked `.ogt` of `type rig2d`): bones, slots, region, mesh, bounding-box and child-armature attachments, IK constraints, child armatures and clips, from og.load.rig2d.

Skeleton2D.description:
Plays a clip of a 2D rig at the entity: the og.skeleton2d system advances it by scaled time (Time.scaledDt) after the game's systems and fires its events as og.Skeleton2DEvent; extraction draws its slots, in their order, as textured triangles of the sprite batch at `layer` (region attachments as quads, mesh attachments weighted to bones and deformed by the clip), lit by og.Lighting2D when the layer is in its range, as a sprite there is. The rig's pixels are `unit` to a world unit and +y is up; the entity's og.Transform places, turns (about z) and scales it.
Changing `clip` restarts at 0 (or at `time`, written in the same tick); writing a different time is a seek and fires no events. The pose is a function of these fields, the Transform and the og.IkTarget2D on it; the playback position is world state (the og.skeleton2d state block).

clip.description: The clip: an index into Rig2DInfo.clips (og.anim.clip finds one by name).

time.description: Seconds into the clip; written every tick, set it to seek.

speed.description: The playback rate: 1 as authored, 2 twice as fast, negative backwards.

loop.description: Wrap at the clip's end; otherwise hold the last pose and set `finished`. Rig2DInfo.clips says what the rig's author meant.

flipX.description: Mirror the rig left to right about the entity's position (a character facing left).

layer.description: The sprite layer it draws in, sorted with the sprites there (after them when they share the layer).

skin.description: The skin it wears: an index into Rig2DInfo.skins (0 is the rig's default; `rig.skins.indexOf("armor")` finds one by name). A skin shows its own attachment wherever the setup pose or a clip shows the default's; a slot the skin leaves alone shows the default's. Change it any tick: the pose is drawn from it.

finished.description: Written: a clip that does not loop reached its end (or its start, played backwards).

Skeleton2DEvent.description: A 2D skeleton's clip, or the clip a child armature in one of its slots plays, passed one of its events (`event 0.2 "step"` in the rig) in the last tick: footsteps, the frame a swing lands. Read in the tick after, like every event; a clip started at 0 fires its events at 0, a looping clip fires each once per pass.

name.description: The event's name (at most 63 bytes).

time.description: The event's time in the clip.

armature.description: Empty for the skeleton's own clip; for an event of a child armature shown in one of its slots, that armature's name (`clip` and `time` are then the child's clip and its time): a flame's crackle apart from the keeper's footsteps (at most 63 bytes).

IkTarget2D.description: Moves one IK constraint of a 2D skeleton (Rig2DInfo.constraints) to a point: a foot planted on the ground under it, a hand on a ledge, a tail's tip. A constraint is a chain of any length: one bone points at the target, two are solved exactly (bending the way the rig says), three or more by FABRIK from the animated pose, curling the way the rig says. Put it on its own entity, one per constraint; og.skeleton2d writes `reached` and `error`, and the drawn pose solves the same way.

constraint.description: The constraint: an index into Rig2DInfo.constraints.

target.description: Where the chain's tip should be, in the frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is written in (the world for an entity without a parent).

weight.description: How much of the solve applies (0 is the animated pose, 1 fully solved), times the constraint's own weight (its `weight` line, or its clip's IK keys).

tolerance.description: The distance at which the target counts as reached.

reached.description: Written: the tip is within `tolerance` of the target after solving.

error.description: Written: the tip's distance from the target after solving (for a one-bone constraint, how far the target lies off the bone's line).

Rig2DClipInfo.description: One clip of a loaded 2D rig.

name.description: Its name in the rig.

loop.description: Whether the rig's author meant it to loop (its `loop` line): copy it into Skeleton2D.loop.

events.description: Its events' names, in time order.

Rig2DInfo.description: What og.load.rig2d registered, or og.anim.rig2dInfo reads back from a handle.

texture.description: The rig's texture (loaded with it).

unit.description: Pixels of the rig per world unit.

slots.description: The slots' names, in draw order.

constraints.description: The IK constraints' names: an index here is IkTarget2D.constraint.

skins.description: Its skins' names, `default` (the rig's own attachments) first: an index here is Skeleton2D.skin.

Skeleton2DBox.description: A bounding box a 2D skeleton's pose shows: a `box` attachment of its rig (or of a child armature in one of its slots) while its slot shows it.

slot.description: The slot showing it (`slot/child-slot` inside a child armature).

name.description: The box's name in the rig.

points.description: Its polygon, moved by its bones (IK included), in the frame the skeleton entity's og.Transform is written in (the world for an entity without a parent).

Ease.description: An easing curve from the start (0) to the end (1). In starts slow, out ends slow, inOut both. back overshoots, elastic rings, bounce bounces at the end.

x-og-variants.quadOut: Gentle ease out: the default for most motion.
x-og-variants.linear: Constant speed: scrolling, timers, colour cycles.
x-og-variants.cubicOut: Ease out: UI sliding in, things settling.
x-og-variants.cubicInOut: In and out: camera moves, deliberate motion.
x-og-variants.expoIn: Exponential ease in: things falling away, warp-outs.
x-og-variants.backIn: Pulls back first, then goes: anticipation.
x-og-variants.backOut: Overshoots, then settles: pops, squash recovery, buttons.
x-og-variants.elasticOut: Rings after arriving: springy, cartoon impacts.
x-og-variants.bounceOut: Bounces at the end: drops, landings.

entity.description: The entity whose component is tweened.

component.description: The component token (og.Transform, og.Sprite, a game's own); null is og.Transform.

field.description: The field, or one lane of it: `position`, `position.y`, `scale`, `color.r`, `opacity`. f32, f64, i32 and u32 fields (rounded), vectors, colours and quaternions (as a rotation) tween; bool, enum and handle fields do not.

to.description: The end value: one number for a scalar or for every lane, or one per lane.

from.description: The start value, written from the tick the tween is started and held through its delay; null takes the field's value when the tween starts (after its delay).

relative.description: `to` is added to the start value.

duration.description: Seconds from start to end (one cycle).

loops.description: Extra cycles: 0 plays once, n repeats n more times, -1 forever.

yoyo.description: Every other cycle plays backwards (pulses, bobbing).

unscaled.description: Advance by real ticks, ignoring Time.scale and hit stop (UI motion).

tag.description: A number of yours, carried by og.TweenCompleted.

TweenGroupDesc.description: How a sequence or parallel group runs.

loops.description: Extra runs of the whole group: 0 once, -1 forever; each run replays the spans its tweens resolved in the first.

unscaled.description: Advance by real ticks, ignoring Time.scale and hit stop.

tag.description: A number of yours, carried by og.TweenCompleted.

TweenCompleted.description: A tween or group ended on its own (read in the tick after).

tween.description: The handle og.tween.to, sequence, parallel, squash or flash answered.

SquashDesc.description: Squash and stretch: the entity's og.Transform.scale jumps to rest times impact and eases back to rest.

impact.description: The x, y and z factors at the impact: (1.25, 0.8) squashes (a landing, a hit), (0.8, 1.25) stretches (a jump). z is for 3D models (a squash bulges in x and z: (1.15, 0.85, 1.15)); left out or 0 it stays at rest, so a sprite's { x, y } is unchanged. A component left out takes its default: x 1.25, y 0.8, z 0; under a project's art contract, ArtMotion.squash scales it (0.5 the same, 1 rubber hose: x 1.5, y 0.6).

ease.description: The recovery curve; backOut overshoots a little, elasticOut wobbles.

FlashDesc.description: A hit flash: the entity's og.Sprite (else og.Mesh, else og.Model) flashColor set and its flash faded from amount to 0.

color.description: The flash colour (white for a hit, red for damage taken).

amount.description: How far it starts towards the colour.

ease.description: The fade's curve; quadIn holds the flash, then drops it.

TilemapAsset.description: A loaded map: its layers, tilesets and objects.

Tilemap.description: Draws a loaded map with its top-left corner at the entity's position (z included) and gives its collision layers static colliders. The og.tilemap system adopts it in the first tick it exists: from then on og.tilemap.setTile and getTile reach it.

layer.description: The sprite layer of the map's layer 0; every layer draws at this plus its z (default: its index).

color.description: A linear tint.

collision.description: Give the layers marked collision static colliders (rectangles merged from the solid tiles).

colliderLayers.description: The collision layers of those colliders, as bits (Collider.layers), for every collision layer of the map that names none of its own (a map layer's `colliderLayers`, with its `colliderMask`, puts a layer of grates on a one-way layer while the walls stay here).

palette.description: A palette swap of every layer (og.Sprite.palette): the tile sets' index textures (the cook's `<id>#index`) drawn through row paletteRow of this texture of N rows; 0 is none.

paletteRow.description: The row of `palette` drawn (past the last, the last).

TileOrientation.description: How a map's cells are laid out (Tiled's orientations).

x-og-variants.isometric: Diamonds on a turned grid: x runs down to the right, y down to the left, cell 0 0 at the top.
x-og-variants.staggered: Diamonds in rows half a tile apart, every odd row shifted right half a tile (Tiled's staggered, odd rows).
x-og-variants.hex: Pointy-top hexagons with corners at a quarter of the tile, rows 3/4 of a tile apart, every odd row shifted right half a tile (Tiled's hexagonal, stagger axis y, odd, side half the tile's height).
x-og-variants.hexFlat: Flat-top hexagons, columns 3/4 of a tile apart, every odd column shifted down half a tile (stagger axis x).

name.description: Its name.

index.description: Its index (what drawing order and z start from).

parallax.description: Its scroll factors: 1 1 moves with the world, 0.5 at half the camera's speed (far away), 0 stays with the camera.

colliderLayers.description: The collision layers (og.Collider.layers bits) of its colliders, from its `colliderLayers` line or Tiled int property; 0 (unset) takes Tilemap.colliderLayers.

colliderMask.description: The layers its colliders collide with (og.Collider.mask bits), from its `colliderMask` line or Tiled int property; 0 (unset) is every layer.

cellColliders.description: Off the orthogonal grid, whether each solid cell collides on its own (a diamond or hexagon per cell, from its `cellColliders` line or Tiled bool property) rather than each connected solid region as one collider, its outline (the default: a static map costs physics per region, not per cell).

terrain.description: The auto-tiling terrain of a terrain layer (its cells are 1 filled or 0 empty); empty for a tile layer.

lit.description: Whether og.Lighting2D lights it when its sprite layer is in the lit range (true unless the Tiled layer's bool property `lit` or the `.ogt` layer's `lit` line says false).

TileObject.description: An object of a map (a Tiled object, an LDtk entity, an `object` block): spawn points, doors, triggers.

name.description: Its name.

position.description: Its top-left corner, in world units relative to the map's top-left corner (y up, so below the corner is negative).

size.description: Its width and height (0 0 for a point).

center.description: Its centre, relative to the map's corner.

tileWidth.description: A cell's width in world units.

tileHeight.description: A cell's height in world units.

layers.description: Its layers, drawing order.

orientation.description: How its cells are laid out.

TileLayerDesc.description: One layer of a map og.tilemap.create makes (empty).

name.description: Its name (unique in the map).

tileset.description: The index of its tileset in TilemapDesc.tilesets.

terrain.description: An auto-tiling terrain of that tileset: a terrain layer (cells 1 or 0); empty for a tile layer.

colliderMask.description: The layers its colliders collide with (0: every layer).

cellColliders.description: Off the orthogonal grid, one collider per solid cell (a diamond or hexagon) instead of one per connected solid region (its outline, the default).

TilemapDesc.description: A map to make at run time: empty layers on tilesets the bundle cooked.

tileWidth.description: A tile's width in pixels (its cell's).

tileHeight.description: A tile's height in pixels (its cell's; half the width for the usual isometric diamond).

orientation.description: How the cells are laid out.

tilesets.description: The tilesets' asset ids (tileset `.ogt` files, such as `tiles/dungeon.ogt`).

layers.description: The layers, drawing order.

ResizeDesc.description: A new size for a map, and where its cells go.

x.description: Where the old cell 0 0 lands: columns added on the left (negative crops them).

y.description: Rows added at the top (negative crops them).

tile.description: A tile layer: the tile id, -1 empty. A terrain layer: 1 fills, 0 clears, and the neighbours re-tile.

inside.description: Whether the point was on the map.

FillDesc.description: A block of cells to write at once: a generated grid (og.procgen's BSP cells or WFC tiles mapped to tile ids).

width.description: The block's width in cells: `tiles` is row-major, `width` per row.

tiles.description: The cells, as og.tilemap.setTile's `tile`: a tile id or -1 on a tile layer, 1 or 0 on a terrain layer (re-tiled once, after every cell is written).

AudioBus.description: The bus a source plays on; every bus passes through master.

x-og-variants.master: The master bus: what every bus passes through.

PanningModel.description: How an AudioListener places spatial sources between the ears, as Web Audio's PannerNode.panningModel.

x-og-variants.equalpower: The stereo panner (Web Audio's equal-power law): for speakers.
x-og-variants.hrtf: For headphones: a spherical-head model (Brown and Duda, 1998) that delays the far ear by the interaural time difference (up to 0.66 ms) and shadows its highs (up to -20 dB), so a source moves between the ears; front and back, up and down are not told apart (no pinna).

AudioResampler.description: How the mixer resamples a voice whose pitch or sound rate differs from the output's.

x-og-variants.linear: Linear interpolation: the engine's mix before round 4, cheaper, with duller highs (-3.4 dB at 15 kHz from 44.1 kHz) and images (-11.5 dB there).
x-og-variants.sinc: A Kaiser-windowed sinc (beta 7, 16 taps, 2048 phases; widened up to 64 taps for a voice pitched up to 4x): flat to the highs, images below -70 dB.

AudioSource.description:
A sound an entity plays. Level-triggered: while `playing` is true it plays (inserting a source plays it), setting it false stops it, and a one-shot that reaches its end sets it back to false and sends og.SoundEnded.
A one-shot of F frames at rate R and pitch p started in tick S ends in tick S + ceil(F * tickRate / (R * p)) - 1. A despawned entity's voice is silenced without an event.

sound.description: The sound, from og.load.sound; 0 plays nothing. A handle not yet loaded waits and starts on the first tick it is there.

pitch.description: Playback rate: 2 is an octave up and half as long.

pan.description: Stereo position of a non-spatial source, -1 left to 1 right.

loop.description: Loop between loopStart and loopEnd, seamlessly.

loopEnd.description: Where a loop wraps; 0 is the sound's end.

spatial.description: Attenuate and pan by the entity's world transform (its og.Transform down og.Parent) relative to the listener.

refDistance.description: Full volume up to this distance, as Web Audio's PannerNode.refDistance.

maxDistance.description: No quieter past this distance, as Web Audio's PannerNode.maxDistance.

rolloffFactor.description: How fast volume falls with distance, in Web Audio's inverse model: ref / (ref + rolloff * (clamp(d, ref, max) - ref)).

playing.description: Plays while true; the engine sets it false when a one-shot ends.

priority.description: When more than Audio.maxVoices would play, the lowest priority is stopped first (then the quietest, then the oldest), with SoundEnded reason SOUND_CULLED.

lowpass.description: A low-pass filter on this source, its cutoff; 0 is off.

occlude.description: A spatial source behind a collider (a physics ray to the listener) plays at Audio.occlusionGain through a low-pass at Audio.occlusionCutoff.

distanceCutoff.description: A spatial source's low-pass by distance: the cutoff at maxDistance, from 20 kHz at refDistance (log-linear between); 0 is off.

startAt.description: Starts at this world time (seconds since tick 0), to the sample, even inside a tick; 0 or a time past starts at once. Music.nextBar and Music.nextBeat give musical times.

startOffset.description: Where in the sound it starts, in seconds of the sound: started at startAt (or at once) from this far in, to the sample and at full gain, so a resumed phrase continues instead of restarting. Past a one-shot's end it plays nothing; a loop wraps into its region.

fade.description: Starts, stops and volume changes ramp over this long: a crossfade is one source stopped and another started with the same fade; 0 is 5 ms.

dopplerFactor.description: Doppler: how much a spatial source's and the listener's motion along the line between them shifts its pitch, from their tick velocities (world positions down og.Parent): pitch times (c - DF * vListener) / (c - DF * vSource), c being Audio.speedOfSound and DF this times AudioListener.dopplerFactor (OpenAL's model). 1 is physical, 0 is off. A jump at or past the speed of sound in a tick is a teleport and shifts nothing; DF * v is held within c/2, so the shift stays within a factor of 3.

coneInnerAngle.description: Directivity, as three.js PositionalAudio.setDirectionalCone and Web Audio's PannerNode: a spatial source plays at full volume while the listener is within this full angle about the source's +Z (its world transform's, three.js's PositionalAudio orientation); 360 with coneOuterAngle 360 is omnidirectional.

coneOuterAngle.description: Past this full angle about the source's +Z it plays at coneOuterGain; between coneInnerAngle and this the gain falls linearly with the angle.

virtualize.description: Past Audio.maxVoices it goes virtual instead of being culled: silent, its playhead running on (a one-shot still ends on its tick), and heard again from where it would be, fading in, once it stands within the cap. Without it the source is culled (SOUND_CULLED, playing false).

retrigger.description: Set true to start the sound again from the top (its startOffset, its startAt) this tick, playing or not, without a level change on `playing`: the voice playing ends (SOUND_RETRIGGERED) and a new one starts in the same tick. The engine sets it back to false and `playing` true.

userBus.description: A user bus of the bus graph (4 to 15, declared by an og.AudioBusNode) it plays into instead of `bus`; 0, or an index no node declares, plays on `bus`.

AudioListener.description: Where spatial sources are heard from: the entity's world transform (its og.Transform down og.Parent, so a listener under a camera rig hears from the rig), looking down its -Z with +X to the right. The first listener in query order is used.

volume.description: A gain on every spatial source this listener hears.

dopplerFactor.description: Scales every spatial source's Doppler shift (AudioSource.dopplerFactor); 0 turns Doppler off for this listener.

panningModel.description: How spatial sources are placed between the ears: equalpower (speakers) or hrtf (headphones). Non-spatial sources keep their pan either way; the stereo path is unchanged while it is equalpower.

Audio.description: Bus volumes; master scales every bus. A change ramps over 256 frames in the mixer.

master.description: Gain of the master bus, applied to every sound.

maxVoices.description: The most sources that play at once; past it the lowest AudioSource.priority is stopped (SoundEnded reason SOUND_CULLED).

occlusionGain.description: The gain of an occluded source (AudioSource.occlude).

occlusionCutoff.description: The low-pass cutoff of an occluded source.

reverbRoom.description: The shared reverb's room size (the AudioBusFx.reverb sends feed it).

reverbDamping.description: The shared reverb's damping of high frequencies.

outputLatency.description: Seconds from a sample's world time to the speaker, as the host reports it (og.audio.outputLatency).

speedOfSound.description: The speed of sound Doppler shifts are computed against (AudioSource.dopplerFactor).

resampler.description: How voices are resampled: sinc (the default) or linear, the mix before round 4, for a game that relies on its exact output. A sound at the output's rate played at pitch 1 is its own samples either way.

AudioBusFx.description:
A bus's insert effects: a high- and low-pass (12 dB/octave), a compressor, side-chain ducking by another bus, and a send to the shared reverb, whose return joins master. One entity per bus (the first in query order counts); without one a bus passes straight through.
Changes reach the mixer through the command stream, so they are deterministic and in the world hash; the PCM is the mixer's.

bus.description: The bus these effects are on.

reverb.description: How much of the bus goes to the reverb.

threshold.description: The compressor's threshold; 0 dB is off.

ratio.description: The compressor's ratio: dB in over the threshold per dB out.

duck.description: Turns this bus down while duckBus is loud: music under effects or dialogue.

duckBus.description: The bus that ducks this one.

duckDepth.description: How far it is turned down.

duckThreshold.description: How loud the key bus must be.

userBus.description: A user bus (4 to 15, an og.AudioBusNode) these effects are on instead of `bus`; 0 uses `bus`.

eqLow.description: The equaliser's low shelf (RBJ, 12 dB/octave): its gain below eqLowFreq; 0 dB is flat.

eqMid.description: The equaliser's mid band (a peak, or a notch below 0 dB): its gain at eqMidFreq; 0 dB is flat.

eqMidQ.description: The mid band's Q: higher is narrower.

eqHigh.description: The equaliser's high shelf: its gain above eqHighFreq; 0 dB is flat.

delay.description: An echo after the compressor: the delay's time, to the sample; 0 is off.

delayFeedback.description: How much of each echo feeds the next.

delayMix.description: How loud the echoes are, added to the dry bus.

distortion.description: A tanh waveshaper after the equaliser: its drive, 0 (off) to 1 (heavy: 20x into the curve), scaled so a full-scale input stays at full scale.

distortionMix.description: How much of the distorted signal replaces the clean one.

AudioBusNode.description:
A user bus of the bus graph: bus `index` (4 to 15) sums the sources whose AudioSource.userBus (or AudioEvent.userBus) names it, runs its og.AudioBusFx (the one whose userBus is the index), and plays into its `parent`: a built-in bus or a user bus of a lower index, so the graph has no cycles (any other parent is master). Its volume is multiplied down the chain to master, so a footsteps bus under sfx is turned down with sfx. The first node in query order for an index counts; a removed node's sources play on their `bus`.
The graph reaches the mixer as commands in the stream (only what changed each tick), so it is deterministic and in the world hash.

parent.description: The bus it plays into: 0 master, 1 music, 2 sfx, 3 ui, or a user bus below `index`.

AudioSnapshot.description:
A mixer snapshot (combat, underwater, paused): per-bus volumes and filters the mix blends towards while `active`, and back from when not, over `fade` seconds. Each tick og.audio moves `weight` by tickDuration / fade towards 1 or 0 and sends the blend in the stream; the bus gains ramp linearly across each tick, so a blend is a straight line to the sample, not a staircase.
At weight w a bus's gain is multiplied by 1 + w * (volume - 1); its low-pass moves from 20 kHz and its high-pass from 20 Hz towards the snapshot's cutoffs in octaves (log2-linear in w). Several snapshots multiply their volumes and take the lowest low-pass and the highest high-pass. Audio's bus volumes and the AudioBusFx filters stay what the game set: the snapshot gain multiplies them, and of its cutoffs and the AudioBusFx's the lower low-pass and the higher high-pass count.

active.description: Blends in while true, out while false.

fade.description: Seconds a full blend in or out takes; 0 is at once.

weight.description: How far it is blended in, 0 to 1 (written by og.audio each tick).

volume.description: Per bus, by index (master, music, sfx, ui, then user buses 4 to 15), the gain it multiplies in at full weight; buses past the list's length keep 1: `{ volume: [1, 0.3] }` turns the music down.

lowpass.description: Per bus, a low-pass cutoff in Hz at full weight; 0 or past the list's length is none: `{ lowpass: [0, 0, 600] }` muffles sfx (underwater).

highpass.description: Per bus, a high-pass cutoff in Hz at full weight; 0 or past the list's length is none.

AudioEventOrder.description: How a AudioEvent chooses its next sound.

x-og-variants.random: A weighted random pick each time (AudioEvent.weights), drawn from the engine's seeded stream.
x-og-variants.roundRobin: The sounds in turn, from the first.
x-og-variants.shuffle: Random, every sound once before any repeats (and never the last one twice in a row across rounds).

AudioEvent.description:
An audio event: one of a set of sounds played on each trigger, with pitch and volume jitter, a cooldown and a voice limit (footsteps, impacts, gunshots). Set `trigger` to play it; the engine sets it back to false.
The og.audioEvents system (before og.audio) picks the sound and the jitter from the engine's own random stream, forked from og.Rng's seed with the label og.audio and kept in the world (never Math.random), so the same seed and the same triggers play the same sounds at the same pitches on every host and every replay. Each play spawns a voice entity (an og.AudioSource, parented to this entity with og.Parent, so a spatial event is heard where its entity is) that is despawned when it ends; nothing of a voice feeds back into the simulation but `played`, `last`, `index`, `bag` and `voices`.

sounds.description: The variations (og.load.sound or og.audio.createSound); 0s are skipped.

weights.description: Weights of a random pick, by position in `sounds`; past the list's length 1.

order.description: How the next sound is chosen.

volumeJitter.description: Each play's volume varies uniformly by up to this many dB either way.

pitchJitter.description: Each play's pitch varies uniformly by up to this many semitones either way.

cooldown.description: A trigger sooner than this after the last play is ignored (and still reset).

maxVoices.description: The most voices of this event at once; 0 is no limit.

steal.description: At maxVoices, the oldest voice is stopped (SOUND_STOPPED) for the new one; false ignores the trigger instead.

bus.description: The bus its voices play on.

userBus.description: A user bus its voices play into instead (AudioSource.userBus).

spatial.description: Its voices are spatial, heard at this entity's world transform.

trigger.description: Set true to play it this tick; the engine sets it back to false.

last.description: The world time of the last play (written by og.audioEvents).

index.description: The position in `sounds` played last (written by og.audioEvents).

bag.description: A shuffle's sounds already played this round, one bit each (written by og.audioEvents).

voices.description: Its voices playing now (written by og.audioEvents).

SoundDesc.description: PCM a game made itself (og.audio.createSound): a tone, a procedural effect, a recording it synthesised.

samples.description: The samples, -1 to 1 (clamped), interleaved by channel: frames * channels values; at least one frame.

ReverbZone.description:
A reverb zone: a box (or a sphere) where the shared reverb sounds like this room. While the og.AudioListener is inside, og.audio eases the reverb's room size and damping, and one bus's send to it, towards the zone's; past the volume's surface it fades out linearly over `fade` metres, so walking in through a door the room grows around the listener.
Deterministic: each tick the listener's weight in every zone is a function of its position (written to `weight`), the strongest zone wins (ties to the first in query order), and the eased values reach the mixer as fx commands in the stream and the world hash. Audio.reverbRoom, Audio.reverbDamping and the bus's AudioBusFx.reverb stay the open air's: the zone never writes them. The listener and the zone are placed at their world transforms (og.Transform down og.Parent): a zone on a child of a moving room moves with it.

size.description: The box's full size along the entity's axes, centred on it (times og.Transform.scale).

radius.description: A sphere of this radius about the entity instead of the box (times the largest of og.Transform.scale); 0 uses the box.

fade.description: How far past the volume's surface the zone fades out, linearly; 0 is a hard edge.

bus.description: The bus whose reverb send the zone sets.

send.description: That bus's send to the reverb inside (its AudioBusFx.reverb outside).

room.description: The reverb's room size inside (Audio.reverbRoom outside).

damping.description: The reverb's damping of high frequencies inside (Audio.reverbDamping outside).

weight.description: How much of this zone the listener hears, 0 to 1: 1 inside, 0 past the fade (written by og.audio each tick).

Music.description: A musical clock: tempo, metre and where bar 1 starts. The og.music system (before og.audio) writes the bar and beat and the times of the next beat and bar line every tick, and sends MusicBeat for every beat; an AudioSource whose startAt is nextBar starts on the bar line to the sample, so stems started together stay in step and a stinger lands on the downbeat.

start.description: The world time of bar 1's first beat.

bar.description: The bar the next tick starts in, from 1 (0 before start; written by og.music).

beat.description: The beat in that bar, from 1 (written by og.music).

nextBeat.description: The world time of the next beat from the next tick on (written by og.music).

nextBar.description: The world time of the next bar line from the next tick on (written by og.music).

MusicBeat.description: A beat of a Music clock, sent in the tick whose interval holds it (systems read it the tick after).

beat.description: The beat in the bar, from 1 (1 is the bar line).

SoundStarted.description: A source started, sent in the tick it happens (systems read it the tick after).

voice.description: The voice id in the command stream.

SoundEnded.description: A sound ended, sent in the tick it happens (systems read it the tick after).

voice.description: The voice id in the command stream.

reason.description: Why: SOUND_FINISHED (0), SOUND_STOPPED (1), SOUND_REMOVED (2), SOUND_REPLACED (3), SOUND_CULLED (4) or SOUND_RETRIGGERED (5).

Navigation.description: A grid, a navmesh or a flow field agents plan on.

NavAlgorithm.description: The grid search a path query runs.

x-og-variants.jps: Jump point search: the same optimal paths as A* with fewer nodes; on a grid with weighted cells it runs A*.

NavAgent.description: An entity that moves itself towards `target` while `seeking`, by a path over `nav` (a grid, navmesh or flow field; 0 goes straight). og.nav re-plans when the target moved more than repathDistance, every repathTicks, or when the grid or navmesh changed, at most 32 plans a tick across agents.

nav.description: The grid, navmesh or flow field it plans on (og.nav.grid, og.nav.load, og.nav.flowField); 0 moves straight at the target.

target.description: Where it goes while seeking.

seeking.description: Moves towards the target while true.

radius.description: Its radius: grid paths keep this clear of walls; separation uses it.

stopDistance.description: It has arrived within this distance of the target.

slowRadius.description: It slows down inside this distance of the target.

repathTicks.description: Re-plans this often while seeking (0: only when the target moves).

repathDistance.description: Re-plans when the target moved farther than this from the last plan.

smooth.description: Pulls grid paths straight where nothing is in the way.

faceMovement.description: Turns the entity to face where it moves (3D: about +Y, its +Z forward; 2D: about +Z, its +X forward).

turnSpeed.description: How fast it turns when facing its movement.

drive.description: Moves the entity (its og.Velocity, or its og.Transform) while true; false keeps planning but leaves the motion to the game (a knock-back, a stun).

status.description: NAV_IDLE, NAV_MOVING, NAV_ARRIVED, NAV_UNREACHABLE or NAV_PARTIAL (written by og.nav).

waypoint.description: The path corner it heads for (written by og.nav).

remaining.description: The path length left (written by og.nav).

plans.description: Paths planned so far (written by og.nav).

Steering.description: Steering behaviours an og.NavAgent adds to its path following, each by weight (0 is off): flee, wander, pursue, evade, separation from other agents and avoidance of colliders ahead (three physics rays).

seek.description: Weight of following the path to the target (seek, then arrive at the end).

fleeRadius.description: It flees (and evades) only inside this distance (0: always).

wanderDistance.description: How far ahead the wander circle is.

wanderJitter.description: How fast the wander point moves round the circle.

pursue.description: An entity to pursue (seek where it will be, from its NavAgent or og.Velocity); 0: none.

evade.description: An entity to evade (flee where it will be); 0: none.

separation.description: Weight of keeping apart from other agents.

separationRadius.description: Other agents closer than this push it away.

avoidDistance.description: How far ahead the avoidance rays reach.

avoidMask.description: Collision layers the avoidance rays hit (0: every layer).

NavFilter.description: Which navmesh areas an agent crosses and what a metre in each costs: beside an og.NavAgent, its plans weigh every polygon's length by its area's cost and never enter an excluded area. Areas are marked at cook time (`area` in a navmesh asset) or at run time (og.nav.setArea); 0 is ground. Without one every area costs 1.

areaCosts.description: Per area id, the cost of a metre in it (past the list's length 1, and at least 0.01): `{ areaCosts: [1, 1, 1, 8] }` makes area 3 (water) eight times dearer, so a path wades only when going round is longer than that.

excluded.description: Area ids the agent never enters (0 to 63): `{ excluded: [4] }` keeps it out of area 4 (lava).

Crowd.description: Reciprocal crowd avoidance (ORCA) for an agent: beside an og.NavAgent, each tick its velocity is the one nearest what its path and steering want that keeps it clear of its nearest agents for `horizon` seconds and of the navmesh's walls for `obstacleHorizon`, each pair of crowd agents sharing the avoidance. Every agent solves from the same start-of-tick state in a fixed order, so crowds replay identically on every host; agents meeting perfectly symmetrically (a ring swapping places) are kept from locking by a margin of up to 5% of the radius picked from the entity, so a game adds no jitter of its own. Without one an agent moves as before (og.Steering's separation only).

neighbours.description: How many nearest agents it avoids (at most 32).

horizon.description: Seconds ahead it keeps clear of other agents: longer turns aside earlier and more gently.

obstacleHorizon.description: Seconds ahead it keeps clear of walls (a navmesh's edges).

weight.description: Its share of each avoidance with another crowd agent (0.5: half each); an agent without og.Crowd is avoided wholly by it.

NavLinkKind.description: How an agent crosses an off-mesh link.

x-og-variants.jump: Through the air on an arc, in its length over the agent's speed (at least 0.3 s).
x-og-variants.ladder: Climbing, at half the agent's speed.
x-og-variants.door: Walking through at the agent's speed, while the link is open (og.nav.setLinkOpen).
x-og-variants.teleport: At once: on the far side the tick after it is reached.

NavLinkDesc.description: An off-mesh link: a way between two points of a navmesh its surface does not join (a gap to jump, a ladder, a door, a teleporter). Each end snaps to the polygon under it within 1 m.

start.description: Where the agent leaves the surface.

bidirectional.description: Crossed both ways; false: from start to end only.

cost.description: What crossing costs a path, in metres of walking; 0 is the link's length. A dear link loses to a shorter walk round.

open.description: A closed link is never planned across (a shut door); agents re-plan when it opens or closes.

duration.description: Seconds a crossing takes; 0 is the kind's own.

game.description: The game moves the agent across (an animation, a cutscene): og.nav holds it at the start until og.nav.finishLink, then lands it at the end.

NavLinkReached.description: An agent reached an off-mesh link and started across it (systems read it the tick after): play the jump or the climb here. With `game`, move it and call og.nav.finishLink when it is over.

kind.description: Its NavLinkKind, by index: 0 jump, 1 ladder, 2 door, 3 teleport.

start.description: Where the agent leaves the surface.

x-og-variants.orientedBox: A box of size `size` round `center`, turned `yaw` radians about +y.
x-og-variants.cylinder: An upright cylinder of `radius` and `height` standing on `center`.
x-og-variants.convex: A convex prism: `points` (x and z, either winding) from `min.y` to `max.y`.

NavShape.description: A volume over a navmesh's floor: an obstacle (og.nav.carve) or an area (og.nav.setArea).

min.description: box: its lowest corner; convex: its bottom (min.y).

max.description: box: its highest corner; convex: its top (max.y).

center.description: orientedBox: its centre; cylinder: the middle of its base.

size.description: orientedBox: its full size before the turn.

radius.description: cylinder: its radius.

points.description: convex: its outline's corners (their y is ignored).

NavAreaDesc.description: A run-time area: the spans under `shape` (their floors from the agent's climb below its bottom to its top) take area `area`, over the baked areas and over run-time areas of lower ids.

area.description: The area id, 0 to 63 (0 is ground).

NavGridDesc.description: A grid of square cells over the plane: cell (0, 0)'s lower corner at `origin`, rows running up.

origin.description: Where cell (0, 0)'s lower corner is (x, y in 2D; x, z in 3D).

costs.description: Row-major cell costs from row 0 (0 blocked, 1 normal, up to 255 to avoid); empty: every cell 1.

TilemapGridDesc.description: A grid over a placed og.Tilemap: one cell per map cell, blocked where a collision layer has a solid tile.

layers.description: The layers whose solid tiles block; empty: every collision layer.

inflate.description: Also block this many cells around each blocked one (wide agents).

inside.description: Whether the point was on the grid.

smooth.description: Pull a grid path straight where nothing is in the way.

radius.description: Keep this clear of grid walls when smoothing.

areaCosts.description: On a navmesh: per area id, the cost of a metre in it, as og.NavFilter's.

excluded.description: On a navmesh: area ids the path never enters.

points.description: Its corners, start and end included.

complete.description: Whether it reaches the end (false: it stops at the reachable point nearest it).

expanded.description: Cells or polygons the search took off its open list.

algorithm.description: What ran: jps, astar or navmesh.

links.description: Where it crosses off-mesh links: each an index into points, the link's start (the next point is where it lands).

FlowDesc.description: A flow field over a grid.

targets.description: Where agents go: each point's cell is a target.

NavMeshDesc.description: A navmesh built at runtime over a flat floor (a procedural level): the floor box, the boxes it carves out, and the agent it is for.

min.description: The floor's lowest corner (its y is the floor's height).

blocked.description: Boxes standing on the floor (walls, crates).

agentRadius.description: Walls are kept this far away.

tileSize.description: Cells per tile side: an obstacle rebuilds the tiles it touches.

mesh.description: What NavAgent.nav and the queries take.

min.description: The lowest corner of the box around its polygons.

max.description: The highest corner of the box around its polygons (its highest walkable floor's y).

profile.description: The agent profile it was baked for (og.nav.load's profile); empty for a navmesh of one unnamed agent and for og.nav.build.

Behaviour.description: A loaded behaviour tree or state machine.

AiAgent.description: An entity that thinks with a behaviour. Give it an og.NavAgent to move and an og.Perception to see and hear.

behaviour.description: The behaviour it runs (og.ai.load); 0 runs nothing.

thinkEvery.description: Thinks every this many ticks (1: every tick); agents are staggered by their order.

status.description: AI_RUNNING, AI_SUCCESS or AI_FAILURE after the last think (0 before the first; written by og.ai).

state.description: The state machine's state, an index into BehaviourInfo.states (written by og.ai).

node.description: The node it ran last, an index into BehaviourInfo.nodes (written by og.ai).

changes.description: Times the state or the running node changed (written by og.ai).

Perception.description: What an agent sees and hears. It sees the nearest og.Perceivable of another team within `sight`, inside the `fov` cone around `forward` (or the way it last moved), unless a collider is in the way; it hears a spatial sound that starts (og.SoundStarted) or a game noise (og.ai.noise) within `hearing` times its loudness, except its own: a sound of its entity or of an entity under it (og.Parent), or a noise whose NoiseDesc.source is one of them.

fov.description: The width of its view cone (360: all round).

eyeHeight.description: Its eyes are this far above its position (+y).

occlude.description: Colliders hide what is behind them.

occluders.description: Collision layers that block sight (0: every layer).

hearing.description: How far it hears a sound of loudness 1 (a source's volume).

memory.description: How long a lost target stays its target.

team.description: Its team: it perceives og.Perceivable entities of other teams.

forward.description: Where it looks; zero: the way it last moved (before it moves, the way its Transform faces: +Z in 3D, +X in 2D).

target.description: What it sees or remembers seeing (written by og.ai).

sees.description: It sees the target now (written by og.ai).

lastSeen.description: Where it last saw the target (written by og.ai).

sinceSeen.description: Seconds since it last saw a target (written by og.ai; 1e6 before the first time).

heard.description: It heard something this tick (written by og.ai).

heardAt.description: Where it last heard something (written by og.ai).

sinceHeard.description: Seconds since it last heard something (written by og.ai; 1e6 before the first time).

Perceivable.description: Something agents of other teams can see.

team.description: Its team (agents of the same team ignore it).

eyeHeight.description: Agents look at a point this far above its position (+y).

AiChanged.description: An agent's state or running node changed (systems read it the tick after).

AiActionStarted.description: A game action (`action <name> args` in a behaviour) started: play it (a reload, a door, a line of dialogue) and call og.ai.finish when it is over; until then the node runs. Read the tick after. Joins the world's types only once a behaviour with a game action is loaded.

node.description: The action's node, an index into BehaviourInfo.nodes.

name.description: The action's name (at most 63 bytes).

args.description: Its arguments as written, separated by spaces (at most 255 bytes; longer ones are refused when the behaviour is parsed).

AiActionStopped.description: A game action stopped: the game finished it (og.ai.finish), or the behaviour moved on first (stop playing it). Read the tick after.

name.description: The action's name (at most 63 bytes).

result.description: AI_SUCCESS or AI_FAILURE, as og.ai.finish said, or AI_INTERRUPTED.

name.description: Its name.

keys.description: Its declared blackboard keys (its subtrees' too).

subtrees.description: The behaviours its `use` nodes inline, every one reached, in the order first met.

NoiseDesc.description: A noise agents may hear next tick.

loudness.description: How loud: heard within Perception.hearing times this.

source.description: Who makes it (0: nobody): that entity, and the agents it is under (og.Parent), do not hear it.

state.description: A machine's state (empty for a tree).

node.description: The node it ran last, such as `chase`.

path.description: The path to it from the root, such as `selector > sequence chase > chase`.

blackboard.description: Its blackboard, keys to numbers, booleans, points and entity handles.

target.description: Its target (0: none).

Story.description: The story's counters (written by og.story; the story itself is a state block). Registered at the first og.story.load.

lines.description: Lines shown so far (DialogueView.seq of the latest).

activeQuests.description: Quests started and not yet completed or failed.

DialogueShown.description: A conversation shows a new line (start the voice, reset the reveal). Sent before the game's systems, the tick after the call that moved it.

DialogueEnded.description: A conversation ended: its dialogue ran out, reached `end`, took a choice without `goto`, or og.story.stop stopped it. Sent the tick after.

DialogueCheck.description: An active check was rolled (d20 plus the stat against the target): reveal the roll. Sent the tick after.

stat.description: The variable read as the stat.

target.description: What the roll plus the stat had to reach.

passed.description: Whether roll + stat reached the target.

QuestUpdated.description: A quest started, counted, changed stage, completed or failed. Sent the tick after.

BarkSaid.description: An entity barked (og.story.bark or og.story.ambient): show its line over it with og.story.barks. Sent the tick after it was asked for.

bark.description: The bark's id in its dialogue.

key.description: The line's i18n key.

StoryEvent.description: A dialogue's `emit name "arg"`: open the shop, give the sword, play the cutscene. Sent the tick after.

name.description: The name written after emit.

arg.description: Its argument, evaluated and written as text (empty without one).

name.description: A dialogue's name or a quest's id: what og.story.start and og.story.startQuest take.

nodes.description: A dialogue's nodes, in order (a quest: its stages).

variables.description: The variables it declares (var: the conversation's; global: the story's).

node.description: The node to start at (empty: the dialogue's `start`).

cast.description: Speaker ids to the entities playing them, `{ smith: entity }`: SpeakerView.entity (for a speech bubble or a camera).

vars.description: Starting values for the dialogue's own `var`s, `{ mood: 2 }`.

id.description: The speaker's id (`narrator` for the narrator).

name.description: Its name, resolved in the active locale (empty for the narrator).

portrait.description: A portrait image's asset path (empty: none).

expression.description: The portrait's variant: the line's `expression`, else the speaker's.

stat.description: The variable read as the stat.

target.description: What the stat (passive) or a d20 plus the stat (active) must reach.

chance.description: The chance it passes, 0 to 1: an active check's share of the d20's faces that pass; a passive one's 1 or 0.

kind.description: passive (a threshold that enables the choice) or active (rolled when chosen).

ChoiceView.description: A choice the node offers (hidden ones are left out).

index.description: What og.story.choose takes: its place among the node's choices, hidden ones counted.

id.description: Its id within the node.

text.description: Its text, resolved in the active locale.

key.description: Its i18n key.

args.description: The arguments its text was resolved with.

enabled.description: Whether it can be chosen now (its `if` holds and a passive check passes).

reason.description: Why it is disabled, resolved in the active locale (empty without a `reason`).

reasonArgs.description: The arguments the reason was resolved with.

visited.description: Chosen before in this conversation (drawn muted).

kind.description: The game's word for its icon: leave, trade, attack, lie...

check.description: Its check, if it has one.

defaultChoice.description: The ChoiceView.index taken when it runs out.

stat.description: The variable read as the stat.

target.description: What the roll plus the stat had to reach.

DialogueView.description: What a conversation shows now: the line in full (the dialogue box paces its own reveal), its speaker and the choices, if it waits on them.

seq.description: Counts lines shown across the story: a new number is a new line, even when a node repeats.

seen.description: The line had been read before it was shown (skip-read, a dimmed backlog); og.story.reset keeps what was read.

key.description: The line's i18n key.

args.description: The arguments it was resolved with (evaluated when it was shown).

text.description: The line, resolved in the active locale.

voice.description: Its voice clip's asset path (empty: none). og.story plays it on its own entity (an og.AudioSource on the sfx bus) from the tick after the line is shown, and stops it when the line moves on.

voiceTicks.description: The voice's length in ticks (0: no voice, or one that did not load).

voiceLeft.description: Ticks of the voice still to play: voiceTicks until it starts, 0 once it has ended (advance then, for auto-advance).

shot.description: The camera shot it is shown in: its `shot`, else its node's (a virtual camera's entity name or a cast role); empty: none. While it shows, og.story makes that og.VirtualCamera og.CameraBrain.solo: a name is the entity of that name, a role the cast entity's own og.VirtualCamera, else the first one whose lookAt is that entity. When no running conversation's line has a shot the game's own solo is handed back.

choices.description: The choices, when it waits on them; empty while a line waits for og.story.advance.

timer.description: The choice timer, while it runs.

lastCheck.description: The last active check this conversation rolled.

ended.description: The conversation has ended (the view keeps its last line).

ChosenView.description: The choice made while a line was shown.

text.description: Its text, resolved in the active locale.

StoryLine.description: A line of a conversation's backlog.

key.description: Its i18n key.

text.description: The line, resolved in the active locale.

seen.description: It had been read before it was shown.

chosen.description: The choice made on it, if any.

entity.description: Who barks: its og.story.barks entry, `self.` in the bark's conditions and arguments.

topic.description: The topic: one of the bark's `topic`s, such as idle or alarm.

dialogue.description: Only this dialogue's barks (empty: every loaded dialogue's).

AmbientDesc.description: An entity that barks on its own.

jitter.description: Up to this many ticks more each time, drawn on the story's stream.

seq.description: The line's number: a new number is a new bark.

key.description: The line's i18n key.

args.description: The arguments it was resolved with (evaluated when it was said, world reads included).

text.description: The line, resolved in the active locale.

speaker.description: The bark's speaker (entity: who says it).

voice.description: Its voice clip (empty: none), played as a conversation's.

voiceLeft.description: Ticks of its voice still to play.

priority.description: Its priority: only a higher one interrupts it.

MarkerDesc.description: Where a quest's objective is, for the map, compass and tracker.

entity.description: An entity to point at (0: none).

position.description: A point to point at, when there is no entity.

MarkerView.description: Where a quest points: the marker og.story.mark set, else the current stage's first undone objective's `marker`.

name.description: Its name, resolved in the active locale.

image.description: Its image's asset path (empty: none).

ObjectiveView.description: An objective of a quest's current stage.

id.description: Its id.

text.description: Its text, resolved in the active locale with `count` and `target` among its arguments.

target.description: Counts needed.

failed.description: Left undone when the quest failed.

optional.description: Not needed to finish the stage.

hidden.description: Not revealed yet: declared hidden and not yet counted (the log leaves it out or shows ???).

QuestView.description: A quest as a quest log shows it.

id.description: Its id.

title.description: Its title, resolved in the active locale.

summary.description: The current stage's summary, else the quest's, resolved.

tracked.description: Shown in the HUD tracker (og.story.track; the first quest started is tracked).

isNew.description: Not looked at since it started (og.story.markSeen clears it).

updated.description: Changed since it was last looked at (og.story.markSeen clears it).

updatedTick.description: The tick it last changed (sort the log by recent).

PlatformOrder.description: How a leaderboard sorts; the first submission to a board fixes it.

PlatformAnswered.description: An answer arrived: sent by og.platform at the start of the tick it was applied, read by systems the tick after (og.platform.result has it at once).

ok.description: Whether it succeeded; og.platform.result has the data or the error.

key.description: The key: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

value.description: Any JSON value, at most 64 KiB encoded.

revision.description: Write only if the key is at this revision (a conflict otherwise, whose error carries the revision the key is at now); 0 writes whatever is there (the last write wins).

create.description: Write only if the key has never been written (a conflict otherwise); revision is then ignored.

score.description: The score, or a time in seconds for an ascending board.

order.description: How the board sorts, fixed by its first submission.

count.description: How many entries: the top `count`, or `count` around the player.

PointDesc.description: Origin Point for something the player did.

reason.description: Why, as the game names it: `level.completed`, `daily.streak` (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`).

amount.description: How many points the game asks for; the platform decides what it grants.

AiMarkDesc.description: Marks content the game shows as generated by AI, for the platform's disclosure.

kind.description: What: `text`, `image`, `audio`, `level`, `character` (1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, `_` and `-`, a letter first).

label.description: What the player sees it as, at most 120 characters.

model.description: The model or service, when known (at most 80 characters).

SaveSlotDesc.description: A save slot: a long text (a world.snapshot()) kept across as many store keys as it needs.

slot.description: The slot's name: 1 to 60 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (`slot1`). Its keys are the name itself (the manifest) and `<slot>.a0`, `<slot>.a1`, ... or `<slot>.b0`, ... (the parts).

text.description: The text: at most 512 KiB of UTF-8 (eight parts of 64 KiB).

meta.description: What a title screen shows of the slot (`{ place, hour }`), kept in the manifest so loadSlot with metaOnly reads it without the parts: any JSON, at most 4 KiB encoded.

LoadSlotDesc.description: Which slot to read, and how much of it.

slot.description: The slot's name, as saveSlot wrote it.

metaOnly.description: Read the manifest alone: the answer's text stays null (a title's Continue label, before the player asks for the world).

code.description: offline, timeout, invalid, unauthorized, not_found, conflict, too_large, rate_limited, unavailable, failed, cancelled or no_fill.

retryable.description: Whether the same call may succeed later.

revision.description: For a conflict of a conditional write: the revision the key is at now (read it again, merge, write at it); 0 otherwise.

data.description: The answer (see each function); null on failure.

tick.description: The tick it was answered at.

time.description: The host's clock when it answered, UTC milliseconds since 1970 (PlatformInfo.clock says whose); 0 when the host gave none. A slot call (saveSlot, loadSlot) answers the time of the store answer that ended it.

host.description: `player` (a Player frames the game), `local` (the native host's JSON store or the browser's own storage) or `none`.

capabilities.description: The methods it answers: store.get, store.set, store.list, leaderboard.submit, leaderboard.top, leaderboard.around, telemetry, point, ai.mark, purchase.products, purchase.buy, purchase.entitlements, purchase.consume, ad.ready, ad.show, achievement.unlock, achievement.progress, achievement.list, player.get, friends.list, invite.send, invite.list, share (og.platform.supports asks for one).

clock.description: Whose clock og.platform.now and the answers' `time` read: `player` (the Player's answers carry its time), `browser` (the web host's own clock: the Player gives no time yet, docs/platform-asks.md), `system` (the native host's system clock), `fixed` (`og run --clock` and playtests: a clock that starts where it is told and moves with the ticks) or `none`.

x-og-variants.rewarded: The player chose to watch it for a reward: the answer says whether they watched it to the end.
x-og-variants.interstitial: Shown at a break the game picks (between levels): the player may close it.

x-og-variants.purchase: A purchase settled: a pending one completed or failed, or one was refunded. Data `{ purchase, product, quantity, state }`, state `completed`, `failed` or `refunded`.
x-og-variants.entitlements: The player's entitlements changed without a call (bought on another device, a subscription expired): data `{ entitlements }`, the entitlements answer's shape.
x-og-variants.invite: An invite to this game arrived: data `{ invite, from: { player, name }, payload, time }`.
x-og-variants.host: A message from the page that frames the game, outside any platform service (a site steering a showcase, a launcher handing over a choice): data `{ name, ... }`, its meaning agreed between the game and that page. The engine gives it no meaning of its own; a game reading it handles an unknown name by ignoring it.

PlatformNotice.description: Unasked host input arrived: sent by og.platform at the start of the tick it was applied, read by systems the tick after; read it with og.platform.notice. Registered when a game first names it (a system's reads); without it notices are still logged and readable.

notice.description: The notice's number, for og.platform.notice: 1 for the first, counting up.

PlatformGrants.description: The purchases this world granted (og.platform.grant), so a consumable is granted once however its answer or notice comes back: a replay, a relaunch, a restored save. World state: saved, restored and hashed. Registered when a game first names it or calls og.platform.grant. Write it only through og.platform.grant.

ids.description: The 64-bit hashes of the granted purchase ids, each as two u32 (low, high), oldest first: the last 256 grants.

tick.description: The tick it was applied at.

time.description: The host's clock when it sent it, UTC milliseconds; 0 when it gave none.

ids.description: Product ids as the game's store lists them (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`), at most 100; empty: every product the game sells.

PurchaseDesc.description: A purchase to ask the player for.

placement.description: Where in the game, as the game names it (`level.end`, `continue`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (default `default`).

id.description: The achievement's id (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`).

percent.description: How far, 0 to 100: 100 unlocks it. Progress never goes back (a lower value keeps the higher one).

count.description: At most this many, those playing this game first.

to.description: The friend's player id (og.platform.friends); empty: the host offers an invite link through the share sheet.

message.description: What the invite says, at most 120 characters; empty: the host's own words.

payload.description: What the game hands the invited player (a room id, a level): any JSON, at most 1 KiB encoded; their og.platform.invites carries it back.

ShareDesc.description: What to share through the device's share sheet.

text.description: The text, 1 to 280 characters.

title.description: A title, at most 80 characters; empty: the game's name.

path.description: A short query the game's own Play link carries back (`?share=<path>`), at most 256 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, `/` and `=`; empty: the plain Play link. The host builds the link: a game names no URL.

image.description: Attach the frame drawn last (a score screen).

name.description: What the room is called (at most 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`); empty for none. The host gives the room its id.

QuickPlayDesc.description: Quick play: what this engine waits to be matched for (og.platform.quickPlay).

mode.description: The mode to play (at most 32 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`): only engines asking for the same mode and players are matched. Empty is `default`.

players.description: How many play together: the room is made once this many wait (set og.Lockstep.players to the same).

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the others, in milliseconds; then og.RoomJoined says `timeout`. 0 waits until roomLeave.

name.description: This player's name, as the other peers see it (og.platform.roomPeers); empty for none.

peer.description: Its number: the room numbers peers in join order from 0 and never gives one twice.

name.description: Its name, as its host gave it; empty for none.

RoomInfo.description: The room this engine is in.

state.description: `none` (in no room), `joining` (roomCreate, roomJoin or quickPlay asked, not answered yet: quick play waiting for its match) or `in`.

room.description: The room's id; empty in none.

host.description: What carries rooms here: `relay` (natively, `og run --room` through `og relay`), `player` (the platform's rooms through the Player, on the web) or `none` (roomCreate and roomJoin are refused).

peer.description: This engine's peer number; 0 in none.

peers.description: Every peer present, this one included, by number.

link.description: The room a Play link to a room (`?room=<id>` on the play page) named: the engine joined it at load (og.RoomJoined answers, as for roomJoin); empty without one.

RoomMessageData.description: A message another peer sent: what og.RoomMessage announced.

message.description: Its number (og.RoomMessage.message): 1 for the first message this engine received, counting up.

tick.description: The tick it was delivered at.

data.description: What it carries, when it was sent as a JSON value; null when it was sent as bytes.

bytes.description: What it carries, when it was sent as bytes.

RoomJoined.description: roomCreate, roomJoin or quickPlay finished, or the host put this engine in a room (`og run --room`, a Play link to a room): sent at the start of the tick after the host answered. With ok false the engine is in no room and `reason` says why.

ok.description: Whether this engine is in the room now.

room.description: The room's id (at most 63 bytes); empty when not ok.

peers.description: How many peers are in the room, this one included.

reason.description: Why it failed: `unavailable` (no rooms here), `not_found`, `full`, `invalid`, `offline`, `timeout` (quick play matched nobody in time) or `cancelled` (roomLeave while joining), then a colon and the host's words; empty when ok.

RoomPeerJoined.description: Another peer joined this engine's room.

peers.description: How many peers are in the room now.

RoomPeerLeft.description: A peer left this engine's room (it left, closed, or lost its connection), after every message it sent; or, with peer equal to this engine's own number, this engine is in no room any more (roomLeave, or the host lost the room).

peers.description: How many peers are in the room now (0 once this engine left).

RoomMessage.description: Another peer's message arrived; read it with og.platform.roomMessage. Messages from one peer arrive in the order it sent them. While lockstep runs (og.Lockstep) a message is this peer's host input alone: a system that changes the world from one makes it differ from the other peers' (og.Desync); carry what all must see in og.PlayerInput.

binary.description: Whether it was sent as bytes (else as a JSON value).

DateStyle.description: How much of a date to write (CLDR's styles; en shown).

TimeStyle.description: How much of a time of day to write (en shown).

offsetMinutes.description: Minutes ahead of UTC to show it in (a player's time zone, which the game passes in; 540 for Tokyo).
Minutes ahead of UTC to show it in.

requested.description: The locale the host or the game asked for (empty: none).

active.description: The table in use (empty: none loaded).

fonts.description: The UI's font chain, first first.

Direction.description: Which way a container lays out its children.

Align.description: Where children sit along the main axis.

x-og-variants.spaceBetween: The free space split evenly between children.

Cross.description: Where children sit across the main axis.

x-og-variants.stretch: Stretched to the container's inner size.
x-og-variants.baseline: In a row, children share their first text baseline (rows of mixed type sizes); a column treats it as start.

TextAlign.description: How the lines of a label align.

FontRole.description: Which configured font text uses; display and mono fall back to body, rounded to display, then body.

x-og-variants.rounded: The rounded font, for levels and scores.

ButtonVariant.description: Button roles: how the style draws each.

x-og-variants.primary: The primary action: one per screen.
x-og-variants.danger: A destructive action: danger ink on the danger tint.
x-og-variants.ghost: Clear inside a strong outline until hovered: a second action beside a primary that still reads as a button.

Scheme.description: The palette: games run on a stage, so dark is the default.
