x-og-variants.arc: A ring segment on the circle in its rectangle: start, sweep and thickness (a ring at a full turn), with caps.
x-og-variants.path: A line through points (CSS px from its top left), Béziers with curves; its fills draw the line.

x-og-variants.squircle: Continuous corners: a superellipse of DrawShape.squircle.
x-og-variants.bevel: A straight cut across, the radius along each edge.
x-og-variants.notch: A concave quarter circle cut in (an inset notch).

LineCap.description: The end of an open line, an arc or a dash.

x-og-variants.round: A half disc past the end.
x-og-variants.square: Cut square half the width past the end.

x-og-variants.miter: Sharp, cut to a bevel past DrawShape.miterLimit half widths.

DrawShape.description: An element's outline; its fills, strokes, effects and clip take it.

radii.description: A rect's corner radii, top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left; null is the element's radius at every corner.

squircle.description: A squircle corner's exponent: 2 is round, 4 the iOS look.

inner.description: A star's inner vertices as a fraction of its radius; 1 (or more) is a plain polygon.

start.description: An arc's start, clockwise from 3 o'clock.

sweep.description: An arc's sweep, clockwise (a full turn or more: a ring).

thickness.description: An arc's thickness, inwards from the circle.

cap.description: An arc's or a path's ends.

points.description: A path's points, CSS px from the element's top left.

curves.description: A path's points after the first come in threes: a cubic Bézier's two controls and its end.

closed.description: A path returns to its first point.

filled.description: A path is an area: its fills cover the inside of the closed outline through its points (even-odd) instead of drawing its line, and its strokes outline it, as any other shape's (an area chart, a radar's polygon, a pie's wedge).

GradientType.description: How a gradient (Gradient.type) runs over the element's box (fractions: 0,0 top left, 1,1 bottom right).

x-og-variants.radial: Centred on `from`, `to` its x and y radii.
x-og-variants.conic: Around `from`, starting at the angle to.x (radians clockwise from 3 o'clock).
x-og-variants.diamond: Centred on `from`, `to` its x and y radii, by |x|/rx + |y|/ry.

GradientSpread.description: What a gradient does past its ends.

GradientStop.description: A gradient's colour at an offset.

color.description: Its colour: a theme token, resolved when the frame is drawn, or a literal.

Gradient.description: A gradient of up to 8 stops, mixed in OKLab (no grey middle between complementary colours) and dithered so a long shallow one shows no bands.

from.description: Its start or centre, a fraction of the box.

to.description: Its end, or its radii, a fraction of the box.

ImageFit.description: How an image fills the element's box.

x-og-variants.cover: Scaled to cover the box, cropped around the focal point.
x-og-variants.contain: Scaled to fit inside the box, placed by the focal point.
x-og-variants.none: At its own size (one image pixel per CSS px), placed by the focal point.
x-og-variants.nineSlice: Nine-slice: corners kept at slice, edges and centre filled by edges.
x-og-variants.pattern: Tiled at tile CSS px, turned, offset and scrolling.

SliceEdges.description: How a nine-slice's edges and centre fill their length.

x-og-variants.repeat: Tiled at the border's scale, cut at the end.
x-og-variants.round: Tiled a whole number of times, stretched to fit.

color.description: The colour: a theme token, resolved when the frame is drawn, or a literal.

ImageFill.description: A texture region with a fit.

texture.description: The texture (og.load.texture).

uv.description: The region, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture.

size.description: The region's size in image pixels (none, nineSlice and pattern read it); zero is the texture's.

focal.description: Where cover crops and contain or none place it, fractions of the free space.

slice.description: A nine-slice's border in image pixels: left, top, right, bottom.

border.description: A nine-slice's border as drawn, CSS px; null is slice.

hollow.description: A nine-slice leaves its centre empty.

tile.description: A pattern's tile, CSS px; zero is size.

scroll.description: A pattern's scroll, CSS px a second of the UI clock.

VectorFill.description: A cooked vector contained and centred in the box.

tint.description: Multiplies its paints; null is white.

Fill.description: One layer of an element's fill, or a stroke's paint.

color.description: The colour: a theme token, resolved when the frame is drawn, or a literal.

from.description: Its start or centre, a fraction of the box.

to.description: Its end, or its radii, a fraction of the box.

oneOf.description: An image with a fit, a nine-slice or a pattern.

texture.description: The texture (og.load.texture).

uv.description: The region, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture.

size.description: The region's size in image pixels (none, nineSlice and pattern read it); zero is the texture's.

focal.description: Where cover crops and contain or none place it, fractions of the free space.

slice.description: A nine-slice's border in image pixels: left, top, right, bottom.

border.description: A nine-slice's border as drawn, CSS px; null is slice.

hollow.description: A nine-slice leaves its centre empty.

tile.description: A pattern's tile, CSS px; zero is size.

scroll.description: A pattern's scroll, CSS px a second of the UI clock.

oneOf.description: A cooked vector (as a stroke's paint, its tint).

tint.description: Multiplies its paints; null is white.

StrokeAlign.description: Which side of the outline a stroke lies on.

Stroke.description: A stroke along the element's outline with a paint of its own (a gradient border is one stroke).

gap.description: The gap between dashes; 0 is the dash's length.

dashOffset.description: Where the dashes start along the outline (move it by the tick for marching ants).

paint.description: Its paint; null is the theme's line colour.

ShadowEffect.description: A shadow: a drop shadow under the element, or an inner shadow cast inwards.

blur.description: Its softness (CSS blur: the Gaussian's deviation is half of it).

spread.description: How far it grows (or with a negative value shrinks) past the shape.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's shadow.

GlowEffect.description: A glow: around the element, or along its inside.

spread.description: How far it grows past the shape.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's primary.

BlurEffect.description: The element and its subtree blurred (drawn offscreen).

radius.description: The blur.

BackdropEffect.description: What is under the element (the scene and the UI below it) blurred, its saturation and brightness scaled and tinted: glass.

tint.description: Over the blur, by its alpha; null is the theme's panel at 60 % (with a glass weight, the weight's tint).

glass.description: One of flat glass's weights (docs/ui.md §5.3): it sets the blur, 200 % saturation, the tint (unless tint is given), a 0.5 px hairline inside the edge and CSS mixing, in the theme's scheme; under reduced transparency the solid raised surface, under high contrast solid with a strong 1 px edge. none is the fields as given.

elevation.description: The soft shadow outside it, as the design language's shadows (with a glass weight, raised by default).

edge.description: A hairline just inside the edge (CSS inset 0 0 0 <edge>px); 0 is none, or the weight's.

edgeColor.description: The hairline's colour; null is the weight's (or the theme's line).

solid.description: The tint drawn opaque, with the hairline and shadow: nothing under it is read (reduced transparency, increased contrast).

cssMix.description: Mix the tint, hairline and shadow in sRGB-encoded values, as CSS does, so a tint reads as it does on a web page (glass weights always do).

GlassWeight.description: How heavy a glass surface is: flat glass, clear and coloured by what passes under it, with no rim, sheen or refraction.

x-og-variants.none: No weight: the backdrop's own fields.
x-og-variants.thin: 10 px of blur and the lightest tint: icons and play discs over art, never text (it does not hold text at 4.5:1).
x-og-variants.regular: 22 px: bars, tab bars, capsules; holds the scheme's text at 4.5:1.
x-og-variants.thick: 32 px and a denser tint: menus, popovers, dialogs, sheets, toasts.

Elevation.description: The soft shadow a glass surface casts.

x-og-variants.none: No shadow (with a glass weight: raised).
x-og-variants.raised: The hairline alone (an outer one in the light scheme).
x-og-variants.float: One soft, short shadow: capsules and menus.
x-og-variants.lift: Two deeper shadows: dialogs and sheets.

blur.description: Its softness (CSS blur: the Gaussian's deviation is half of it).

spread.description: How far it grows (or with a negative value shrinks) past the shape.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's shadow.

blur.description: Its softness (CSS blur: the Gaussian's deviation is half of it).

spread.description: How far it grows (or with a negative value shrinks) past the shape.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's shadow.

spread.description: How far it grows past the shape.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's primary.

spread.description: How far it grows past the shape.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's primary.

radius.description: The blur.

oneOf.description: Glass: what is under it blurred.

tint.description: Over the blur, by its alpha; null is the theme's panel at 60 % (with a glass weight, the weight's tint).

glass.description: One of flat glass's weights (docs/ui.md §5.3): it sets the blur, 200 % saturation, the tint (unless tint is given), a 0.5 px hairline inside the edge and CSS mixing, in the theme's scheme; under reduced transparency the solid raised surface, under high contrast solid with a strong 1 px edge. none is the fields as given.

elevation.description: The soft shadow outside it, as the design language's shadows (with a glass weight, raised by default).

edge.description: A hairline just inside the edge (CSS inset 0 0 0 <edge>px); 0 is none, or the weight's.

edgeColor.description: The hairline's colour; null is the weight's (or the theme's line).

solid.description: The tint drawn opaque, with the hairline and shadow: nothing under it is read (reduced transparency, increased contrast).

cssMix.description: Mix the tint, hairline and shadow in sRGB-encoded values, as CSS does, so a tint reads as it does on a web page (glass weights always do).

ClipMode.description: How an element cuts its children.

x-og-variants.none: Not at all (a scroll container still clips to its rectangle).
x-og-variants.shape: To its shape, antialiased (a round avatar, a hex frame).
x-og-variants.mask: By DrawDesc.mask's alpha (the subtree draws offscreen).

MaskDesc.description: An alpha mask over an element's subtree: a gradient's alpha, else an image's.

gradient.description: The gradient whose alpha masks (a list fading at its edge).

texture.description: The image whose alpha masks, stretched over the element.

uv.description: The image's region; null is the whole texture.

MaterialName.description: What a layer composites through: a built-in UI material, or a custom one. params is read per material.

x-og-variants.dissolve: [threshold 0–1, edge width, noise scale (CSS px), _], [edge colour rgba].
x-og-variants.shine: [position 0–1 across the diagonal (negative sweeps by the clock at -position a second), width, angle (rad), intensity], [colour rgba].
x-og-variants.hologram: [scanline spacing (CSS px), flicker 0–1, chromatic split (CSS px), scanline strength], [tint rgba].
x-og-variants.glitch: [strength 0–1, slice height (CSS px), split (CSS px), rate (Hz)].
x-og-variants.ripple: [amplitude (CSS px), wavelength (CSS px), speed (CSS px/s), _], [centre x, y as fractions].
x-og-variants.outline: [width (CSS px), _, _, _], [colour rgba]: an outline of the layer's alpha.

LayerDesc.description: The element's subtree drawn offscreen, then composited through a material (a card that dissolves, a hologram panel).

custom.description: The custom material, for material custom.

params.description: Its parameters: up to four vec4s, flattened (16 numbers); for a custom material, missing ones are its defaults.

TextShadowDesc.description: A shadow under an element's text.

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's shadow.

TextOutlineDesc.description: An outline around an element's glyphs.

width.description: Its width (up to the font's distance range).

color.description: Its colour; null is the theme's shadow.

align.description: Across the glyph's edge, inside it or outside it.

TextEffectsDesc.description: Effects of the text an element holds (its labels and rich text).

fill.description: A gradient fill over each line's box instead of its colour.

DrawDesc.description: What an element draws with (og.ui.setDraw), over its background: its shape, fills and strokes in order, effects, opacity and blend, how it clips its children, and whether its subtree draws offscreen through a material. Colours given as theme tokens follow the style; every value is data an agent can read and set.

shape.description: Its outline; null is its rectangle with its radius.

strokes.description: Strokes, over the fills and the children, bottom first.

opacity.description: Multiplies its paints (with a layer, its composite).

blend.description: How its paints (or its layer) mix with what is under them.

layer.description: Its subtree drawn offscreen and composited through a material.

text.description: Effects of its text.

dressable.description: The draw is a component's own look for the part its element names (ElementDesc.part): where the style dresses that part, each list the dressing sets (fills, strokes, effects, material, mask, blend) replaces the draw's, a rect takes the dressing's corner, and atlas art replaces the draw. The draw's shape stays, so a ring, a star or a segment keeps its geometry in every style. False: the draw is the game's and the style never touches it.

BlendMode.description: How a paint mixes with what is under it.

x-og-variants.overlay: Multiply under half grey, screen over it.
x-og-variants.colorDodge: Brightens what is under it by the paint.

SemanticsDesc.description: What a component tells the accessibility tree about an element it built from containers (docs/ui.md §11): a role other than its kind's, a name, a value and states. Absent fields leave what the element's kind gives it.

role.description: Its role: button, link, text, heading, image, checkbox, radio, switch, slider, spinbutton, textbox, combobox, listbox, option, tab, tablist, tabpanel, radiogroup, progressbar, meter, timer, status, alert, log (a feed whose new lines are read: a killfeed, subtitles), dialog, alertdialog, tooltip, separator, group, region, navigation, toolbar, menu, menubar, menuitem, menuitemcheckbox, menuitemradio, list, listitem, tree, treeitem, table, grid, row, rowheader, columnheader, cell, gridcell, figure or scrollbar; empty keeps its kind's.

name.description: Its accessible name; null keeps what it shows.

description.description: Read after the name; null is none.

value.description: Its value as people read it (`3 of 12`, `Sorted ascending`); null is none.

checked.description: Checked (a menu item's check); null is not checkable.

selected.description: Selected (a tab, a row, an option); null is not selectable.

expanded.description: Expanded (an accordion header, a tree item, a menu button); null is not expandable.

disabled.description: Shown but inert (a disabled menu item, a locked tab): disabled in the tree, and its interaction state group's disabled state.

valueNow.description: A range's value as a number (a scroll position, a page); null is no range.

WorldTarget.description: What an anchored element or a world panel is placed on: an entity (its world pose, down og.Parent) or a world point.

entity.description: The entity; null places it on point.

point.description: The world point, when entity is null.

AnchorScaleMode.description: How an anchored element's size follows its distance from the camera.

x-og-variants.constant: Its laid-out size at every distance (a nameplate that stays readable).
x-og-variants.distance: 1 at reference world units, larger nearer and smaller farther, between minScale and maxScale (a tag that feels in the world).

WorldOcclusion.description: What the scene in front of an anchored element does to it: a depth test of its point against the frame's depth, on the GPU.

x-og-variants.none: Drawn over the scene.
x-og-variants.fade: Drawn at occludedAlpha where the scene is in front.
x-og-variants.hide: Not drawn where the scene is in front.

Declutter.description: How an anchored element that overlaps one of higher priority (or as high and nearer) resolves.

x-og-variants.none: It overlaps.
x-og-variants.shift: Moved the shortest way clear (else stacked above).
x-og-variants.stack: Moved above what it overlaps, one over another (a crowd's nameplates).

EdgeClampDesc.description: Edge clamping for a waypoint or a ping: off the screen or behind the camera it stays inside the safe area, on the edge toward its point, with an arrow pointing there.

margin.description: Inset from the safe area's edges.

arrow.description: The arrow's ink; null draws none.

WorldAnchorDesc.description: An element anchored in the world (docs/ui.md §14): laid out at its own size and placed each tick on its target's point projected with the tick's camera. A nameplate, an interaction prompt, a speech bubble, a waypoint.

target.description: What it sits on.

offset.description: Added to the point in world units (above a head: 0, 2, 0).

screenOffsetX.description: Moves it right on the screen.

screenOffsetY.description: Moves it down on the screen.

pivot.description: Its point that sits on the projected point; the default is its bottom centre.

direction.description: Which way it lays out its children; the default is a column.

align.description: Where children sit along the main axis.

radius.description: Corner radius.

scale.description: How its size follows its distance.

reference.description: For scale distance: the distance at which it is its laid-out size.

minScale.description: For scale distance: the smallest it gets.

maxScale.description: For scale distance: the largest it gets.

occlusion.description: What the scene in front of it does.

occludedAlpha.description: Its opacity behind the scene, for occlusion fade.

lod.description: Level-of-detail distances, ascending: level k from lod[k - 1] on (AnchorInfo.lod; build less at a higher level).

maxDistance.description: Hidden past this distance, fading over its last tenth; 0 never.

declutter.description: How it resolves against the anchors it overlaps.

priority.description: Higher keeps its place; equal priorities favour the nearer.

clamp.description: Edge clamping; null lets it leave the screen.

fadeTicks.description: Ticks a fade (declutter, distance, appearing) takes; 0 is 6.

contain.description: Without clamp: while its point is in the safe area its box is kept inside it (a nameplate near the edge slides in rather than being cut), and it fades out as the point leaves the safe area.

AnchorInfo.description: Where an anchored element stands: its distance and level of detail from this tick's camera, the rest as last tick placed it.

inView.description: Its point is in front of the camera and within maxDistance (or clamped to the edge).

onScreen.description: Its point projects inside the screen.

distance.description: From the camera.

angle.description: Toward its point from the screen's centre, clockwise from +x (the edge arrow's).

scale.description: The scale it was drawn at.

WorldPanelDesc.description: A world panel (docs/ui.md §14): a UI tree drawn into a render target that a mesh shows (a terminal, a cockpit screen, a shop sign), reached by the pointer through a ray onto its quad.

target.description: The colour of an og.render.renderTarget made with format rgba16float (RenderTargetInfo.texture); give the mesh's material it as map (lit) or emissiveMap with colour black (unlit). It shows the frame after the UI drew it. Null: laid out and hit, drawn nowhere.

width.description: Its layout width; the target's pixels spread over it.

quad.description: Where its quad is: centred on the target's pose, facing its +Z (an og.render.planeGeometry of quadWidth by quadHeight on that entity). Null: no ray reaches it.

rotation.description: The quad's rotation after its target's.

direction.description: Which way it lays out its children; the default is a column.

background.description: Its fill; null draws none (the target clears to transparent).

PanelInfo.description: What the pointer does on a world panel this tick.

pointed.description: The ray from the pointer meets the panel's quad (and no screen element is under it): its controls take the press.

x.description: Where on the panel, from its top left.

y.description: Where on the panel, from its top left.

distance.description: Along the ray to the hit.

MassKind.description: What a mass element template draws.

x-og-variants.number: The instance's value as a number (a damage number, a score).
x-og-variants.text: One of strings, by the instance's value (a nameplate, a loot label).
x-og-variants.bar: A bar filled to the instance's value 0–1 with a ghost at its ghost (an overhead health bar).
x-og-variants.icon: Frame value of frames on texture (a status icon).

MassEase.description: How a mass element's timeline moves into a key.

x-og-variants.back: Out, past the key and back (a pop).
x-og-variants.step: Holds the key before until this one.

MassSpace.description: Where a mass element's position is.

x-og-variants.world: A world point, projected by the GPU each frame.

x-og-variants.square: A rectangle of size (a long thin one is a streak).

MassKey.description: A key of a mass element's timeline, evaluated in the shader.

ease.description: How it moves into this key.

MassTemplateDesc.description: A mass element template (docs/ui.md §14): declared once, then instanced thousands of times a frame with a few values each. No instance is laid out; its motion is the timeline, evaluated on the GPU.

font.description: Numbers and text: the font (one page); null is the UI's body font.

texture.description: Icons: the texture its frames are in.

strings.description: Text: the strings an instance's value picks.

frames.description: Icons: uv rectangles, four numbers each (u0, v0, u1, v1).

barBack.description: Bars: the track's ink; null is near black at 85 %.

barGhost.description: Bars: the ghost's ink; null is pale.

size.description: Text and numbers: x is the em size; bars, icons and particles: width and height.

pivot.description: The element's point on its position, fractions (0.5, 1: its bottom centre).

lifetime.description: Ticks an instance lives; 0 shows pushed instances for their tick only.

keys.description: The timeline over its life (up to 8).

drift.description: Each instance drifts sideways up to this far over its life, by its seed.

gravity.description: Added downward over its life, this much at its end.

drag.description: Instances' velocity slows to rest over the life.

reference.description: World space: the distance at which it is its size, nearer larger and farther smaller; 0 keeps its screen size.

minScale.description: World space: the smallest distance scale.

maxScale.description: World space: the largest distance scale.

occlusion.description: World space: what the scene in front of an instance does.

occludedAlpha.description: Its opacity behind the scene, for occlusion fade.

outline.description: Text and numbers: an outline's ink; null draws none.

MassInstance.description: One mass element: a few values; its template does the rest.

position.description: A world point, or CSS pixels (x, y) in screen space.

value.description: The number, the string or frame index, or the bar's fill 0–1.

color.description: Its ink (text, icon tint, bar fill, particle); null is white.

scale.description: Multiplies its timeline's scale (a critical hit).

EmitFrom.description: Where on its element a particle starts.

ParticlesDesc.description: UI particles from an element (docs/ui.md §5.5): confetti, sparks, coin streams, rarity bursts. Drawn over it on its layer, clipped by its clip, seeded so a replay throws the same. Nothing under reduced motion.

rate.description: Particles a second while it is built.

burst.description: Particles at once on a tick fire is set.

lifetimeMs.description: How long a particle lives; 0 is 900.

size.description: Its size.

colors.description: Picked by each particle's seed; empty is the accent.

travelMin.description: The shortest way a particle flies over its life.

direction.description: Its heading, clockwise from +x (-π/2 is up).

spread.description: The spread about the heading (2π is every way).

gravity.description: Added downward over its life, this much at its end.

spin.description: Turns over its life, up to this many either way.

align.description: Its rotation follows its heading (a streak flying outward).

endScale.description: Its scale at the end of its life.

clip.description: Clipped by the element's clip (a scroll view, a masked panel).

MetaKind.description: What a meta layer draws over the scene.

x-og-variants.vignette: Its colour at the edges, clear in the middle (a damage vignette).
x-og-variants.material: The frame under it composited through a UI material (a ripple for sanity, a glitch for a hit).

MetaDesc.description: A meta layer (docs/ui.md §14): full screen, over the scene and under the screen's elements, never taking input.

color.description: Vignette and tint: its ink; null is a deep red.

inner.description: Vignette: clear out to this fraction of the half diagonal.

outer.description: Vignette: full colour from this fraction on.

material.description: Material: the built-in material, or custom.

params.description: Material: its parameters, up to four vec4s flattened.

pulseHz.description: Pulses this many times a second (a low-health heartbeat); 0 is steady.

pulseDepth.description: How far a pulse dims it.

SceneViewportDesc.description: The viewport element (docs/ui.md §5.5): a camera's view of a scene layer shown in the layout (a character on a turntable, an item to inspect). Draw it with an og.CameraView into a render target on its own layers, with its own lights; this element shows the target and passes input in.

texture.description: The target's colour (RenderTargetInfo.texture).

width.description: Its width; null is 320 CSS px.

height.description: Its height; null is 320 CSS px.

cameraTarget.description: What its camera looks at, for rays.

fov.description: Its camera's vertical field of view; 0 gives no ray.

radius.description: Corner radius.

label.description: What the probe and the accessibility tree call it.

SceneViewportInfo.description: What the pointer does in a viewport this tick.

pixelWidth.description: The target width that fills it at the device's pixel ratio.

pixelHeight.description: The target height that fills it.

pressed.description: A press that started in it is held.

drag.description: The pointer's move while held this tick (orbit, turn).

at.description: The pointer in it, fractions of its box from the top left.

ray.description: The ray into its scene through the pointer.

UiDocEvent.description: Something a document did (docs/ui.md §10.2): a click, a changed control, a list row selected, a named event (`emit`, a timeline's callback), an action, a two-way write, or Back on a layer whose Back is `emit`.

mount.description: The document's mount: the screen's name, or a component instance's path.

kind.description: click, changed, select, emit, action, set or back.

name.description: The element's id (click), the prop (changed), the list (select), the event or action's name, or the viewmodel path a `set` wrote.

value.description: The new value (changed, set), the row's index (select); null otherwise.

UiDocResponse.description: What mounting a document answers: its events this tick (and, for a screen, those of its builds code did not see), its root's path, and for a component its props after its two-way writes.

path.description: Its root's path; empty when it was not built.

props.description: A component's props after its writes (a screen's viewmodel is og.ui.screenVm's).

UiLayer.description: A layer of the stack (docs/ui.md §8.1), as its screen declares it.

serial.description: Its number, unique for the UI's life: what push answered.

screen.description: The screen's name; also its layer's id, the first segment of its elements' paths.

kind.description: hud, menu, modal, popover, toast, tooltip or system.

input.description: game (input reaches gameplay), menu (input stays in the UI) or all.

capture.description: It takes the pointer on its gaps too.

pause.description: The game pauses while it is on the stack.

under.description: What happens to the layers under it: none, dim, blur or hide.

back.description: What Back does: pop, none or `emit <event>`.

focus.description: Where focus starts, a path below its root (empty: its first control).

remember.description: Focus returns where it was when it is the top again.

hidden.description: A layer above hides it: it is not built.

inert.description: A menu layer above takes its input.

x-og-variants.hold: When it has been held holdMs.

UiActionDesc.description: A named UI action (docs/ui.md §8.2) bound to og-input's controls: a component asks for an action, not a key.

name.description: Its name: confirm, back, tabNext, tabPrev, details, or the game's own.

toggle.description: A hold's toggle alternative (XAG 107): a tap turns it on, the next tap off; og.ui.actionHeld answers true between.

label.description: What it says when no document gives it a hint.

action.description: A gameplay action (og.input.defineAction) it follows instead of keys and buttons: it is down when that action is, and its glyph is that action's binding on the device used last, so the player's rebinding moves the prompt too. Empty: keys and buttons.

UiDevice.description: The device a glyph set is for: the one the player used last.

x-og-variants.switch: A Nintendo Switch pad (south is B).

UiGlyph.description: An action's control on the device used last.

icon.description: The icon a style's set draws: `key.enter`, `xbox.a`, `ps.cross`, `switch.b`, `pad.south`, `touch.<action>`.

text.description: The text that names it: `Enter`, `A`, `×`.

UiActionHint.description: One entry of the action bar: an action the top layer accepts, its hint and glyph.

hint.description: What it does here (the document's `actions` line, else its label).

icon.description: Its glyph's icon.

text.description: Its glyph's text.

CoreAction.description: The actions the engine ships. Arguments follow the action, separated by `:`.

x-og-variants.screenshot: `screenshot[:path][:full|:N]`: capture the next frame. Without a renderer it writes nothing and logs, not as a warning, that the frame is unchecked.
x-og-variants.listen: `listen[:path][:seconds]`: write the last seconds of rendered audio as a WAV.
x-og-variants.touch_move_to: `touch_move_to:<ui id>`: move the pointer to a UI element.
x-og-variants.touch_move: `touch_move:x,y`: move the pointer to CSS pixel coordinates.
x-og-variants.touch_start: `touch_start`: press the pointer where it is.
x-og-variants.touch: `touch:<id>:<down|move|up>:<x,y | ui id>`: a further touch (pointer 1 to 4) held while the pointer is busy elsewhere.
x-og-variants.gamepad: `gamepad:<a+b+...|->[@pad][:lx,ly[,rx,ry]][:lt,rt]`: set a pad's whole state (pad 0 unless `@1` to `@3` follows the buttons); `gamepad:off` disconnects it.
x-og-variants.key_down: `key_down:[Mod+]<Key>`: hold a key by its code, with the modifiers named before it (`Shift+ArrowLeft`, `Meta+ArrowLeft` for Command, apart from Ctrl).
x-og-variants.key_up: `key_up:[Mod+]<Key>`: release a key, then the modifiers named before it.
x-og-variants.type: `type:<text>`: type text, two ticks per character: its key press and the character as typed text (input.TextInput); a character no key types is typed text alone. The text runs to the `;` exactly, a trailing space included; after it a text field takes typed text only, so a bare key_down types nothing.
x-og-variants.compose: `compose:<text>`: an input method's composition so far (input.TextInput composing); a focused text field shows it underlined at the caret, `compose:` with nothing ends it.
x-og-variants.commit: `commit:<text>`: an input method commits text; a focused text field inserts it and the composition ends.
x-og-variants.move_to_text: `move_to_text:[=]text[@N]`: move the pointer to the UI element showing the text (exactly with `=`, the Nth with `@N`).
x-og-variants.frame_entity: `frame_entity:<entity>`: point the camera at an entity.
x-og-variants.dump_world: `dump_world[:path]`: tables, systems and their matched counts.
x-og-variants.dump_ui: `dump_ui[:path]`: the UI tree with bounds, and `style`, the configured UI style's name (empty for the engine's default style).
x-og-variants.set: `set:<entity>.<component>.<field>=<value>` or `set:<Resource>.<field>=<value>`: a Tune write through the schema: a number, `true` or `false` for a bool, `x,y,z` for a vector, an enum's variant name or its index; refused outside the field's FieldOptions min/max, never clamped.
x-og-variants.get: `get:<Resource>[.<field>]` or `get:<entity>[.<component>[.<field>]][:path]`: read through the schema as game code sees it (an enum as its variant's name, `"music"`; og.Time whole, with rate and the time scale; the DirectionalLight og.DayNight drives with the colour, intensity and direction it is drawn with), logged and written as JSON to `get-<tick>.json` (more unnamed ones on one tick: `get-<tick>-2.json`, ...).
x-og-variants.pause: `pause`: hold the clock; advance still steps.
x-og-variants.advance: `advance:<ticks>`: take fixed steps; the steps the script schedules for the same time after it run once it has stepped (a time is seconds: `0:advance:300;0:screenshot` shoots tick 300).
x-og-variants.describe: `describe[:path]`: write the frame as data (probe.Description): the visible entities with screen boxes, depth order and occlusion from the entity-id pass, what each secondary camera (og.CameraView, og.Mirror) shows from its own pass, the UI elements with rects and text, the camera.
x-og-variants.expect: `expect:<what>`: assert at this tick (probe.ExpectResult): `entity:<id>:within:x,y,w,h` (its visible box, CSS pixels) or `:within:x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` (its position, world units), `event:<Name>[:count]`, `ui:text:[=]<text>`, `region:x,y,w,h:color:#rrggbb[:tolerance]`, `frame:<ref.png>:rmse:<=v`, `state:<path>==<value>` (also != < <= > >=), `entity:<id>:<path>==<value>` (a field of its dump_entity: `render.lod==2`, `og.Transform.position.y>0`), `timings:<path>==<value>` (state().timings: `triangles<=1500000`). A failure is a warning with the tick and the observed value; `og run --json` lists every result and exits 1 on a failure. Frame expectations without a renderer are unchecked, as are an entity's `render.*` fields and the renderer's timings (`triangles`, `render`, `passes`).
x-og-variants.save_scene: `save_scene[:path][:spawned]`: write every scene the world was assembled from back from the world (the boot scene's, then each og.world.instantiate made, each to its own `.ogt`): only the lines whose values changed (comments and order kept), the fields set or patch tuned, and resources as `resource <Name> { }` blocks; with `spawned`, the entities the game spawned at run time under the boot scene's marked section. To each scene's source, or with a path the boot scene's to that file under the output directory and the others beside it.
x-og-variants.help: `help`: list every action the channel knows, core and registered.
x-og-variants.mouse_move: `mouse_move:dx,dy`: move the mouse by relative CSS pixels (movementX/Y, summed in og.Pointers.movement: mouse-look) with the pointer's position held, as a locked pointer moves.
x-og-variants.pointer_lock: `pointer_lock:<on|off>`: report the pointer locked or released (og.PointerLock.locked), as the web shell does from pointerlockchange; headless hosts never lock on their own.
x-og-variants.apply_prefab: `apply_prefab:<entity>[:<Component>[.<field>]][:base]`: move an entity's prefab overrides (all, a component's or one field; a field set at run time too) into its prefab's `.ogt` at the entity's node, and out of its scene's instance block, so the scene cooks to the same world and every other instance takes the values; with `base`, into a variant's base (docs/design.md §2.5, prefabs).
x-og-variants.revert_prefab: `revert_prefab:<entity>[:<Component>[.<field>]]`: drop an entity's prefab overrides (all, a component's or one field) from its scene's instance block, and set the live values back to the prefab's.

A `grass` field is seen at field fidelity, not per blade: its coverage is the ground it grows on lifted half its tallest blade, so a pixel between blades answers the field and a tip above that height answers what is behind it.
