TerrainData.description: A loaded terrain: its heights, control map and layers.

TerrainBrushMode.description: What og.terrain.edit does under its brush.

x-og-variants.raise: Raise the heights by `strength` metres at the centre.
x-og-variants.lower: Lower them by `strength` metres at the centre.
x-og-variants.flatten: Pull them towards the brush centre's y, by `strength` (0 to 1) at the centre.
x-og-variants.smooth: Pull each towards its neighbours' mean, by `strength` (0 to 1) at the centre.
x-og-variants.paint: Paint `layer` into the control map, by `strength` (0 to 1) at the centre.
x-og-variants.hole: Cut holes: every cell whose centre the brush weighs at least half (its falloff times `strength`) is cut out of the surface, neither drawn nor collided with.
x-og-variants.fill: Fill holes in again where `hole` would cut them.

TerrainStampMode.description: What og.terrain.stamp does to the height field under a stamp's mesh.

x-og-variants.carve: Lower the ground under the mesh to `depth` below its underside (the lowest of its triangles over each height sample), so the mesh is the surface there: a cliff's face and lip, an arch, an overhang. On the edge of what the mesh covers the ground goes down to the underside itself, so the ground beside the mesh meets its foot with no trench. Ground already lower is left as it is.
x-og-variants.hole: Cut out every cell whose centre the mesh covers (seen from above), neither drawn nor collided with: the mesh stands in the ground's place (a cave mouth, a tunnel's portal).

Terrain.description: Draws a loaded terrain placed by the entity's world transform (centred on its position, turned and scaled with it), with its layers (as cooked, or as og.terrain.setLayer left them), casting shadows unless told not to.

visible.description: Draw it; false keeps it only as the ground its og.TerrainScatter copies stand on (nothing else sees it).

castShadows.description: Cast the directional and local lights' shadows (it always receives them).

horizonShadows.description: Shade it by its own horizon, baked by the cook: past the sun's shadow cascades a valley behind a ridge falls into its shade (to the horizon), and everywhere the sky a valley's walls hide lights it less.

lodSpacing.description: The finest clipmap level's spacing (0: the terrain file's, or the samples' spacing).

lodRing.description: Quads per side of every clipmap level at least (0: the terrain file's, else 64; 16 to 256, rounded to a multiple of 4). The levels grow to 128 quads where a coarser level's height error would show (`lodError`); 256 draws every level that large, at about 3 ms more on an M4 Pro.

lodError.description: Pixels of height error a coarser clipmap level may show before the finer one reaches further out (0: 1): a peak that is large on screen keeps its shape at any distance. Larger draws fewer vertices.

displacementDistance.description: Metres from the camera within which layers with a `displacement` raise and lower the drawn ground by their height maps, fading out over the last 40%. Near the camera the clipmap's levels then grow finer than the samples (down to a 32nd of the finest displacing layer's `tile`, a 32nd of a sample at most; `lodSpacing` above 0 decides instead) to carry the relief, which costs vertices, mostly in the depth prepass (island-near with every layer displaced 8 cm: 0.9 to 2.8 ms of prepass on an M4 Pro). 0: no displacement.

TerrainStamp.description: Draws a mesh as part of a loaded terrain: a cliff, arch or overhang the height field cannot make, placed by the entity's world transform. It is shaded with the terrain's own layers and rules (by its own normal: grass on its top, rock on its walls, biplanar where steep) and, within `blend` metres above the ground under it, takes the ground's look and normal, so it meets the terrain without a seam. Drawn with the og.Terrain drawing the same data. Only drawn: carve the ground under it with og.terrain.stamp, and make it solid with an og.Collider naming the same geometry.

blend.description: Metres above the ground under it over which the mesh fades into the ground's look: wholly the ground over its lowest third, then fading to the mesh's own (0: a hard edge).

castShadows.description: Cast shadows (with its terrain's own castShadows).

TerrainScatter.description: Scatters copies of a mesh (grass, flowers, stones) over a loaded terrain near the camera, where one of its layers shows: on a jittered grid fixed to the terrain, so each copy keeps its place, size and turn as the camera moves, every cell growing one with the probability of the layer's weight there (its control-map channel times its slope and altitude rules, over all the layers' weights). Over the outer `fade` of `distance` copies shrink and thin out, each shrinking to nothing over its own part of the fade (no dither, so no grain under TAA). The renderer places them itself, a chunk of the grid at a time, once, and draws the chunks in range: copies cost about nothing per frame while the camera stays. They grow over the og.Terrain drawing the same data, placed as it is. Drawn only: no colliders, and the copies are not entities.

geometry.description: The mesh, its origin at its root. When it belongs to the named impostor model, all of that primitive's node placements are applied in model space, at every distance (including impostorDistance 0). Other geometry must already be in that space.

layer.description: The terrain layer that places it, 0 to 15.

density.description: Copies per square metre where the layer's weight is 1.

distance.description: How far from the camera, along x and z, copies are placed.

fade.description: The outer part of `distance` over which copies shrink and thin out to nothing.

align.description: How far copies lean with the ground: 0 upright, 1 along its normal.

seed.description: Another seed places the copies elsewhere.

castShadows.description: Whether the copies cast shadows (grass usually does not: three.js meshes cast only with castShadow set).

sway.description: How much og.Wind sways the copies: 1 as it blows, 0 still (stones), between for stiffer stems. Each vertex above the mesh's origin moves by its height, so model the copy with its root at the origin.

impostor.description: A glTF (og.load.gltf) of the same complete mesh, cooked with an octahedral impostor (its import settings' `model { impostor true }`): copies farther than impostorDistance draw as that impostor, cross-dithered over the last tenth before it by a blue-noise pattern that changes every frame, which temporal antialiasing resolves to a smooth blend. Mesh and impostor bounds must agree in model space; a mismatch skips the scatter and reports render.scatterIssue in its entity dump and a runtime warning. None: the supplied geometry at every distance, without model placement.

impostorDistance.description: How far from the camera, along x and z, copies draw as their mesh before their impostor takes over; 0 never switches. Useful below `distance`.

noiseScale.description: The size of the patches noiseThreshold gathers copies into.

noiseThreshold.description: Gathers the copies into patches: a cell grows its copy only where a smooth noise of noiseScale patches (0 to 1, about half of it past 0.5) rises past this, the patches' edges thinning over a short band. 0: everywhere.

footprint.description: How far, along x and z, this scatter's copies keep from the copies of every og.TerrainScatter placed before it over the same og.Terrain: the larger of the two footprints (trees placed first keep flowers from their trunks). 0: none.

priority.description: Scatters of a higher priority over the same og.Terrain are placed first, their footprints cleared in the ones after; equal priorities are placed in entity order.

avoidWater.description: Grows no copy whose ground stands less than this above an og.Water surface over it (an endless sea everywhere), nor under it: reeds stop short of the shore. 0: anywhere.

densityMap.description: Thins the copies where its red channel is below 1, over the terrain's extent (its top row along the terrain's -z edge, as the control map; loaded linear), each copy kept while its own value is below the map's: a path cleared through the flowers. Drawn only, where the renderer culls copies on the GPU (RenderCapabilities.compute): placement and footprints do not read it. 0: none.

Grass.description: A field of grass over a loaded terrain where one of its layers shows, generated on the GPU every frame out to `distance` (a meadow with every other field at its default). Blades are curved strips placed on a blue-noise pattern fixed to the terrain, so each keeps its place as the camera moves; they grow where the layer's weight is (its control-map channel times its slope and altitude rules), never over holes, in clumps that share their tint and height. With distance they thin out, the ones left widening to keep the ground covered, and take fewer vertices (15, 7, then 3); under and past them the terrain takes the field's average colour (`farTint`), so the far field reads as grass to the horizon with no seam. og.Wind bends them in gusts that roll across the field, each blade swaying on its own; lit like the terrain under them, with light through blades lit from behind (`translucency`), a sheen on the upper blade and the roots shaded by their neighbours. Visual only: drawn from the tick, nothing in the simulation reads it, the same tick draws the same blades on every run. It grows over the og.Terrain drawing the same data (a visible one).

layer.description: The terrain layer that places it, 0 to 15.

density.description: Blades per square metre near the camera where the layer's weight is 1.

distance.description: How far from the camera blades are drawn; they thin out to nothing there.

farTint.description: The terrain takes the field's average colour under its blades, where they thin out and past them, so the gaps and the far field read as the same grass.

heightVariation.description: How much shorter blades are than the tallest: 0 all alike, 1 down to nothing.

width.description: A blade's width at its root.

curve.description: How far blades droop along their length: 0 straight, 1 arching over.

lean.description: How far blades lean at rest, as a share of their height.

clumpSize.description: The size of the clumps blades grow in, sharing their tint and height.

clumpLean.description: How far blades lean out from their clump's centre, as a share of their height.

tufts.description: How far blades are pulled in towards their clump's centre: 0 an even lawn, 1 tight tufts.

dryColor.description: Dry grass's colour (linear): dry clumps and drying tips.

colorVariation.description: How much blades vary in brightness by clump, blade and patch.

dryness.description: The share of clumps that are dry, and how far tips dry.

translucency.description: How much sunlight passes through a blade lit from behind, tinted by it.

sheen.description: The upper blade's gloss: gusts show as a moving sheen.

sway.description: How much og.Wind bends the blades: 1 as it blows, 0 still.

stiffness.description: How stiff the blades are: 0 bends furthest, 1 least, and sways faster.

flutter.description: How much the tips of near blades shiver in the wind.

castShadows.description: Whether the blades cast the sun's shadows (near the camera, into the first two cascades). Either way a blade is shaded by the field's own canopy between it and the sun, darker towards the roots the denser the field and the lower the sun.

seed.description: Another seed places the blades elsewhere.

recovery.description: How long blades pressed by an og.GrassPusher take to stand again after it leaves.

types.description: Up to three more kinds of blade growing in the field among its own (a meadow of grass, taller reeds and flowers): entities carrying an og.GrassType. The field's own height, width, curve and colours are its first kind. Each clump grows one kind, chosen by `typeMap` or, without one, by the kinds' `share`; 0s and entities without an og.GrassType are skipped.

typeMap.description: Where each of `types` grows, over the terrain's extent (its top row along the terrain's -z edge, as the control map; loaded linear): red, green and blue the share of the first, second and third of `types` at each point, the rest the field's own kind. 0: every kind everywhere, by its share.

densityMap.description: Multiplies the blades' density over the terrain's extent (its red channel, laid out as typeMap; loaded linear): black grows none, a path through the meadow. 0: none.

heightMap.description: Multiplies the blades' height over the terrain's extent (its red channel, laid out as typeMap; loaded linear): short grass by a path, tall in the hollows. 0: none.

GrassType.description: Another kind of blade for og.Grass fields that list this entity in their `types`: its shape and colours replace the field's for the clumps that grow it, the rest (density, wind, lighting, dryness) is the field's.

height.description: The tallest blade of this kind.

width.description: A blade's width at its root.

curve.description: How far its blades droop along their length: 0 straight, 1 arching over.

tipColor.description: The tips' colour (linear): a flower's petals.

share.description: How many clumps grow this kind for each one of the field's own, where no typeMap says.

GrassPusher.description: Presses og.Grass blades and og.TerrainScatter copies where the entity stands: a vertical capsule from its position up `height`, reaching `radius` on the ground. Blades under it bend away from it and flatten, and stay pressed after it passes, standing again over the field's `recovery` (a trail behind a walker or a horse); swaying copies part the same way. Blades shorter than the gap under a pusher floating above them are not touched. Visual only, where the renderer can (RenderCapabilities.compute; elsewhere it does nothing): nothing in the simulation reads it. The 32 nearest the camera press.

radius.description: How far it reaches on the ground.

height.description: How tall it is: its bottom is the entity's position.

strength.description: How hard it presses: 1 flattens the blades, 0.3 parts them.

data.description: Its handle, for og.Terrain.data and this module's functions.

geometry.description: The height field registered with physics under this handle: the mesh of an og.Collider of shape SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD.

size.description: Its extent along x and z, centred on its entity.

minHeight.description: The lowest point above its entity.

layers.description: Its material layers (up to 16).

collision.description: Whether its terrain file asks for a collider (`collision`, default true).

holes.description: Whether it has holes (its terrain file's `holes` map, or og.terrain.edit's `hole` brush): cells cut out of the surface, neither drawn nor collided with.

seaLevel.description: A generated terrain's sea level (`generate { sea <m> }`) above its entity: place an og.Water there, the terrain's size; null without a sea.

origin.description: Where it stands: its og.Terrain entity's world position.

quaternion.description: How it is turned: its og.Terrain entity's world rotation (the zero value: along world x and z).

scale.description: How it is scaled: its og.Terrain entity's world scale.

height.description: The world y of the surface (the triangles drawn at the finest level and collided with) on the terrain's up axis through (x, z): straight down for a terrain turned only about y.

normal.description: The surface normal, smoothed between samples as the renderer shades it.

slope.description: The normal's angle from straight up.

inside.description: Whether the point is over the terrain (outside, the nearest edge answers).

hole.description: Whether the point is over one of its holes: nothing collides there, and `height` is the surface the hole was cut from.

TerrainBounds.description: A terrain's box in world space.

TerrainBrush.description: One runtime edit of a terrain (og.terrain.edit).

origin.description: Where the terrain stands: its og.Terrain entity's world position.

quaternion.description: How it is turned: its og.Terrain entity's world rotation.

scale.description: How it is scaled: its og.Terrain entity's world scale.

center.description: The brush's centre in world space; its y is flatten's target height.

radius.description: The brush's radius in world metres (across the terrain's surface).

strength.description: World metres at the centre (raise, lower), or how far to go, 0 to 1 (flatten, smooth, paint; hole and fill cut where it times the falloff is at least half).

falloff.description: The outer part of the radius over which it fades to nothing (0: a hard edge, 1: fading from the centre).

samples.description: Height or control-map samples it touched.

stamp.description: og.terrain.stamp: the stamp's id, for og.terrain.unstamp (from 1). 0 for every other edit.

TerrainStampDesc.description: One stamp of a mesh into a terrain (og.terrain.stamp).

origin.description: Where the terrain stands: its og.Terrain entity's world position.

quaternion.description: How it is turned: its og.Terrain entity's world rotation.

scale.description: How it is scaled: its og.Terrain entity's world scale.

position.description: Where the mesh stands: its og.TerrainStamp entity's world position.

rotation.description: How the mesh is turned: its entity's world rotation.

size.description: How the mesh is scaled: its entity's world scale.

mode.description: What it does to the ground.

depth.description: carve: how far below the mesh's underside the ground goes, so it stays hidden under the mesh.

TerrainLayerDesc.description: One material layer of a terrain: its look and the rules that place it. A layer shows where its control-map channel (1 without a map) times its slope band times its altitude band is high; the layers' weights are normalised.

color.description: Multiplies the layer's texture (linear).

tile.description: Metres per repeat of its textures.

triplanar.description: Sample by three projections blended by the normal (for cliffs). `projectSlope` above 0 decides instead.

projectSlope.description: The slope past which the layer is sampled by the two projections facing the surface most (biplanar: no projection seen edge-on, so a steep face does not streak) instead of from above, faded over 10° around it; below it, from above. 0: `triplanar` decides.

antiTiling.description: How far the texture's repeat is broken: each point blends three hexagonal tiles of it, each turned (by up to half a turn at 1) and moved by its own hash, so no period shows across a field. 0: the plain repeat.

heightContrast.description: How sharp the height blend (the terrain file's `heightBlend`) is at this layer's edges: 0 the default window, 1 ten times narrower (a crisp rim).

macroVariation.description: A slow drift of brightness and hue over the ground and, with distance, the texture at a quarter of its frequency blended in, so a field of one layer does not read as one texture from afar. 0: none.

displacement.description: Metres the drawn ground rises and falls by the layer's height map (its albedo's alpha, about its middle) near the camera (og.Terrain's `displacementDistance`), where the layer shows and the ground is not steep: pebbles, cobbles and rock stand out of the ground at its silhouette and in its shadows. Only drawn: collision, og.terrain.sample and picking keep the height field. 0: flat.

normalStrength.description: How strongly its normal map bends the surface.

slopeMin.description: The flattest slope it shows on.

slopeFade.description: How far past its slopes it fades out.

altitudeMin.description: The lowest height above the terrain's origin it shows at.

altitudeFade.description: How far past its heights it fades out.

StreamCell.description: A world cell: loads its sub-scene's entities while an og.StreamAnchor is near its box, and despawns them when none is (the module's doc). The box is the entity's world position ± half `size`, turned with it; a zero size is a point.

scene.description: The sub-scene it loads: set from the entity's `scene "<id>"` line when its scene spawns, or og.load.scene's handle for a cell spawned by game code. 0: none (the cell never loads).

size.description: The box's full extents, in metres along the entity's axes (its scale does not apply). Zero: a point at the entity's position.

load.description: Loads while an anchor is within this distance of the box (0: only while one is inside it).

unload.description: Unloads once every anchor is farther than this from the box, so an anchor on the edge does not load and unload it every tick; 0: 1.25 × load. Less than `load` is taken as `load`.

pin.description: Loaded whatever the anchors while true (a cell game code needs, such as a quest's destination); set it false and the anchors decide again.

persist.description: Keep what happened in it: when it unloads, its entities as they are (moved, damaged, opened; every component and name) are kept in the world's og.cells state, carried by snapshots, saves and the hash, and they come back as they were when it loads again instead of its sub-scene as authored. False: it loads as authored every time.

budget.description: The most of its entities spawned per tick while it loads, so a large cell spreads over consecutive ticks instead of one long one (0: all in one tick). `loaded` turns true, and CellEvent is sent, in the tick its last entity spawns; a cell that stops being wanted before then despawns what it spawned and sends nothing.

loaded.description: Written by the engine: true while the sub-scene's entities are in the world (from the tick it loaded until the tick it unloaded).

StreamAnchor.description: What loads cells: every entity with one (the player, a vehicle, each player of a networked game) loads the cells within their StreamCell.load of it, from its world position. Without any anchor the og.Camera resource's position anchors (refused in an og.net session).

reach.description: Added to every cell's load and unload distances for this anchor: a fast vehicle reaches further than a walker.

maxSpeed.description: The fastest it moves, for reading ahead: a cell's asset group (`cell` in its sub-scene's stream block) is fetched once this anchor is within the cell's load distance plus reach plus 2 seconds at this speed, so it has landed when the cell loads and the tick never waits for it. Read only for fetching, never by a tick (0: fetched at the load distance).

CellMember.description: Which cell an entity came from: every entity a cell's sub-scene spawns carries one, and when the cell unloads every entity naming it, with its descendants, is despawned, wherever it has moved. Remove it from an entity to keep it past its cell's unload (an item the player picked up); the cell spawns the item again from its sub-scene when it loads again.

CellEvent.description: A cell loaded or unloaded: sent in the tick it happened, before any system runs, so the tick's systems read it with the cell's entities already spawned (or despawned).

loaded.description: True: its sub-scene's entities spawned; false: its members and their descendants were despawned.

entities.description: How many entities spawned or were despawned.

x-og-variants.unloaded: Not wanted; its assets draw and play their stand-ins.
x-og-variants.queued: Wanted, waiting for room in the memory budget.
x-og-variants.loading: Admitted: its pack is being read (its memory already counts).
x-og-variants.resident: Its assets are in place of their stand-ins.
x-og-variants.failed: Its pack could not be read, or it alone needs more than the budget (StreamStatus.reason says which).

StreamEvent.description: A group changed state: sent by og.stream at the start of the tick after the change.

state.description: Its new state: STREAM_UNLOADED, STREAM_QUEUED, STREAM_LOADING, STREAM_RESIDENT or STREAM_FAILED (StreamState's order).

name.description: Its name.

wanted.description: Whether its trigger or a request wants it now.

requested.description: Whether og.stream.request asked for it (until og.stream.release).

priority.description: Higher loads first and is evicted last.

memory.description: What its assets take once loaded, in bytes.

reason.description: Why it is queued or failed; empty otherwise.

since.description: The tick of its last change.

loads.description: How many times it became resident.

kept.description: The bytes of its assets kept for the frame after it unloaded (counted in StreamBudget.used until let go); 0 otherwise.

StreamBudget.description: The streaming memory budget and every group.

budget.description: The bytes resident and loading groups may take.

used.description: The bytes they take now, with what unloaded groups keep for the frame.

kept.description: Of `used`, the bytes of assets kept for the frame after their group unloaded (an array a sprite still draws, the map the frame is lit by, ...).

peak.description: The most they ever took (never above the budget at the time).

Video.description: Cooked footage: its frames as a texture array, its sound (og.load.video).

texture.description: The texture that shows the frame its og.VideoPlayer is at (frame 0 until one plays it).

sound.description: Its sound track (og.load.sound's kind of handle, for an og.AudioSource); 0 when it has none or was cooked with `audio false`.

format.description: The frames' encoding on the GPU (`rgba8`, `bc7`, `astc4x4`, `etc2`; a stream's texture is `rgba8`).

bytes.description: Bytes its frames take on the GPU (a stream: its texture's, one frame).

streamed.description: Whether it is a stream (`stream true`: decoded as it plays) rather than a clip of cooked frames.

codec.description: A stream's codec (`av1`); empty for a clip.

poster.description: A stream's first frame as an ordinary texture, ready as soon as the bundle is (a menu's thumbnail, the picture while the stream is fetched); for a clip, VideoInfo.texture.

VideoCapabilities.description: How this host plays streams. Backend limits are reported here, never by missing members: every host loads and plays a stream through the same API.

streamed.description: Whether streams decode here: false only on a host without a renderer (a headless run without a GPU), where a stream's texture shows nothing and its sound plays as usual.

decoder.description: The AV1 decoder: `rav1d` (native, a thread per stream), `webcodecs` (the browser's VideoDecoder), `rav1d-wasm` (rav1d in a Worker of its own, where the browser has no AV1 decoder) or `none`.

hardware.description: Whether the browser reports its decoder as hardware-accelerated (WebCodecs' `prefer-hardware` is supported); false for rav1d.

maxWidth.description: The widest stream this decoder plays in real time at 30 fps (wider ones still play, with frames held where decoding falls behind): 7680 for rav1d natively and WebCodecs, 1280 (by 720, or 720 by 1280 for a portrait stream) for rav1d-wasm, which plays a larger stream's 720p rendition, cooked beside it, instead (measured; docs/design.md §2.9).

VideoPlayer.description: Plays a loaded video: VideoInfo.texture shows its current frame (frame n is the source at n / fps seconds; a stream's once decoded), and when the entity has an og.AudioSource the og.video system sets its sound, playing, pitch, loop and loop region (the picture's length) each tick so the sound plays in step, however long or often it loops: a seek or a restart starts the sound again at the new time on the next tick (AudioSource.startOffset). Each player has a texture of its own (written to `texture`): the first player of a video takes VideoInfo.texture, each further one a texture the og.video system makes for it over the same decoded frames (one frame of GPU memory each), so two players at different times show different frames. Show a player's `texture`, not VideoInfo.texture, once a video has more than one player.

time.description: Seconds into the video; written every tick, set it to seek. Double precision, as the sound's playhead: summed in f32, an hour at 60 Hz would fall 2.8 s behind its sound.

speed.description: The playback rate: 1 as cooked, 0.5 half speed (the sound's pitch follows).

loop.description: Start again at 0 past the end; otherwise hold the last frame and set finished.

frame.description: Written: the frame shown, floor(time * fps).

finished.description: Written: a player without loop reached the end.

texture.description: Written: this player's texture (VideoInfo.texture for the video's first player, a texture of its own for each further one), for a material, sprite or UI image set up from the player. It keeps it while it lives.

DebugDrawDesc.description: How a debug shape looks and how long it lasts.

color.description: The linear colour.

duration.description: How many ticks after this one it stays; 0 is this frame only (draw it every tick it should show).

rotation.description: The shape's rotation: a box's or a sphere's circles', the axes' frame.

Path.description: A path: its points, kind and arc-length table.

PathKind.description: How the points make the curve.

x-og-variants.catmullRom: Through every point, as three.js CatmullRomCurve3: tension scales the tangents (0.5 is Catmull-Rom).
x-og-variants.bezier: Cubic Bezier segments: anchor, two controls, anchor, ... (3n + 1 points open, 3n closed).

CurveDesc.description: What makes a path (three.js's Curve; PathDesc is og.nav's path query).

points.description: The points, in order: at least 2 (catmullRom, linear), 3n + 1 open or 3n closed (bezier).

closed.description: Join the last point to the first; t wraps.

kind.description: How the points make the curve.

tension.description: catmullRom's tangent scale, as three.js's tension.

up.description: A unit up perpendicular to the tangent: world +Y made perpendicular (world +Z where the path runs straight up or down).

PathNearest.description: The point of a path nearest another point.

distance.description: How far it is from the point asked about.

PathFollower.description: Moves the entity along a path at `speed`, by the engine's og.path system after the game's systems and before physics: og.Transform.position is the path's point at `distance` plus `offset` (in the path's frame with align, else in world axes). Advanced by scaled time (slow motion, hit stop). The distance is the component's own field, so a snapshot, a restore and the world hash carry it, and writing it moves the entity there.

path.description: The path (og.path.create or og.path.find); 0 does nothing.

speed.description: Metres per second along the path; negative goes backwards.

distance.description: How far along the path it is, from its start; written every tick, set it to place the entity.

loop.description: Wrap at the end (and the start, going backwards); otherwise stop there and set `finished`.

align.description: Turn og.Transform.quaternion to face along the tangent (local -Z forward, +Y the path's up).

offset.description: Added to the path's point: along the path's right, up and backward axes with align, else world x, y and z.

finished.description: Written: a path without loop reached its end.

TimelineAsset.description: A loaded timeline: its tracks, paths, sounds and clips.

Timeline.description: Plays a loaded timeline. Set `playing` (or call og.timeline.play) to run it from `time`; write `time` (or call og.timeline.seek) to jump; og.timeline.stop goes back to 0 and lets go of what it owns.

time.description: Where it is, in seconds; written every tick it plays, set it to seek.

speed.description: Playback rate: 1 as authored, 0.5 half speed (0 holds the time while playing).

loop.description: Start over at the end; otherwise stop playing there, hand the camera back and send og.TimelineEnded.

TimelineStarted.description: A timeline started playing from stopped or ended (not on a resume from pause, nor on a loop).

TimelineMarker.description: Playback passed a marker key (a seek over one does not send it).

name.description: The marker's name (at most 63 bytes).

TimelineEnded.description: A timeline without loop reached its duration and stopped playing.

TimelineTrackInfo.description: One track of a loaded timeline.

kind.description: camera, transform, animation, audio, music, caption, event, transition, marker, property, light, visibility, post, blendshape, material, timeline or shot.

target.description: The entity a transform, animation, property, light, visibility, blendshape or material track drives, the path a rail rides, the entity a camera follows; empty otherwise.

name.description: Its `name`.

markers.description: Its markers' names, in time order.

NetMode.description: How a room's peers take their ticks (og.Lockstep.mode).

x-og-variants.lockstep: Each tick waits until every seated player's input for it is in: no prediction, no rollback; a late input holds the world.
x-og-variants.rollback: A tick runs on a missing input predicted as that player's last one, up to maxPrediction ticks past the last tick whose inputs are all in; when the real input differs the world is rewound to its own snapshot and the ticks run again within the frame (GGPO-style). Every peer agrees on the confirmed world, so hashes and og.Desync cover it alone.

Lockstep.description: Lockstep's settings and this peer's place. The game sets enabled, players, inputDelay and hashEvery (the authority's are the room's once it starts: changes while running wait for the next start); the engine sets localPlayer and running. It is this peer's own: never hashed, never compared.

enabled.description: Whether the world takes its ticks in lockstep when in a room.

players.description: The seats: the peers lockstep waits for before it starts, and whose inputs each tick waits for.

localPlayer.description: This peer's seat, the og.PlayerInput.player its input drives; `players` while it watches (a peer beyond the seats). 0 before the start.

inputDelay.description: Ticks between a player's input and the tick it acts on: the time the input has to cross the room. 2 (33 ms at 60 Hz) on a LAN, 4 to 6 over the internet.

hashEvery.description: How often the peers exchange their world hashes, in ticks (every tick is hashed, so the first divergent tick is exact); 0 compares nothing.

running.description: Whether lockstep runs: the room filled the seats and the authority started (until this peer leaves the room or turns it off).

mode.description: lockstep (the default: every tick waits for every input) or rollback (ticks run on predicted inputs and are rewound when an input differs; set before the room starts, the authority's is the room's).

stallTimeout.description: Milliseconds a running peer may stay silent before its seat is dropped (og.SeatDropped); 0 never drops a peer still in the room, so the room waits for it as long as it takes. The authority's is the room's.

rejoin.description: Whether a dropped player that comes back (or a newcomer of the same name) takes its seat again (og.SeatRejoined); when off, a seat once dropped stays empty and newcomers take only seats never held. The authority's is the room's.

maxPrediction.description: In rollback, the most ticks this peer runs past the last tick whose inputs are all in before it waits (a peer also predicts no further than it can re-simulate in half a frame). 8 (133 ms at 60 Hz) covers most internet latency on top of inputDelay.

PlayerInput.description: One player's input for this tick, the same on every peer: the engine writes every field but `player` at the start of each tick from the seat's input (zero for a seat nobody holds, and before its holder's first input). Its packed bytes are what crosses the room, read through this layout.

player.description: The seat whose input this entity carries (0 to og.Lockstep.players - 1); the game sets it when it spawns the player.

buttons.description: The buttons held, one bit each, as the game numbers them (bit 0 fire, bit 1 dash, ...).

x.description: The move axis, left -1 to right 1.

y.description: The move axis, back -1 to forward 1.

aimX.description: A second axis (aim, a cursor's world x), as the game uses it.

aimY.description: A second axis (aim, a cursor's world y), as the game uses it.

tick.description: The tick these values are for: the tick now, once the engine wrote them.

Desync.description: This peer's world and another's differ: sent once, at the start of the tick after the hashes showed it. The probe's `desync` dump (`dump_desync`) names the component and field that differ, once the other peer's snapshot of that tick arrived.

tick.description: The first divergent tick: the world after it differs (og.Time.tick of the snapshots compared).

peer.description: The first peer whose world differs from this one.

peers.description: How many peers' worlds differ from this one.

SeatDropped.description: A seat's player was dropped: it left the room, or stalled past og.Lockstep.stallTimeout. Sent at the start of the first tick the seat is empty, the same tick on every peer (a hashed event: the confirmed world holds it); from then on its og.PlayerInput is the zero value until og.SeatRejoined.

tick.description: The first tick the seat is empty (og.Time.tick now).

left.description: Whether the peer left the room (else it stalled and may come back).

SeatRejoined.description: A seat held before is taken again, by its returning player (og.Lockstep.rejoin) or a newcomer: sent at the start of the first tick of its new holder's input, the same tick on every peer (hashed).

peer.description: The peer that holds it now.

tick.description: The first tick of its input (og.Time.tick now).

PeerStalled.description: A running peer has sent nothing for a second (or half of stallTimeout, if shorter): for a "waiting for player" message. This peer's own (wall time decides it): never hashed, and a peer that speaks again is reported again the next time it falls silent.

seat.description: Its seat; og.Lockstep.players for a spectator.

silentMs.description: How long it has been silent, in milliseconds.

InputDesc.description: This peer's player's input: og.PlayerInput's fields but `player` and `tick`.

buttons.description: The buttons held, one bit each.

NetShapeDesc.description: A game's own input shape (og.net.shape): the record each seat's input fills in place of og.PlayerInput, and the commands a seat gives on single ticks (an RTS's orders).

input.description: The component every seat's input fills, one entity per player, in place of og.PlayerInput: a game's own with a u32 `player` field (the seat it carries, set by the game) and any others (a u32 `tick`, when it has one, is written as og.PlayerInput's is). og.net.submitInput gives this peer's. Null keeps og.PlayerInput.

command.description: The component whose values are the commands (og.net.command, read with og.net.commands): a game's own with a u32 `player` field, which the engine sets to the seat that gave the command. Used as a record shape only: no entity needs to carry it. Null: no commands.

maxCommands.description: The most commands one seat gives for one tick; og.net.command refuses one more.

LockstepSeat.description: One peer's hold on a seat.

peer.description: The peer that holds (or held) it.

since.description: The first tick of its input.

until.description: The last tick of its input, once it was dropped.

left.description: Whether it was dropped because it left the room (else it stalled).

LockstepStatus.description: Lockstep on this peer, as the probe and a HUD read it.

peer.description: This peer's number; null in no room.

startTick.description: The tick lockstep started (or this peer joined it) at.

spectators.description: The running peers without a seat.

waitingFor.description: The seats whose input for the next tick has not arrived.

waits.description: Tick boundaries this peer waited at for an input.

desync.description: The first divergent tick, once og.Desync was sent.

rollback.description: Whether the room runs in rollback (og.Lockstep.mode, the authority's).

maxPrediction.description: The room's maxPrediction while running in rollback; 0 in lockstep.

confirmedTick.description: The last tick whose every seat's input has arrived.

finalTick.description: The last tick whose world is final: run on real inputs only, the world og.net.finalHash and the hashes the peers compare cover.

acknowledged.description: The last tick through which every other running peer has all of this peer's inputs (each input message acknowledges); null alone or before the start.

predicted.description: Ticks the world now runs past its last confirmed tick (0 in lockstep).

rollbacks.description: Rewinds this peer made since lockstep started.

resimulatedTicks.description: Ticks this peer ran again after a rewind.

stalled.description: The running peers silent for a second or more (og.PeerStalled).

drops.description: Seats (and spectators) this peer has seen dropped since it joined the room.

snapshotBytes.description: The bytes of the snapshots kept for a rewind: one per tick not yet final.

ArtRotation.description: How the style's pixel art turns (ArtPixels.rotation).

x-og-variants.free: No constraint: sprites turn with their texture's filter.
x-og-variants.nearest: Rotated with nearest sampling: pixels stay square and hard, with the jagged edges of a rotated grid.
x-og-variants.cleanEdge: Rotated through the cleanEdge filter (torcado, MIT): no blur and no jaggies, the edges of the art redrawn at the angle.
x-og-variants.prerotated: Rotations baked into the sheet, ArtPixels.rotationSteps of them per turn, each redrawn as pixel art: the sprite shows the nearest one and never turns between.

ArtFilter.description: How the style's textures are sampled (ArtTexels.filter).

x-og-variants.any: No constraint: each texture's own import settings.
x-og-variants.nearest: Nearest: texels stay square and crisp up close, as low-resolution 3D and pixel art.

ArtMips.description: The mip maps of the style's textures (ArtTexels.mips).

x-og-variants.any: No constraint: each texture's own import settings.
x-og-variants.full: A full mip chain: no shimmer in the distance.
x-og-variants.none: The base level only: texels stay as crisp far away as near, as on early 3D hardware.

ArtNormals.description: How the style's models are shaded across their faces (ArtShape.normals).

x-og-variants.any: No constraint: each model's own normals.
x-og-variants.smooth: Smooth: vertex normals averaged over the faces that share them, soft forms.
x-og-variants.flat: Flat: one normal per face, every facet visible (faceted low poly, paper craft, voxels).
x-og-variants.angle: Split where neighbouring faces meet at more than ArtShape.normalAngle: hard edges stay hard, curves stay smooth.

ArtLinePlace.description: Where the style's line lies against a shape (ArtLine.place).

x-og-variants.outside: Round the shape: the line grows the silhouette by its width.
x-og-variants.inside: On the shape's own edge pixels: its size is unchanged.
x-og-variants.both: Centred on the edge: half outside, half inside.

ArtBrush.description: The brush a sprite's baked line is drawn with (ArtLine.brush), as Pixelorama's outline effect draws it: which texels within ArtLine.width of the shape's edge take the line.

x-og-variants.diamond: The texels within width steps along the grid (|dx| + |dy| at most width): a 1-pixel line touches the four sides and leaves the corners, the classic pixel-art outline.
x-og-variants.circle: The texels within a disc of radius width + 0.5: rounder corners on wide lines.
x-og-variants.square: Every texel within width across and down: the line fills the corners, so a 1-pixel line touches all eight neighbours.

ArtProjection.description: The projection of the style's camera (ArtCamera.projection).

x-og-variants.any: No constraint: the camera as the game makes it.
x-og-variants.orthographic: Orthographic: every distance at one scale (2D, isometric, top-down tactics).

ArtPalette.description: The style's colours: the palette the assets' texels sit on, how many a single asset may use, how many shades a hue ramps through, which colours are kept for signals, and how two colours mix where a tone falls between them. The frame's own quantise is Stylise.palette; this is what the assets are made of, 2D and 3D alike. Every field is no constraint at its zero value.

colors.description: The palette (og.load.palette of a `.hex` or GIMP `.gpl` file; a look names one under assets/ or a built-in `@palettes/<name>`); 0 is none, any colour.

strict.description: Every opaque texel is exactly a colour of colors (indexed colour, as hand-placed pixel art); false lets texels between them (shading, filtering) and holds only the hues to the palette.

maxColors.description: The most distinct colours one asset (a sprite sheet, a texture, a model's colours) may use; 0 is no limit.

rampSteps.description: The most shades one hue ramps through from its shadow to its highlight (3 or 4 for 8-bit art, 4 to 6 for 16-bit); 0 is no limit.

accents.description: The colours of colors kept for signals (the player, danger, the goal, a pickup), by their index in the palette (0 its first colour): scenery and backgrounds stay off them. A look gives them on one line (`accents 3 7`); empty keeps none.

dither.description: How an asset mixes the two nearest colours where a tone falls between them: none in flat bands (the zero value), or an ordered or noise pattern as Stylise.dither.

ArtPixels.description: The style's pixel grid for 2D art: one logical pixel size for every sprite, tile and backdrop, the resolution the art is drawn for, the cell sizes sprites come in, how pixel art turns and whether it stands on whole pixels. The frame's grid is Stylise.pixelHeight; this is what the assets are drawn at. Every field is no constraint at its zero value.

unit.description: Logical pixels per metre (per world unit in 2D): one pixel of every sprite, tile and backdrop covers 1/unit metres, so no two assets show pixels of different sizes (16 with 16-pixel tiles one metre wide); 0 is no constraint.

logicalHeight.description: The rows of the logical resolution the art is drawn for, as Stylise.pixelHeight counts them (180, 224, 240); 0 is no constraint.

spriteSizes.description: The cell sizes, in logical pixels, a sprite, a flipbook frame or a tile may have: each side is one of them (`spriteSizes 16 32` takes 16 x 16, 16 x 32 and 32 x 32). A look gives them on one line; empty is any size.

rotation.description: How pixel art turns: free (no constraint), nearest, cleanEdge, or prerotated in rotationSteps.

rotationSteps.description: With rotation prerotated: the rotations baked per full turn (8 is one every 45 degrees); 0 is none.

snap.description: Sprites and tiles stand on whole logical pixels: their positions are multiples of 1/unit metres, so no pixel of the art lies between two of the grid.

ArtTexels.description: The style's texel density on 3D surfaces: one density for the whole world, so no model is sharper or blurrier than its neighbours, the largest texture, and how textures are filtered and mipped. Every field is no constraint at its zero value.

density.description: Texels per metre on the surfaces of 3D models (a 2 m character at 64 texels per metre takes a 128-texel-tall texture); 0 is no constraint.

maxSize.description: The longest side of any texture of the style, in texels (256 for low-resolution 3D); 0 is no limit.

filter.description: How the style's textures are sampled: any (no constraint), nearest or linear.

mips.description: Their mip maps: any (no constraint), full or none.

ArtShape.description: The style's shape language for 3D models: triangle budgets, how faces are shaded, bevelled edges, a voxel grid and the smallest feature a silhouette keeps. Every field is no constraint at its zero value (normalAngle matters only with normals angle).

propFaces.description: The most triangles one prop may have (50 to 500 for faceted low poly); 0 is no budget.

characterFaces.description: The most triangles one character may have; 0 is no budget.

normals.description: How models are shaded across their faces: any (no constraint), smooth, flat, or angle (split past normalAngle).

normalAngle.description: With normals angle: the angle between two faces past which their edge is shaded hard.

bevel.description: Hard edges rounded by a chamfer of this radius (clay, toys, diorama pieces); 0 is none.

voxel.description: Models built of cubes of this edge (voxel worlds); 0 is no voxel grid.

silhouette.description: The thinnest feature a model's silhouette keeps at the style's scale: thinner detail does not read and is left out; 0 is no constraint.

ArtLine.description: The style's line: the outline round its sprites and meshes, its colour, where it lies against the shape and how it thins with distance. The frame's own lines are MaterialStyle.outlineWidth and Stylise.ink; this is the line the assets carry. Every field is no constraint at its zero value (color matters only with a width).

width.description: The line's width: in logical pixels round a sprite (1 is one dark pixel round the shape), in pixels at distanceFalloff round a mesh (as MaterialStyle.outlineWidth); 0 is no line.

color.description: The line's colour (linear; a look may write an sRGB "#rrggbb").

place.description: Where the line lies against the shape: outside (the zero value), inside, or both.

distanceFalloff.description: Round a mesh: the distance at which the line is width wide, nearer wider and farther thinner (as MaterialStyle.outlineDistance); 0 keeps one width.

brush.description: Round a sprite: the brush the cook draws the line into its cells with: diamond (the zero value), circle or square (docs/art.md §2.3).

ArtMotion.description: The style's motion: animation held on steps as hand animation is, how many frames a clip may hold, and how much squash and stretch its movement takes. Every field is no constraint at its zero value.

stepFps.description: Clips and flipbooks advance this many times a second whatever the tick, holding each pose between (12 is on twos at 24 fps, 8 on threes); 0 is smooth, no constraint.

maxFrames.description: The most frames one clip or flipbook may hold; 0 is no limit.

squash.description: The default squash and stretch of the style's movement: og.tween.squash's impact where a call leaves it out, 0.5 the preset's own (1.25, 0.8), 1 as rubber hose (1.5, 0.6); 0 is no constraint (the preset's own).

ArtCamera.description: The style's camera: its projection, a fixed angle (side-on, top-down, the isometric presets), the range of its field of view and whether a 2D camera moves by whole pixels. Every field is no constraint at its zero value (pitch and yaw matter only with fixedAngle).

projection.description: The projection: any (no constraint), perspective or orthographic.

fixedAngle.description: The camera keeps one angle, pitch and yaw: false is no constraint.

pitch.description: With fixedAngle: how far below the horizon the camera looks (0 side-on, 90 straight down, 30 the 2:1 pixel isometric, 35.264 true isometric).

yaw.description: With fixedAngle: its turn about the vertical axis (45 for isometric).

fovMin.description: The narrowest vertical field of view a perspective camera of the style takes; 0 is no limit.

fovMax.description: The widest vertical field of view a perspective camera of the style takes; 0 is no limit.

pixelPerfect.description: A 2D camera moves and zooms by whole logical pixels only (ArtPixels.unit), as Stylise.pixelSnap does the frame's: pixel art never shimmers as it scrolls.

x-og-variants.none: No goal: the character holds where its last goal left it.
x-og-variants.pose: A library pose where the character stands, keeping its facing.
x-og-variants.place: A library pose at a place, facing a heading.
x-og-variants.face: Turn to a heading where the character stands.
x-og-variants.walkTo: Walk or run to a point, then take a pose.

x-og-variants.none: Nowhere yet: the weights are not resident (still loading, or failed: MotionCapabilities.reason says why); agents draw og.anim's pose.
x-og-variants.gpu: On the GPU beside the renderer.

MotionAgent.description: A humanoid the motion model animates: the entity needs an og.Skeleton whose asset is a humanoid rig (og.anim.humanoid recognises its bone names, or `rig` names them). Goals queue with og.motion.pose, place, face and walkTo. The generated pose is drawn in place of og.anim's (presentation only); og.anim still poses the skeleton every tick for everything the simulation reads, and is what is drawn until the model is resident.

rig.description: The humanoid map of the skeleton (og.load.rig); 0 detects the bones from their names, as og.anim.humanoid does.

drive.description: og.motion moves og.Transform to the goals in the tick (walkTo, place, face) with fixed math, and the pose is re-rooted onto it; off, the game moves the Transform and the motion follows it, and only pose goals are taken.

turnSpeed.description: How fast a driven character turns to its heading.

lookahead.description: How much motion the model keeps generated ahead of what is drawn: more absorbs a slow GPU, less follows a changed goal sooner. Presentation only.

PoseGoalDesc.description: A pose of the model's library where the character stands (og.motion.pose).

duration.description: How long the goal is current.

PlaceGoalDesc.description: A pose of the library at a place (og.motion.place): the character's hips over `position`, facing `heading`.

position.description: Where the character stands (y is ignored: the ground is the Transform's).

heading.description: Its facing: 0 looks down +Z, π/2 down +X.

duration.description: How long the goal is current; a driven character moves there in a straight line over it.

FaceGoalDesc.description: Turn to a heading where the character stands (og.motion.face).

heading.description: The facing: 0 looks down +Z, π/2 down +X.

duration.description: How long the goal is current at least; a driven character's turn at turnSpeed may take longer.

WalkGoalDesc.description: Walk or run to a point (og.motion.walkTo); needs og.MotionAgent.drive.

speed.description: How fast: the motion walks below 2.5 m/s and runs above.

pose.description: The pose taken on arrival; empty is `idle`.

arrivalHeading.description: Facing after arrival; omitted keeps the travel heading. The goal ends only after this turn completes.

deceleration.description: Braking near the target; 0 uses 3 m/s². A CharacterController owns ground height and collision when present; otherwise motion keeps the Transform's height.

LookAtDesc.description: A timed look over locomotion: spine, neck and head share the turn, never the hips or legs. An omitted target releases the look over blend seconds.

target.description: World point to look at; omitted releases the current look.

duration.description: Seconds held after blending in, before blending out.

blend.description: Seconds to enter and leave; 0 is immediate.

maxYaw.description: Maximum yaw from the animated forward.

maxPitch.description: Maximum pitch from the animated forward.

ReactionDesc.description:
An authored humanoid reaction over locomotion. Entry, a held interval, and exit come from a cooked type motion-action asset. Timing and strength belong to the tick; the generated pose is presentation only.
**Action asset.** An .ogt starts with `type motion-action`, `version 1`, then `---`. Its body has `source "anims/brace.glb"`, `clip "brace"`, optional `rig "rigs/meshy.ogt"`, `holdStart 0.5` and `holdEnd 1.5`, each on its own line. Paths are relative to assets/. The hold must lie inside the clip (0 <= holdStart < holdEnd < clip duration), with matching poses at both ends for looping. Use a stationary root, +Z facing the reaction source, entry before the hold, and recovery after it. A 30 Hz clip is recommended; the cook also accepts other sample rates.
**Hood contact.** Optional `hand right` (or left) and `handTarget x y z` attach that wrist to an offset from the head during the hold. Supply the offset in metres along the source head bone's local axes, independent of the GLB's unit scale. Retargeting adjusts it to the target's proportions; IK follows the final head pose after lookAt. The clip owns the stance step and lean: the engine does not synthesize an untrained action. Keep provenance and licensing beside the source asset.

action.description: The motion-action asset path, such as actions/brace.ogt. Empty releases the current reaction.

direction.description: World direction the character reacts toward (toward the wind source for a brace); zero keeps the character's facing.

strength.description: Contribution of the authored reaction; 0 leaves locomotion unchanged.

duration.description: Seconds to hold between the action's holdStart and holdEnd, after its entry; then play its exit.

blend.description: Seconds to blend in and out; 0 is immediate.

MotionStatus.description: An agent's goals, as the game set them: the current goal and how many wait. Deterministic: the same on every GPU, the model's progress never shows here.

goal.description: The current goal (none: the queue is empty and the character holds).

pose.description: The current goal's pose (walkTo's arrival pose), empty for none and face.

target.description: Where the current goal goes (pose and face: where the goal started).

heading.description: The heading the current goal faces (walkTo: towards its target).

elapsed.description: How long the current goal has been current.

queued.description: Goals waiting after the current one.

completed.description: Goals finished since the agent's first.

looking.description: A look is active, including its entry or release.

reacting.description: A reaction is active, including its entry or release.

MotionPresentationState.description: Presentation progress, dependent on GPU timing, never simulation state.

x-og-variants.loading: Waiting for the model or renderer.
x-og-variants.warming: Weights are resident; this agent has no generated palette yet.
x-og-variants.ready: Generated frames and their palette are ready for the current rendered frame; authored fallback never counts.
x-og-variants.failed: Loading, inference or this agent's retarget failed; reason explains why.

MotionPresentationStatus.description: Visual readiness only, outside snapshots and hashes.

reason.description: Why it is loading, warming or failed; empty when ready.

MotionCapabilities.description: Where the motion model runs and what it knows. Presentation: a frame's answer, not the tick's; never branch the simulation on it.

backend.description: gpu once the weights are resident; none before, or when they failed.

reason.description: Why the backend is none: loading, the reason a load failed, or no GPU adapter (empty for gpu).

modelBytes.description: The size of cooked/motion/model.ogb, once read (0 before).

Destructible.description:
Makes the entity's og.Model, a model cooked with a `fracture` block, break into its chunks. A prop that stands (no og.RigidBody, or a static one) is its chunks from the first tick: each a static og.Collider (the hull of its piece) on an entity with og.Chunk, and the entity's own og.Collider and og.RigidBody are removed, so hits land on the chunks. A prop that moves (a dynamic or kinematic og.RigidBody) collides as itself until its first break, when its chunks take its place, moving as it moved, and it loses its og.Collider, og.RigidBody and og.Velocity. Until the first break the model is drawn whole; from it the model is hidden and each chunk draws its piece of it (with og.Model's tint, variant and shadows). Anchored islands stay static, the rest fall.
Scale it uniformly: a chunk's collider and mass follow og.Transform.scale's mean.

toughness.description: How much damage a square metre of bond takes before it breaks: an impulse of that many newton-seconds through 1 m² (a hit spreads over impactRadius). Glass about 50, wood 300, brick 800, concrete 2000.

strength.description: The stress its bonds hold in tension and shear before they weaken (compression holds thirty times as much, shear more for the compression across it (friction), and a bond breaks outright at twice the stress): low, an overhang falls and a wall shot out at its foot comes down; high, it holds whatever is left. 0 turns the stress solver off.

friction.description: How much more shear a bond holds for the compression across it, per pascal (Mohr–Coulomb, the tangent of the friction angle): a joint pressed by what stands on it holds where an unloaded one slips, so a wall shot out at its foot keeps its loaded piers and drops what hung over the hole, cracking in steps along its courses. 0 is shear at strength alone.

tension.description: The stress its bonds hold pulled apart, as a fraction of strength (shear and compression keep strength's). Masonry and dry stone hold almost none: mortar cracks long before brick does, so brickwork stands by its weight and friction (Heyman's no-tension masonry, the premise of masonry limit analysis), and at about 0.1 no block is left hanging from the course above over air, and a wall shot out at its foot steps back course by course over its piers. 1 is tension at strength.

density.description: The chunks' density: their mass as bodies and their weight in the stress solver.

impactThreshold.description: A collision's impulse (og.CollisionStarted.impulse) that does no damage: what is above it is the damage of the hit, and, on a prop that stood still, the push the pieces it breaks loose take along the striker's path (shared by falloff, none faster than the striker closed), so a ball through a pane carries its shards on; a moving prop's pieces keep the velocity its hit left it.

impactRadius.description: How far a hit's damage reaches round its point (all of it within a third of this, falling to nothing at it).

anchored.description: Whether its anchors (the chunks on its floor) hold it to the world; false, every island falls.

breakFx.description: A one-shot emitter (og.load.emitter, `looping false`) burst where each island breaks loose, at its broken faces: the material's own, a lit dust puff for stone and brick, splinters and a little dust for wood, shards and glints for glass. 0 none.

hitFx.description: A one-shot emitter burst at each hit that damages it: the material's own, grit and a puff off stone, splinters off wood, glints off glass; sparks only off metal, and a few. 0 none.

debris.description: Fine debris, as visuals only: a mesh-particle emitter (`render mesh`, best with `collision` and `lit true`) burst where a chunk shatters, in place of its pieces smaller than og.Destruction.debrisVolume, which then never become bodies. It is simulated and drawn on the GPU (og.destruction.capabilities' visualDebris) and never touches the simulation, so the world is the same on every device. 0: every piece is a body.

fractured.description: Written: true from its first break (the model hidden, its chunks drawn).

broken.description: Written: its bonds broken so far.

loose.description: Written: its chunks that have broken loose and still exist.

Chunk.description: One chunk of an og.Destructible, written by og.destruction when the prop fractures. A loose chunk is a dynamic body (with og.RigidBody and og.Velocity, or a child collider of its island's body); an anchored one a static collider. Drawn with its part of the destructible's model. Despawn it to clear it away.

chunk.description: Its index in the fracture asset.

level.description: 1 a support chunk, 2 a chunk's child.

body.description: The entity whose og.RigidBody moves it: its own, its island's body, or 0 while anchored.

looseTick.description: The tick it broke loose; 4294967295 while anchored.

Fractured.description: An island of chunks broke loose from a destructible during the tick (or the destructible shattered): read the tick after, for its sound, its camera shake, its score. Sent in the order the islands broke.

body.description: The island's body: the entity with its og.RigidBody.

point.description: Where it broke: the centre of its broken bonds.

cause.description: What broke it: one of the CAUSE_* codes.

maxChunks.description: The most loose chunks alive at once, over every destructible: past it the oldest loose islands (the smallest first among those that broke in the same tick) despawn, each with every chunk it carries.

debrisVolume.description: A loose island smaller than this is debris: it despawns debrisLifetime after it broke loose.

debrisLifetime.description: How long debris lasts (0: until maxChunks takes it).

fxLifetime.description: How long a breakFx or hitFx burst's entity lasts before og.destruction despawns it.

stressIterations.description: The stress solver's iterations when a destructible's support changes (Blast's maxIter). 0, the default, solves until it converges (at most six times its bonds), so a large structure's weight reaches every bond it rests on; a cap is cheaper on a slow device, but an unconverged solve loads distant bonds too little, and what should fall can stand.

stressBudget.description: The stress solver's work in one tick, across every destructible, in bond-iterations (one solver iteration over one bond). A solve that would start past it waits for the next tick, so a tick's worst case is this plus one solve (six iterations a bond) whatever comes down at once; the order is the destructibles' entity order, so a replay waits the same way. The 200-chunk brick wall's largest solve takes about 41000. 0 sets no limit.

point.description: Where it lands, in world space.

radius.description: How far it reaches; it falls linearly to nothing here from innerRadius.

innerRadius.description: Within this the bonds take the whole amount.

amount.description: The damage, as an impulse through a bond (Destructible.toughness says how much a square metre takes).

impulse.description: The momentum the blow carries, along its direction (a hammer, a wrecking ball, a shot): the pieces it breaks loose share it by its falloff and fly on, as a hit's do. Zero, the default, crushes without pushing, and what it breaks out of a standing prop can stay standing on what holds it.

radius.description: How far it reaches.

innerRadius.description: Within this everything takes the whole damage and push.

damage.description: The damage to every destructible's bonds in reach, as og.destruction.damage's amount.

impulse.description: The push outwards given to every loose chunk in reach, as an impulse at its centre, falling off as the damage does.

DestructibleInfo.description: What a destructible holds and how much of it stands (og.destruction.info).

bonds.description: The bonds of its support graph.

anchored.description: Its support chunks still held to the world.

health.description: Its bonds' remaining health over their total, 1 intact to 0 rubble.

DestructionCapabilities.description: What destruction does on this device.

visualDebris.description: Whether og.Destructible.debris bursts are simulated and drawn on the GPU here (a renderer with compute passes: og.render.capabilities' compute); false draws none of them. The bodies are the same either way: pieces given to `debris` are never bodies, on any device, so a game never depends on it.
